history.text: Do not confuse this movie with the new Krampus movie coming to theaters in 2015 Do not watch this movie unless you love amateur college films. The beginning is a little confusing, you see a child being dragged in a sack, carried by Krampus. It is then thrown into a lake, and the child managed to get free and ran away (the date was 1983- or something). Suddenly you are seeing a man getting out of bed, no date appeared/ did not even say "present day", so it takes a while before you realize it's the present day. It isn't until the bar scene when you discover that the child had been the man who woke up, who in fact was a detective-or something. ---who cares The music does not lend itself well to the movie, the acting is college student bad, and the sound effects are blah. There is one scene where the detective gazed at a wall of missing children. The scene had noises of children, however, you can tell it's on a loop, because of one unusual sound a child makes- plays over and over again. Krampus was not scary. on his hands he wore gloves, with black press on nails glued to them. He had hooves, but in certain scenes I could see the snow boots that the hooves were attached to. The acting, and pacing are off. One scene the detective/man puts a gun in his mouth, but it comes out of no where, and I wasn't sure if it was due to a flash back or what? But I didn't care. Honestly, I didn't even finish watching the movie.

history.title: Foodfight!
history.review_title: Why, but yes, I will watch it again
history.text: I would never buy this film for a child, or loved one, due to how stupid it is. However, I had bought this for myself because of all the negative feedback it had received on the internet. I had heard soooooo many reviews on this film, and how horrible it was, so I bought it, and yes, it is really bad. The animation is lifeless, and weird. Watch the movie, and you will notice that there is very little facial/ eye expressions when the characters are talking. Instead, the characters respond/react with weird jerking motions, and other bizarre body gestures/movements. For example, in one seen the dog detective is having a show down, and during his tough guy speech, he twirls around, and then points his fingers at the bad guys. The dialogue is nothing but one liner jokes, and yukkkeeeee! There is adult dialogue in this film, that is suppose to go over a child's head, but adults are suppose to get it. I liked this movie in the sense that I WATCHED it only because how bad it was suppose to be, and on that level, this movie did not disappoint me. Will I watch this movie again? The answer is yes. It is one of those films that is so awful in its appearance, music, jokes, movements, and so on that you can't help but watch it in amazement. The whole time of watching this you will say "why" and "what". It is fun to watch this and try to figure out who ever thought this was a good idea. However, the verrrrryyyyyyyy basic story line, is one that could have been salvaged, and in fact, made successful, if Disney or Pixar had create it. But for how it was made, it is an awful film. SIDE NOTE: Please do not buy this if you think it will shock you, or you think it will offend you (for it's adult jokes), because if you do you will be disappointed. Buy this with the expectations that you will be watching terrible animation, bizarre dialogue, and go no where moments that can be verrrryyyyy boring. Also, the design of the dog character was the only really cute one in this film- my opinion.

history.review_title: This film is like a Christmas version of the horror movie, "trick or treat"
history.text: The movie felt like a Christmas version of the film, "trick or treat." It followed the same concept/ idea, however, instead of the movie revolving around a Halloween theme, it instead revolved around Christmas. This film had several different stories occurring at the same time. Do not confuse this movie with the sort of film, which deals with one story at a time (like the movie "creep show"). Instead this film, as I had written above, had several different stories occurring at once. One minute you're watching the teenagers locked in the basement, and then the movie shifts to two adults- concerned about their child's bizarre behaviors. At first I became frustrated with this film, because I thought that all the people/occurrences in the movie some how connected to each other. However, I was wrong. I tried to piece all the movie segments, in my mind, together, and just couldn't do it. I believed that some how Krampus had something to do with all the situations that were occurring in this film. I wish I would have known that this was not the case, and I could have enjoyed the film more. For those who are into the Krampus theme this movie does not make him the main villain. There is no one villain/ horror character in this film (just like in the movie "trick or treat"). Krampus only had one story in this film (where he is suppose to be real). However, there was also a final story, which involved him, but in an entirely different way. As I watched the last story unfold (Santa vs Krampus) I once again thought, "is the director trying to tie the stories together (ones that involved Krampus)? The answer was no, but I LOVED THE ENDING anyway. I will watch this movie again, and I know I will enjoy it more the second time (now that I KNOW the purpose to each story) Some additional information: (1) This movie, unless you are new to the horror genre, is not scary. I would say that the only scary parts of this film were the jump scare moments. However, This movie can be intense at times, and also has its creepy moments. (2) This movie is not perfect. It does have its moments of bad dialogue, bad acting, and so on. However, the overall performances/ movie are good. This movie is hard to explain when it comes to it's build. It is not a college student style film, but it is not perfect Hollywood style either. However, if I had to put it on a scale of college, to Hollywood style, I WOULD say that it was way closer to Hollywood style-good. This movie is meant more for people who want a little horror put into their Christmas this year. Another reason that I loved this film was because, not only was a lot of effort put into making it, but unlike a lot of Christmas horror films it didn't try to be funny/silly horror (like "Silent Sleigh"), or B-rated bizarre horror (like, "Christmas Evil"). Don't get me wrong, there are one or two moments where the director added in some subtle jokes, but it wasn't enough to ruin the film. This film was not perfect, but it was refreshing to watch, especially compared to the typical cliché Christmas movie crud out there these days. I also liked how there were very few S-x scenes. As the movie played (watching the teenagers kissing) I thought, "oh brother," I waited for endless drug, and S-x scenes. However, there was only one scene, and it was nothing graphic. Maybe this lack of S-x is a downer for most, but for people like me (who have seen a lot of s-x in horror movies) it was a refreshing change of pace. It reminds people that they don't have to have loads of love making to make a horror movie good/ interesting.

history.review_title: The bees, the bees!!!!!!! can not be found any where, not even on TV!!!!!!!
history.text: This film is not great or good, it is just okay. The dialogue is some times off, and the characters' presentation (through movement, physical gestures, and so on) are either not enough, or too much. Throughout the film there are continuous dreams that Cage has about the little girl. At first it adds a creepy element, but after about the third to fourth one, the audience starts yawning and loosing focus. There are several times where Cage runs around trying to find the girl, and after a while, the audience becomes disoriented. "Where is he going now? and who cares?" The story is weaker then the original movie. Also, there are times where Cage over reacts to events around him. Like the pulling a gun on the teacher and screaming at her to get off of her bike. Yelling at the mother of the missing girl about the child's doll being burnt, and the scene where he sluggishly walks down the stairs, and punches the tavern owner in the face in order to use her bear costume. Also, I noticed several reviewers are complaining that amazon cut out the bees scene (which, by the way, you can see on youtube). The truth is that I have just watched this movie on TV, and there was no bee scene in that as well. So chances are that Cage, or the director realized how much more ridiculous the bee scene made this film, and simply had it removed. Personally, I prefer the original one (yes the original could have it's corny moments- naked girl dancing in her room trying to seduce the cop, on other side of her room). However, at least with the original, for the most part, it remand interesting, and introduced the audience into a whole new culture/ what they believed/ how they lived. This movie on the other hand does a watered down version of the culture/ life style. This film spends more time watching Cage running around, and giving bizarrely paced dialogue. Is this the worst film I have seen????? The answer is no. I have seen far worse. Did this film make me laugh, like some viewers have said it would????????????????? The answer is no. Personally, this film just annoyed me from beginning to its end. Is this the worst Cage movie I have ever seen??????? the answer is yes.

history.title: Pink Flamingos
history.text: Its an okay movie. Its overall purpose is for shock value, and in the 70's a lot of these acts were considered shocking. However, with todays mass media, and internet experience, most of this movie seems silly, and not so much shocking. There was only one scene that shocked/ angered me, and that was the (spoiler alert) man having relations with a women, while holding chickens. He eventually killed the chickens....yes...he really killed them. However, most of the film's shock value consists of: large male walking down a city street dressed in drag (like I had said, in the 70's this was shocking). A couple making love, and continuously sucking on each other's toes. Devine eating actual dog poo. Devine shoving raw meat up her dress...Okay? and the crazy egg lady, who always wants eggs. There is more, and it is an interesting movie. However, for my own personal taste, I was not impressed by this film. The acting feels like acting, and the film feels very old/dated. However, I have invested in this film, and I will eventually watch it again...for whatever reason. If you're that interested in knowing what this film is about, just buy it (for a decent price). It's worth the investment just to get that curiosity monkey off your back. THE STORY: Devine is a woman who has the reputation of being the most disgusting person in the world... or something like that? There are two other people (a dude with blue hair, and woman with red) who are trying to earn that title for themselves. This, bizarre couple has an adoption agency. The babies come from women, who the couple keeps locked in their basement. These women are rap-d by the couples man servant, and that's where the babies come from (gross). Devine has her own little bizarre life/ family. A mother who is obsessed with eggs, a son who likes strange s-x, while his sister likes to watch. And that is pretty much the movie in a nut shell.

history.title: Krampus [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: What you should know about this film
history.text: This is a very awesome, yet strange movie. It starts out as a comical dysfunctional Christmas family movie...Then it becomes dramatic and dark. Later it has a mix of both humor, and drama combined. It is hard to fully describe this film because it feels like a gambit of different movie genres combined. Sometimes it'll make you laugh, but when the serious drama kicks on, I almost felt weird for laughing at all during this movie.. THE MESSAGE: (1) be careful what you wish for (2) Remember to keep love, kindness, and hope with you, other wise you will be consumed by the darkness, which is Krampus WHAT THE MOVIE IS LIKE: If you mixed a monster movie, with a twisted Christmas fairy tale, with the Gremlin movie, with the Nightmare Before Christmas Movie (the bizarre toys), with Demonic Toys, with a helping of originality, then you have the movie Krampus THE FLAWS: Yes the movie was wonderful, and on many levels original, but it also had some flaws. (1) The one that jumped out to me was why did the grandmother have to stay and face Krampus? She did nothing to try and save her family, all she did was stare at him...and what kind of son leaves his 70 year old mother to face a demon?????????? THE GENRE I would never call this a horror movie....there is very little blood, and really no gore. It is more of bizarre/ dark/ comical film. This movie is not for children, It is more of a 13 year and older film. THIS MOVIE IS PERFECT FOR This movie is perfect for people who love strange/ original dramatic films. Also, for people who are just sick of the sappy holiday themes that most Christmas movies have. If you're tired of Christmas, or want something darker to watch during the holidays, then this is a great film to watch. SIDE NOTES: When I first saw Krampus' face I was surprised how it didn't move. However, I watched the behind the scenes part and I discovered that the face you see is not his. It is infact the face of a dead man that Krampus wears over his own....interesting. THE STORY: A boy losses his belief/ love of the Christmas season, and it is all due to his dysfunctional family. The boy tares up his letter for Santa, and throws it out the window. Due to the boy losing his love/ belief in comes Krampus. Krampus abducts the boys entire family. He does this with the help of his helpers, which are demonic elves, creatures which suck people under the snow, a killer teddy bear, a psycho tree angel, and a demented jack in the box...with the help from some killer gingerbread man cookies. In the end all is not well... remember, "Krampus does not give, he only punishes and takes"..... AWESOME MOVIE! MAJOR SPOILER ALERT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Non- of the family dies....Watch the movie to find out what happens

history.title: The Witch
history.review_title: You have to have the same point of view/ belief as the movie.
history.text: YOUR POINT OF VIEW HAS TO MATCH THE MOVIE'S: "The Witch" movie is similar to the old silent film, Haxon. In Haxon views on witch craft are presented almost like a documentary. This movie, "The Witch", accomplishes that same overall idea. The audience is not suppose to view witchcraft with modern day logic, but instead, the audience must have/believe in puritan logic. For example, when the boy is in a comma, and the parents believe that he is possessed by a witch's spell, you, the audience are expected to believe it as well. Modern day witch movies often tend to create a judgmental atmosphere where you, the modern day viewer, are suppose to view witchcraft as primitive. The audience is meant to be left with the feeling of "how ignorant could people be back in the day," However, that is not the same case with "The Witch" film. Personally, I have watched a lot of horror movies in my time, and I can't honestly say that I would classify this as a true horror film. There are moments in the movie that can be shocking, and there are one, or two jump scares. However, to me that does not make a horror movie. I would classify this film more as an intense period piece drama. THE MOVIES DOWN SIDE: Although the acting was wonderful, it was sometimes difficult to understand what the actors were saying. The dialogue not only contained very old school terms/ words, but it was often said quickly, low, and with accents... so for me I had to concentrate more on what the characters were saying (the first time I had watched this film). THE STORY: A father falls away from his church, and moves his family out into the woods. As the family builds their new life a witch abducts the baby and kills it. As the story progresses family members begin to turn against each other- and accusations of witch craft begin. I would never call this a great film...but it is good, and worth watching. P.S. Before watching this film it might help the audience to know a little bit about the puritan's beliefes...such as witches using babies' blood in spells, and the devil expecting witches to sign their names in his book of evil.

history.title: Sausage Party [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: I have not watched Seth Rogen's movies before, so I can not compare them to this film.
history.text: I have not watched Seth Rogen's movies before, so I can not compare them to this film. I love bizarre and over the top films, and this "Sausage Party" film was over the top. However, there were a few things that I felt they could have improved on. (1) I know that other viewers have complained about the over-use of the F word / S word in this film. Yes, it seems like every other sentence has the F and or S word in it. At first the cursing was funny, however, hearing these curse words used over and over again got really old, really fast. What at the beginning was funny, became annoying after a while. This is a hard movie to place for adults. It either had very immature humor, clever humor, or trying to be funny when there was nothing funny going on. Some of the jokes were both clever and charming, but others made me role my eyes. I loved the overall message of the film when it came to questioning one's beliefs, and realizing there is a possibility that there is no God. Also, that there is no sin in feeling the natural urges that your body tells you. In all, the film had both toilet humor, and a deeper theme/ message. The story tended to go extreme at times. For example, the food products realizing they shouldn't blindly follow a belief that is not supported by any real proof. To the food having a bisexual s-x orgy. In all honesty, I don't think that most people are expecting this mix-up within this film, so the first time watching it is a little puzzling? What do you make of it when it goes from being philosophical to a food orgy???? The first time I watched this film I did not like it. However, I watched it a second time (three weeks later) and I actually laughed, and liked it more. It grows on you the more you watch it. However, I could not take a daily dose of this film either. It's a film that requires a breathing period before the next time a viewer sits down to watch it again.

history.title: Feud Season 1
history.review_title: A detaile review about this series.
history.text: I have waited for years for Hollywood to create a series/ movie related to the turbulent relationship between Joan Crawford and Bette Davis. Before I continue I want to clarify that I am not going to review the DVD and or Blue Ray set of this TV series, but instead the show itself (SPOILERS). Anyway, I loved how this series really tried to stay accurate to the Bette and Joan feud. The series starts off with the two movie stars working on the film of Whatever happened to Baby Jane, and it ends with (SPOILER) Joan Crawford's final B-rated movie, Trog. The series itself ran (roughly/ what I remember) for about eight to nine episodes, and each episode was about an hour long. Each actress (Ms. Lang, and Ms. Sarandon) did an amazing job with their portrayal of their characters. I am not saying that either actress came across 100% as the real Bette or Joan, but instead that their take/interpretation on the two stars (Lang's and Surrandon's) acting was superbly done. This series is enjoyable for both Bette and Joan fans, as well as for those who have never heard of these old school actresses. The overall series revolved around Bette and Joan, whose movie careers were passed their prime. These two middle aged actresses struggled and fought for movie roles, and played in the movie, Whatever Happened to Baby Jane. During the shooting of the film the two actress were intentionally set against each other by having their hatred for each fanned by the higher powers that be. Both actress, and the Warner Studios were surprised at the enormous hit that Whatever Happened to Baby Jane became. However, the movie's success created a new type of genre for older actress (aging actress play crazy roles), and both Bette and Joan still struggled to get descent movie roles. Despite the success of Baby Jane both actress were discriminated against due to their age. During this series both ladies both dislike each other, yet have so much in common. It is a brilliant series, and I also love the real life details that were added into it. Some of them included (SPOILER): (1) Joan Crawford's supposed (never proven) porn film that she had created at the beginning of her career. (2) Crawford's leach of a brother, (3) Bette Davis actually kicking Crawford in the head during Baby Jane, (4) Bette complaining about landing on Crawford's false chest (5) Davis' daughter being cast as the next door neighbor, yet not having any previous acting experience, (6) Crawford always having to come across as the glamorous movie star, (7) Crawford accepting the academy award for Ms. Bancroft, (8) Davis making Crawford's life difficult on the filming of Hush Hush Sweet Charlotte (9) Crawford having to dress in an old van during the filming of Trog, and not being able to remember her lines, and so on. I really appreciated the little details that only a Crawford and Davis fan would pick up on. I remember hearing how Jessica Lang wanted as much true to life examples added into this series, and I say God bless her for that! If you don't know anything about Bette or Joann, or their history together this series is still enjoyable to watch. It really delves into the sexism, and discrimination against an older actress during that time in film history. Also, how brutal the Hollywood System could be to two older female stars.

history.title: Cult of Chucky [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: This Child's Play Film is the same, yet different form the other ones. (spoiler alert)
history.text: Once again, the director, just like in "Curse of Chucky", brings the Child's Play Movies back to what it was originally (comical, creepy, intense). I don't know if the director had enough complaints after he created the badly written "Seed of Chucky" (all comedy, and little to no tenseness), but in the last two installments of this series he has certainly improved on his story telling. This newer film "Cult of Chucky" --- Yes, it is the same story of a killer doll, but in this version it not only takes place in an mental institution, but it also messes with the audience's perception of Chucky. I have to admit, I really respected the director for changing his story telling with this newer film. However, when I first was watching it, the film kind of annoyed me. The overall film is not explained until the end. I am not use to this regarding a Child's Play Movie. I have seen all of these films, and I know what to expect, and there is no mystery to them. However, with this one, most of it (first time watching) is a mystery. What I mean is, "is Chucky with Andy?" Or "is chucky in the institution?" "Is the director going to change the story where Nika is the killer and Chucky isn't really there with her?" So yes, initially I was not expecting this, and it did throw my interest in the film. But towards the end I really enjoyed this film, and I really respected the director with his newer ideas. This is the director's 7th Child's Play movie, and yet he continues to improve on each sequel. Unlike other sequels like "Jason Goes to Space, or Hell" this one still takes the story and villain seriously, and I do appreciate that. Is this a perfect movie? =no. There are certain plot holes, certain things that are not fully explained, and parts that could have been written better. However, for a sequel it is darn good. The director had tweaked the story a little form its original 30 year overall story telling of Chucky needing a human to transfer his soul into. At the end of every child's play film the audience wonders if chucky will finally succeed. However, in this film that is not the case. SPOILER ALERT- I will say that I was a little disappointed towards the end of this movie. I thought it was going to be a final show down between Andy and Chucky= no, I was also expecting Tiffany to come back in doll form (she does in a way, but only in the last several seconds of the film). If you are a die hard Child's Play fan like I am, you will certainly want to buy this, and add it to your Chucky collection. Also, towards the end of the film it is highly suggested that there will be an 8th sequel, which I am looking forward to. The Plot Nika (from the Curse of Chucky) is in an institution. She has been convicted of killing her family, and the doctor tries to get Nika to admit to the murders. While she is institutionalized murders occur, and Chucky dolls are being introduced throughout the film. Andy Barkley hears about Nika/ Chucky and drives to the institution to have a final show down with Chucky (I guess), while at the same time Andy has a Chucky head that is alive and can talk. As the murders continue Nika continues to protest her innocents, and blames Chucky for the murders (no one believes her). During the murders the audience is left wandering if Nika is still sane or insane, and is she commiting some, or all of the crimes? The story is still about the killer doll, but it takes some newer, and darker turns that make in worth watching.

history.title: Francesco Di Assisi
history.review_title: Thank you, Liliana for this masterpiece.
history.text: The Vatican rated this as one of the greatest of all religious movies, ignoring a plethora of others. Is it great? I think it is. Cavani shows movie making skills of the highest order. Lou Castel shows acting skills almost without equal. I would rate him over Marlon Brando. Heartbreaking, realistic performance. He somehow portrays his soul's progress toward God without becoming less like himself or overtly pious, his growing sanctity is as natural as breathing is for us. He portrays what is impossible to portray, a man becoming a saint. We rejoice in his every virtue as they manifest themselves. God's grace flows through him undiluted and unimpeded. An extremely wise and intelligent piece of filmmaking.

history.title: My Man Godfrey (Color/Black and White)
history.text: This is the one movie that I tell my friends about first. It just comes together beautifully due to exemplary direction and acting that can not be imitated. Its theme? We all live on the knife's edge: Riches / poverty, Selfishess / charitableness, Honesty / Deceit, Expertise / Idiocy and we are guided by the inner gyroscope of morality and most of all, love. But the deep question is: Who is saving whom? Hint: Carol looks into his eyes when she has only just met Godfrey and says: "I'm not going to do this anymore. It is really kind of sordid (using people) when you think about it, I mean when you think it over." Actually there is no direct answer to this question. Love saves them all. The movie more deeply examines the mystery of love. The mystery being of how God, who is love, creates the profound dynamic between those who love to heal and build and perfect and accomplish the impossible. Love is the source of all virtue. PS You will want to check out Carole Lombard's dress in the opening scene. It is the most beautiful dress ever made. No actress has ever looked so radiant with the possible exception of Julie Andrews in the Sound of Music.

history.text: I streamed this original series under my husbands account. Great back stories and accounts to some of the greatest stores of our generations. Well done researched. Looking forward to a Season 2.

history.title: Automobiles: 1988 IROC-Z Camaro
history.text: This product looks just like the DVD's of the History Channel's "Automobiles" series. It is not! This was part of a reality show series in which two "teams" of people would modify an IROC-Z Camaro and drag race them head-to-head. Frankly, I thought it was boring. Neither team really impressed me and just added bolt-on equipment onto the motor. There was nothing more sophisticated than that. I was very disappointed. It definitely wasn't worth the money and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone wanting to learn more about the IROC-Z Camaros that Chevrolet built in the 1980s. Not worth the money. Two stars.

history.title: Nova: Iceman Reborn
history.text: Iceman Reborn is the story of Gary Staab's commission to create a synthetic duplicate of the Iceman, or Otzi, so that it could be more accessible to more than the tiny number of researchers who have access to this prehistoric man's remains. That's what this DVD is about. Gary Staab has reproduced many now-extinct animals for museums and other exhibitions. Beginning with a 3-D printed plastic copy of the Iceman's basic form, it's up to Gary to reproduce the colors and textures of Otzi's body for display. There's really it. There's no information about the man, despite a short segment on his DNA which we wasn't new. I was expecting more. If the artist's craft is what you're wanting to see, this is the DVD for you. I, frankly, was expecting more about Otzi and I can't give this video more than three stars.

history.title: Battlefield Series 6: Scandinavia; The Forgotten Front
history.text: This "Battlefield" series title tells the story of the Winter War between the Soviet colossus and the tiny army of Finland. First of all, let's get the length issue out of the way - this is part one of a two part Battlefield production...but it is complete in and of itself. The DVD is about the Winter War only. The Battlefield series is usually about a single-topic that lasts two hours. Some, such as Pearl Harbor and the Fall of Singapore are on the same DVD with each topic getting one hour each. What they did was to give you half the regular DVD of a two-parter. Back to the review of this product. Like any Battlefield product, this DVD tells the story of a battle or a campaign. In this case, it's the 1940 war between the colossal might of the USSR and the tiny nation of Finland. You'll get a fairly comprehensive review of the strategic situation before the war, Soviet and Finnish objectives, commanders, weapons and the course of the campaign. I think the DVD did an excellent job of showing the viewer the uniqueness of this campaign in which the small, citizen army of Finland performed remarkably well after the initial shock of combat wore off. The Soviets would use the same brutal-but-effective mass tactics in which they would gladly sacrifice large numbers of their own soldiers in the cruelest of attrition warfare. In the end, the Finns were overwhelmed and their hope of Western intervention was unrealized. It's not the same length as other Battlefield DVD's but still fairly good for it's length. Four stars.

history.title: Last Man On The Moon, The
history.review_title: He made the last footprints on the Moon.
history.text: In this DVD, we have the story of the American space program from Gemini to Apollo as told by Eugene "Gene" Cernan. The naval aviator who was given the opportunity to join the space program and walked in space and on the moon narrates this video with period film, interviews and the reminiscences of Cernan and others. This is the story of Cernan, his comrades in the space program, their families and the missions they flew. Cernan has a unique perspective to give since he came in fairly early (the Gemini missions) and stayed in the program until he ended up being the last man to walk on the moon, the last to leave a footprint on the powdery surface of the moon in the Apollo 17 mission. He and the others interviewed in this DVD give us insight into the times, the technology, the personalities and the life of the astronauts. This is a really good DVD about the space program by one of the men who was there. Recommended with five stars.

history.title: Race To Space - America's Greatest Journey
history.text: I will be frank. I did not like this series. It's a black-and-white series from the 1960's with Mike Wallace about the space program. It's very old, very dated. There's a lot of footage here, but just not a very good production. I was not happy with the purchase. Unless you just want it for nostalgia, I'd steer clear of this series.

history.title: Tractors at War Volume 1
history.text: Though not a very long video (43 minutes), there's a lot of information presented to the viewer regarding the importance of American agriculture and agricultural machinery makers. The DVD shows the revolutionary new agricultural products brought to market during the war to increase food production, save man-hours or use les materials such as the Ford "N" series with the Ferguson hydraulic-operated 3-point hitch system and the Massey-Harris combines. What is often forgotten is that the United States produced so much of the allies foodstuffs during WWII. By the end of the war, virtually every mouthful of food the Soviet soldier ate came from the US or Britain - mostly the US. The American farmer was one of the unsung victors of WWII. The video also relates the war production that agricultural-machinery makers undertook instead of tractors. The DVD highlights John Deere and Allis Chalmers and JI Case (which made a number of construction vehicles that could be air-landed to build airfields), but oddly enough does not mention the work done by International Harvester which, among other things, built 7500 half-tracked armored personnel carriers. The DVD gives credit to farmers who went to war or fought to keep the world from starving as well as the women who were pressed into male roles in the factory and the farm. I would have liked to have seen more of the models that were allowed to be built during WWII, but a good video for the tractor enthusiast none-the-less. Four stars.

history.title: The Finest Hours
history.text: At last! An action/adventure film without a single gunshot! Not that I have anything against a good shoot-em-up, but a man vs. nature tale is just what the doctor ordered. This is the story of Coast Guardsmen at their best, risking their own lives to save others. The story takes place in the winter of 1952 when two aging WWII tankers break in half off the Massachusetts coast in a storm. The story focuses on the rescue of the SS Pendleton in which a small boat must brave towering waves and gale-force winds just to get to the stricken tanker...or, rather, the aft part of the ship since it broke in half and the bow section sank. There are two related stories in this film. The first is the Coast Guard crew of Bernard C. Webber, Andrew J. Fitzgerald, Richard P. Livese and Ervin E. Mask. These men must risk everything just to get over the bar, a task likely to get them killed even before the rescue even begins. The second story is of the crew of the Pendleton who must overcome their disunity to keep the aft section of the ship afloat long enough for help to reach them. It's an engrossing film...once it gets moving. The reason it lost a star with me is the rather clumsy romance between Chris Pine and Holliday Grainger which is the focus of the first 15 minutes of the film. None the less, the rest of the film is worth it. A great action/adventure film and definitely worth four stars.

history.title: Winning: The Only Denominator - The Story of the 2010 Indianapolis Colts
history.text: This is an NFL Films team highlight reel. In this case, it's the 2010 Indianapolis Colts and each game played - including the losing playoff effort against the NY Jets - is chronicled. This DVD recounts the last season Peyton Manning was quarterback for the Indianapolis Colts and for that reason alone it has a special place in the hearts of Colts fans. As a highlight film, there are no interviews, but there's audio from the players and coaches that were "miced up". With a 10-6 record, it was one of the least successful seasons for the Manning-led Colts and at various points in the season, one could, with hindsight, see Peyton's diminishing physical abilites. It's a good "highlight reel" for Colts fans and will bring back memories of better days.

history.title: NFL Super Bowl XLI - Indianapolis Colts Championship
history.review_title: Highlights of the Colts Superbowl season.
history.text: This is an excellent DVD and a "must have" for any Colts fan. This is the story of the 2006 Indianapolis Colts team that finally brought the Vince Lombardi Trophy to Indianapolis. First off, this is NOT the broadcast of Superbowl XLI. What it is, is the highlights of the entire season, game by game. The DVD chronicles the games played, the victories, the losses, the playoff games and the Superbowl. This DVD is all about the season which culminated in the championship. This is an NFL Films product and includes the cinematography and original music we've all come to expect from them. This is the story of the whole season, one game at a time. Each game is highlighted and the heroes and acknowledged. The major actors in the season were Quarterback Peyton Manning who was the leader of the team, Coach Tony Dungy who would prove to be the first black coach to win a Superbowl and a defense that was one of the league's worst during the regular season but became a dominant defense in the post season. If you're looking for the broadcasts of the playoff games and Superbowl, go here: [[ASIN:B000RPD0IC Indianapolis Colts: Road to Super Bowl XLI (Post-Season Collector's Edition)]]. This DVD is an excellent companion to those broadcasts because it chronicles the road the Colts trod to get to the playoffs and championship.

history.title: NFL: America's Game: Oakland Raiders
history.text: I'm not a Raiders fan, but I am a fan of sports stories. The "America's Game" series originally shown on NFL Channel is an excellent, well produced series of documentaries. This three-disk set covers the three Super Bowl winning Raiders Teams. The first, the 1976 Raiders, is the story of the original "renegades" told by John Madden, Ken Stabler and Phil Vallapiano. The second disk is about the 1980 Raiders told by Jim Plunkett, Gene Upshaw and Matt Millen. The third is the 1983 LA Raiders whose story is told by Marcus Allen, Todd Christiansen and Howie Long. The stories you hear about these athletes as they chase a championship! The often hilarious quotes! Ken Stabler on having a night life on the eve of games: "How much sleep do you really need to play a three hour game? A lot of the time, I studied the game plan by the light of the jukebox." Matt Millen on his teammates when drafted by the Raiders: "All I knew about John Matuzak was that he was supposed to be crazy...and he didn't disappoint." The Raiders was the team that was often the only hope for players cast off by the other teams and as Guard Gene Upshaw pointed out to players who found themselves on his team, "We told people there aren't many stops after this one." These basically hour-long documentaries are studies of men in a competitive endeavor and as such they reveal much about human nature. They're well made, well produced and have excellent music and cinematography. The three-disc set was a bargain to boot!

history.title: The Assassins [Blu-ray]
history.text: I thought this was going to be a great Chinese drama, but something must have been lost in translation. I could not, for the life of me, figure out why Ling Ju loved Mu Shun. They grew up together, so what? The movie only shows that part for maybe five minutes. At the end, their storyline didn't move me at all. There are several parts I just could not figure out. One in particular, was when Cao Cao is outside with his medicine and Ling Ju comes walking up the stairs, he pours it out in front of her then throws the dish. Why? Were things cut out? He eventually mentions her love for another, but I don't know how he knew, he didn't seem to take much notice of her the whole movie. I couldn't figure out if she was supposed to be his concubine or his wife. I did like Chow Yun Fat's acting. He really did well as a world-weary general who just wants to put down his sword and rest. The guy playing the Emperor was just absolutely ridiculous, I hope that was his intention, because I just could not take him seriously. Also, he must have a night gig singing in hell, because that was just absolutely atrocious.

history.title: Sin City: A Dame to Kill For (Blu-ray 3D + Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD) [3D Blu-ray]

history.title: Maggie [DVD + Digital]
history.text: This was absolutely one of the most boring zombie movies I have ever seen. The preview was incredibly misleading, I thought I was getting an action movie about a man searching for his wayward zombie daughter. Instead I got a movie about people reacting with what I thought was good survival instincts, but I guess I was supposed to feel sorry that everyone wanted to stick the zombies in a place far, far away. The movie kept acting like it was so contagious (hence sticking zombies in quarantine), but no one else seemed concerned? I am unsure if it was contagious by anything other than being bitten. A real let down.

history.title: San Andreas (2 Disc/DVD)
history.text: It's an okay movie. All the action gets a little tedious after a while, and it's a little far-fetched (I'm pretty sure a tidal wave doesn't move that slow). The special effects are really good. It's not a movie I could watch over and over like Day After Tomorrow or Oblivion, but it's good for date night.

history.text: The action was okay, I just couldn't bring myself to care about any of it. If it had been anyone but Jason Statham, I would have shut it off after the woman gets kidnapped. I just don't get the incentive (or how they found him in Thailand). I also don't care for Jessica Alba's acting, she never sells me the character she's playing.

they are amazing. I have no idea why this show was cancelled so soon, unless season 5 is what killed it. Season 5 is a snooze fest, with flashbacks to the past that have no drama, since we already know what happens. I say watch the first four seasons, then pick up a history book and read the rest.

history.title: The Railway Man
history.review_title: Kidman is always excellent. Firth was disappointing
history.text: Kidman is always excellent. Firth was disappointing, however. His acting was lukewarm and expressionless, especially given the story content. Overall it was a mediocre film that had a lot of unrealized potential. A shame really.

history.title: Wrinkles
history.text: Nothing funny here. A spot-on piece of nursing home realism. Unfortunately, critics of nursing care don't understand that all people and families are not equipped to care for elderly parents, especially when they've been away from them most of their lives and are barely making ends meet in their own stressful lives. At a time when they should be looking forward to some final peace at retirement they are faced with becoming parents to parents. It's unbearably sad all around. I would've found this more uplifting if it hadn't hit home so depressingly hard.

history.title: World War Z (Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD)
history.text: Loved it. Brad was excellent and the movie was fast-paced.

history.title: Spartacus: The Complete Series [Blu-ray]
history.text: Beautiful packaging! That said, this series is an annoying and amateurish production if you've already seen Game of Thrones. It looks fake, has poor character development, and an absurd recurrence of splish splashing cherry red blood that flies through the air and supposedly hits the camera lens. If that weren't silly enough, the film has constant speed changes to stop and slow the motion in case you didn't get a good enough look at these supposed "spectacular " special effects. Laughable attempt to titillate the gullible viewer.

history.title: Be Yourself
history.review_title: The real Fannie in an okay movie with several musical highglights
history.text: Early in "Be Yourself," which was made in 1930, someone tells Fannie Brice, "You know, you're a funny girl." That she is, playing a nightclub entertainer in love with a boxer. The songs are so-so, except for "I'm Cookin' Breakfast for the One I Love," the film's comic highlight. But you get to see the original Funny Girl mugging, singing songs both dramatic and antic and wearing period clothes elegantly. This was a lady who had style, who knew how to use every talent she had at her disposal and brother, she had plenty. She almost never walks out of frame without a funny look, as if she doesn't want a dull frame in the picture. A bit hokey-poky, but who cares when you're watching one of the great entertainers of the twentieth century?

history.title: Marlowe
history.review_title: Cool Updating of Raymond Chandler's "Marlowe" character
history.text: This under-appreciated 1969 update of Raymond Chandler's "The Little Sister" should have been more successful than it was. James Garner isn't an intense Philip Marlowe, he's more a cool, laidback private eye, in his "Rockford Files" style. But the story is solid, the screenplay is by the excellent Stirling Silliphant and there are three great leading ladies: beautiful Gayle Hunnicutt, bitchy young Sharon Farrell (whatever happened to her?) and Rita Moreno as a stripper in a blonde wig. Also, a parade of great character actors: Carroll O'Connor, William Daniels, Jackie Coogan and -- surprise, surprise -- Bruce Lee in a knock-out two scenes. In the last one, he makes the most dramatic exit from a movie since Agnes Moorehead in "Dark Passage." Directed by a major TV talent -- Paul Bogart -- who should have had the same kind of movie success that one-time TV director Norman Jewison did.

history.title: Lady of Burlesque
history.review_title: Backstage Burlesque comedy-mystery with Barbara Stanwyck and lots of great character actors
history.text: Burlesque, not the way it really was, but the backstage atmosphere, wisecracks and mystery from Gypsy Rose Lee's novel "The G-String Murders" make it worth your time. (The book is more complicated, with several twists at the end that aren't here, but isn't that always the case with books turned into movies?) Star Barbara Stanwyck began as a dancer on Broadway and her challenge dance with Pinky Lee to cover up a backstage brawl is astonishingly good. This babe could could do it all! The cast is wonderful: Michael O'Shea as Rags Ragland-type comic,the hilariously sublime Iris Adrian as Stanwyck's gal pal, Stephanie Bachelor as "The Princess Nirvina," J. Edward Bromberg as the cop investigating the crimes, Gerald Mohr as a gangster and glorious, lisping blonde Marian Martin as the danseuse Pinky Lee fancies. Stanwyck gets a funny, gritty song: "Take it Off the E-string, Play it on the G-String." This is a movie I can -- and do -- watch again and again.

history.review_title: Boogey Man Burlesque Great family fun
history.text: A classic horror spoof, in which Bud and Lou tangle with the Frankenstein Monster (Glenn Strange), Dracula (Bela Lugosi, playing the vampire for the last time on film) and The Wolf Man (Lon Chaney Jr.). Costello sitting in the Monster's lap, the plot calling for Lou's brain to be transplanted into the Monster's skull and the Wolf Man's travails when the moon is full, delight fans no matter how many times they see this Boogey Man burlesque. Some cool, if rudimentary special effects involving Dracula, are both hokey and spookey. Great for both adults and kids. Get the popcorn popping and gather the whole family around for this one.

history.title: Cry Wolf
history.review_title: Two great stars in one nutty melodrama
history.text: Flynn and Stanwyck in a standard, formulaic old dark house and strange goings-on in a laboratory melodrama. Both stars must have been given lobotomies to persuade them to do this one. Stanwyck has played the Lady-in-Jeopardy well in other films, but never one as nutty and lame as what we have here.

history.title: The Two Mrs. Carrolls [Remaster]
history.text: Bogie as a psycho artist who paints his wives as dark, grotesque harpies, kills them and goes on to the next as his precocious little daughter observes it all with cool detachment. Rather unpleasant unless you get into the nasty spirit of the piece. A good double feature would pair "The Two Mrs. Carrolls" with "Conflict." In both, Bogie's lusting after Alexis Smith at her freshest and most alluring.

history.title: Horror Island
history.text: Good-ish littleUniversal B-movie horror film, set in an island castle with sliding panels, secret passages, etc. Too bad they don't make better use of Iris Adrian, one of the movies' primo. wisecracking "Gal pals." See Iris at her best in "Lady of Burlesque."

history.title: Long Day's Journey Into Night
history.review_title: O'NEILL'S BEST PLAY, WITH A SUBLIME CAST
history.text: One of the great plays of the 20th century, with a superb cast: Katharine Hepburn, Ralph Richardson, Jason Robards, Jr. and Dean Stockwell, each one at their best. The unsparing story of playwright Eugene O'Neill's wildly dysfunctional family, barely disguised, which is why he didn't want it performed until after his death. With each viewing, its impact grows.

history.title: These Glamour Girls
history.review_title: Lana and fellow starlets shine in MGM comedy
history.text: Great early Lana Turner vehicle as a dime-a-dance girl invited by Lew Ayres as a drunken joke to "frat house parties." Marsha Hunt outstanding as a party girl who's been to one too many, a very young Richard Carlson, debs Jane Bryan, Anita Louise, Ann Rutherford and the inescapable Mary Beth Hughes. Great fun to see all these starlets just getting a foothold in movies..

history.title: The Village
history.text: I actually went to a movie theater and paid big bucks to see "The Village." I can't believe I did that. This is not a scary movie. It isn't a psychological thriller. It isn't a good ghost story. It isn't even interesting. It is boring, obvious, and really disappointing. Don't buy this movie. I wanted to like "The Village"; I even thought I would like it. Didn't happen ... bored, bored, bored. Google Roger Ebert's review (rest his soul). Google any critic's review. Save yourself.

history.title: Frontline: The Long Walk of Nelson Mandela
history.text: The person I gave this to as a gift is very happy with it. He said that it is an excellent addition to his Mandela collection and African American history collection. He's very satisfied.

history.title: Arne Dahl
history.text: Each of the 5 disks contain a two part episode, and each part is 90 minutes long. For binge watchers, this doesn't represent any problems, but for me I only watch one part of an episode on one day, and the next part another time. While the team at first seemed disjointed, I quickly warmed up to the characters. It doesn't make sense to compare this series to The Killing or The Bridge; if that's what you're looking for, don't purchase these. However, if you want very well acted police procedurals and a diverse team of experts, then give this series a try. These dramas are not fast-moving, and while they are suspenseful, they won't keep you on the edge of your seat. Rather than focusing on one really strong character as The Killing or The Bridge, you get to know a team that has been pulled together by Commander Jenny Hultin, an older female officer. It takes time for the team to gel, but they do, and the rewards are great if you stay with them through five, two-part stories.

I heard so much buzz about The Good Wife that I finally decided I needed to give it a look. I was hooked from the first episode, and I usually don't expect much from any TV series' opener. I expected Julianna Margulies to be good - I've always liked her - but she's far better than good; she's excellent. The really great thing about The Good Wife is that everyone else is good too, even Chris Noth. I have to admit, I'm not a big Chris Noth fan, but he's better in this series than I've ever seen him. I've only watched about half a dozen episodes so far, and I'm looking forward to many more to enjoy. If you've hesitated to try this series for any reason, give it about 50 minutes. It's not just another lawyer show; it's a cut above.

history.title: The Good Wife
history.review_title: Very entertaining and well acted series
history.text: Keeps getting better and better!

history.review_title: Takes Kalinda's character down the wrong path
history.text: I commented on another reviewer's statements regarding the unfortunate decision to take Kalinda's character down the wrong path. The addition of an abusive husband who has some type of sick hold over an otherwise strong character did nothing to enhance the mystery of Kalinda. In fact, it diminished her character. I don't think the writers really understood the strength of the character they had created. Whatever they intended her to be, Archie Panjabi took her beyond that scope and created a truly unique and memorable woman. It's no wonder Panjabi left the series after Josh Charles, and now, Julianna Margulies appears to be leaving as well. Even the Kings are leaving. In my opinion, the problems start with not fully appreciating the complexity of Kalenda's character. The decision to portray her as just another of Peter's conquests to damage her friendship with Alicia was the first of several miscalculations in developing the character of Kalinda Sharma. The writers took the easy way out with Kalinda and focused on superficial sexual encounters rather than providing more substantive character development. There are still many fine episodes in The Good Wife. But the heart has gone out of it.

history.review_title: While season 5 is better than season 4
history.text: While season 5 is better than season 4, the show continues to trend downwards. I understand why Josh Charles wanted to leave the series - its decline is obvious - but why kill off his character? Let me say here, that I'm not a fan of killing off characters in a TV series. For me, it shows a lack of imagination. But seriously, having a client shoot Will in the court room by grabbing the gun of a careless guard was a real stretch, and it's been done before on TV. And now the series has to keep exploring Alicia's grief - not just in season 5 but beyond. Enough already. This truly is pure soap opera material, and when The Good Wife began, it was much better than a night time soap drama. Unfortunately, the soap opera aspect is taking over more and more of the show. I'll still watch for the few episodes that are actually good, but I can see why the show is coming to an end. And, for me, the beginning of the end started with the writers taking Kalinda's character in the wrong direction in season 4. It's all over but the shouting.

history.title: Blue Bloods: Season 5
history.review_title: One of my favorite TV series
history.text: I'm a big fan of Blue Bloods, and I purchase every season. Season 5 is great, and I received the DVD set fast. If you've never watched Blue Bloods, you're missing out on an excellent series. Give it a try.

The actor playing Eve Winter is very good, but she's short-changed by the character. I found myself wishing for Prime Suspect and Jane's tough yet complex character. Winter is just not very interesting and not very good at her job. The show plods on for six episodes and only perks up during the last two. Winter lets things happen that shouldn't and wouldn't if she were better at her job. I see that this is titled, Winter: The Complete Series, and I understand why. I would not watch a second season of this show. I hope the actors move on to better scripts.

history.title: Midnight Man [DVD] [2008]
history.text: I love James Nesbitt and even though his character in this series, Max Raban, makes some pretty bad mistakes, the mistakes seem plausible. Raban has a diagnosed phobia of daylight, thus the title. He's is a journalist trying to make a come back when he unearths a very scary conspiracy. I'll just say that the bad guys in Midnight Man are really evil, and I was able to forgive Max for not fully realizing that sooner. The young actress who plays his daughter, Martha (Romy Irving), is wonderful, and the relationship between Max and Martha struck me as real and unique. Nesbitt and Irving also star in a film called Blessed; they really do have an excellent on-screen rapport. It would be interesting to see a second series of Midnight Man with Nesbitt and Irving as a father/daughter journalist team.

history.title: Intruders
history.text: A lame story with slow, plodding directing. Even Clive Owen could not save this sad attempt at a scary story. John Farrow's (played by Owen) young daughter, Mia, begins writing a scary story for school. At night she is being visited by a presence without a face who is trying to capture her to steal hers. There is a twist that you don't see coming, which is always fun, but in this case, it was too little too late. Just a big disappointment.

history.title: All Is Lost [DVD + Digital]
history.text: There were some scary situations written into this movie that could have been heart-pounding scenes, but to me, Robert Redford's rather "stoic", expressionless acting took a lot of the excitement out of this movie. (I've been a fan of his throughout his career, but this time he looked like he was phoning it in.) SPOILER ALERT: Even the ending left you wanting to see him having some human interaction, but we were even denied that. I hope I saved you time and money.

history.title: Sicario
history.review_title: Interesting story, great action, heart-pounding pacing! I highly recommend it!
history.text: Difficult to watch in places because of the violence but necessary to tell this story of our understaffed, under-funded FBI (with law tying their hands behind their back) fighting Mexican drug cartels. The story makes you question how far can you morally push the boundaries in the name of saving the most lives. Emily Blunt stands in for our belief that we should obey the law at all cost. history.title: Megan Leavey
history.review_title: Best Movie I Have Seen in a Long, Long Time! SO well-written & acted! Gives a view of war we don't see!
history.text: This movie stuck with me long after I had seen it. It was so much more than about a bomb-sniffing dog and his trainer. There are so many of us, I think, that can relate to & understand animals better than we can with people. Megan instinctively understood Rex's needs and how to relate to him. He had been labeled as "aggressive" by the veterinarian (who would have been extremely believable as one of the more cruel Nazis in WWII). Megan came from a broken family and a narcissistic mother, so she had issues of her own. This movie showed VERY CLEARLY the fear you feel fighting in a war, how the Marines have each other's backs, what it feels like to be tossed through the air by a bomb and what the noise and compression does to you and teaches you that the heroes who save thousands of lives by sniffing out bombs for their handlers can also suffer PTSD. Well written, directed, filmed, edited and GREAT acting that captured you and didn't let go. Highly recommended.

history.review_title: A Well-Made Sequel to A Christmas Carol
history.text: This film is a well-made sequel to the classic tale, A Christmas Carol, by Charles Dickens. The quality of the "film" is so high that you can see pimples under heavy make-up. The colors are vibrant. The filming location, at least for some of the outdoor scenes, is, apparently, Fort Atkinson, Wisconsin, and clean, luxurious neighborhoods therein. The costumes and props are well-designed and believable. Overall, this is a positive, heartwarming, Christian film, ideal for people of all ages. The story begins in December, 1844, approximately one year after Ebenezer Scrooge entertained the ghosts of Jacob Marley and the Christmases Past, Present, and Future. Then, when he goes outside to go Christmas shopping, he miraculously finds himself in the fictitious city of New Britain, Wisconsin. (Fort Atkinson apparently plays the "role" of this city. I was able to determine this by Googling the name of one of the businesses whose name appeared on a window.) Adjusting to simple things, such as squeezable ketchup bottles, Mr. Scrooge soon discovers that it's 2013, approximately 170 years after he went out shopping in London. He also soon discovers that a descendant of Tiny Tim has inherited his business, and is as miserly as he (Scrooge) was, in November, 1843. He's about to foreclose on the Dinner Belle dining establishment, owned and operated by a young blonde woman named Belle, who is a charitable woman, a lot like the Belle with whom Scrooge fell in love in his younger days. I'm docking this film One Star for having a Subtitles link which doesn't work. You can put the cursor on the word Subtitles, and hit Enter; you can put the cursor on the word Off, next to the word Subtitles, and press Enter, but you can't get any subtitles to appear. I'm also docking this film another Star for shamelessly pandering to Hispanics. Belle's employee is a brunette woman with a thick accent and an attitude problem who often lapses into speaking Spanish. Scrooge cheerily greets one of Timothy Cratchit VI's Hispanic employees in Spanish, in Wisconsin, in 2013. According to the census of the year 2000, less than five percent of Fort Atkinson's population was Hispanic. Incorporating Hispanics and Spanish into this film in such an affirmative way is obviously a ploy to market this film to Hispanics and liberals who don't think we can have enough Hispanics in the U.S., or pander to them sufficiently.

history.title: Christmas Carol [VHS]
history.review_title: Odd Combination of Stage Play and Special Film Effects
history.text: This adaptation of A Christmas Carol by Charles Dickens is an odd combination of stage play and special film effects. Overall, it is a reverent film, in which portions of the Christmas carols "God Rest Ye, Merry Gentlemen!" and "Good King Wenceslas" are sung, and the phrase "God bless us, everyone!" is repeated by Tiny Tim and Mrs. Dickens. This adaptation is "framed" by a fictitious Charles Dickens, who is trying to finish his novel, A Christmas Carol, on Christmas Day, or Eve. His children want him to tell them his new story for bedtime. His wife and father, try to persuade him to join in their Christmas celebration, but he insists on being left alone at his desk. As Charles begins to read his work out loud, Scrooge and Cratchit appear in their office. The story follows the novel fairly well. Fred and the portly gentlemen pay their visits. The portly gentlemen address Cratchit as "Scrooge," and Scrooge as "Marley." Scrooge doesn't mind, but sends them on their way without a donation anyway. En route to his domicile, Scrooge forces his way through the carolers, and sends one on his way without a tip. Back at his domicile, Scrooge receives a visit from the ghost of Jacob Marley, and the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. The most disturbing ghost is the Ghost of Christmas Past, who is too effeminate for my personal taste, and sounds and dresses like a homosexual pimp. The Ghost of Christmas Present has an interesting staff/torch. It has a flame at the point of a metal cornucopia, which can be adjusted as if it were a lantern. The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come is, in my opinion, the most effective, with the lighting and set used to the best advantage to show him as the real Charles Dickens described him, almost blending into the darkness around him, and always silent. A few liberties are taken with the original novel. For example, Fan visits young Scrooge at school, but, rather than taking him home for Christmas, she informs him that she has snuck away from their father to bring him a Christmas present, which is a paperweight like the one on Dickens' and Scrooge's desks. He proposes to Belle the day before he begins to work for Mr. Fezziwig. In a later scene, she arrives late to Mr. Fezziwig's magnificent Christmas Ball. Mr. Fezziwig insists that the ball come to an immediate conclusion, so that everyone can leave Belle alone with young Scrooge. Unfortunately, she takes that opportunity to break off their engagement. The scene at Old Joe's Pawn Shop is missing altogether. A funeral procession is added. The play ends with Charles Dickens' wife serving flaming pudding, like Mrs. Cratchit's, and saying, like Tiny Tim, "God bless us, everyone!"

history.title: It's Christmas Carol!/The Wishing Tree

history.text: As the Editor-in-Chief of the Dickensian Christmas Carol Blog, I collect and review every adaptation of Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol that I can access a copy of, so I was delighted to discover this one, starring Emmanuelle Vaugier as "the Scrooge." The late Carrie Fisher plays Eve, who stands in for all of the Ghosts. It was a little awkward for me to see these actresses, whom I've come to think of as CSI:NY's Detective Jessica Angell and Star Wars' Princess Leia, respectively, in such drastically different roles - especially Carrie, whom I had never seen so old! But the ravages of time helped me see Ms. Fisher in this new role. Set in a fictitioius version of Chicago, in the Twenty-First Century, this adaptation is rewritten enough to stand alone, but gives a nod to the classic novel that inspired it, as Carol Huffler, the modern "Scrooge," looks it up, online, to see what happens next, right before Eve comes creeping up behind her, looking like the Grim Reaper in a cowl. Olivia Cheng plays Kendra, who stands in for Bob Cratchit. Kendra is single, so there doesn't seem to be a Martha, Peter, or Belinda, let alone a Tiny Tim. Perhaps Carol's elderly, neglected mother (Susan Hogan) is the "Tiny Tim." There's no "God bless us, everyone!" But least there's "Merry Christmas!" and "Happy Hanukkah!"

history.title: The Man Who Invented Christmas(DVD)
history.review_title: I Can Hardly Wait for the BluRay!
history.text: My wife (Libertad Green) and I celebrated our wedding anniversary by watching this film together, alone, coincidentally - just the two of us, in an empty theatre. This is a shame, because this is one of the best Christmas films I've seen. As a fan of A Christmas Carol, with a collection of approximately sixty adaptations on VHS and DVD, I rank this adaptation among my favorites. It's a historical period piece, which provides what could have been sights and sounds similar to those which Charles Dickens experienced during his visit to the United States of America, and approximately two years later, when he felt inspired to write "A Christmas Carol." This film also enters the realm of imagination, as it recreates what could have been Charles Dickens' own nightmares and demons, as he struggled to be kind and generous, yet felt the natural inclination to become impatient with his financially burdensome parents, and with his servants and family who were constantly interrupting him while he was trying to write and publish A Christmas Carol in six weeks, on a constantly shrinking budget. Characters from A Christmas Carol are represented well enough to form a loose adaptation of the classic, while the film can stand alone as a biographical tale of this difficult period in Charles Dickens' life. Various items from Dickens' life and A Christmas Carol appear in this film, such as his fireplace with white and blue tiles, as mentioned in his novel. I look forward to receiving the BluRay so I can rewatch, rewind and pause it! I received my copies of the BluRay and DVD, and have literally lost track of how many times I've rewatched this film! It seems as if every time I watch it, I catch something I missed! This is going to be one of the adaptations of Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol that I watch every Christmas season.
