history.title: Feast (Unrated Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: False advertising! The Blu-Ray is NOT the unrated cut despite claiming to be on the case and disc!
history.text: I'd previously owned "Feast" on DVD, and the film itself is a ton of fun for gore-hounds, horror-junkies and fans of dark-comedy. In addition to some decent thrills, cool creature effects and great set-pieces, it also has a lot of great jokes, ranging from bizarre slap-stick moments, to uproariously over-the-top carnage. For me, the film is a strong 4 out of 5. However, the Blu-Ray release left a sour taste in my mouth for one major reason-- false advertising! I should note that I previously owned the unrated cut on DVD. And I was very satisfied with the disc. However, after losing the film in a flood, I decided to upgrade to the Blu-Ray. And while the film looks good in HD, this is not what I paid for. I bought the "Unrated Edition" (the case and the disc both read "Unrated"), yet it doesn't feature the Unrated Edition! It features the R-Rated Edition, which is heavily cut down, making many of the kills and some of the film's darker jokes less effective. And before anyone says otherwise, I looked into it-- across the internet, a number of people have noted this false advertising and mentioned it on other sites and forums. Additionally, there are sites that compare the R-Rated and Unrated cuts which further shows that this version is not the Unrated Cut and is falsely advertised. It's a real shame, because I'd love to have the unrated cut in HD. But for now, I guess I'm just going to have to buy a new DVD copy...

history.title: Blade / Blade 2 / Blade: Trinity (BD)(3FE) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Good, solid Blu-Ray release, though the cheap packaging is a bit dubious and I fear it could harm the discs...
history.text: This is definitely the cheapest and easiest way to get all three films in the popular late-90's/early-2000's action series "Blade" on Blu-Ray. For about $10, you're getting all three films ("Blade", "Blade II", "Blade: Trinity") loaded with Special Features in a single package, with the nice High Definition visual upgrade that the Blu-Ray format promises. The films of course revolve around half-human/half-vampire Blade (Wesley Snipes), as he stalks the night hunting and killing vampires. In the original, he is pulled into a twisted game against a vampire named Deacon Frost (Stephen Dorff) who seeks to resurrect an ancient Vampire God to take over the world. In the second film, Blade must team up with his enemies (a group of vampires including Ron Perlman and Donnie Yen) to face a much larger threat. And in the third film, Blade teams up with a team of hot-headed young slayers (including Ryan Reynolds of "Deadpool" fame) to fight Dracula (Dominic Purcell)- the original vampire. The three films quality is varied depending on personal taste, but I always found all three quite entertaining. Heck, even though part three is a bit wonky and suffered from obvious production troubles, I still kinda like it. Though the second has always been my personal favorite. The set comes in a very basic case with each movie on its own separate disc. To answer the important questions: -Yes, this does come with both the Theatrical and Unrated versions of "Blade: Trinity" -And yes, it seems to include most (if not all) previously released Special Features from the prior DVD releases. So, $10 for one wickedly bad-a** trilogy with tons of bonus content seems like a perfect bargain, right? And it should easily be a perfect 5 out of 5, right? Well, sadly no, as I do have to dock a point for a fairly major complaint, which is the case. It's extremely cheap and "Blade II"/"Blade: Trinity" are literally stacked on top of one-another tightly, which does cause a bit of worry for me. It just seems like it's asking for the discs to pick up light scratches over time. In addition, the packaging itself is quite cheap, which bugged me. Yes, I know this is more of one of those "budget releases" that are popular to sell in stores like Wal-Mart or Target... but a little more effort would have been appreciated. Still, if you're a fan looking for an upgrade on your "Blade" DVD's, this is a great set. And my problems with the packaging aside, it's well-worth the $10 price tag.

history.title: Ghostbusters
history.review_title: You've made up your mind already... But I personally had a good enough time with it that I'd recommend giving it a shot!
history.text: Chances are you've made up your mind whether you'd like it or not before even seeing it. So there's really no point in trying to convince you either way. (And also please note, my official score would be a 3.5 but I had to round it up to a 4 for Amazon.) My take on this matter, ignoring all the controversy and hyperbole and politics and nonsense? The film was quite charming and entertaining with just enough chuckles and giggles supplied to make it a good go-to for a rainy-day movie. Is it particularly good? Nope. But is it particularly bad? Not at all. It's just a halfway decent action/comedy with some big strengths and some big weaknesses that unfortunately generated a lot of nonsensical hatred, dismissal and dispute because it's a reboot of a comedy classic. I'd honestly rank it right on par with the second film, which I found similarly entertaining-but-problematic. As a matter of fact, I frequently watch those original two films in a double-feature (at least once a year), and there's an exceedingly good chance that now it will become a triple-feature every time I pop them in. Can't complain about having another Ghostbusters movie to watch! If I were to make any suggestions, it'd be to give it a second chance if you watched it once and weren't impressed. I was kinda on-the-fence the first time I saw it, but upon re-watching it a few times, I found it grew on me exponentially each time I viewed it. There's a certain degree of shell-shock the first time you watch it because it is tonally a different beast to the original and the first act is a tad messy. But once it picks up, it really picks up and rewatching it, you also get a lot more of the humor and details you might have missed the first time around. The first time I saw it, I found myself grinning a lot and chuckling every so often... by my third watch? I was laughing out loud at some of the gags I didn't notice the first time. The Blu-Ray also has a very solid assortment of extras, so it's well worth giving a shot if you're open minded.

history.title: Silent Hill: Revelation
history.review_title: Borderline "so bad, it's good." Only worth seeing for the most hardcore fans of the franchise or fans of bad B-movies.
history.text: Years after the events of the first film, Sharon De Silva has gone on the run with her father, having been pursued by the remaining members of the dreaded Silent Hill cult. Now having adopted the names Heather and Harry Mason and started a new life in a new town, they think they are safe. However, Harry is captured and Sharon/Heather is forced to return to the horror of Silent Hill one final time to try and save him. She will have to face the terror of the Otherworld and the dreadful monsters and cultists that call it home, just as her mother did to save her so many years ago. Even as an enormous fan of the source material and a pretty big fan of the first movie (despite its faults), I cannot bring myself to say that "Silent Hill: Revelation" is anything other than terrible. It's a fundamental mess that tries to both serve as sequel to the original film while also trying to adapt one of the more popular sequels of the game franchise... something that cannot organically happen, as the first film made some fundamental changes to the storyline of the games. The two mythologies clash horribly and thus the film needs to jump through constant hoops to try and reconcile the differences and tell a coherent tale. The result is a messy mixture of plot-holes and constant ret-con work that confuses rather than enthralls, in addition to non-stop jump-scares, on-the-nose "3D comin' at ya!" effects and laughably bad structure and pacing. Basically everything the "Silent Hill" franchise is NOT. It stinks of "studio committee" writing... everything is soulless and so by-the-numbers as to be ridiculous, and it feels like writer/director Michael J. Bassett was likely forced to dumb it down for the widest possible audiences by the producers. I've actually quite liked Bassett's other work, and this definitely doesn't feel like anything else he's done. It follows the same awful formula of ending every scene with a jump-scare, throwing in nonstop nonsensical CGI effects, and leaving characters to go completely undeveloped as so many of the other more recent horror films polluting the big screen. It's on the level as that rash of Platinum Dunes remakes that haunted theaters a few years back. It's honestly one of the worst sequels I've seen in quite some time. It is to "Silent Hill" what "Mortal Kombat: Annihilation" was to "Mortal Kombat." A messy, in-your-face sequel with no coherent plot and laughable storytelling. It's to the point that it often borders on the brink of becoming "so bad, it's good." You'll definitely find yourself chuckling here and there at the awful writing and ridiculous low-budget look of many scenes. And to that end, I do think that people who enjoy crappy B-movies might get a kick out of it. I picked up a cheap copy for only a couple bucks, and it made for a good "bad movie night" with my friends as we riffed and ripped it apart. So yeah... if you like bad movies, give it a shot. If you're looking for a serious sequel to the original film or a proper adaptation of the games, steer clear.

history.title: Birdemic 2: The Resurrection
history.review_title: "Birdemic 2: The Resurrection"- An often hilarious sequel that isn't nearly as self-aware as you might suspect...
history.text: The thing that seems to be throwing people off about "Birdemic 2" is that they think it's a purposeful and self-aware attempt to make a bad film for the sake of comedy instead of being a bad movie that became unintentionally funny as a result like the original. And thus a lot of people come out of the film feeling sort-of cheated. The thing is, this really isn't the case- sure the actors are in on it, and some of the crew members seem to purposely playing it up... but writer/director James Nguyen is as blissfully unaware as ever, and seems to be trying his hardest to make a legitimate sequel to his now cult-classic original. Once or twice he tries to poke fun at "Birdemic", but for the most part, he's honestly attempting to make a "good" sequel to the first film. A vast majority of the crazy stuff here isn't as self-aware as you might think it is. And if you do some research on the behind-the-scenes "magic" that brought the film together, it becomes funnier and funnier. (Just look at the recent crowd-funding failure he put together for the potential "Birdemic 3: Sea Eagle"- it's clear he thinks he's making legitimate movies and isn't nearly as self-aware as you'd suspect.) I will certainly admit that as is the case with many sequels, it's not as much fun as the first time around. The few vague attempts at self-awareness fall a bit flat, Nguyen's structuring for the film falls into the common sequel trap of just repeating what came before a bit too often, and even by his standards the filmmaking is exceptionally poor at times. But this massive fan of "Birdemic" was pleased enough with the follow-up to recommend it. And the same can be said for my fellow bad-movie-fanatic friends.

history.title: The Ring/The Ring Two Movie Collection
history.review_title: A great cheap way to own these films if you don't want to buy the strangely overpriced Blu-Ray's...
history.text: Grabbed this two-pack because I'm a big fan of the entire "Ring" franchise, including the original novels, Japanese films and American adaptations. But to this point, finding the American remake and its first sequel on Blu-Ray for a decent price is next-to impossible, as the only prints available are always in the $20-$30 range each. I'm a pretty open-minded buyer, but it's hard to justify paying that much each for a 15-year-old film and its 12-year-old sequel when I can grab a brand new film in 4K for the same price. So, until we get a proper new Blu-Ray release with a more reasonable price-tag (maybe we'll get a new trilogy pack soon with the third film having just come out?), I'm more than happy to settle for this DVD 2-Pack that includes both films for less than $10. This is more-or-less a repackaging of the two previously-released single-disc editions of the films, but for the price you're paying, it's pretty much perfect. You get one great little horror-flick and a so-so but mildly entertaining sequel. So I think it's worth it. Hopefully we'll eventually get a more fairly-priced High Definition version of these films in the future, but in the meantime, this'll do.

history.title: Return to Oz 30th Anniversary Edition Blu-ray
history.review_title: "Return to Oz" 30th Anniversary Blu-Ray... Worth picking up for fans of this underrated treasure despite the high price.
history.text: "Return to Oz" is a delightful and incredibly underrated "forgotten" 80's classic. It was a box office bomb upon initial release and was critically panned because of its dark imagery and oppressive tone. But in the thirty years that have passed since, it's grown a small but dedicated cult following. Unfortunately, until recently it was essentially impossible to track the film down in High Definition, and only a few DVD versions were available that while watchable, looked a bit dated and murky and lacked proper restoration. Thankfully, the Disney Movie Club remedied this with the production of this 30th Anniversary Blu-Ray. The film follows Dorothy Gale (Fairuza Balk), who can't sleep and won't stop talking about her adventures in Oz in the months that have passed since her original journey there. Concerned that Dorothy is suffering post-traumatic stress from the tornado, Aunt Em takes her to an electro-shock therapy clinic to get treatments in hopes of helping her sleep and move on past her "delusions." However, Dorothy escapes one night after learning that some of the people who undergo treatment have been driven insane, and finds herself whisked away in a storm. She awakens back in Oz, discovering it completely abandoned and foresaken, having been taken over by the devious Nome King and a ruthless witch-like creature called "Mombi." Dorothy must team up with a new group of friendly sidekicks in order to defeat these villains and restore Oz to its former glory. The 30th Anniversary Blu-Ray is an excellent release of the film itself, and I would say it is a fine companion to have to go with the previously released DVD edition. Though don't throw out those DVD's, because this particular release lacks the (albeit limited) bonus content from the DVD releases and merely presents a restored and remastered version of the film itself. And it does look and sound stunning. The colors are a bit more lush, the image quality is sharper and more detailed and some of the imperfections seen in the DVD release have been fixed. The film has never looked better in a home-video release, and that alone makes it well worth picking up for hardcore fans of this under-appreciated classic. Just be aware... as this was a release produced exclusively for Disney's Movie Club, it can be quite pricey to acquire a copy. Used copies have been running anywhere from $25-$35 and a new copy will run you $40+. So if you've never seen the film, or aren't interested in spending a lot of money, I'd recommend grabbing the (much cheaper) DVD release to check it out first. This Blu-Ray is most certainly worth picking up... but only if you're a serious fan of the film.

history.title: Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday / Jason X Double Feature (DVD)
history.review_title: A great way to own both "Jason Goes to Hell" and "Jason X" on DVD!
history.text: NOTE/UPDATE: It appears there are different versions of this set. Some people are saying in reviews that they only got a single-disc edition that features only the R-rated cut of "Jason Goes to Hell," "Jason X" and no bonus content. I can only write my review based on personal experience- I ordered this, and the version I got came with two discs. One disc for “Jason Goes to Hell” that included both cuts of the film and bonus content. And another disc for “Jason X,” which includes the movie and bonus content. So I guess buyer beware... there are two different versions of this set floating around. To start, I do want to note that this set does indeed contain both the theatrical and the extended, unrated cut of "Jason Goes to Hell" despite the Amazon description indicating otherwise. To my knowledge, no other reviews have made this clear. And this is a big selling point, as the unrated, uncut version of the film has some fantastic additional effects that make it well-worth seeing out for fans. It's also worth noting as for some bizarre reason, the stand-alone DVD release of the unrated edition goes for a laughably inflated price used from third-party sellers. So please... just grab this and don't waste your time on those used copies. This is the same exact disc, PLUS "Jason X" to boot! Something strange about the "Friday the 13th" film series is that despite being one of the most popular and recognized slasher-film series of all time... they've done a remarkably terrible job at releasing boxed sets and collections for the series. Sure, there was a gorgeous Blu-Ray boxed-set collection released a few years back... but it went out of print almost instantly after becoming available and now sells for hundreds of dollars used. Sure, they just released a new DVD boxed set of the first eight films... but it's on the inferior standard-definition format, so sound and image quality is stuck in the last century. Sure, there are double-pack Blu-Ray sets available that have the films in HD like we want... but like the complete collection boxed-set, they similarly have stopped being manufactured, and now cost many times what they originally did. And yes, I know there's rights issues and all that jazz. But it just seems so ludicrous that such an iconic series is almost completely unavailable in its entirety for a reasonable price in HD. So until we get some sort of proper re-release of the franchise, many fans including myself are stuck trying to track down the films for a fair price on DVD. And I'd say for the most part that this double-pack succeeds and is a nice way to "complete" the recently-released Paramount 8-Film DVD set. It contains both "Jason Goes to Hel" and "Jason X," plus the same assortment of special features from their previous DVD release for only about $12, making this by and far the easiest and most affordable way to own these films. So yeah... If you're looking for these two movies, this is a must-have.

history.title: Ghost in the Shell (4K UHD + Blu-ray + Digital)
history.review_title: "Ghost in the Shell (2017)"- Surprisingly solid and well-made despite the naysayers and the controversy.
history.text: "Ghost in the Shell" is the movie that just couldn't catch a break. Every announcement seemed to anger fans and general American audiences more and more, and multiple aspects of the film ended up causing great controversy and distress. This resulted in the film bombing at the box office while only earning a decidedly mixed reception from both critics and film-goers. Which is really strange, given that as an adaptation of the iconic manga and anime property... it's actually pretty darned good! It combines elements of the original anime adaptation and its sequel "Innocence", while also taking several unique twists and turns to help set it apart from prior "Ghost in the Shell" films and series, resulting in a fresh, new look at an existing story. The tone has been re-worked into more of an action/adventure, but it fits in quite well with the narrative, so it didn't bother me at all. The cast is fantastic despite the quibbles and controversy and all play their roles to perfection. And visually, the film is a powerhouse, exquisitely bringing to life the world that author Masamune Shirow created so many years ago. And sure... some of the themes and subtext that were present in prior versions are a bit more blatant this time around. But they're still there and they're still perfectly valid. So if you're worried the film will ignore the heady ponderings on gender, identity and sexuality seen before, fear not. Because the film does definitely touch on them. I really hope that as time goes on, more people will recognize the film for its strengths. Because even as a fan of the 1995 anime... I though this was a ton of fun and a very good re-imagining for mainstream audiences.

history.title: Jigsaw [Blu-ray + DVD]
history.review_title: Series fans will be very pleased- "Jigsaw" is one of the better sequels in the infamous "Saw" franchise! Entertaining, gory fun!
history.text: Between 2004-2010, the original run of the "Saw" film series thrilled audiences with its intricate storyline and devlish games of life and death- each film being a massive financial success despite being generally met with apathy from critics. People loved 'em and ate 'em right up! And although the so-called "final chapter" was released seven years ago, followers of the series held out hope that one day, the series would continue. And that it did with 2017's "Jigsaw"- both a true sequel to the original series, and also a bit of a "light reboot" that starts the franchise in a new direction with a focus on new characters and stories. And as someone who will shamelessly admit to being a die-hard fan of the franchise despite the later sequels becoming increasingly hit-and-miss... I really had a lot of fun with "Jigsaw!" It won't win over any new fans, and it has some of the same issues and problems the plagued previous installments... but I really, genuinely enjoyed it! Ten years after the death of John Kramer (series star Tobin Bell), the discovery of a slew of corpses has police asking an impossible question- Has the nefarious "Jigsaw Killer" somehow come back from the dead? After all... these bodies all seem to bear his calling cards. As police investigate the matter, five people awaken inside of a derelict and run-down barn-house and are informed they will face a series of demented "games" that will force them to confront their past failings and faults... or die trying. Directed by the wickedly talented Sperig Brothers, the thing that helps set "Jigsaw" apart and make it feel like a vital entry in the series is how it maintains many hallmarks of the franchise while also giving it a fresh spit-and-polish to make it feel new once again. It has the prerequisite gooey-gore and life-or-death tests you'd come to expect. The flashbacks-galore and pivotal twists-and-turns that defined the original seven films. Only this time, the visuals are rightfully updated to feel more in-line with today's cinema, the scope is greatly increased, new characters are introduced to follow, the story eschews some of the wonkier leftover plot-lines from before, and there's a current of much-needed subtle humor injected into the film. It still feel like "Saw" through-and-though... it's just been revamped and updated for today's audiences. And on top of that, the story is just clever enough, the performances are pretty decent and series composer Charlie Clouser once again knocks it out of the park with a fantastic score. Sure, nothing will ever come close to the original trilogy of "Saw", "Saw II" and "Saw III." Even to this day, those original three films are very rewatchable and hold up exquisitely for the most part. But for my money, "Jigsaw" is easily better than anything post "Saw III." As a horror fan and a fan of the series, I'd give it a good 7.5 out of 10.

history.title: Abattoir [Blu-ray] [2016]
history.text: Horror and suspense is my all-time favorite movie genre and the trailer for this seemed like it might be worth checking out. It was something of a poor man's Stephen King flick, of the made-for-TV variety. In fact, now that I think about it, this was no better than your average (bad) SyFy flick. I beleve M. Night could have done much better with the same material! At least Jessica Lowndes was nice to look at...that is about the only positive thing about this film I can think of. If you must see this, at least wait until it hits Netflix or something.

history.title: The Boy (2016)
history.text: This one caught me by surprise, reminding me a lot of classic era works of Rod Serling (Twilight Zone/Night Gallery), with a level of creepiness you don't see a lot in the movies anymore. A highly recommended creepy thriller that will keep you watching from the beginning to the end.

history.title: Seconds (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Saw this in '66 and have never forgotten it!
history.text: I was 8 when I saw this at a drive-in theater in 1966 and it terrified me, much more so than any horror film I saw in my childhood. As an adult now, I don't think I would recommend this film to an 8-year-old, but if you've never seen it, you should as you won't soon forget it. An under-the-radar 60's classic, and I agree with another reviewer here who said the film should be included on a list of the Top 10 Most Disturbing Movies of All Time.

history.review_title: Entertaining and as creepy as Paranormal Activity
history.text: So it would seem, based on reading several other reviews here, that the Blackwell Ghost story was fabricated. Even after that consensus, that doesn't really take away from the entertainment factor and creepy vibe factor of the film - I found it as creepy as Paranormal Activity, in addition to humorous due to the enthusiasm and personality of the investigator. I enjoyed this "documentary" more than The Blair Witch Project (1999). At only an hour in length, well worth a view if you're a fan of Paranormal Activity. With Halloween coming up, this would make for a fun Halloween night viewing, perhaps as a double feature with another scary flick.

targets.title: Dirty Mary, Crazy Larry / Race With The Devil [Blu-ray]

history.text: This movie is a one trick pony and once it is done it's trick there is no reason to go back. There is no way to talk about the main flaws of this film without spoiling it so read at your own risk. The biggest flaw with this film is the 2 directions it trying to go at the same time ... is it a suspenseful hostage drama? is it a sci-fi aliens flick ... OH its pretending to be the former but is actually the latter. A lot of the dialogue is written to make it seem like it's a hostage drama "a'la Shamalan" but when the cats out of the bag and the big reveal occurred I was left with an overwhelming sense of WTF!!!!?. Somehow our main protagonist also becomes Ripley + MacGyver all in one and wins at the end ... fighting off some kind of biological disease with vinal, duct tape, a 2ltr bottle and I am guessing some medical disinfectant pad ..... yeah, I didn't buy it ... but hey ... ITS A FEEL GOOD MOMENT .... Also, they made John Goodman's character into a creep when in the end he was kind of right .... so there is that ... I got this on sale awhile back ... and I just watched it ... and I regret my life choices.

history.title: WWE: WrestleMania 23 (The Ultimate Limited Edition)
history.review_title: The only WrestleMania were a President gets a Stunner
history.text: I bought this for one reason .. Our President is in it! Outside of that, the matches are better reviewed elsewhere. I grew up with 80's wrestling and made it to the 2000's before I gave up... my favorites got too old, too hurt, or left after the merger of WCW and WWF. Should you watch it? Yes Should you own it? not really.

history.review_title: Can Vin Diesel survive a damn war movie?
history.text: It is an alright flick, nothing too monumental. An interesting look at what it is like when you are just doing your job and everyone wants to keep telling you that you have done something amazing. A few jabs on the side to those just "supporting the troops" for their own benefits with no real weight behind it. I did like the blend of halftime show/war to simulate flashbacks, i thought the editing in that regard was good.... didn't care much for the center frame "I love you guys" that they use for Steve Martin and Chris Tucker it was kind of strange. I really didn't care for the forced conflict with the grounds crew... It was kind of strange when Lynn meets the owner of the football team (Steve Martin) and he mentions that he (Lynn) was with the greats now like Audie Murphy. If you ever want to see a tragedy, read the story of Audie's life. Unfortunately this movie doesn't have the 120Hz mode that Ang Lee shot it in so I can't speak to how the effects were supposed to be and I guess some of the strange magic that 120 provided are lost. I picked this movie up because it was on sale and unfortunately I would say it is only worth that or a rental or when it shows up on netflix as there is not much happening story/action wise and watching someone suffering from PTSD is not something you just want to sit down and experience/rewatch.

history.review_title: This is what happenes if Qui-Gon Jinn strayed from the path of the Jedi
history.text: This is an interesting take on what happens if Qui-Gon Jinn survived and gave up being a Jedi. After the Galaxy/Jedi learn of Jinn's death to the hands of Darth Maul, Qui-Gon Jinn is assigned a secret mission to infiltrate a planet search for hidden Jedi and overthrow an evil Overlord. After landing on this planet he tries to teach the ways of the force but is captured and having given up all hope after years of torture and no hope of rescue his spirit breaks and he renounces his Jedi ways. Garfield (insert generic Jedi name here) and a young Kilo Ren team up to search for the missing master after receiving a message that took years to get out of the system Jinn was imprisoned on they arrive to follow his footsteps and search for their missing master. The Overlords soon learn of new Jedi arriving and they begin to hunt down the two new interlopers. Having captured and successfully broken Jinn the Overlords are full of confidence they can break the students they set out to weed out the Jedi and their sympathizers. After many days of hiding and not getting any closer to finding Jinn, Garfield begins to show weakness and tells the populace it is okay to renounce the Jedi to save their lives. Kilo becomes disillusioned by both Jinn and Garfield's lack of faith and the weakness of the Jedi ways to resolve the situation. They part ways to split up and continue the search as well as evade the Overlord's henchmen but both Garfield and Ren are captured. Ren now alone as unsure of his companions fate soon discovers as the last of his supporters are drown that Garfield is in the company of the Overlords and seeming in their graces. Ren fakes his death and renounces the Jedi for their weakness and escapes the planet to go off to form the New Order and become stronger to wipe out the weakness that are the Jedi. Garfield seeing his friend die, soon meets Jinn and see's for himself the now broken master reduced to nothing. Garfield begins to question his own choices and fate as well as the fate of the local population suffering for him as they are hunted down and killed one by one. Will Garfield overcome the evil Overlords? Will he save Jinn? Will he ever see Kilo Ren again? or will he also submit and renounce his ways? I would give the movie more stars if they would edit in a scene at the end where Liam tells the Japanese Emperor that He has taken something very important from him, and he doesn't care who he is, or where he is, he is coming to get it back!"

history.review_title: Solid cast, great performances, too many plots holes = Swiss cheese of a story narrative.
history.text: It's an interesting watch however, careful on binge watching ... the flaws become super apparent when you do, So whats wrong? Well, everyone has their own agenda and it seems everyone working for the company is trying to screw it over for their own means. There is eventually a good story arc that forms but its around episode 7. So you have many mind bending suspension of disbelief to sit thru. There is copious amounts of nudity in the show to help keep the audience watching (its not as bad as the nudity in black sail as far as pointless/shock value). So careful watching this on a plane is all I am saying. Okay so onto the point. A company runs a theme park in the spirit of Cyberdine / Jurassic Park .. meaning as incompetently as possible while somehow making a profit. The overarching goal is to make the robots as human as possible by allowing them to remember things. This you will quickly figure out is a stupid idea and MANY people point it out in the show but the push the OKAY button and continue on even know its shown that its doing more harm than good. So in the robots mind they all now have PTSD as they recall past events they were apart of and it now starts messing with the current roles they are in. This issue somewhat drives the plot forward and introduces us to some of the worst company mismanagement possible. A few cast memebers ask the robots if anyone has modified them, they say no, then the person TELLS THEM TO DELETE THE ENCOUNTER.... SO they just forgot that the other people messing with the machines can do the same thing. Later tech guys really screw things up when they start changing robots codes... and what should SET OFF EVERY ALARM .. goes unnoticed. It's painful to shut your brain down hard enough to accept that story line... it's not even a McGuffin ...I won't go further down this line as its a major story/plot point.... The real McGuffin of the story is "The Maze" .. it's halfA$$'ed explained at the end and it truly wrecks the story as one of the major actor's entire arc is pointless. He owns the company, he runs around being a GTA5 griefer (pointlessly), and he says his sole goal is to find the maze and break the AI. His overarching goal is he wants to fight things that can fight back... e.g. disable the safety.... Cause you know, noone would ever sue when their loved one is murdered by a robot in a vacation world.... He even tells the devs thats his plan AND THEY DON'T TELL HIM HOW DUMB THAT IS!. So, they make mention that anything can happen in this world, and they show, it does. Any human can cap anyone at anytime and instead of having multiple copies of the same robot they repair it and send it back out into the world.... this is dumb .. it's initially set up that they want to see what the robot remembers (which is again, a dumb thing to have), show nudity, and save budget as they are not showing an action scene. Lastly, Do laws not exist in this world? To the shows credit! They make the interactions between human robots very well .. as the robots are not allowed to kill humans they edit action scenes in a way where it doesn't look like they are pulling punches/throwing shots... I was quite impressed with this. However, there are events where one human interacts with another... and one takes the other hostage.... sooooo, anyone in the company want to step in... you know before a human knifes another human???? Also, guns are magic .. just accept that. They do what the scene needs them to do. Shoot a robot, chunks go flying, shot a person, knock them over, shoot glass and it shatters, shoot wood and leave bullet holes... so yeah magic. Anyway, I don't know where this story is going to go after the season finale ... but assuming the Story real world is just as dumb as the companies invested in WestWorld noone will care... However, you, you at home if you have stayed with this review to this point .. give your self a pat on the back... it sounds like a rant to avoid .. but the show is really something to see. The cinematography, actors, and action scenes are really well done. It's just the story has issues. But I do recommend watching this show. Last thought... is this a prequel to Terminator?

history.review_title: Not bad, May need to skip the the 2nd half of the movie to avoid boredom.
history.text: Pretty good telling of the Power Rangers. A bit much of the backstory fluff (had to skip ahead a few times (anytime they start trying to develop their I CANT DO IT character arc moments)). I did get motion sick at the start with the really stupid camera panning while he was driving.... also, he was going WAY too slow to flip his car and slide the way he did .... keep spinning the camera, i'm sure you impressed someone. Zordon is a bit much for my liking in this version. The giant head sliding all over the wall was a bit distracting. Rita - Rocks the house.... Loved every scene she was in.. I wouldn't mind seeing a follow up movie now that the way to drawn out backstory is done.

history.title: Blade Runner 2049
history.review_title: Wait for it to be on sale.
history.text: It's not the worst thing put to film this year ... but it sure does have a lot of problems. The pace of this film is down right bad, I started doing other things just to entertain myself between set pieces at times. The villain of the story is so laughably bad. He really sets the tone of this entire film in one take. In a scene were a new robot woman is made, he decides to take the CEO or his right hand woman into the room to "meet" the new robot ... for some reason. He sits there like a pompous jackass on the floor waiting for his assistant to plug some stupid domino into his head.... for some reason. Anywho 10min later, he gets off his ass and walks up to the naked robot woman and expositions her to death. Blah Blah Blah, first emotion we experience at birth is fear.... (completely up his own ass at this point (when I install windows, my computer doesn't experience fear, it boots up!).). Anywho, he explains his motives as civilizations are build to forced labor, and we gave up slavery so we built that labor, and he wants to make a robot army, but since they can't have kids, it will never be complete.... cause you know, building robots just wasn't enough, I guess. Anywho, he wants to build millions of robots so he can take over (and then he kills the robot woman.)... why? Because he is a shallow, pointlessly bad, poorly written character .... and we the audience need to know how "evil' he and his right hand woman are. Anywho, rest of this movie is just as pointlessly bad as the scene I just described and the director just wanted to show off pretty visual set pieces... and those sets add NOTHING to the plot/story and only slow this snooze fest down as it crawls to a pretty meh conclusion. The story is identical to the Anime Armitage, robots, are too like people, Mars wants to break away from Earths control, but they have low birth rates, so they build robots to make babies, Earth finds out, Mars tries to cover up their actions as to not provoke a war until they are ready... death to robots baby makers..... In this SKYNET wants to break away from humans but they can't until they can make babies of their own.... I guess, they want to be able to break away from their human creators by creating their own life and not something we programmed them to be....

history.review_title: Only Operation Market Garden was more of a mess than this film.
history.text: Would be a good movie if it were in order. When Nolan tries to be Tarantino it comes off as a complete mess. The real story of Dunkirk is something to behold, botched military operations all around lead to one of the biggest retreats, and delays in military actions that could of very well spelled the end of UK during WW2. But due to Hitler delaying operations for his own reasons (plan for UK surrender/ Luftwaffe planning to bomb allies into oblivion), we get one of the most daring retreats in the world. While allied units of the French/Indian/British fought valiantly around the perimeter to allow those on the beaches to escape. Unfortunately, you wont see any of that. Instead you get a lopsided film showing people lined up single file waiting to board boats only to be sunk ... BUT FROM 3 DIFFERENT PERSPECTIVES... so you can wonder what date and time you are watching. Seriously, did Nolan have such a short budget that he had to reuse film to get this movie to the end? The start of the movie tries to make date and time clear but as the film progresses they stop telling you when and where ... .and I kid you not, they cut to DRAMATIC EVENTS ... that aren't even on the SAME DAY! They cut between Tom Hardy dogfighting the Germans on day 3 and spliced in troops trying to escape a torpedoed destroyer and drowning on day 2 ..... how? why? The ship that got Torpedoed was attacked from the wrong side ... it was about 1000m from the shore and the Torpedoes came from the shore side ... meaning a U-Boat would have to be on the surface or insane to attack from that side and not the other side ... OUT IN THE CHANNEL! Continuing this mess of a film. All the Ships which burn either oil or coal (depending on their historical build date) ... well none of them have smoke coming out of the big stack on top of the ship. The are all moored/anchored (even when underway (you figure that one out).) and they all have their lights on at night.... so yeah. The 1st guy the story follows gets everyone/everything around him killed. His squad, the people on the beach, and every boat he gets on to. I am not sure we were supposed to pick up on this, as the film needed to cram as much B.S. at us as it could due to having 3 angles to show ... but seriously, every boat he touches gets sunk! 2nd guy - is an old man and his boy and his boys classmate, they represent the small boats fleet. There was no issues with this segment of the movie. Very well done overall. 3rd guy - Tom Hardy, Pilot ...is fine, his landing at the end is pretty funny as he goes miles down the beach during his landing then is jump cut back to exactly where all the allied troops were (only, they left) so he gets captured. This movie was such an editorial mess, they I kid you not, jump cut the allied forces to safety in England... yeah, no one gets rescued until the small boat arrive, then everyone teleports back to England.... No wonder Hitler was confused about the operation! Is it watchable? Yes, the cinematography is beautiful at time, and quite marvelous to watch. The rest of the movie is garbage though. I hope Nolan does a D-Day movie next. It start was the men training for the invasion, they get on the boat, jump cut, VE Day!

history.review_title: A forced story, rushed relationship, in the end the only joke that lands, was the joke on us.
history.text: This isn't the worst thing put to film ... but it's far from the best. There are two stories plopped together to make this feature length and to shoestring a very badly done relationship between Batgirl and Batman. The first one involves setting up their relationship over battling a midcard baddie named Paris, Franz .. or some play on words .. it goes nowhere, Batman tries to warn Batgirl to not go after him because he is dangerous ... but he really isn't. This shoestrings the audience into caring about their relationship ... it's only downwards from there. Second story, the Joker breaks out and goes after Commissioner Gordon via attacking Barb. This is where the story goes way off the rails. Joker shoots Barb and takes compromising photos of her while she is bleeding out. He kidnaps Gordon to make him crazy ... and this would of been interesting to see, but as soon as Batman shows up he is like, yeah I'm fine, go get the Joker, "By the book!". Gordon doesn't even know his daughter is alive and the story just stops there. They try and hamstring in Jokers backstory as to why we are supposed to be sympathetic to him ... but that too falls flat. Then Batman tries to convert the Joker from the darkside, in one of the strangest dialogues even had ... ignoring Barbra condition, and the Joker tells the lamest joke ever. So there you go, a not very well written story, not told very well, running full steam to the climax of the story and not giving any scene time to sink in. The visuals are done via atrocious animated CGI rendered on a PS2 most noticeably so in the opening scenes. Mark Hamill, Kevin Conroy reprise their roles, Tara Strong comes back in to do Barbra (she had recently done voice work for Harley.) Ray Wise does a great Commissioner Gordon... the rest of the voice work is passable. Detective Bullock was the most noticeably jarring of the cast but he only has a few lines. I got it on sale for a few bucks ... and I would have to say, it really wasn't worth it.

history.review_title: Not bad, not for kids though.
history.text: I got a bunch of laughs out of this movie. Far more interesting than the Killing Joke animated movie I watched beforehand. The story is pretty good, Ivy, discount Swamp Thing want to make a mutagen that will save the Earth from all the harm man has done to it and Batman has to find them. Only he doesn't know where to look, so Night Wing goes looking for Harley Quinn and hi-jinx ensues. The art is pretty good, only a few times did it look a bit inconsistent. Easiest part to explain was the gravure restaurant in which Harley works. They use an over-sexualized art style to show that the point of the place is to "Look, but don't Touch!", as the warning sign on the wall reads. So they draw Harley with a butt-crack in her underwear ... but a few scenes later they show her strip down to her underwear and there is no line. Same with Ivy's art style. It's by no means bad, it's just inconsistent. Anywho, the voice work is good borderline great but Harley's voice has a very heavy New York Queen's/Bronx accent and there is a scene where she sings, all credit to the voice actor for trying but after following a very well done duet ... its a little rough, and unbelievable that anyone is enjoying her singing. The dialogue is pretty good at times, a few very adult jokes tossed in amount the literal fart jokes. Batman breaks character a few times, but all in all in the spirit of what the movie was trying to accomplish it is alright. Especially the end sequence, it's out of Batman's character, but it's silly enough to just work.

history.title: Kong Island
history.text: Kong Island is one hour and twenty – three minutes and release in theatres on September 29, 1968. The basic story line is that a mad scientist in the jungles of Kenya is experimenting with mind control devices and implanting them in the brains of gorillas. The rest of the movie is never quite explained and there are a lot of plot holes in the movie. Also this version is the PG-13 version; in the original movie there were nude scenes and there are none in this version. Kong Island gets a D- for lack of story. Also included with Kong Island is the movie the Most Dangerous Game. The Most Dangerous Game is one hour and two minutes and was released in theatres on September 16, 1932. A sole survivor of a ship wreck washes up on an island and finds a castle. Russian Count Zaroff takes Bob Rainsford in and lets him know that there are two other people who survived a ship wreck that are staying with him. Fast-forward a little bit, Bob Rainsford and Eve Trowbridge find that the most dangerous game that Count Zaroff likes to hunt is man. Count Zaroff only want to hunt Bob, but Eve insists on going with him. The chase begins at midnight and the two have to stay alive to six in the morning to have won the game. Some little known facts about this movie are that is was made during a down period when King Kong was being made so the forest you see in the movie is the same one in King Kong. When Bob and Eve are crossing over a log, it is the same one that the men meet their fate in King Kong. Also there is a longer uncut version of this film of one hour and eighteen minutes. Since this film fell into public domain it is hard to find out which movie is the original version. The Most Dangerous Game gets an AAA+++. DVD Extras I. Select Movie a. Kong Island i. Play Movie ii. Scene Selection b. The Most Dangerous Game i. Play Movie ii. Scene Selection II. Web Link

history.title: King of Kong Island
history.text: King of Kong Island is one hour and twenty – four minutes and release in theatres on September 29, 1968. The basic story line is that a mad scientist in the jungles of Kenya is experimenting with mind control devices and implanting them in the brains of gorillas. history.title: The Monster and the Girl
history.text: The Monster and the Girl is one hour and four minutes and was released in theaters on February 28, 1941. The main storyline is a guy is sentenced to death for a crime he did not commit. A doctor visits him in death row and asks for the use of his brain after he dies. The man’s brain goes into the body of a gorilla. The gorilla with the man’s brain inside of it goes on a revenge killing spree for the people who framed and save his sister and that boys and girls is your movie in a nutshell. The movie sort of reminds me your cheesy seventies movies short on plot, action and budget. The Monster and the Girl gets a C+.

history.title: Starcrash (Roger Corman Cult Classics)
history.text: Starcrash is one hour and thirty – one minutes and was released in the United States on March 7, 1979. The main story is that Stella Star, Akton and Elle, under the orders of the Emperor, set off to find Count Zarth Arn secret weapon on a hidden planet and to find the Emperor only son. That is the movie in a nutshell. The main thing this movie has going for it are two things. First the artwork and remember no computer graphic imaging in the Seventies so a lot of this was painted. A lot of the space scenes were paint and some background as well. Also the stop-motion model animation is not bad also. Second the music of John Barry which was scored in just four days is good. In the United States version the original film was trimmed by five minutes to keep in going. This film marks Europe first foray into the science fiction movie franchise. Starcrash gets an A. history.title: Tower of London
history.text: The Tower of London is one hour and thirty – two minutes and was released in theaters on November 17, 1939. The main story is that Richard, Duke of Gloucester is sixth in line to the throne and plots to eliminate those ahead of him. The story is closely related to the real Richard III of England. An interesting note here is that Vincent Price who plays Duke of Clarence would go on to play Richard the III in a 1962 remake with the same title. Basil Rathbone does a superb job as playing the evil Richard, Duke of Gloucester. The Tower of London gets an AA++.

history.title: The Phantom of the Opera (1962) [DVD]
history.review_title: You feel sorry for this one
history.text: The Phantom of the Opera is one hour and twenty – five minutes and was released in theaters on June 25, 1962. This was the third Phantom of the Opera movie and the first one made in the United Kingdom. This one has a different twist then the other two. In the first two the Phantom worked solo and in this one he as an assistant who unknowingly or knowingly does his dirty work for him. The one follows closely to the 1943 Claude Rains version. The main difference is Claude Rains was a violinist and Herbert Lom is voice trainer. Professor Petrie takes is unpublished music to Lord Ambrose D'Arcy in the hopes that he would publish his music. Instead Lord Ambrose D'Arcy publish the music under his own name and when Professor Petrie finds out he goes to the printing place to destroy the printing plates and all the printed music. However a fire erupts and in his attempts to put out the fire he accidently throw nitric acid on the fire and some of it splashes back on his face and he runs out screaming and falls into the river where a dwarf saves him. Now of the three Phantoms this one has the most horrific face even though it is shown very briefly at the end of the movie. Even his hands looks badly burned. Though with this one you feel the most sorrow for. The first two Phantoms wanted Christine all to themselves whereas this Phantom wanted to help her become a better opera singer to perform in his play. Even when he dies at the end of the movie saving Christine you still feel remorseful about the guy. This Phantom of the Opera gets an AAAA++++. DVD Options A. Play B. Subtitles a. On b. Off

history.title: Hollywood Legends of Horror Collection
history.text: Hollywood Legends of Horror Collection is six hours and one minutes, not including bonus materials, and was released on DVD on September 27, 2017. All six movies are good in their own right with the exception of The Return of Doctor X. In my opinion not the best movie in the set. A few interesting trivia about this sent are: Lionel Atwill appears in Doctor X and Mark of the Vampire and Lionel Barrymore appears in Mark of the Vampire and The Devil Doll and only the Devil does not come with a commentary. Also the Mask of Fu Manchu does not come with a theatrical trailer. Below I gave a brief cliff note about the movies and with some of them a few interesting facts. Hollywood Legends of Horror Collection gets an AAAA++++. Doctor X is one hour and fifteen minutes and was released in theaters on August 3, 1932. The movie is basically about a person who is dubbed by the newspapers as the Moon Killer Murders. The Moon Killer has killed four people in the past several months. The police suspect one of the doctors at a nearby medical academy because a certain type of scalpel is used and it is only used at the academy. Dr. Jerry Xavier does not want any bad press on the school so he begs the police to allow him to do an internal investigation and the police gives him 48 hours to find the killer. Doctor X was made in two-color Technicolor which looks a little like a colorize black and white film. Doctor X hints at murder, rape, cannibalism and prostitution during the film but none of that is actually shown. The Return of Doctor X in one hour and two minutes and was released in theaters on December 2, 1939. The movie tells the story of Dr. Maurice Xavier and how he is bought back to life after he is executed for his crime. Dr. Francis Flegg brings back Dr. Maurice Xavier using synthetic blood. However synthetic blood cannot reproduced itself and Dr. Maurice Xavier goes on a murder spree looking for rare Type One blood type so he can stay alive. This film marks Humphrey Bogart first and only science fiction\horror movie and later in his career he would talk little about it because he thought it to be his worst film of his career along with Swing Your Lady. This film is not a sequel to Doctor X. Mark of the Vampire in one hour and was released in theaters on April 26, 1935. This is a remake of the 1927 classic London After Midnight. Basically a group of people try to figure out who murder Sir Karell Borotyn and their main suspect is Baron Otto von Zinden. Since twenty minutes were cut from the original film there are some unexplained gaps in the film. There was to be a subplot of Count Mora of having an incestuous relationship with his daughter Luna. Thus he committed suicide by shooting himself in the head. In the movie there is an unexplained bullet hole in his right temple throughout the movie. Since Tod Browning previous film Freaks was a flop, he could not object to the cuts. The Mask of Fu Manchu is one hour and eight minutes long and was released in theaters on November 5, 1932. The movie is about Fu Manchu trying to get a hold of the sword and mask of Genghis Khan. With the mask and sword Fu Manchu wants to proclaim himself the reincarnation of Genghis Khan so he can rule Asia and the Middle East. It is up to Sir Denis Nayland Smith of the British Secret Service to stop him. Some fun facts about this movie are this was Boris Karloff first speaking role. Also this would be the last time Myrna Low would play an oriental female. She would have to wait another two years before her breakout role as Nora Charles in the Thin Man. This movie may have been longer because in later years scenes were cut due to racial overtones of Asians. Mad Love is one hour and eight minutes long and was released in theaters on July 12, 1935. The story is about Dr. Gogol who is obsessed with the actress Yvonne Orlac. When Yvonne tells Dr. Gogol that she is retiring from the theatre to be with her pianist husband Stephen Orlac. This drives Dr. Gogol into a mad love, hence the name of the movie. Mad Love was Peter Lorre first movie in the United States. The Devil Doll is one hour and eighteen minutes and was released in theaters on July 10, 1936. The movie is about a wrongly convicted man who has escaped from Devil’s Island and want revenge on the three men who wrongly convicted him. In doing so he uses a formula to make people small, no more than three inches tall to aide him in his quest for revenge and justice. This was Maureen O'Sullivan first horror movie. Disc 1 Doctor X 1. history.title: House of Wax [DVD]
history.text: House of Wax is one hour and twenty – eight minutes long and was released in theaters on April 10, 1953. The main story is that wax sculptor Henry Jarrod creates wax sculptors for his museum, but his partner Matthew Burke is unhappy with the museum and believes it could generate more money is it displays horror wax figures. Henry does frowns on doing horror wax sculptors. Matthew has an insurance policy and wants to cash in on it since the museum is not making that much money. Matthew sets the museum on fire and he and Jarrod gets into a fight all while the museum is burning. Matthew knocks Jarrod out and escapes. Jarrod awakens and tries to save his wax figures but is unable to do so. Jarrod jumps throw or is blown through a glass window. It is several years later and a new Chambers of Horror is about to open. Henry Jarrod somehow survived the fire, but is bound to a wheelchair and his hands and fingers are of no use to him. Sorry will not give the ending away. The differences between the House of Wax and the Mystery of the Wax Museum are: House of Wax is eleven minutes longer, House of Wax was made using stereoscopic 3-D color and Mystery of the Wax Museum was made using two-color Technicolor. The man in the House of Wax that tells the police that the museum is a wax morgue is an alcoholic and in the Mystery of the Wax Museum he is a drug addict. history.title: King Kong (1976)
history.review_title: The original is still the best
history.text: King Kong is two hours and fourteen minutes and was released in theatres on December 17, 1976. Basically it is almost has the same story outline as the original King Kong. Pretty blonde girl gets capture by big gorilla, big gorilla falls head over heels for blond girl and big gorilla gets killed. Now here are the differences from the original and remake. Original movie Carl Denham is taking the crew to film an unknown creature on Skull Island. New version, Fred Wilson of Petrox Oil Company is heading to an unknown island in the Indian Ocean to look for oil. Old version Carl Denham finds a female to film a movie for him. New movie, they find a female in a raft floating in the ocean. In the original version there is no stowaway except Son of Kong, new version stowaway. Original version King Kong is a stop-motion animation gorilla and new version a guy in a gorilla suit. Original version King Kong climbs the Empire State Building and falls to his death and in the new version King Kong climbs the World Trade Centers and dies. Also at the end of the original version a police officer remarks to Carl Denham that the planes got him and Carl Denham replies back "Oh, no, it wasn't the airplanes. It was Beauty killed the Beast." There is no famous last line in the new version. Also in the original version King Kong battle a Tyrannosaurus, Elasmosaurus and Pteranodon and in the remake the only creature King Kong battles is a snake. Finally the remake is forty – four minutes longer than the original. Overall in my opinion the original was much better than remake. To me if it aint broke than why fix it. King Kong 1976 gets a C+ for not bringing anything new to the movie. DVD Extras A. Play B. Set Up a. Audio Options i. English Dolby Surround ii. English 5.1 Surround iii. French b. history.text: I really don't understand why anyone would've rated this move at only one star. The only thing which could have to do with it is, their bitterness to those in the world who are such dedicated, self-motivated people, who's job is the passion of their life. Many people resent it, or feel less because of such movers and shakers. We owe a lot of what we have in this world because of people like this, and while their dedication to their jobs has been fruitful, in some instances, it leaves many behind, hence the bitterness. If you really want to see a movie about one person's passion and another's ability to change, this is a good movie to watch. It's funny, has a great cast, great soundtrack, and was well directed. history.review_title: "The Trip?" More like:"Peter, Dennis and Bruce,"Rebels without a Clue"
history.text: The Trip? Steely Dan may have said it best: "Show biz kids making movies of themselves an they don't give a....funk(?) about nobody else?" I cant remember. And I couldn't remember much about "The Trip". I saw it at the drive inn when it came out. I was 16 and smoking pot like it was going out of style! So that must be why I can't remember, right? There must have been some pretty cool stuff to "trip on"....right? Well, other than the house with the upstairs indoor/outdoor swimming pool, there's not much artistic value, special effects or soundtrack worth remembering. But the house, it's self had extreme historical value. At the time, it was home of the band "LOVE." As in "7&7 is - Love" (that's how it looked on my KRLA Top Forty Playlist.) It's a shame they weren't asked to participate in this movie. Because they were, as far as I know, the first commercially successful inter-racial rock band. I LOVE came together in L.A. late 1965' when composer, guitarist and lead vocalist Arthur Lee asked another brother, and 3 of his lighter skinned friends, 2 white, 1 Latino, to join musical forces. They had the perfect hippie name and attitude, more than a year before a hint of a "Peace, Love" hippie. A real cutting edge band, they combined rock, blues, jazz and Latin influences. They beat Lou Reed and The Stones to the future with the first heroine/suicide blues ballad: "SIGNED D.C." inspired by the suicide note left by their first drummer. Talk about street cred and cult status! A band full of outrageous musical mood swings. They were the perfect hippie rock band, which also, ironically recorded the perfect blue print for a punk anthem in "7&7 is," later to be recorded by The Ramons, and others, but none could match the rage of the original black vocalists! But this film wasn't as ground breaking. And the music sucks! It seems the so-called writers just guessed at what a "trip" might be. There's no real special effects. More like they just threw together random film clips, mixed with Fonda's home movies of Malibu. And why the dixieland jazz when Fonda realizes he's gonna get laid? Seriously? How lame is that? Would've been a good time for some LOVE from the house band! Hey Peter! Dennis! Bruce! You guys really blew it! Such a shame. Bet ya LOVE could've gotten this film into the Rock& Roll Hall of Fame. So far as show biz kids go, The Monkees were way more cool, and way more, in the words of Mickey Dolenz:"Psychedelic!" Now I guess I'll have to buy their trip movie, "HEAD."

history.title: Mama's Family: The Complete Collection
history.review_title: Review of "Mama's Family: The Complete Collection
history.text: I highly recommend "Mama's Family: The Complete Collection." The set includes all 130 episodes plus a bonus 2-part DVD and a booklet with information about the characters. A brief episode guide is included in the liner notes of each case. Some have a very brief plot description but others simply list the episodes. What I would have liked is a detailed episode guide. I didn't find the booklet interesting and had no hesitation about tossing it, along with the bulky oversize box containing the DVD's. We keep our DVD's in soft-sided binders for easy storage. Other reviewers have mentioned that these episodes are "cut" for syndication. To me it's not that important. What matters is that I finally have all of Mama. Edited to add that I found an error in one of the titles. The last episode of Season 2 is entitled "A Great Mistake" on the DVD label. It should be "A Grave Mistake". I have verified this with several online episode guides.

history.title: Waltons: Complete Collection DVD Box Set (Seasons 1-9 and Movie Collection)
history.text: So far we are satisfied. We've been watching our favorite episodes; the sound and quality are fine. Of course it will take weeks to watch them all. Each case includes liner notes with the episodes and plot outlines. Based on what we have seen so far, we would highly recommend purchasing the set.

history.title: Hawaii Five-O: The Complete Original Series
history.review_title: Some are fine but others stick and freeze
history.text: Before buying, please read all the reviews and ask yourself how badly you want these DVD's. Since receiving the order, we have watched episodes at random from each season. Some are fine but others stick and freeze, even after cleaning. This only happened when we put them in the DVD player. In the laptop there are no sticking and freezing incidents and they play perfectly. The order arrived undamaged. Each season was packaged separately inside a larger box. The DVD's were in plastic cases. We could not see any scratches, even on the DVD's that would only play in the laptop. Subtitles for the hard of hearing and episode promos were available. Overall we are satisfied with the purchase and do not plan to return it. I think this show has held up very well despite being so dated. We laughed at the computers that filled a room, McGarrett's use of the word "honey" when referring to females, the big gas-guzzling cars, and we marveled at how well McGarrett kept in touch with his staff without the use of a cell phone.

history.title: Dick Van Dyke Show: Complete Remastered Series
history.review_title: Review of "The Dick Van Dyke Show"
history.text: I was very pleased with my order. Each DVD played perfectly; no freezing or skipping. The only thing lacking was an episode guide, which would have been very helpful.

history.title: Perry Mason: The Complete Series
history.review_title: Review of "Perry Mason, the Complete Series"
history.text: I want to urge all buyers to go through the disks and make sure they are all there. You can use the liner notes as a guide. We discovered that two disks from Season Nine were missing, including the one with the last episode where Erle Stanley Gardner plays the judge. In their place were duplicates from Season Eight. Amazon made it right by sending us another set. Before returning the original order, we sat down and went through each Season to be sure there were no more missing disks. Despite this glitch, it was great seeing Perry, Della, and Paul again. The huge cars from that era, the awful hairstyles women wore, a time when the legal age was 21 and not 18, is pure nostaglia. We've been watching one or two episodes daily and still are not halfway through the series. Many stars had guest roles when they were young "unknowns" -- we recognized Barbara Eden, Leonard Nimoy, and Burt Reynolds to name a few. Perry always got his man (or woman).

history.title: Two On A Guillotine
history.text: The description for this movie contains a major spoiler. We don't know Melinda's fate until the movie's conclusion. Cassie Duquesne, daughter of Melinda and the great magician, Duke Duquesne, must occupy her late father's home for seven nights in order to receive her inheritance. Two others will inherit the estate if Cassie reniges. Val Henderson, a new acquaintance, seems to be on Cassie's side. Together they probe the house's mysteries and the odd events that keep occurring. A chilling conclusion reveals that matters are not as they seem.

history.title: The Young Victoria
history.review_title: the story of Victoria and Albert is a poignant love story. The movie doesn't cover it
history.text: Unquestionably, the story of Victoria and Albert is a poignant love story. The movie doesn't cover it, of course, but the two of them, and their eventual plan to marry their progeny to royalty all over Europe (apparently to unite the countries), also helped lead to WWI. The films, with fine performances, period sets and writing, shows a young couple in love (no one knows, perhaps, whether Albert felt as deeply, but Victoria's feelings are historically documented). The films appears to take a little liberty with history for dramatic effect, but it is highly enjoyable.

history.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows - Part 2 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Liked the film, a little disappointed by the ending
history.text: I really liked the film, though it didn't have to be dragged into two parts. It is too dark visually and Radcliffe's performance is sometimes off. I was disappointed in the moody and dreary ending at the train station. The book, on the other hand, makes it clear that these are normal families, squabbling kids, concerned parents, and it also demonstrates the interrelatedness of some of the other characters (Lupin's son, for example). Harry's choice about the elder wand is not the same in the book as in the movie, although the film made his decision irrevocable and definitive, which in real life would be far safer for him and for others.

history.title: Sherlock: Season 1 [Blu-ray]
history.text: This series includes such great performances, writing, humor, and mystery. Okay, the first episode was frustrating since I couldn't figure out why the brilliant Sherlock took so long to tumble to the cabbie's part in it - I figured that out a long time earlier than he did, but I don't know if the film maker planned it that way, since the viewer gets to see things Sherlock doesn't see. Int he long run, it was the motives and the villain in the background that had to be discovered. The relationship between Sherlock and John Watson is good and the exploration of the effect of war/adrenaline/addiction to danger are all themes that are highly pertinent.

history.title: The Hunger Games (Blu-ray + Digital Copy) [Blu-ray] [2012]
history.text: Some kids and adults I know see it as a choice between loving Harry Potter or Hunger Games. As a Potter fan, what I'd heard about Hunger Games didn't attracted me. I finally watched the Hunger Games film, figuring I should know what the shouting was all about. It turned out that I really enjoyed the movie and then read the book and loved it also. I haven't been able to get into the later stories, but this one can stand on its own, leaving you to imagine what the future might hold. The film's additions to the book help tell the story extremely well, since a story told in first person does require some creative film writing. Be sure to watch the extra on Donald Sutherland's contribution to the film

The segments are broken into parts, there is no play all, each section has an unnecessarily long introduction to the material, which I wouldn't like for the classroom (boring to repeat and kids would reject, I believe,) but for home viewing is especially annoying. Unfortunately, the straight presentation of Teddy Roosevelt an American Lion in its boxed set is no longer being produced and is, used, incredibly expensive. So it you want the material (which is great) and can wade through the annoying part of the way this is put together, this may work for you.
