history.title: History Classics: Decoding The Past
history.review_title: Uneven and not worth a lot
history.text: Some of the History Channel shows are not the best and this series joins that infamous group of shows. The series is uneven. For the purpose of this review, I watched the Mysteries Of The Garden Of Eden and was very disappointed in some of the "facts" concerning the old testament, which for the knowledgeable viewer, would raise red flags. First off, this episode takes the approach that the O.T. is a relative recent invention, going back no more than the first millennium B.C. The Dead Sea Scrolls, which are copies in and of themselves, refute that idea. We don't know how old the records are, but the view taken in this show is not widely held, by any means. Plus, the show presents a sensationalist view, which is even worse. I strongly recommend other history shows that are much more comprehensive in their approach to the facts.

history.review_title: Bad choice of actors, bad character development -- MIssed the Boat!
history.text: I don't hate it, but I do not like it, either. The biggest problem was the casting. Richard Dean Anderson was a very rugged individual and he had a wry way of looking at things. Every once in a while, Jack Dalton would show up and give Mac an absolute headache. This new series has a "pretty boy" (Lucas Till) play the part of Mac and "tough guy" (George Eads) playing Jack Dalton, who is Mac's gun-happy backup, rather than pain in the butt. I have a major problem with the cast and though I don't mind a female playing the head of the Phoenix Foundation, both my wife and I really dislike the way the characters were put together. Lucas Till was just plain a bad choice. And Jack Dalton's character should never have become a regular. Mac worked alone in the original series, not with a partner.

history.title: Pete's Dragon (BD + DVD + Digital HD)
history.review_title: Missed the music of the original.
history.text: Very good and especially excellent special effects. However.... almost everyone misses the music of the original. Pete's Dragon was a treat as a musical live-action/cartoon mix, so this, without any of the songs, has to stand on its own. While it does a credible job and the scenery is wonderful, it isn't the Pacific Northwest (wasn't filmed there), and the performers were very good, the story itself could have been better.

history.title: CSI: Crime Scene Investigation: Season 1
history.review_title: Okay Crime Show -- more to come
history.text: First, T\there is a significant difference between closed captioning and subtitles. These discs are closed captioned, which is not the same thing as subtitled. You DVD player or compatible device should support closed captioning, so look for it. If it is not there, then blame your DVD playback device. Now to the show. I looked at the BD through Netflix and I agree with the thoughts that have been expressed. The video is overexposed and there is some significant pixelization that is annoying. I suspect this artifact was introduced when Paramount prepared the widescreen production. Yes, the original was shot in standard definition and the widescreen (on the BD) was created by trimming the top and bottom of the standard definition show. That was unfortunate, because the resulting BD episodes are very large in size. Now to the show -- My wife and I watched the first show (pilot) and were not overly impressed. While seeing a multiple threaded episode is not uncommon, having too many threads is annoying. I'm not passing judgment yet, but will wait until I have a chance to see later episodes. The characters are well-formed and I liked them, but wanted to see fewer characters and more focus on a single leader of the shift. The boss was annoying (he was a jerk) and I don't think he lasted past the pilot episode. I least, I hope not. Right now, my feeling is that it is okay, but nothing to write home about. Bypass the BD version because it does not add anything and chops off the top and bottom to produce the faux widescreen. Over saturating the color and the pixelization is also a problem.

history.title: LIBRARIAN TRILOGY - MOVIE
history.text: I appreciate getting the three pack of the BD discs at a reasonable price, but wanted a product with English subtitles. These are imports and contain only German subtitles.

history.title: CSI: NY - Nine Season Pack
history.review_title: Honest-to-goodness New Yrokers play New Yorkers
history.text: Like CSI: Crime Scene Investigation and CSI:Miami, this show follows a similar format. In New York, the investigation folks are referred to as CSU (Crime Scene Unit), but the technology is the same as with the other two shows. Like CSI:Miami, the CSU folks are actual police officers, whereas in the original series, they are essentially scientists who do/can not make arrests, etc., The appealing part of this series is that the performers are actors who either now live or have lived in New York and understand what life is like in that compact city. This series reveals a better look of New York that is missing in shows such as Castle and White Collar, which are both, in their own way, good series. The amount of dependency upon the CSU for not only resolving crimes and "who did it" is amazing. In most instances, we never see the outcome of any trials, only the evidence that the person or persons apprehended actually committed a crime. Having the entire series as a package is wonderful because we can binge watch this show to our heart's content. My wife and I are now watching the second season and I love the characters, though CS:Miami remains my favorite.

history.title: CSI: Miami - The Complete Series
history.text: Of the three series, (not comparing CSI:Cyber) this is my favorite, mostly because of the characters and Horatio always expresses appreciation for jobs well done. Being able to obtain the entire series at a great price adds to the value of the series and is appreciated. My wife and I are not watching the second season and really enjoy all three series.

history.review_title: Continuing an excellent series in celebrities researching their family's history.
history.text: While this series follows each celebrity as they visit the places where their ancestors lived, it also points out the importance of on-the-scene investigation. Much material is now readily available from the internet for doing genealogy, but when you can visit where your relatives lived, it becomes so much more alive. The only season not available is season three, which is the last year that the show was seen on one of the big three networks. I wish that season would be made available, either on disc or as a streamed series.

history.title: O Come Little Children
history.text: This includes the concert (as it will be broadcast on PBS) from last year (2016) with three bonus features. The DVD quality is as is expected and the performances are equal to recent years. Be aware that both performers - Rolanda Villazon (not Mormon) and Angela Brower (a Mormon) are professional opera performers and that the concert has a number of opera pieces. However, the focus is a performance of an adaption of The Little Match Girl. Besides the two "Backstage with..." the two guest performers, the third bonus is a "Behind the Scenes" feature on setting up and producing the story for not only the video, but also live in the 20,000-seat of the Salt Lake Mormon Conference Center. If there is a drawback, it is that the concert production is not available on Blu-ray in HD. However, an upleveling player works well and the stereo sound is magnificent.

history.review_title: Semi-serious Science Fiction Trek-like TV series
history.text: I was pleasantly surprised by this new series from (and staring) Seth MacFarlane. The advertisements made it look like it was going to be a spoof on Star Trek and the similarities to the Trek type of universe are familiar. But, I do not consider this a comedy, certainly no more than The Next Generation was a comedy. There are comedic elements, but they lie more with the not quite dysfunctional members of the crew, who are actually more believable in their individual natures, than most Trek characters. Don't get me wrong, I enjoyed Trek, especially the original cast series and films, but these stories are, in my opinion, just about as good. So far, five episodes have aired and they are decently written, good CGI and FX, and the performers approach their characters as if they were really there. Galaxy Quest (the real Trek spoof) this is not.

history.text: A part of me now regrets to have watched this film over another blatantly superior art film. You see, I had a holiday freebie day from work and decided to take a bus while I still lived in the boonies to the closest major city to see a movie. I was feeling somewhat ill that day and decided I was only going to see one film so that I could go take the 45 minute bus home and rest. One option was an indie film starring Liev Schrieber and Tobey Maguire where they play a legendary chess game. The plot sounded original and I knew for certain that any kind of indie film wouldn't last a week in the multiplex. However, I really enjoyed Zoolander 1 and had high hopes that the sequel would deliver some laughs while I felt infirm. I feel like I made the wrong choice. While watching Justin Bieber die in the first 3 minutes made the ticket worthwhile, it's like the writers believed moviegoers are brain dead morons and that we all concur that Malibu is located in the Sahara desert. Some gags are back including Owen Wilson's peyote tea drinking orgy party buddies but the writers made the characters so stupid that the few laughs turn into brief grumbles. While I find some scenes to be really funny (I laughed when Zoolander meets his obese son), the fashion police Interpol is dumb and a lot of the gags to be mild giggles at best. Will Ferrel played Mugatu very well, but again the gags were so dumb that I wondered why they waited so many years to make a sequel. The movie would have been better if they made it 8 years ago. The wait was too long and the result disatrous. A Sunday rental at best.

It seems like Amazon made a blooper and pasted reviews of another film from 2007. This film is from 2017 and it seems like my review is the first one that will actually cover the correct one. Emma Watson plays the role of the protagonist Mae Hollard and uses a fake Americanized accent (while she tried pretty hard to tone her British accent a bit, it's still there and she definitely doesn't have the accent of a California girl, sorry!). She lives in a small town south of San Francisco in a dead end customer service job at the Water Company when a friend of hers named Anna that works for the Silicon Valley megacorporation "The Circle" lands her the chance to get a job interview for a starter position. Mae is overwhelmed by the good news that she will have the chance to work somewhere more prestigious and with a fatter check to help her father who has Multiple Sclerosis. She lands a job at the company and is initially awed at the shiny installations and all of the facilities that allow employees to enjoy yoga, art and other recreational activities. The company also offers the perk of living in an apartment in the complex. She lands a rudimentary job at customer help services which is somewhat similar to her previous job. The guy that is training her tells her that it's important to gain 100% satisfaction. She frowns at the pressure but she begins to work hard. She even joins Anna that seems to be constantly traveling all over the world for mysterious business meetings without rest to the weekly company meeting with the CEO that is played by Tom Hanks. Mae feels elated with the company that is releasing a barely legal mini camera product that has been placed all over the world without anyone's consent. This is where the shininess of the awesome company ends and the creepiness begins. The Circle wants to upload everything happening in the entire world to the internet and use their own patented Social Network called "True You" for a creepy and very intrusive agenda. Mae doesn't seem bothered by any of this and returns home to talk about her awesome job with an accquaintance named Mercer. Mercer is a friendly boy next door type that does handyman work and made a nice antler chandelier for her parents. While he clearly feels attracted to Mae, he tells her that he doesn't like wasting his time playing on the internet and prefers his simple life. Mae returns to work and one day is approached by two coworkers that pull the definite "Office Space" homage. She performs very well leaving customers satisfied, but she isn't "participating" in any of the company's extracurricular activities that are supposed to be "voluntary" but in reality they are "obligatory". That scene made me frown as I recalled the scene in Office Space where Jennifer Aniston gets berated at her waitress job because she doesn't have 23 pins on her uniform. Mae confesses to these creeps that she went home that weekend to tend to her father and they creepily admit they already knew he had that disease. This should be private medical information and yet Mae sheepishly doesn't seem irritated with the uber "openness" philosophy of this company. Things turn weirder after this point. Mae is dragged to a medical facility in the complx and without signing a medical waiver form or any kind of informed consent, she happily drinks a mysterious concoction that perhaps contains nanomachines (the movies never specifies what that green thing was) and now a fancy watch she must now wear at all times registers everything that is happening to her body. The medical "service" is free at the cost that she is being used as a guinea pig without any sort of waiver of the potential risks or any kind of financial compensation. It seems like she was cornered to the wall to accept being used like this so that her father could get health insurance. After Mae is rescued from the ocean after stupidly kayaking alone in the middle of the night, she accepts Tom Hank's offer to become the poster child of the company's Big Brother dream and allows cameras to record her exploits all day long. She doesn't seem even remotely bothered by all of this and even seems to enjoy the idolatry. While most employees in this company love what The Circle plans to do worldwide, Anna and a mysterious man named Ty don't like it and sort of hope Mae comes to her senses and realizes this is just creepy and wrong. Mae doesn't seem to care until something terrible happens to poor Mercer... The photography of the film is great and the story remains interesting till the very end, but I just can't seem to fathom that people would be so delighted that a corporation would have so much control over their private lives. They practically want to know that you dumped in the toilet bowl and leave all of your bank account passwords in the open, force everyone in the world with US citizenship to vote against their will and collect their private data and it seems like the US government doesn't seem to care about doing anything about it. The film seems to fall short with Mae's ridiculous degree of naïvety and that Ty and Anna's suspicions were not developed further. The thing about placing computer servers in a damp and very wet tunnel beneath the ground also seems odd. Oh and BTW, everyone at the company believes Mercer needs psychotherapy because he's just you know... so mentally ill because he has a blue collar job and doesn't have the time or interest to be playing on his cellphone. I mean, what's freaking wrong with him right? Even Mae agrees that Mercer is a wacko because he was too busy making a living doing carpentry and mechanical work. Oh, and nobody trolls Mae when she is the Big Brother internet star? The movie places the random messages she gets from users and not one single message with spelling errors and nasty racist comments or anything? All in all, the film is interesting, weird but I felt like some things were missing. I really wonder if people that work in Silicon Valley really think like this...

The movie has some good scenes. I like the part where Jack is all crazy talking to himself in this magical dimension and the awesome story of the curse of the captain of the Meandering Dutchman ship. But we have to agree that the movie sort of meanders all over the place with flashy scenes but underdeveloped new characters that nobody cares about (they could have killed all of the new pirates and I wouldn't have cared). There is some good scenes in the film but the movie falters from a confusing script. It seems like it was written and rehashed 20 times by 20 different writers that had to check on a checklist of essentials that were demanded by marketers to appease a large audience. The story seems convulted and rushed at some parts yet slow in others. I still find the good parts of the movie to be entertaining, Depp plays his star role well and I enjoyed the tragic love stories despite the tedious parts of the plot.

history.title: Repo Men
history.text: Don't get me wrong, this movie has a lot of good things. Jude Law and Forest Whitaker are an interesting duo, there's action and an interesting plot. Imagine a world in the future where mechanical organs that cost a lot of money are leased to infirm people that end up owing staggering debt to the manufacturing companies. When the person is unable to cope with the debt, there is no chance to file a Chapter 11. Instead, a crony member of the company's repossession team locate the person and rip the organ out of their bodies. Gruelsome and gritty, Jude seems to enjoy his job but he's having problems with his wife that hates what he does for a living. During a raid of a musician that ended up bankrupt and unable to pay for his mechanical heart, a defibrillator that he uses to extract the organ fails and he ends up with severe heart damage (I sort of find this to be ridiculous given he's young an healthy, but meh...) and now he owns his very own mechanical heart and a heap of medical bills. He begins to have second thoughts about the morality of his job and he starts to stack up debt... The story is fortunately fast and gets to the point but it suffered from several mishaps. 1- Unnecessary filler scenes. It seems like this movie was hastily made and the post production didn't do a very good job of removing fluff filler scenes that agitate the pace of the story. The scene where Forest's character plays a prank of Jude Law in the organ reposession warehouse could have been removed. There are many other scenes in the film that could have been cut out and made it a much smoother flick. Leave the fluff scenes for the extended DVD. 2- Sue the bastards. This movie takes place in the USA where I'm certain a company employee with a stellar track record that ends up severely maimed due to a malfunctional work related device while on the job wouldn't be saddled with debt. Maybe the company wouldn't buy him the fanciest state-of-the-art heart, but they'd try to appease his wrath before the inevitable civil lawsuit takes place. 3- Hackers anyone? The film seems to be too perfect in the sense that people that have organs they can't afford to pay live in slums. This makes sense, but in a world where jobless people can get extra mechanical organs on the black market installed don't seem to realize there has to be a way to erase the debt of the organ. If the security system to remove the debt on an organ is so foolproof, wouldn't it just be easier to locate a chump that already finished paying for his mechanical organs, kill him, make the body vanish and steal his organs to sell at a ridiculous price? 4- Poor people can afford some luxuries. Jude Law befriends a woman that occasionally works at a bar he frequents after work that owes big cash on several organs in her body due to her drug addiction. The woman no longer consumes drugs but she doesn't have stable income, the reposession people are looking for her and despite her minimum wage job, she can afford to have super fancy mechanical eyes and a sexier voice machine. Huh? I will give the ending to the movie credit, I thought the pivotal scene where Forest Whitaker located Jude Law and his new girlfriend to be kind of uncredible until I saw the ending. The finale is rather surprising and it improved the review a bit. I'm probably being injust with this review, but while the movie is indeed entertaining, the plotholes killed it for me.

Michael Bay has treated us with those dreadfests known as the Transformer films. He's not known to make thought provoking films but there is still something that is really charming about The Island. Ewan McGreggor named Lincoln in this flick wakes up in a sort of huge laboratory with confusing memories of a long lost life and told over and over again that he is very special and awaiting a chance to win a ticket to a mysterious place called the Island. Brainwashed to believe the world was destroyed by a nuclear war and they live underground to avoid the contamination, he never gives any thought about things that don't make any sense such as why would the aforementioned island be devoid of contamination and how come those security guards that watch his every movement are never allowed to go to that place. He starts to grow suspicious when he locates a moth and shows it to some of his friends that ignore him. After sneaking out of his comfortable prison and seeing that the true winners of the island getaway are brutally murdered to have their organs harvested, he escapes with a female friend played by Scarlett Johansson named Jordan. They discover their compound was beneath a desolate desert and they reach Los Angeles and locate Lincoln's "sponsor". He discovers they are all clones of wealthy people who are sacrificed for their organs. Jordan's sponsor is a famous actress that suffered massive brain damage from a car crash and the Island committee want to harvest her organs immediately. It becomes a race against time for these two characters to find their place in this alien world before they are killed. The movie loses some points with pointless action scenes that only slow the plot, but the character interaction is definitely there. I truely enjoyed the distinct personalities of each character and Steve Buschemi shines in his role of slimy sleazeball that helps the duo locate their respective sponsors. While the film indeed has some flaws, it's still vastly enjoyable with a mostly positive vibe to it despite the grim premise.

Set in a spooky rendition of Earth 10,000 years into the future where humanoid monsters cause havoc and vampires still rule the night in a chaotic world, their numbers have been dwindling after being hunted by professionals such as D. When a woman named Charlotte is kidnapped by a powerful noble vampire named Meier Link, her wealthy father hires two competing vampire hunters to find her: The Marcus brothers and D who go their separate ways for the same goal. However, little do they know, it starts to become obvious Charlotte decided to run away from home willingly and wants to marry the mysterious and powerful vampire. D knows all too well what it feels like to grow up as a half-vampire in an unforgiving world and will do everything in his power to separate the ill-fated lovers. With a gothic animation style and great fighting scenes, we get to enjoy a truely fascinating story that has interesting characters, a great soundtrack and a surprising conclusion. I wished they made more movies that were half as good as this one.

I watched this film last night and mostly had a good time. I won't really detail the plot because that has already been addressed in other reviews. The basic plot is that 6 13 year old teenagers that aren't particularly popular at school live in a small town in Maine where a series of children and teenagers have gone missing. The protagonist lost his younger brother Georgie and holds high hopes the kids is still alive somewhere in the sewage system. Lauded as a nut by his family and treated with a certain degree of condescendence by his friends, he still chooses to embark on a dangerous mission to find his brother and uncover the mystery of the kidnappings once and for all. I recall seeing the original film ages ago so my memory is mostly fuzzy. However, given this film is a modernized remake (that still strives to take place in the 1980's), it has an engaging plot, interesting characters and despite a somewhat slow middle is mostly good. The CGI is rather good albeit I wasn't particularly scared during the film. I was busier removing slices of jalapeño chile in my serrano ham sandwich. It's obvious this reboot is going to create a huge string of sequels that will likely do well in the box office. If you easily get startled with horror films, this is probably going to be one of the tamer ones out there. Mostly worth the hype.

I will be frank here, I have never seen the previous two films of the trilogy so I cannot say how good they are. However! World's End is sufficiently self explanatory to be regarded as a standalone film in its own right where you get introduced to the 5 oddball friends that get together to fulfill their dream of a successful pub crawl in their home village. Simon Pegg plays the mentally unstable Gary King that suffers from delusions of grandeur coupled with a blatant alcohol and drug problem that cannot seem to get his act together and fervishly lives in the past. He manages to escape a mental institution and recruits his old childhood friends to a legendary pub crawl with a mixture between begging and deceit. Gary is so ballsy that he asks 3 of the friends to lend him 100 pounds that he gives to the friend that holds the strongest grudge because he went to jail as a juvenile due to him. After reaching their old village, the pub crawl seems to start normally with the expected tension due to Gary's past mistakes. And then things go weird for no reason when they discover most of the inhabitants of the village have been cloned by a strange alien race while the originals end up killed and turned into compost. The group must find the way to pretend to act normal and finish the crawl before they become the next batch of victims to this malignant scheme. Aimed at making this a silly comedy instead of a drama, the acting was great, the characters memorable and the tension nonstop that keeps you engaged. Gary's character is a delight to watch despite his massive defects and you just want to start rooting for him to achieve his long lost dream of finishing the pub crawl suitably at the Worlds End Tavern. If people claim that the previous movies are so much better than this one (already a huge feat because this film is undoubtedly very funny), I'll just have to find the way to see the full trilogy and see for myself.

history.review_title: Ugly haircuts coupled with a weird plot
history.text: I cannot be too judgemental of this movie because I haven't read the original comic but in a way, Scott Pilgrim functions as a sort of guilty pleasure. Scott is some seemingly ordinary teenager that lives in Canada that wants his really crappy pop band to succeed. He doesn't seem to have any real direction in life until he meets a mysterious american 20 something woman with rainbow colored hair, an ugly haircut and the gulls to wear thin leggings in the middle of winter without freezing to death. The beginning of the film feels like a well produced indie film where Scott tries to woo the girl without great success... and then BAM! things go all videogame weird for no apparent reason. He becomes confronted by a indian guy that can float in the air and has a team of magical succubus demons send firebombs at the unlikely hero. The movie turns 180 degrees from an indie romance drama to a weird conglomeration of campy jokes and Street Fighter battles. Everytime Scott turns an angry ex boyfriend into mush, the foe turns into coins and the screen issues him points like his entire life has been merely a videogame. I initially wanted to place bleach on my eyes with the ridiculousness of the videogame battles, but after rewatching the film several times, I find them to be the funnest parts. If you try to set aside the realism factor and enjoy the film such as it is, I find it to be rather enjoyable for a Sunday afternoon.

When you associate Britain with spy film, you automatically think about James Bond. Presuming filmakers wanted to combine the elegance of James Bond with a younger cast and without the sex tourism Bond jokes, this is how Kingsman was created to fill that void. In a way the film has some nice merits. Starring a troubled British teenager that was the son of a spy that had an honorable death, he grows up with a chip on his shoulder due to living with an abusive stepfather. After getting arrested protecting his friends from a pub fight and booked on assault charges, he phones the mysterious Kingsman number that was passed to him after his father's death and is strangely enough released from jail within a handful of minutes. Colin Firth isn't best known for action roles and he almost seems out of place as a sort of mentorship role in this film. While the training scenes have some high and low points, they can confuse younger viewers thinking some of the applicants were killed during the individual tests. It's as if life was easily discarded as something useless. While the supporting spy cast are okay, the villains are totally unrealistic. Samuel L. Jackson plays a lot of great villanous roles but he seems silly in this film at best. It's hard to believe he's the big enchilada. The film gets some merit from the mostly fast pace, but the head explosion scenes are so ridiculous that a movie that was striving for a grim theme ends up being hard to take seriously. Might be worthy as a rental, but there are far better action films out there.

history.title: Fun Size
history.text: Silly, unbelievable plot. Waste of time for adults. The older sister is in charge of her little brother, who never speaks, and plays pranks and gets lost. She takes him to a rather adult party, and pays no attention to him, so he wanders off and gets into all sorts of "funny" situations. Totally unbelievable. In the download to my HD TV, there was poor image quality, with pixilation on moving objects (my TV has a 120Hz refresh rate).

history.title: THE SHELTERING SKY (1990) / REGION FREE NTSC DVD / Audio: English / Subtitles: English, French, Korean / Actors: Debra Winger, John Malkovich, Campbell Scott, and Jill Bennett / Directors: Bernardo Bertolucci / 139 minutes
history.review_title: I'm very satisfied with this disc.
history.text: This is a beautifully filmed version, shot in Morocco, of a novel by expatriate Paul Bowles (who appears in the film briefly). It was a very entertaining, but tragic film that had a rather strange ending. It was almost as though a whole reel was left out. Not the case, of course, but that is the impression left by the vague ending.

Vastly overrated film. All action; no logic. Apparently, there was little water left on the planet, and the tyrant was holding back on the supply. Then the valves were opened and the water gushed out to the downtrodden waiting below. They were allowed to wallow in the mud for a short time, and then the water was shut off. Why? If it was in short supply, why waste it? The main character, played by Charlize Theron, was apparently trusted by the tyrant, but rebelled, and sped off with a tanker truck full of water. Where was she supposed to be taking it before she deviated from the plan? After the end (spoiler) where was Mad Max going, since it was established that there was no place else to go? Second worst movie of the year.

history.title: Black Emmanuelle Collection - 4-DVD Set ( Emanuelle nera / Emanuelle bianca e nera (Black Emanuelle/White Emanuelle) / Suor Emanuelle / La via della prostituzione (Emanuelle and the Girls of Madame Cl
history.text: Image quality is good. Laura Gemser is gorgeous. However, all discs have poor lip-synchronization, and the one listed on the boxed set as "Black Emanuelle, White Emanuelle" is actually, "Velluto Nero, " (Black Velvet). It keeps switching from Italian to English and back with no logical reason. No subtitles. If you know a bit of Italian, as I do, that is no great loss, but the plot would be difficult to follow in any case. Beautiful photography of Egypt. No logical plot, and no reason for the characters to react to each other the way they do. The other discs are okay, but dubbing is poor. Soft-core porn with beautiful girls. Lots of National Geographic type travel videos.

history.title: King Kong - Edición Especial Coleccionista (Incluye Libreto) [Blu-Ray] [Blu-R
history.text: The prints are high quality. There are four-disc set. Two versions of the original (Blu-ray & DVD). Some of the films are ones I didn't know about, such as King Kong Lives (or King Kong 2, as it is in this Spanish version. Be aware that, although they can be played in English, some of them have subtitles I can't get rid of. Be aware, toor, that these discs are for Region 2, and won't play in most U.S. players. The good thing, though, is that I was able to fast-forward through the dull bits in that film, and still be able to read the Spanish sub-titles. Not a great film, but if you want a complete set of Kong movies, it is a set worth having. Includes the original Black-and-white with Fay Raye, "Son of Kong," and "Mighty Joe Young," as well. I thought it was worth the purchase, never having heard of "King Kong Lives" before. It stars Linda Hamilton and Brian Kerwin. It is the usual such film, where the military want to kell, and the heroine wants to save. Some very bad acting with a few of the characters, although Linda Hamilton is okay. She deserves a better film.

history.title: Wodehouse Playhouse: Complete Collection
history.text: These story's are GREAT!!! A thought, if you are not familiar with P. G. Wodehouse's stories, read the books first. This series, along with Blandings Castle series, follow the books faithfully. If you like British humor, don't miss this series.

history.title: Western Pacific Vintage West
history.review_title: This is another of Charles Smiley's great video's, and the third of the four that ...
history.text: This is another of Charles Smiley's great video's, and the third of the four that compile this series ( the Southern Pacific is the fourth movie for me). The other's in the series ( the Western Pacific, the Union Pacific, and the Santa Fe) show railroading in the 40's, the 50's, and 60's, If you are interested in this era, the Western Pacific, along with the others, is a must-have. The transference from film to DVD disk is, for the most part, just perfect! A great DVD!

history.title: Blandings, Series 2
history.text: I happen to be a big P.G. Woodhouse fan, and his stories about Blandings Castle are some of the best. Needless to say I have both series One and Series Two. Timothy Spall is great as Clarence, the head of the family, and Jennifer Saunders is perfect as his sister( and his foil) is great. I just hope the come out with more Series, we can but hope.

history.title: Coupling - The Complete First Season
history.text: This is an interesting British Comedy that revolves around 6 people, 3 guys and 3 ladies. I can remember this when it was live on BBC America. It's really funny, with razor sharp writing, and great actors make for a great storyline. If you were alive in the 70,s, and you enjoy British humor, you can't go wrong with this series.

history.title: Aloha [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Stay far, far away unless you just like seeing Hawaii in the background of shots.
history.text: Ignoring the bad reviews, I went to see this film in the theater and walked out disappointed by all involved except the cinematographer. I expected better from Cameron Crowe - the story is just haphazard. Emma Stone and Bradley Cooper have zero romantic chemistry, and frankly it felt really really creepy (he is 40 in real life, compared to Emma's 26.) There was a good movie in here, especially with Rachel McAdams and the new husband, but it got lost in among the forced romance and the usual Defense Department is EVIL claptrap.

history.title: Larry Crowne [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A sweet and tender modern movie.
history.text: When I originally saw this film in a theater, I thought it was "just OK" and was nothing special. Over repeated pay TV viewings, I've really come to appreciate it and especially how natural and unforced the romance between Hanks and Roberts is. Unlike most modern films the characters don't immediately fall into bed together and are aware of the awkwardness (and implications) of their student/teacher relationship. Perhaps my favorite line is when, thankful that Hanks has kept a kiss one night secret, he states he can keep a secret and Roberts states "Gentlemen do." Sweet and very endearing.

history.title: Olympus has Fallen
history.review_title: Blatantly pro-American and that's what I like about it.
history.text: This film is just plain fun. The scenario is actually quite realistic and it's unabashedly pro-American, a true rarity these days. If you're the type of person who finds "Top Gun" and "Independence Day" to be too pro-America, you won't enjoy this film. For anyone else, it's a pretty good action film.

history.title: Back to the Future: The Complete Adventures [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Blu-ray discs packaged in cardboard "scratch your disc" sleeves. :-(
history.text: I don't know when Universal started this, but with both this and Jurassic World 3D collector's tin, they now pack your movie discs in cardboard sleeves rather than proper Blu-ray cases. Ironically, the included animated series in the package comes in a normal DVD case, but the movies - presumably the reason you're buying the set - do not. So unless you've no issue purchasing your own Blu-ray cases, stay far away from this edition. Pathetic, Universal - no wonder more people are just buying digital media when you treat people purchasing physical media so poorly.

history.title: Xanadu [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Finally on Blu-ray, and absolutely beautiful!
history.text: I won't go into the merits of the movie itself here, but rather want to comment on the Blu-ray release. Simply put, this movie has never looked better on home video. It's a bit grainy at times, as was the case for the film stock used during the period, but that also means it doesn't suffer from excessive noise reduction. The audio is presented in a 5.1 DTS HD mix, which I have a few misgivings about simply because the original film was only mixed to Dolby Stereo. There seems to be excessive channel separation applied but it still sounds good with no "phasing" artifacts. However, flipping briefly over to the Spanish and French mixes, they are very, very bright and harsh, musically. The Spanish mix in particular was so bright as to be painful to listen to. The extras are nothing special, just the Back to Xanadu documentary from 2008 and a trailer. Still, it's awesome to have this title on Blu-ray at all, and it looks much better than the HD version floating around the pay movie channels for several years and the streaming version available for purchase from the iTunes store, among others. Especially for the price, it's definitely worth it for any fan.

The good thing is the effect only seems to affect the narration, not the musical sequences (the audio of the PBS broadcast did NOT have this issue, so it happened somewhere in the disc mastering process.) I was, however, quite disappointed that the disc does NOT include the full, unedited acoustic video of "(You Make Me Feel Like a) Natural Woman" that PBS posted to their web site, so on-disc you're left only with the interrupted by narration clip that is part of the show itself. Still, if you haven't seen it, it's well worth your time; personally I would not have purchased the disc if I had known the version of the above song included as an extra was not the unedited clip from the documentary as seen on the PBS website.

history.title: White Christmas (Diamond Anniversary Edition) [Blu-ray]

The liquid satin gowns in the finale look as sumptuous as they likely did in person. The movie is enchanting and perfection itself, an incredibly sweet story that gets far too little airtime at Christmas. Do yourself a favor and pick up a copy and avoid the commercials and resolution drop of cable or satellite.

history.title: Peanuts Holiday Collection (4K Ultra HD + Blu-ray) [4K UHD]
history.text: The video quality on this new UHD collection is absolutely wonderful - the best these specials have ever and will ever look. However, the audio quality is the problem. As when they originally released them on Blu-ray, Warner decided to include a fake simulated surround audio mix on these specials, which means that you get to hear an echoey fake stereo mix for the Vince Guaraldi soundtracks that made these specials famous. They could have done the right thing and included an original mono track, but they did not, and because of the echo even if you set your sound processor to "Mono" it doesn't sound quite right. The only way of hearing these with the correct audio is to sync up the disc with a copy of the old DVDs, which had a mono soundtrack. This is truly sad and disrespectful to these classics; it's like if Miracle on 34th Street and It's a Wonderful Life were ONLY available in the horrible colorized versions rather than the original Black & White.

history.title: Maverick: Season 1
history.text: This series debuted in 1957 but still feels fresh, with well-crafted plots, laid-back script, and very engaging actors (both the leads and the guest stars). Technically, Maverick was a Western, but the plots were varied and interesting, and rarely relied on the traditional themes of "Westerns". I've just finished watching the whole set, and almost every episode is a delight, with light-hearted, self-deprecating humor and just enough plot twists, drama, and action, even occasional philosophizing. For those who've seen the somewhat more recent movie "Maverick" with Mel Gibson and Jodie Foster, that movie was entirely faithful to the spirit of the series. If you liked the movie, you'll appreciate the TV series.

history.title: Interstellar (Blu-ray)
history.text: Utterly incomprehensible. Begins with an Apocalypse, segues into Space Opera, wanders into junk physics, manufactures a climax, resolves the climax with more junk physics. Downbeat throughout. Relentlessly depressing. And, yes, everyone whispers, and you can't even follow much of the dialogue. Dei ex machinis are thrown in willy-nilly to move the plot along. Almost every development in the story has no logical basis and some even have no explanation whatever, from the farmer who just happened to be a former astronaut, to the secret organization that was first outraged it was discovered then blase about its existence leaking, to the extra-galactic search for habitable planets that eventually resulted (apparently) in None Found, to the final disconnect between the Here and There, and the dispirited last-minute attempt to end upbeat by having the hero mount a rescue when for 80 years no one else in humankind cared enough to make the effort (yet the hero is able to steal a needed galaxy-hopping-capable craft without any problem).

history.title: Monkey Business
history.text: Most of the humor is of a very low order, appealing to puerile mentalities. (Examples: dropping a live goldfish in a man's pants and then having him sit on a pie, materialized out of nowhere in a chemistry lab; long and pointless reckless-driving scene; a bride crying uncontrollably in a hotel room over a recollection of her mother; absent-minded and blind-as-a-bat professor; “playing Indians” sequence that is painful to sit through; an opening-screen joke that is repeated over and over, when it wasn't even worth doing once.) It is beyond me how Howard Hawks could have made this film, which labors on and on as it depicts a chemist and then his wife behave like adolescents after taking a youth potion. There are a few flashes of verbal and visual wit related to Charles Coburn and Marilyn Monroe, but the leads Cary Grant and Ginger Rogers just aren't funny in this film. All of these actors had appealing, funny, and heartwarming roles in other movies, including some madcap or French farce type comedies. In Monkey Business, they're all wasted. If it weren't for the famous director and famous players, this movie would have been forgotten long ago.

history.title: Jeeves & Wooster Complete Collection
history.text: Superb series, captures the exact feel of the books. Much of the screenplay is in fact word-for-word from the Wodehouse text, and couldn't have been better portrayed than by Hugh Laurie and Steven Fry. When I re-read the novels, it's the Laurie and Fry voices that "play" in my mind. My only lament is that many of the actors for various roles were replaced or changed around. With each successive season, you need to make a serious effort to figure out Who's Who. While some of the actor substitutions were almost unnoticeable (the aunts), others were a real shame (the original Barmy and Gussie were just precious).

history.title: Miss Marple: The Complete Collection
history.review_title: Waste of Re-Mastering Effort, but Very Good Series
history.text: I watched snippets of an episode from my original, and of the same episode from this "Remastered" re-release, one after the other, then back, and the result is a disappointment. (This was on a new Samsung UHD 55" TV, with a new Samsung Blu-Ray player.) While it is true that there is some improvement in color saturation and sharpness, there are still fuzzy artifacts and extensive pixelation. Blacks are deep blue with grey haze. If BBC was going to go through the trouble of remastering, they should have released it on Blu-Ray, optimized for UHD televisions (the likely intended vehicle for someone who re-buys the collection). Even without Blu-Ray, they could have done better; I have some quite old TV series DVDs which, though not even remastered, look quite smart on my screen, after up-conversion. If you already own these movies, I wouldn't spend money to acquire this set. If you don't yet own these movies, these are great mysteries, and very good value for many hours of entertainment. Joan Hickson is well-cast as Marple.

history.title: Inferno
history.text: This is a visually stunning movie with lots of great chase and fight sequences, set in some very lovely cities. But the storyline just has too many unbelievable elements and non-sequiturs, and the clues are so labored, that after a few minutes all that's left are the visuals. The starting premise is fine, stock thriller fodder. A genius wants to cull the world's population by half in order to save both the planet and humanity itself. He develops a plague virus. Okay so far. But instead of just releasing the virus he puts it in an aerosol bomb somewhere, with a countdown timer. The genius has associates. Some know exactly where the bomb is but are content to wait there and be infected when it blows up. Other associates are deliberately not told where the virus bomb is, and instead are given an obtuse starting clue that might lead them to the bomb (if they are very smart, and dispose the services of the hero's expertise), where their mission would be to ensure that no one prevents it from blowing up. The clues are so obtuse, in fact, that no one could follow them, unless he wrote the screenplay. By the way, many of the characters seem to be able to teleport from one locale to another, too. If you like Dan Brown and Tom Hanks, you will still like this movie. Just ignore the plot.

history.title: Bones Seasons 1-12 Box Set
history.review_title: Thoughtlessly-Designed Packaging and Disc Play Commands
history.text: The packaging and the disc programming must be designed by people who really don't watch TV series on DVD and thus cannot anticipate even basic expectations of their customers. Packaging: the box is annoying because instead of the usual orientation, the DVD booklets go in face-to-front, two abreast, then there is a top cover over everything. The set either doesn't fit, or takes up too much space, on a DVD shelf. To pull out a booklet is a big operation, and all the pieces (box, top, and the booklet in use) wind up getting left strewn around. Disc programming: No Play All command in earlier seasons. Worse: Choosing an episode doesn't play it yet; it leads you to another interface first. Worse yet: at the end of an episode, the disc doesn't advance to the next episode, but re-sets to the opening interface for the episode just played. All in all, to progress from the last episode to the next, you need to make about 4 clicks (with pauses) instead of none. Don't they understand that people buy these sets so they can watch multiple episodes in a row? However, this design was corrected midway through the seasons. Further update: Having now watched nine seasons, I can confirm that most of the stories are ingenious and the characters evoke our empathy. But a new quibble has emerged. While Emily Deschanel has many fans, when you watch more than one episode at a time, her voice and delivery become annoying - ponderous, self-important, with the curious tic of repeating or stretching vowel sounds every few words. Example: "Now that he's ba-ack, his pa-ast is catching u-up." Several of the other actors have caught the same tendency.

history.title: Saving Mr. Banks
history.review_title: This Mostly-True Story Did Not Need to Be Told on the Silver Screen
history.text: This is a tedious and unpleasant-to-sit-through movie, about a relentlessly nasty and thoroughly dislikable person. The audience is supposed to slowly begin to sympathize with her as more of the "justifications" for her nastiness are revealed, but the screenplay takes much too long to get to any point where you would even want to like her. The ending is hokey and apparently untrue as to the emotions and motivations involved. If you think you might be interested in this movie because you liked the Disney movie Mary Poppins, you should stay away and hold on to your memories. If you like the female lead, you will end up despising her. If you like the male lead, you will find nothing in this movie to bolster your opinion. In sum, as a movie-goer you will experience two hours of "discomfort", and about 2 minutes of "heartwarming".

They are not doing this young person favors by hiding and delaying his ability to move on to a life or a profession. The story line is very incomplete. history.review_title: I liked the story and the style.
history.text: I like movies where acting and reacting to important events is the story...It is low key and I like low key where the story doesn't get lost to car chases, shootouts, loud music and noise to hype it all. The story is what is most important...and the acting has to be good enough to sell the story. Not so many people in our country can relate to or understand what was really happening in East Germany and many countries behind the iron curtain. They don't understand that just a questionable attitude could have a desasterous on your circumstances or on the people you know... This was a very good story and very believable.... It fell a little short in being a little too low key...really important events seemed at times not very important to the actors... Some of the acting and actors was excellent...and some was OK. There didn't seem to be music that supported the events properly...music can make your heart race, cause fear or interest, make you sad or joyous....and there were times that seemed to be missing... But, I was made to think, enjoy and remember....it was a very sad time in East Germany...

history.text: I loved this movie which explores some of the economic and family crises (abetted by "respectable" economic institutions such as banks) facing ordinary, hard working americans. The characters are well drawn and well acted from the starring roles of the bank robber brothers to the Texas rangers who are persuing them to the ancillary characters of diner waitresses, gamblers and hookers who work the casinos. This movie is not "preachty" nor is it a typical shoot en up gangster movie. If you are looking for either you will not find it here. It is character driven. If you appreciate the characters, their desperation, and their actions-fueled by determination to set things right-you will enjoy the movie

history.review_title: Michael Parks gives another superb performance
history.text: This story resembles the 1993 standoff at Waco (Bill Clinton President/Janet Reno Attorney General). That incident resulted in numerous deaths when FBI forces failed to get armed residents of the Branch Davidians' compound, led by David Koresh, to surrender peacefully. As always, Hollywood is shows bias against the US government in the narrative. However, the movie did not make the members of the congregation harmless innocents. They were clearly portrayed as murderous bigots. Except for the young children, viewers are unlikely to have sympathy for the group. Michael Parks is absolutely superb as the fundamentalist leader of the group with able assistance from the rest of the cast, especially Melissa Leo and John Goodman. I bought the movie because I am a great fan of Michael Parks' work. This is one of last movies as he died this year (2017) at the age of 77.

I enjoyed the first John Wick movie and was eagerly awaiting the second installment, pre-ordered through Amazon. For me, this movie was unmitigated crap. There is minimal plot with dialogue interludes of about 5 minutes each, scattered throughout the movie. The rest is just choreographed strike block, strike block. If you are interested in a martial arts match and NOT a movie, you will probably like this. For movie goers who are looking for plot and characterizations (as opposed to caricatures) along with action-this is a big disappointment.

Excellent character study. A Texas Ranger is sent to a small Texas settlement on a reconnaissance mission. He is to gather information on a charismatic and violent preacher who has been hunting, capturing, and killing Mexican nationals who venture across the border between Mexico and Texas. The US wants to stop the preacher and his followers before war is renewed between the United States and Mexico. The Ranger is brilliantly played by Liam Hemsworth with an equally excellent performance from Woody Harrelson as the preacher. The cast is uniformly fine and there are many surprising moments as Hemsworth confronts and is confronted by the Preacher and his followers. The movie has episodes of violence. What really makes The Dual worth your time are the situations and character studies that emerge from those situations.

I watched this movie to the end because I could not believe that a movie with so many fine actors could be this baaaaaaad. Well, at least they got a pay day out of it. If you are a stoner this may be your cup of tea, otherwise give it a pass.

This is an outstanding movie which depicts the conflicting emotions/behaviors experienced by people caught up in extreme circumstances-wanting to save themselves yet-a few-willing to do the right thing in spite of terrible danger. The plot concerns a Nazi officer who is sent to guard aging Keizer Wilhelm. He is a loyal officer of der Fuhrer who believes that vicious sadists are the "exception" among the Nazis. At the Keizer Wilhelm's estate he meets a maid who is actually a spy for the allies. Each of the characters, including the Keizer, his wife, and their servants must decide what path to follow, according to their own moral code. The cast is absolutely outstanding-without exception. This movie is attempting to illuminate the moral choices one must make under acute stress. It is not a historical document in the sense of a documentary.

Basic plot: Policeman's girlfriend is a prostitute. She is murdered. The rest of the story focuses on "who did it". Policeman (played by Coltrane) works with his girlfriend's young daughter to find the killer. But was it the policeman himself who was the culprit? Very disappointing production. This story could have been told in half the time. What the writer apparently thought added to suspense, for me just dragged the story out to the point of boredom. Coltrane was so badly miscast as the police detective/suspect/hero that I was almost glad to see the "surprise" ending. At least, the movie was included with "Prime".

history.review_title: Trace Adkins fans will enjoy the movie
history.text: This movie is not a great!! movie but for Trace Adkins fans it is worth the watch. Adkins plays a genial bar/brothel owner who turns out to be an absolutely convincing villain. It's also fun to watch Bruce Dern and Kris Kristofferson play non-staring character parts. Adkins is actually a convincing actor and is the primary reason to watch the movie. The plot revolves around Bill Hickok who comes to town, agrees to hire on as Marshall, and requires the men to check their firearms while in town. Needless to say this move stirs up animosity and sets the stage for some entertaining confrontations and displays of shootin' prowess. Soon after taking the job, Hickok meets his long lost love, now engaged to the villain and creating a romantic sub plot. For history buffs, gunman John Wesley Hardin also figures in the story as a Hickok ally. There are other accurate historical references (Wyatt Earp/Tombstone) for fans who enjoy this genre.

Trace Adkins is a believable western hero/outlaw. He has the right "look", the right accent, and a natural manner that makes him believable as opposed to an "actor". Several ancillary roles were also fine, including Judd Nelson, Claude Duhamel as outlaws and Artine Brown as another law man. Although I usually enjoy actor, Kim Coates, he was a little too much of a cartoon bad guy in this role and the female bounty hunter sidekick was unconvincing and unnecessary. (Maybe actress Helena Marie is somebody's sweetie.) The story holds your attention thanks mainly to Adkins who fits the role of western anti-hero so well. If you enjoy westerns, you will probably like this movie.

This fine documentary is respectful of the people filmed and shows their intelligence, courage, and self-awareness in spite of poverty, physical illness and psychological problems.There is nothing condescending in the work which allows people to speak for themselves without "interpretation" by the filmmaker. This is a film of compassion and understanding. Bravo!

history.title: By the Sea [DVD]
history.text: I expected more from this movie because I like Pitt and Jolie but had to force myself to finish watching in hopes that the lifeless performances, particularly by Joli, were headed someplace. To me, too much of the movie became focused on the hole in the wall between their room at an old French hotel and that of a newly wed couple, discovered first by Jolie, then by Pitt. We see scene after scene of Jolie, then Pitt and Joli, watching the couple in states of undress and in various sexual positions which finally inspires Jolie to move far enough out of her wooden depressed state to allow her husband to kiss her and make love with her. What's confusing is that after that first step towards letting him back into her life, she goes to the room next door when the newly wed man is alone and Pitt looks through the hole seeing him begin to undress her and bursts in to stop it. The point of her attempted seduction? No clue except to create a rift between the couple. Pitt tries to explain to the angry, broken hearted wife that there was a deeper reason for what his wfe did but his explanation doesn't justify it to me. Jolie tries to come across as moody, depressed but only suceeds in appearing angry and selfish. The owner of the bar/eatery put in the best performance in the movie in his interactions with Pitt and the descriptions of his wife whom he treasured who died earlier.

history.title: 10 Cloverfield Lane
history.text: I gave this three stars rather than fewer only because John Goodman is so superb in this role. The movie? Confusing. He saved the female lead's life from a demolition of the world, or so he tells her, but she wakes chained to the wall in a room that is metal and locked. As he eases up on her restrictions, along with a man who worked for him, also there, she discovers a 'help me', written in bloody fingernaild, facing out for someone to read, behind a window cover along with an earing. The earing is on the ear of a photo of a young woman John Goodman has identified as his daughter but his former worker tell her, no, it was a picture of a neighbor who disappeared two years earlier. Everything points to this being a hoax, a trap. In the last ten minutes of the movie everything turns around. I found the ending disappoimting and inconsistent with the rabid, murderous character John Goodman plays (yes, he kills the former worker for stealing scissors to make a weapon). Given more believable foreshadowing or a different ending, this could have been great.

history.title: Total Recall
history.text: I had loved the original Total Recall so looked forward to the remake. What a disappointment. All of the interesting parts of the plot had been removed to make this into a pure action movie with only a thin thread of a plot. Even the ending was compromised by just more pure action with no satisfying plot closure. If you love speed chases and a lot of fighting and killing and need nothing much more, then this movie is for you. It wasn't for me.

history.review_title: Not a charming film but well acted especially by Daniels and Eisenberg. Not fun to watch people wreck their own lives.
history.text: We might learn more about the early life of writer director Noah Baumbach by watching this semi-autobiographical film than we are comfortable with. The characters that he creates -or perhaps remembers- each have interesting quirks but the adults are not attractive personalities and the two sons are harried and damaged to various degrees. Baumbach did get an Oscar nomination for writing the screenplay. The writing is good but the subject simply does not reward us. I watched it only for the acting. Jeff Daniels builds his character of the brilliant author dad bit by bit until we know him quite well and hate him. Simply put, he is an xxx hole. Laura Linney has less screen time as the mom, also an accomplished writer. Her character also has such flaws that we cannot root for her either. Jesse Eisenberg is very very good as the teen age older son, suffering through adolescence while trying to cope with the flayed marriage of his parents. I only watched this movie to see his earlier work, before he became a star. He handles his task well and we can feel some sympathy for his character. William Baldwin and Anna Paquin play lessor roles. Set in Baumbach's home town of Brooklyn NY the film resides in 1986, apparently his teen years. Baumbach also wrote The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou, which some might have seen.

history.title: Ghost in the Shell (2017)
history.review_title: Fast action, serious subject submerged under shoot'um up story, visual delight.
history.text: Ghost in the Shell Part Robocop, part Frankenstein and part Avatar, Ghost in the Shell, a remake of the 1995 Japanese Aname' animated feature, comes at us hard as a 100% rock'em sock'em no holds bared action flick that totally delivers. This $110 million production delights the eye while providing the kind of action thrills that we yearn for. Poor Major, Scarlett Johansson's character, has nothing left of her physical self save for her brain, neatly tucked into a manufactured body by a nefarious defense company in Japan as a new kind of weapon. Things like this never turn out well. Director Rupert Sanders has managed only one other feature film, the quite acceptable and successful Snow White and the Huntsman. Here he brings the most intensely imagined future city spaces since the incomparable Blade Runner. He scatters giant hologram advertisements around his Tokyo to confuse and mesmerize our eyeballs while at the same time rushing us through the non-stop action. For a particular and fortunately very large slice of the movie going public, this kind of flick brings us rushing into the theater. This make the third time Johansson has appeared as a somewhat more than human heroine after the recent Lucy and her continuing roles as The Black Widow in the Marvel films. She has the backing of not famous but skilled actors, including Michael Pitt, lately of Boardwalk Empire. The writing delivers a double surprise, first this movie satisfies us in all respects even if it comes from a Japanese comic book, not a promising lineage. Second, four writers have their names in the credits, often a bad sign. But this time we get just enough of a back story, slowly revealed to us, about the central character, to keep us interested in her fate. Once again the tiny movie lion, New Zealand, provides the place where the film came to be made. A very great deal of the frames in the film are done with movie magic. The vast invented city in all of its complexity could only exist in a computer. It doe look real, it surely does. Ghost in the Shell runs for a solid two hours and carries a mild PG-13. The non-stop mayhem results if a fair body count but no slow motion blood and guts shots like some films. No language or nudity problems arise. I liked Ghost in the a Shell lot better than Lucy. Lucy did very very well at the box office. Ghost in the Shell is a much better film and I expect it to gather a giant audience.

history.review_title: A very worthy film crushed by a sub par ending.
history.text: Life What could be scarier than to be trapped in a tiny space station with some horrible space monster? What could be more fun than to see amazing space pictures flow across the screen? How did the director get all those actors to float around in the space station, seemingly with no gravity? How does the movie come together to please us? Keep reading. Born in Sweden and never mind his name: Director Daniel Espinosa comes with a couple of very solid movies to his credit. He directed Safe House with Daniel Washington, an absolute knock out in the suspense/action genre. He also directed Child 44, a tight as a fiddle tale set in contemporary Russia. Espinosa knows how to keep us on edge. The writing team of Rett Reese and Paul Wernick have worked with each other numerous times before. The co-wrote Zombielandd, arguably the best Zombie film of all time and a great success commercially. They also penned Deadpool, the stupendously successful and vastly entertaining comic book super hero flick. These writers have mastered the art of the quip. The film has two strong male stars to anchor our attention. Jake Gylienhall and Ryan Renolds (Deadpool) are two of the astronauts in the orbiting space station. They are supported by Rebecca Ferguson, also born in Sweden. The busy Ferguson has three films in release in 2017. In a space/horror flick the actors are not heavily taxed in the drama department and all turn in credible efforts. The film has a lot going for it. Espinosa has a keen eye for faces in his camera lens and the space shots are awesome. The monster is creepy and pretty terrifying, so that's good too. But ultimately the film fails to please. In a recent space epic, Gravity, an astronaut sacrifices himself to save another astronaut. In Life, a whole series of astronauts make heroic sacrifices to save not just their crew mates, but at the end the entire human race. We don't like it when heroism of the highest caliber goes for naught. It makes great courage and great character seem pointless and the entire human experience a futile and nihilistic pursuit. Phooey. Cinematography and clever direction cannot overcome a terrible ending. Life runs for one hour and 43 minutes. It carries a strong 'R' rating for the usual language reasons, but not for naked people. They made this space/horror movie for a fairly modest $58 million and it will do reasonably well and never mind the lack of logic and cheap ending. Just relax and watch the action. Two saw blades.

history.review_title: Instantly forgettable summer filler brightened by some very good acting by Pena and Shepard.
history.text: I watched this at the theater. Chips Actor Dax Shepard will seem familiar to TV viewers. He has appeared in a long line of home screen shows. I had no idea that he also wrote screen plays and directed films. Well, he writes his first big screen big movie with "Chips" and ditto with his screen play. But to write, direct and star in a $25 million Hollywood revival of a classic TV series must be a real thrill for him. Co-star Michael Pena can do anything from very serious drama ("World Trade Center") to a brilliant comic role in "Ant Man" that made that otherwise so so film more interesting for me. He as an astonishing 84 acting credits. Other notable actors include Kristen Bell (wife of Director Dax Shepard) in a smaller supporting role and Jessica McNamee (many TV credits) also in support. I loved Vincent D'Onofrio in his role as a mountain man in the recent "Magnificant Seven". Also appearing are Adam Brody and Ben Falcone in cameos, both solid actors and familiar faces. Jane Kuczmarek who played the mom in "Malcome in the Middle" also serves. Fans will want to watch closely for a quick take of Erik Estrada who played Pena's character in the 1977-1983 TV show. This forgettable, hot weather entertainment tries to break some new comedic ground with a recurring sexual reference joke that didn't break a laugh on the first try. Set in LA, the stream of homophobia jokes also seem flat. What excellence writer/director Dax Shepard gives to the audience comes from discrete moments-many of them as it happens-of very nice bits between actor Dax Shepard and his co-star Michael Pena. Dax plays an earnest (LA style earnest) but dim Mr. Nice against Pena's hard driving FBI man with some character quirks. The not convincing story provides a place to put sight gags and jokes in bad taste-but not any more than that. The Motion Picture Association of America quite rightly awarded "Chips" a hard R rating. The film includes frequent objectionable language issues of the worst kind. Not content with drug use, booze and cigarettes the film has total nudity and many examples of lesser degrees of nakedness. Watch out for some graphic injuries also. Please leave the wee ones at home. The film lasts for one hour and 40 minutes. So far "Chips" has brought $25 million to the box office. Pena and Shepard can only bring the movie to an average three saw blades.

history.review_title: Not much here except plenty of naked and half naked girls.
history.text: Director Sean Ellis made a clever little short. He picked up an Academy Award nomination for best short film. Then he expanded the short into an hour and a half feature film. This version is the result. Ellis reportedly made the expansion in a single week. After seeing the film, I believe it. Lots of naked girls make Cashback interesting. The central character, an art student who suffers insomnia, cannot carry the film alone. Ellis gives him the ability to stop time. The artist uses the time stoppage to disrobe customers in his grocery store and sketch them. All the while he morns his breakup with his girlfriend. It makes pretty thin soup. Ellis does have a good eye with his camera and the cast does well with what they are given.

history.review_title: Truly outstanding Zombie movie from Korea.
history.text: I have watched loads of Zombie flicks, some made in out of the way places (please see my book of Zombie movie reviews "A Gross of Zombies _144 reviews of Zombie movies) but never a Korean Zombie flick. Holy smokes, this one has every thing you want in a Zombie movie and more. What we want is good production values-this one is professional level, even if not as slick as Hollywood's best efforts. We want it to be scary (or sometimes to be funny but scary fits here). Imagine being trapped on a train as a Zombie Apocalypse begins. Our protagonists are faced with increasing numbers of Zombies and fight and flee from car to car. It is terrifying. Why? Because director Yeon Sang-ho carefully took the time to introduce us to the characters before feeding them to the un-dead. The main guy is some kind of fund manager, a guy whose marriage has failed because of his devotion to his work. In an early, situation setting scene, he gives his daughter a Wii game system, only to discover that he had given her one previously, on children's day. So, distant dad takes his little daughter on the Train to Busan so she can spend time with divorced mom. We get not just a rip roaring Zombie flick but a good dose of social commentary as well. The young Korean girls are adorable, totally cute. When they turn you can hear hearts breaking in the darkness. We have examples of genuine heroism and genuine swinish selfishness. Korea is a largely Christian country so we are shown people exhibiting the best kind of Christian virtue-laying down one's life for a friend sort of stuff. And because it is an Asian country, we see Karmic Justice dealt out with satisfying rapidity. The Zombies themselves are jerky but and clumsy but fast. People do have some chance to survive. I always like it when there is an avenue to survival for the characters. Some of the Zombie scenes are very well set up and well imagined. These people really thought about every scene and it pays off for the watchers. This was the 6th highest grossing (hee hee) movie in Korean cinema history. Even with subtitles rotten tomatoes gave it a stellar 97% which is huge. It runs for just shy of two hours and has an R rating. This is one of the very best Zombie movies ever made.

history.review_title: Low grade shoot um up, great cast wasted by terrible script.
history.text: Even the stellar cast cannot save this repetitive offering. They took the standard Jason Statham movie and wrung out any of the things that make his best work interesting, fun and even exciting to watch. The all important connections were just left out and what we have left is a long series of well staged fight scenes. He shoots lots and lots of bad guys but the bad guys might have just as well have been clay pots for all the excitement they generated. The Plot was very thin to start with and by the end slipped off into a parody of a lessor Bond film. Jessica Alba, totally cute, had no chemistry with her co-star. But what do I know? The public lapped it up and made it into a very profitable project.
