history.title: Ghost in the Shell (2017)
history.review_title: Pretty but very flawed - stick with the original
history.text: This really deserves about 2.5 stars. It has an exciting and pretty visual style, and the nods to the original piece (like a remix of Kusanagi's underwater scene, Bateau's eyes, and opening music that is inspired by but different from the original theme) are intriguing and usually clever. Clearly the makers of this movie had a liking of and respect for the original. I'm not sure what went wrong. On to the flaws - the dialog is weird, the acting is off, the cinematography is all over the place, the plot doesn't make a lot of sense, the motives are inconsistent, the main character's body is kind of silly (why does she have no feeling of touch, why is she vulnerable to electric shock if she is a combat model), the main character is subdued much of the time so Scarlett Johansson has little to work with, and there's manufactured drama because reasons. Also, they kinda dropped the ball on the scene with the spider tank. It's not terrible, but it's not very impressive compared to its anime counterpart. It moves stiffly and slowly, can't turn invisible, and has a boxier design. Also, the cinematography does it no favors - it is a dark color on a dark background, engages the characters at night in a dark place, and the camera angles are often wrong to view it properly. It takes real derpiness to mess up a concept as cool as a *expletive* SPIDER TANK, but there you are. Also, since they flubbed the chance to introduce the concept of HV rounds, there's really no explanation for how Major (yeah, that's apparently her name as well as her rank in this one...because reasons) manages to overcome the tank. The movie isn't entirely without merit - you can see they really liked the original, and weren't just trying to cash in on something popular; the nods to the source material are, like I said, intriguing; it is fun to see how they insert elements without just copying them, and they mostly manage this without spoiling the effect, kind of like a nifty remix of a favorite song. The visual style is also fun, and the core concept is workable. Unfortunately, this isn't really enough to make up for the flaws I mentioned earlier. The only reason I watched all the way to the end was to see the spider tank, and you heard how that turned out. Overall, I'd say skip this one, unless you've already seen the original and are willing to sit through a two-hour movie just to see the little homages I mentioned. I think they are well-done, but not worth the time it takes to see them all.

This is a really fun movie. I didn't know what to expect going into it, but it turned out to be a great ride, and the climax was really intense. The concept is also intriguing. The underlying cause is a little out there, but whatever, it's a film with a giant monster in, what do you want? Just to be clear, it's not really ABOUT the monster; if you come into this looking for a monster movie, you'll be a bit disappointed. The creature isn't onscreen much, but that's OK - it's really a motivator for the human characters, and unlike some OTHER movies I could name, that works out pretty well. The characters were interesting, the acting was great, the twists were surprising but there was a groundwork for them so they never came out of nowhere. Also, the special effects were good - I never felt like the monster wasn't in the scene it was part of, which can happen when doing that kind of shot. All in all, a fun film.

history.review_title: Hold onto your butts - the ride only gets more intense from here on
history.text: Hold onto your butts (old Jurassic Park reference is old) - this is where stuff gets real. This season is intense, and a lot darker than previous iterations, so if you've got younger viewers in your house, you might want to proceed with caution - at least one major character is confirmed to be straight-up, no-backsies dead-fo-sho and at least one other character's life/death status is kind of left hanging if you think about it for a second. I feel like this jumps from G to PG, if the previous season didn't already do that, but it doesn't feel needlessly dark, like some other properties that are just turning all serious so they can seem edgy and relevant (and marketable). The sad bits are sad, the funny bits are funny, and the climax of the current story arc is IN-TENSE! I can't wait to see where they take things next; I am excited. This show has really grown, and refused to yield to the tiresome "status-quo is god" trope that so many shows fall prey to.

history.review_title: I couldn't stand it long enough for a single episode, but your mileage may vary
history.text: Your mileage may vary, but I found the main character irritating and I couldn't put up with his constant, over-dramatic narration of things that didn't need narrating (at one point, we see something through a window, and then his inner monologue TELLS us what we JUST. GOT. DONE. SEEING. This is a TV show, not a podcast). I'm not this show's target audience, for sure, but I feel like it doesn't give its actual audience much credit, what with the predictable plot line and constant narration of the obvious (and no, I don't think it's suitable for children young enough to need simple scenes explained to them). Everybody's different though - if you think this one is great and the kid is charming, who am I to argue?

history.review_title: A bit silly and not very scary, but I had fun and so might you - lots of gore, so be warned
history.text: This movie was a little silly, and not very scary, but it was a fun (in a horror movie sort of way) watch all the same, and it had some interesting concepts. I may be biased, though, because the movie featured a favorite actress of mine from Stargate Atlantis and another I liked in Stargate Universe. The effects were good enough that I was never taken out of the movie, the acting was good, and like I said, the story was fun. The collision of supernatural and scientific tropes was a little jarring (if it can't be killed by bullets, it can't be killed by drugs - magic problems require magic solutions, guys) and the theology is a bit unclear, but I was having a good time and prepared to overlook that. Also, apropos of nothing: Torri Higginson is still a stone fox as well as a talented actress ;)

history.review_title: Breathtakingly stupid garbage, and a sequel to Prometheus, just to rub salt in the wound
history.text: I didn't have high hopes for this one after Prometheus was excreted into our collective face, but I tried to keep an open mind, since I'd heard it was a replacement for Prometheus rather than a sequel. Turns out that was just a filthy lie or wishful thinking. Things took a turn when I saw Micheal Fassbender reprising his role as David, because the movie loves to 'explore' philosophical concepts with him in the same way a runaway bulldozer "explores" an art museum, only with more damage and less subtlety. I hung in there though. In the end, it wasn't even my loathing for Prometheus that made me stop watching - it was the bland, stupid characters and their blaring disregard for common sense or training. The last straw was when a character orders a ship full of hibernating colonists suicidally close to a storm system, not to rescue people (he can't because this colony ship only has one shuttle for all umpteen thousand people and their supplies) but to maybe, MAYBE get better reception on a report about his wife. I just couldn't relate to that kind of blind stupidity, and I stopped. I've since learned that it gets even worse. I won't go so far as to say this movie shouldn't exist, but it's an even bigger load of crap than the one before it, and if you watch it, you have nobody to blame but yourself. It does look nice, but if that was all I wanted, I'd buy some artwork.

history.review_title: Boring and bland - shouldn't exist, but makes no real impact on the world
history.text: This movie isn't terrible, but it's not very interesting or engaging either. The characters are all very bland and forgettable, the mummy has no real presence or gravitas, and the plot is dull and predictable. I only finished watching this movie because it made decent background noise for other stuff I was doing. This movie really shouldn't exist - the best thing I can say about it is "it made me want to learn more about mercury and its use in ancient times". Like I said, not terrible, but that's a pretty low bar. If you want a mummy movie, see the Brendan Fraser vehicle instead; it's campier, but has more impressive visual effects, memorable characters, funny moments, and action sequences you're actually INVESTED in. Plus, it's fun.

history.review_title: Clever minimalist movie well worth watching
history.text: This was a very entertaining and engrossing film with some clever ideas and good characters. A word of warning - it's kind of a bittersweet film too; I wouldn't recommend watching it in an emotionally fragile state, but otherwise, it's a great ride.

history.review_title: Hits all the right notes - a fun movie with genuine feeling, not too serious, but not too silly either
history.text: This movie has great acting, good special effects, a good plot that strikes the right balance between over-the-top fun and serious stakes, and a beautiful color palette. I love the armor of the Nameless order. It is a nice touch that the Western stuff is all colourless and dull while the Eastern stuff is all bright and vibrant; it subtly underscores how unrefined and unprincipled the two strangers are, and could be a nod to how their lives are empty with no higher purpose to devote themselves to and no desire to pursue such a thing. That's just my speculation, however - the movie certainly isn't heavy-handed with symbolism or anything. The battle scenes did get a /bit/ silly in parts, but it was always in keeping with the over-the-top action tone - this is a legend, after all, and those tend to feature aspects that stretch the bounds of belief. Overall, a great movie, and very fun.

history.review_title: Huge, boring, weird waste of time (with bizarrely good FX in places)
history.text: First, full disclosure: I couldn't watch all of this - it was just too dull and weird. I started watching in real-time, then skipping boring bits, then jumping ahead to find anything good, then skipped to the end hoping for something interesting there. This movie is supposed to be about killer rabbits, but the bulk of it is poorly acted human-human subplots too badly written for daytime soap opera. Most of it is boring, and what isn't boring is too weird to be relatable (e.g. the guy who stores pee in jugs). The actual rabbit attacks are few, far between, and quickly get repetitive. The rabbits themselves are neither scary nor funny, and it is never clear whether the movie is making fun of itself or not, so it's not very fun to watch. The whole movie lacked energy, there was zero investment in the plot, and few of the actors seemed to be having any fun, so it was just a bummer overall. Some movies are so bad they are good - this is not one of those. There is ONE thing that might make this movie worth skimming: some of the FX are as bad as you'd expect for a film this poor, but a lot of them are bizarrely good, and some of them are a perplexing mix of the two. The best examples of this are the aliens and the rabbits. The rabbits don't look exactly real, but they move really smoothly and naturally, and their bodies and fur are so painstakingly rendered they wouldn't look out of place in Monsters Inc. or Golden Compass - they are that high-quality. However, this incredible work of CGI is then lazily super-imposed on the practical scenery with only token effort to match lighting and zero attempt to make the real objects react to the rabbits' presence (e.g. no bent grass under them, no shadows, no dust raised when they hop). Weird. Likewise, the aliens feature convicingly lively CGI eyes laid over the sort of high-end prosthetic masks that need hours to put on or take off...and then the mouths are almost completely static and come complete with random movements of a lazily superimposed CGI tongue. I...I literally can't even. The weird mashup of impressive and laughable could be down to which effects were carefully done at the beginning and which ones had to be hastily thrown in to meet the deadline (or before the money ran out), but even so, who blows Pixar-level animation cash on a movie with zero acting or writing budget? Additional note: early on, we find out this is a Mars-needs-women scenario (google it), which some of us might find titilating, so let me save you some time - it's about as bad as it could be. The women aren't so much impregnated as infested, with finger-like bulges crawling under their abdominal skin, and it all ends in a lot of screaming and blood. If I cared, I might wonder why those aliens were so hot to use females, since they don't seem to need the womb or the vagina for anything.

history.title: Paul McCartney - Wingspan - An Intimate Portrait [DVD]
history.review_title: Paul again gives short shrift to Wings
history.text: Like the CD collection "Wingspan," Paul is again treating Wings the group with little respect. This documentary is far from being the definitive retrospective on Wings, and it would be more properly titled "Linda McCartney's Life with Paul, Vol. 1 1967-1980." The focus is relentlessly on Linda and her life with Paul, while the contributions of the other members of Wings (which was ever-changing save Denny Laine, who was there from beginning to end) are largely overlooked. There are some nice clips, but the focus never seems to settle on the group and their music for very long before veering back to the McCartney's domestic life. The documentary is steered along by a present-day "interview" of Paul by daughter Mary McCartney, supplemented by lots of audio clips of Linda. The bonus song promo clips are nice, but I would have been happier with a complete collection of Wings promo clips. This sort of documentary pales in comparison to more objective work like the "The Beatles Anthology" and even "John Lennon: Imagine." I hate to say it, but I wish Paul would have done the Wings retrospective before Linda died. Or let someone else make it.

history.title: Conquest of Space (Widescreen) [DVD]
history.review_title: See one of the inspirations for "2001"
history.text: For me this was the great unseen film that I had seen stills from since childhood. After avoiding the VHS tape I had heard so many bad things about, I got the DVD the day it went on sale. I had heard that this was one of the many many science fiction films Stanley Kubrick watched with Arthur C. Clarke during preproduction of "2001: A Space Odyssey," but I was unprepared for some eerie similarities that I cannot write off as mere coincidence. "Conquest of Space" is a film in which a civilian scientist arrives by transport on a wheel-shaped space station orbiting Earth, astronauts watch TV from Earth and watch one-way messages from their loved ones, a spacecraft's mission is prepared in secrecy and its destination changed just before launch, an astronaut is killed while making a repair to a spacecraft antenna and his body must be retrieved, and the crewmember in charge of a space mission goes insane and tries to kill other crew and sabotage the mission... ...and this was in 1955, not 1968. But I don't want to build this up too much for those of you unaccustomed to 1950's science fiction movies. This isn't as good as "Forbidden Planet," but if you've enjoyed George Pal's other '50's films such as "Destination Moon," "War of the Worlds," and "When Worlds Collide," then you will probably see a great deal of the charm in this admittedly lesser though perhaps more ambitious work.

history.title: Apollo 13 [DVD]
history.text: I am rating this four rather than five stars just because I think Universal is overhyping an inferior reissue that they easily could have gotten right. They have upgraded the picture quality (which *could* make the upgrade worth it if you've got a really big screen), but it's shameful that they did not include the DTS soundtrack as an option with the normal version (it was previously available as a stand-alone DVD). The only new extras are two documentaries about the space program and Apollo 13 itself (there are enough of those documentaries already out there for any Apollo fan) and the IMAX version of the film--with a DTS soundtrack option! The IMAX version is stupendous when seen in an IMAX theater, but to present this edited version (made before IMAX upgraded their film platters to accomodate longer theatrical release conversions) on a DVD makes little sense other than as a throwaway extra. I saw "Apollo 13" at least seven times during its original theatrical release and three times in IMAX. The original Dolby Digital DVD was the first DVD I bought. Back then they issued a separate DTS DVD which I never found in a store, and some people said it lacked some or all of the bonus features so I had not been willing to buy it online just for the superior sound--hey, this was back when Universal SE DVDs were priced at about twice what they are now. As many separate DD/DTS DVDs were reissued with both soundtracks, I was sure "Apollo 13" would so I never bothered to pick up the DTS version. Looks like I'll have to wait for the HD release for them to fix this glaring oversight--or now go find the out-of-print DTS version....

history.title: Desk Set
history.review_title: For Those Curious About the Commentary--Don't Bother
history.text: A great movie, a so-so DVD transfer, and as for the commentary: Neva Patterson recites background info on every actor as they each make their entrance, along with a few other items that are less than what one could find on IMDB, while Dina Merrill gives us lots of Dina Merrill anecdotes about just about every film she was in except "Desk Set." Not a very good commentary for "Desk Set." I could just live with the Prime HD stream.

history.title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
history.review_title: JJ Really Wanted To Do A Reboot
history.text: After all this, after all the years and talk and discussion, what we actually get is just a thinly-disguised reboot done as an ersatz sequel. I was frankly dumbstruck at how the opening so closely followed the original "Star Wars." For those who have seen the YouTube video that shows "Star Wars" alongside all the classic films that influenced it, you could take "The Force Awakens" and show it alongside all the scenes it lifts from preceding films. Oh, yeah, maybe it follows "633 Squadron" more than the original "Star Wars" does, but that's perhaps the only exception. I can't believe all this time was wasted on something so clearly derivative of the preceding films. One of my complaints about "Return of the Jedi" was that it was clear George Lucas wanted to remake the ending of "Star Wars," but, geez, JJ, what were you and Lawrence Kasdan thinking during all your long walks composing the screenplay? Was that all just to come up with Han Solo's lines?

history.review_title: Really Nice HD Transfer From Amazon Video
history.text: Not my favorite movie, but if you're a Bogie fan and want to see this, forget about which DVD to get and just buy the Amazon Video HD version. You will not be disappointed in the quality--clean transfer, correct early 2.55:1 CinemaScope, good sound. Nice job, Fox!

history.review_title: The Man Behind the Iconic Images
history.text: A very enlightening documentary on the career of a premier architecture photographer, who worked extensively with Frank Lloyd Wright, Alexander Calder, and Louise Nevelson. I had no idea how much his vision influenced how I perceive these three great artists.

history.title: Johnny Cool
history.text: What a weird little movie, not great, not flashy, but a lot of great character actors, and the editing and script seem to know exactly what they're trying to do and no more or no less. I liked that there was a lot left unsaid and unexplained, because it didn't need to be, which so many people seem to miss with movies like this. And what an ending. Nice to see a young Elizabeth Montgomery playing an ingenue. It's mediocre, but head and shoulders above a Roger Corman film, and enjoyable as a curiosity. I completely understand both sides of the reviews here where some hate it and some love it--if it sounds interesting to you, then you will probably like it.

history.review_title: Don Johnson: Master of the Reaction Shot
history.text: This isn't a great movie, but it is an interesting (mostly) true story that I was not familiar with. Don Johnson gives one of his better performances--and it's all in his reaction shots. If you dig that, then you'll like it.

history.review_title: Precise Artifice Achieved, But It Doesn't Hold Together
history.text: It's another one of those Coen Brothers movies where they seem to take their eye off the whole in sacrifice of achieving a series of Rube Goldberg-like setups and scenes. Taken individually they're fun, but it doesn't really add up to a fully realized piece as in their best work. Jennifer Jason Leigh channels Katharine Hepburn-cum-Rosalind Russell throughout, and she's a hoot.

Kirk Douglas's casting as the title character is undoubtedly one of the finest examples of "type casting" in the history of Hollywood, but the true star of this film is Kirk's horse who dominated, and stole the movie with a magnificent performance worthy of an "Oscar".That he did not win one is more evidence of the politics and political correctness involved in these awards.

history.title: The Dead Room [Blu-ray]
history.text: There are ultimately no surprises here - we've seen the paranormal investigators gig before, and none of the plot developments are new - but this is nonetheless a reasonably decent haunted house story. Highlights include a cast of competent actors, and the unusual element of their being only three characters in the entire movie. use of sound effects is also effective, and the fact that the filmmakers made the very intelligent choice to NOT go with the found footage/first person recording format, which the first Blair Witch did well and none of those who have since turned it into a cliche have done effectively. Note: some web reviews have complained that Dead Room leaves too much unexplained. No. This would only be true for those who are really unfamiliar with ghost stories or ghost flicks. Dead Room doesn't explain or show everything precisely because the filmmakers knew that most viewers would be familiar with ghost story tropes. Their bothering to offer all kinds of exposition would be like a new vampire movie wasting time explaining that vampires don't like crucifixes and the way to kill one is putting a stake through its heart. Why both when everyone watching already knows? The movie shows the viewer everything they need to know. Expecting further explanations is missing the point. So: if you like ghost flicks, you might want to rent this (I don't think it's worth buying). It does not compare to the original version of The Haunting, or other more contemporary ones like Darkness Falls, but it's worth a look.

history.title: Midnight Run
history.review_title: Still hilarious decades later, has held up well over ...
history.text: Still hilarious decades later, has held up well over time. Much more character development than most action movies, handled with enough deftness to not bog down the comedy or action. Lots and lots and lots of f-bombs, but all the cursing is spoken with such effective peevishness and relish that it becomes part of the movie's comedic tapestry.

history.title: The Great Wall [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Best action fantasy movie since Lord of the Rings
history.text: Above-average action movie dialogue, even a bit of character development, and very solid chemistry among all of the actors. Others have commented on the special effects. Some of the CG is a little soft, but the effects are indeed very, very good, and coupled with the production design and cinematography, they contribute to a rich, beautiful tapestry, exploding with colors. The film obviously owes a lot to the Lord of the Rings trilogy, and yet even though a lot of the action and battle sequences seem familiar, the creative team none-the-less manages to distinguish them from LOTR's. In addition, while the score certainly cannot hold a candle to the LOTR's, it is nonetheless a wonderfully effective epic score, and adds an important element to the film. One final note: it is really nice to see an action movie that does not waste time on a two-dimensional romantic subplot. Men and women are complete equals in this film, and to the extent that there is a gender plot, it emphasizes men and women working alongside each other for a common goal, with mutual trust and respect.

A fun, suspenseful ride. The acting is sometimes over the top, characters make dumb choices on a few occasions, some of the action toward the end is too by the numbers, and some of the stylistics, makeup FX, and set pieces toward the end too derivative of Hellraiser and Jacob's Ladder. That said, still a solid 3 star movie for fans of Lovecraft and Clive Barker. One final point: some have complained that the very ending is too oblique, or asked "What the heck is 'the void' anyway"? The answers to these questions will be readily apparent to anyone paying attention, and certainly to anyone who understands the worlds Lovecraft, Barker, and Carpenter (a la In the Mouth of Madness). The final shot of the movie is a superb coda to what comes before.

I generally dislike faux documentaries, and, with the exception of the original Blair Witch, I despise found footage or similar movies; but this one is simply superb. Savageland is cleverly written, masterfully edited, and if you didn't know better it would be a while into it before you'd realize it wasn't a real documentary. It uses genuine documentary techniques, and key roles are played by people who actually function in the given capacity in real life (e.g., a real life reporter plays the reporter, a professional photographer plays a photographer consulted for the purposes of discussing the role of photos that are at the heart of the "documentary," and so on. The tone of Savageland is creepiness, more than straight out horror, per se, which is a good thing. There's also a compelling but not overpowering social commentary dimension that is so cleverly woven into the form and content of the movie that it does not detract from the creepiness or horror. On the contrary, this aspect enhances the creep factor because it is so true to life. Horror is perfectly fine as horror, and I do not believe films that don't convey some kind of "message" are somehow less valuable than other movies. However, this film does provide an excellent example of how horror cinema can be filled with meaning or used to convey a message, and do so while still fulfilling the other imperatives of the genre; that is to say, providing creepy, compelling entertainment.

history.title: Jigoku (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.review_title: Worth watching at least once for fans of Japanese horror
history.text: While acknowledging the historical importance of this film, and it's apparent impact on subsequent, modern Japanese horror directors, it does not stand up as well as the Ghost of Yatsuya and Kwaidan. In the first half we see the sins and debauchery, and the second half we see various depictions of hell. It all seems more symbolic and allegorical than anything. It is horrific, but not scary or creepy, so don't go into it expecting the latter. Nonetheless, it's an interesting movie, even if not as interesting, entertaining, are beautiful to look at as the other two I've mentioned above. It's most redeeming quality consists of the wonderful sets and use of color in the second half or so. That alone makes it worth a look, not to mention the interesting aspect of seeing what many consider to be the precursor of modern Japanese horror cinema. Any aficionado of J-horror or Asian horror in general really should check Jigoku out at least once.

history.title: The Plague of the Zombies [DVD]
history.text: This movie is not only plagued with zombies, but lifeless production values and an anemic script. I do not say this lightly, as I am a fan of many Hammer horror movies. The Mummy, (The Horror of) Dracula, Brides of Dracula, Quatermass and the Pit: these are great horror and Sci-Fi movies. Plague of the Zombies simply doesn't measure up. Here are some reasons: Much of the film is supposed to take place at night, but the cinematography is truly abysmal; it's filmed day for night, and it shows. It is perfectly obvious the characters are walking around in slightly filtered sunshine instead of under "the full moon," as one of them claims. In some scenes blue, daylight sky is seen behind characters when it is supposed to be the middle of the night. Not only does this simply look cheap, but it utterly saps the scenes of any creepiness. An inexpensive filter over the lens would have improved things greatly, so even the low budget isn't an excuse. The makeup is cheap-looking, too. In a number of shots you can see that the zombie makeup essentially ends at the bottom of the jaw line, when it would have cost mere tuppence to bring it below the collarbone so the entire person would look zombified, not just the head. Even the Bernard Herrmann score is uninspired. The movie's only redeeming quality is Andre Morrell, who is very good, except in the climactic scenes, in which poor scriptimg has him acting like kind of an imbecile. The final nail in the coffin is the actor who plays his protege, whose name I will not even bother looking up for the sake of this review, who has absolutely no screen presence, and, it would seem, little capacity for acting. If you're familiar with Hammer movies, generally like them, and haven't seen this one, you're probably going to watch this anyway. If you're new to Hammer, start with the other ones I've listed above and introduce yourself to the studio by way of some of its greatest moments.

history.title: Ghost Train [DVD]
history.text: Friendship melodrama is not uncommon to J-horror, but is more tedious than usual in this movie. There is also little internal logic, as the movie seems to establish certain rules for itself, but then tosses them out toward the end. The climactic moments are kind of cool, but ultimately make no sense because they occur at the height of said breakdown of narrative logic. Additionally, and as an extension of the problems with the friendship melodrama, the movie frequently comes to a grinding halt with additionally tedious scenes that are extended well beyond what is necessary for providing information about the story, or what is effective for building suspense. I've seen worse, but Ghost Train is at the bottom of the heap insofar as J- and other Asian horror.

history.title: Blade Runner 2049 (Blu-ray) (BD)
history.text: A few editing missteps toward the end don't prevent BR49 from being a solid 5 star movie. Even those who have not seen BR19 will find much to enjoy in the top tier acting, beautiful vistas, affecting score, and compelling story. I've also checked with some who weren't enamoured of the first film but who ended up enjoying the sequel. As you can tell from the fan reviews, most who love BR19 also love BR49. Now we just have to hope they don't go minimalist on Blue-ray bonus features. Update: Well, they went minimalist on bonus features. This movie deserved so much more in its Blu-ray release. What is here is very good {comma} insofar as some brief documentaries and the web shorts released prior to the film itself. They're just is not much of it.

history.title: Snowbeast - Digitally Remastered
history.review_title: Worth a look if you like 1970s made-for-tv horror
history.text: Silly, fun made-for-tv 1970s horror. In no way shape or form on par with classics like Don't Be Afraid of the Dark and The Night Stalker, or even the lesser-known but still fun Horror at 30,000 Feet; but if you grew up in that eara and had a fondness for these movies as a kid, and/or understand and appreciate the 1970s made-for-tv horror sensibility, you might find it a worthy way to spend an hour and a half, especially if you have some laundry to fold, or something, while watching.

history.review_title: Rob Zombie’s Halloween tries too hard and ends up terrible!
history.text: The film cannot hold a candle to John Carpenters original movie. It seems to me that the remake is trying too hard to be scary causing a reverse effect. For one thing Michael Myers is much scarier as a normal sized male 6ft and skinny, not 6 foot 8, 290 lbs. The blonde kid portraying Michael didn’t look like Andre the giant as a grade schooler, so no way would he grow up to be that big. Having Michael Myers be that huge makes him less scary. Like Frankenstein’s monster people would spot him coming from a mile away. He wouldn’t be able to hide anywhere. It was a problem for Halloween 4 as well having Linebacker Michael is less scary than your average person. The original film’s version of Michael as a child prodigy from a normal average suburban loving home is a much more interesting premise than Michael coming from a white trash family. The original film builds a lot of tension and left a lot of his back-story up to the viewer’s imagination. In the remake Michael is bullied, but not to the tipping point where he would commit homicidal murder. The psychiatric hospital breakout was utterly ridiculous. Since when does Michael Myers have super human strength like Jason Vorhees in the later Friday the 13th movies? That whole scene came off as comical nothing more. Michael kills the guard’s and just happens to slowly walks out of the whole maximum security complex like a Sunday stroll in the park. Another thing about the film that really bothers me is Michael not killing his sister Laurie onsite. Since when would he just gather her up in his arms take her for a stroll around the block, Ludicrous Speed GO!!!!! The Michael Myers from the original would have killed her instantly in a millisecond. The body count is much higher in this film and you never really care about these characters in general. It cheapens death in a way making it feel less final. I think network TV shows are doing this far to often nowadays as well. The original Halloween did not have a lot of blood, guts or gore, it was far more about the suspense with much better storytelling. In this movie the gore is overboard as well once again giving us the opposite effect of scary. I saw this film in the movie theater on its original run and when the movie finished walking out of the theater I thought man that sucked. Now I am a fan of Rob Zombie. I like Rob’s music and saw him in concert a few times and he puts on a great show. I thought House of 1000 Corpses was not bad just a little above average. I hated The Devil’s Rejects and thought it was stupid. So let’s hold the praise for calling Rob Zombie some great director. He is not in the same league as John Carpenter, Wes Craven, Alfred Hitchcock etc etc. I would rate this film 1 to 1 ½ stars. It is definitely not worth your time or money. It does nothing but tarnish the original Halloween’s legacy. Rob needs to learn that sometime less is more when it comes to horror movies. The movie needed more suspense and less outright gore and a normal sized Michael Myers not Kane from the WWE.

history.review_title: “IT” is the best horror movie I have seen in years. The kids and story are worth your time.
history.text: After just seeing the movie in the theater, "IT" is the best horror movie I have seen in a long time. The film is not really that scary but the suspense and creepy factor definitely hit home. The acting and story pacing is excellent. You end up caring about these kids and they all seem realistic and talk and act their age. Richie is hilarious, while the film mostly focuses on Bill and Beverly, all the kids get screen time. I am a sucker for the nostalgia as well. Crazy to think how 1989 was so long ago but to me it feels like last week in a way. The movie definitely gets the psychological terror right, which is much more interesting than a high body count. The film will keep your glued to your seat and that is the sign of a good movie. Pennywise the clown reminded me a lot of Freddy Krueger from the Nightmare on Elm Street series. Because IT terrorizes the children with their worst fears before it kills them. Tenderizes the meat from what I read somewhere. I have not read the book which seems longer than the Holy Bible. I did know a little about the story from the old ABC miniseries. But let’s be honest made for TV movies almost always suck no matter how good the acting by Tim Curry. You can’t get away with anything near an R rated film on network TV. So right off the bat I knew the production was going to be much better. I liked how this film stuck with just 1 of the books focusing on the children’s story and the sequel will follow the kids as adults. Great move by the filmmaker’s part and it’ll pay huge dividends at the box office for them. IT is a recent horror movie worth watching it isn’t 4 hours long, it does have some very chilling moments. The bully’s are all believable Gretta is a real bitch, and the Bower’s kid is just nuts. After awhile I was rooting for IT to find and eat Gretta. Maybe IT does in the sequel? One can always hope right. I was also hoping Ben eventually ends up with Beverly. Excited to see the next film to see what happens next. I read somewhere that the only part of the movie that didn’t seem realistic was the kids bicycles no BMX or 10 speeds. The bikes would have fit more in a 1970’s time period. But besides that slight oversight the film is excellent.

history.title: High Noon
history.review_title: High Noon is a thrilling western with a great cast and a good story but kind of a dull climax.
history.text: High Noon is a classic western movie coming out in the golden age of Hollywood. I recently viewed it on Hulu Classics and thought it was good. It is a pretty basic story of a small town marshal Will Kane on his last day on the job, who gets married and then finds out a man he put behind bars is once again free looking for revenge and coming in on the noon train that day. The characters are all pretty interesting and you can see a lot of different points of view from all the towns’ people. Gary Cooper and the whole cast do an excellent job. With the way the word spread around this tiny western town of the outlaws return in less than an hour’s worth of time you would think everyone had society media like Twitter, Facebook or Instagram back then. The film is good and I liked the feeling of impending dread and fear the townspeople display. The clocks are in nearly every scene in the film as it gets closer to 12 O’clock. The marshal repeatedly fails to get together a pose to take on the outlaws. Eventually abandoned by everyone he takes on 4 outlaws by himself. Now each minute in the film feels like 20 minutes gone by, it is hard to believe the Marshal would have time to get into a fistfight and get fixed up by the local barber, let alone make it to a tavern, a church and several house calls all in the short amount of time before the train arrives. The marshal had maybe an hour tops once he found out the news. I liked how his wife shot one of the bandits and didn’t act like a helpless damsel in distress and actually took matters in her own hands. I would have liked it even more if she would have shot at Frank Miller as he attempted to abduct her leading to the finale. I recognized Lee Van Cleef right away at the beginning and I thought he was the main villain and the train would be coming with more goons or bandits. Another thing that I thought about was how much one of the outlaws was drinking before the shootout, I would of thought the film would have made a point of showing him stumble or bumble his weapon because of all the liquor he drank up til that point but nothing really becomes of it. If anything the only thing I found a bit lacking was the final confrontation with the lead villain Frank Miller. The film seemed to end very abruptly without the Marshal shaming the townsfolk for their cowardice or at least have Will Kane slowly look around at all the people and let them know they were wrong to abandon him during his time of need. That is the only reason why I would not give this 5 stars. Overall I think this is a 4 star film. The plot is good with an interesting cast of characters. The running out of time aspect is well done and you can feel the tension in the air, but ultimately the shootout was not as good as the buildup.

history.title: Blade Runner 2049 (Blu-ray) (BD)
history.review_title: Blade Runner 2049 has an original story, lots of similarities to the first film and leaves a lot up to the viewer’s imagination.
history.text: This is an incredibly deep film like its predecessor. I thought it was a good solid film but not as good as the original movie. You see lots of scenes that are very similar in style and substance. The breaking through the wall, the girl with the frizzy orange/pink hair looking homeless, the Blade Runner getting the hell beat out of him, a main character committing a selfless act of sacrifice etc etc. Similar to the first film, lots of plot lines are left open to the viewer’s imagination. I thought Jared Leto character Wallace was actually a pretty good mastermind villain in the movie and it is a shame we don’t really find out what happens to his character, similar to Tyrell from the first movie but far more ruthless. Luv was also a very good female villain character echoing how difficult it is to kill a combat Replicant like Roy Batty (Rutger Hauer.) Blade Runner is one of those Sci Fi films where the future is not all bright warm and fuzzy. More bleak and full of despair a dystopian future gone bad. The premise from the 1st film is loosely based on the Replicants who were made by man to be slave labor and colonize other planets in the solar system. The whole Blade Runner theme is about a detective unit design and constructed to retire or destroy any rogue Replicants that makes it’s way back to Earth. The new film explores a world where the replicants coexist with humans in just about every manner of life. The new film opens up a lot of new ideas kind of like opening pandora’s box in a way. I thought the scenes with K and Joi were kind of dull and lifeless whereas I think the relationship with Mariette the pleasure replicant could have been very intriguing. What if agent K happened to get her pregnant how deep would that rabbit hole go and could a cool sequel be made out of that movie? A lot can be made out of a hologram wanting a host body to make love to a non human. I rather like the idea of Rachel having twins and thought that could have been very unique as well. Alas these are just ideas the film does not really explore. If anything the film is not as strong as the original movie because there wasn’t a group of Replicants to chase after and hunt down. In this film there is only 1 Replicant K retires. You never get the feeling that he is tracking a group of outlaw Replicants returning to Earth seeking more life like the Nexus 8’s from the original movie, which seemed like a noble cause. I always imagined the Replicants working in space like the Sean Connery movie “Outland”, and in many ways like the movie “Logan’s Run” but Blade Runners instead of Sandmen, both Sci Fi films that have mild similarities to Blade Runner but not as deep plots more straightforward. Blade Runner 2049 doesn’t really touch on either of those subjects. We don’t see any of the Replicants in space or the hunting down of the rogue Replicants. I also thought K would have found Deckard much earlier in the movie instead of the last 3rd of the film. So much time seemed to be devoted to Joi and K’s relationship it seemed to hurt the rest of the movie. Although robot sex might be interesting it is not the reason I came to see this movie. I was expecting more of a detective story set in a future world. The Gaff scene I thought would carry more weight as well. Gaff seemed to be ok with letting Rachel and Deckard live showing us his own humanity to do the right thing. The film doesn’t really roll with that dimension either. Was he ordered to hunt them down? Did he have any choice words about K being a Replicant Blade Runner? Maybe something to ponder when they release the deleted scenes on the extended DVD. Blade Runner 2049 is one of those films you really need to see a couple of times to make sure you didn’t miss anything. There is a lot going on and it is like a puzzle you are trying to solve. Many people will find the movie too long or not enough action for our ADD society that can’t think outside of an action scene every few second of the movie mentality.

history.title: Happy Death Day [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Ultimately an interesting idea ruined by the PG-13 rating and dumb moves by the main character.
history.text: Those of you familiar with Bill Murray’s “Groundhog Day” and The newer Tom Cruise film “Edge of Tomorrow” will feel right at home with this plot. It is basically a woman stuck in the same days set of events trying to figure out who keeps killing her resetting each day. It seems to me there would be an easier way to break the chain in this movie. The movie borrows heavily from just about every other slasher film in existence. I did like the mask the killer used and the film does have some decent scenes. While the film is interesting for the most part what pisses me off is the lack of an R rating. Seriously why tease us with a possible nudity scene walking naked through campus and not show any skin. I get why the studio’s stay away from the R rating to make more money and have more of an audience view the film but it hurts the overall film. If the lead actress Jessica Rothe was that sensitive about showing her body I am sure the studio could have rounded up another good looking blonde body double. Also with all the new computer technology they can practically photo shop her in any way she would like. That is why Happy Death Day is like “I know What You Did Last Summer” a minor weak horror film instead of something more you'll remember. Nobody goes to a horror movie expecting to see a made for TV movie. Seriously I paid $15 to see this movie in the theater I don’t want it to skimp out on anything sex, gore, violence, suspense I want to see it all. As in the famous words of Booger from Revenge of the Nerds, “I want to see bush pan down.” There didn’t even seem to be any chemistry between the Jessica Rothe and Israel Broussard. You don’t get the feeling that they are going to be rolling on the carpet or bed anytime soon. Also for young college girls all the sorority girls look to be in their early to mid 30’s not early 20’s. And you don’t get any scenes of them naked either. What kind of horror movie/sorority house is this, pathetic. Overall I would rate the film 3½ stars. The movie had potential but the weak PG-13 rating and no smart thinking by the main character hurt the movie.

history.review_title: Unforgiven is an authentic version of the Wild Wild West
history.text: Unforgiven is the best western movie I have ever seen. It rings true shot for shot, scene for scene. I love just about everything in this film. The hero is sometimes the villain Sheriff Little Bill (Gene Hackman) and the villain is sometimes the hero William Money (Clint Eastwood) depending on your point of view. The characters are so rich and deep. Little Bill maybe the big boss man sheriff but he is a horrible carpenter. The same can be said of William Money being a terrible hog farmer, but also an outlaw to be feared. Some things in life god intended for us to do more than others. Even hired guns like English Bob have their faults lying to his own biographer to make himself look better. The movie is full of characters with realistic human faults which makes the movie so believable. You sympathize with the whores in this film who are treated as little more than meat. When some drunken cowboy carves up the face of a young girl, for a tiny slight. No justice was done and the poor girl received nothing while the tavern owner received all the compensation which was horses in this case. The movie is unflinching in its brutality and authenticity of how the west really was. This is the first film in ages to depicted what it is like to kill a man. It is not something glorious that you see in the standard action movies but something you have to live with. When William Money tells his young outlaw partner “it’s a hell of thing killing a man” you believe it down to your core. Yet even deep down with all Will’s faults he does right by his partners and ends up being a just human being and a good father to his children. His story is one of sadness but also redemption and a hope that one day he will find salvation. This isn’t your modern day country music theme of celebrating the almighty pickup truck, being true to your first love, your dog and lovin your mumma. Far from it. There were brothels and whore houses. Cowboys were more ruffian and scoundrels than good Christian folk. Life wasn’t easy for anyone on the frontier. Clint Eastwood’s acting and directing are superb in this film. Whenever I hear a list of top 10 movies of all time if this movie isn’t on the list then it is hogwash. I have seen the movie well over 20 times and yet when I see it on TV no matter where it is at in the movie I stop to finish watching the film. That is the sign of a great movie. This is a 5 star movie and probably the best western ever made. This is one of those rare movies where the casting seems perfect for every character. The final shootout is gripping and it glues you to the screen.

history.review_title: Cabin Fever is a terrible movie. It is so bad it’s almost a guilty pleasure to watch!
history.text: Oh where to begin with this turkey. The movie has just about every bad horror movie cliché within the film except the obvious masked killer. Instead you get a virus and “Cujo” combined. Now the acting is god awful and the stupidity of the characters will make you chuckle. While watching the movie I was thinking no one can be this dumb. Then I realize that we elected Donald Trump. The thing is this movie is so damn bad it is actually worth watching. Like Battlefield Earth bad, but it is worth your time to soldier on to the end. Back to the movie. You do get cussing, nudity and violence so kudos to the director for making an “R” rated horror movie. God Bless him for that, so sick and tired of watered down PG-13 horror movies tempting us with skin and cutting the camera away for possible death scenes not showing you anything. You basically have 2 couples and the stoner tagalong going on a spring break trip to a remote cabin in the woods. Now right off the bat the plot of “Evil Dead” comes to mind. No way was this movie going to touch that masterpiece. I was a little surprised they didn’t try and cram in a third woman for Bert’s character which is the stupidest human being on the planet in this movie. You get cliché after cliché over and over again. Marcy rowing solo in the lake in a canoe is your “Friday the 13th”moment. Several things in this movie just seem out and out goofy. The cop obsessed with underage drinking and riding a bicycle similar to the goofball cop in “Scream”. I was thinking what was the director smoking that day? The blonde kid biting people just seemed oddball crazy right out of something like the kid from “Deliverance”. The saving grace in this film is actually the beautiful Cerina Vincent who plays Marcy. For her nude scenes alone I would give this film an additional star. Don’t know why some actresses are afraid of nudity. Never hurt Jamie Lee Curtis or Sharon Stone’s career. Overall this is a 1 star quality film, but because of the R rating and nudity I have to at least give this 2 stars. Several parts still don’t make a lot of sense but if you are in the mood to see a bad movie as a guilty pleasure this should be your go to film.

history.title: Swingers (Collector's Edition)
history.review_title: Swingers is a wonderful movie about friendship and moving on with life.
history.text: Swingers is a very different kind of film. It is a guy flick but women can easily relate. I saw the film years ago and just thought it was kind of average, nothing special. However seeing it again recently in my mid to late 30’s I have grown a new appreciation for the film. The heart of the movie is really about how your friends help you through the toughest times in life and are there for you when you need them. It reminded me a little bit of the Entourage show years before that show was ever created. This movie could have been a blue print for that show years later. Who hasn’t been in a position like Mike’s in the film where he is trying to move on and get past his old girlfriend. Or meeting someone new and looking at the phone wondering should you call or wait a day or two. Mike has a group of pals who keep him motivated to hit the town and meet new women and move on with his life. Dorothy looked pretty hot to me in the movie. Vince Vaughn who plays “Trent” in the movie is excellent and really steals the best scenes in the movie. But at the same time that Trent is a showman and a ladies’ man, he is most fulfilled when his best friend Mike is happy. I love the way the guys talk in the film I thought it was funny and interesting throughout. So funny when Mike's buddy says “I was playing Hamlet 2 months ago and now can’t even play Goofy at Disneyland” just kills me, hilarious scene. The movie is a little bit hard to watch at times because in many ways I was like Mike’s character, when I was single in my 20’s I couldn’t get a date to save my life. Felt like I had the black plague or leprosy when it came to meeting single women. Yet when I found a girlfriend every hot girl in the world wanted to get to know me. It’s like where the hell were they when I was single? Such is life. The movie is strongest in these scenes where you know Mike is going to make a mistake or come off as too desperate but you are constantly rooting for him to succeed. The film doesn’t really explore his actual job and you wonder where all the guys get money to go out on the town every night. You would think that being a standup comedian would make you a very big extrovert providing lots of people to meet and get to know. Mike could make fun of his failures in the dating world like Woody Allen and meet women that way. The title is a bit misleading when I saw the title I didn’t think they were referring to the swing dance music scene. By the end of the movie I felt the film had a positive message about taking a chance on someone new. Mike’s friends are over the moon for him and you wish you had buddies like that in real life. Overall I think Swingers is a very good movie I would rate it 4 1/2 stars. Be ready for a lot of cussing and “baby, you’re in the money”. This is the type of movie I want my own kids to watch when they get older and start the dating process. I know they will get hurt and make mistakes but I want them to see how having such a good group of friends can help you get through the toughest obstacles in life.

history.title: Hired Gun: Out of the Shadows, into the Spotlight
history.review_title: I loved the content, but many of the Hired Guns had long successful music careers which makes the title kind of misleading.
history.text: Hired Guns is a film that had me at hello. The film mainly focuses on rock musicians who were hired at the last minute to replace permanent band members on short notice. I loved watching this documentary. It could easily have been a whole series or several hours longer. It is a very broad subject and really only focuses on the 1970’s- present day. Watching the Billy Joel band behind the scenes was fascinating how those classic albums were formed and the people behind the scenes. But it wasn’t a case of hiring a studio musician at the last minute. The film does have a lot of focus on pop and glam rock musicians and doesn’t focus much at all on R&B and other genres of music. The documentary earns creditability by interviewing real rock stars Jason Newsted, Rob Zombie, Rudy Sarzo, Alice Cooper, Eric Singer, David Ellefson. I kind of wish the director would have reached out to Aerosmith, KISS, and Dave Mustaine from Megadeth to get there points of view as well. Because all of those bands have had revolving musicians come and go in their bands as well. Some of the films highlights include Jason Newsted’s interview about taking over Cliff Burton from Metallica, Brad Gillis with the impossible job of replacing Randy Roads to finish off the Diary of a Madman tour with Ozzy Osbourne’s band in 1982. Rob Zombie talking about replacing a bandmate with a better player but screwing up the chemistry in the band by losing the glue or personality of that person that made the band function. Alice Cooper listening to his take on what they are looking for in replacement musicians if a band mate is sick or up and leaves the group for a better opportunity. These are all high quality great interviews. Alice Cooper seemed to have a revolving door of great musicians that came and went in his band. I knew that Derek St Holmes was the singer for the Ted Nugent band and never really got the credit he deserved. Likewise I didn’t know Ray Parker Jr. was a long time studio musician before he became famous with the Ghostbusters one hit wonder song. I had also heard that the singer from Filter was greedy and kind of destroyed his own group. There were no interviews from Trent Reznor so we don’t get his point of view either on how that went down or what went down with his former guitarist for Nine Inch Nails. That is the thing with this documentary it shows Billy Joel in a bad light but really if you look at it from Billy’s point of view He probably had his reasons. Not everyone has been swindled out of 100 million dollars. That would make you mistrust everyone in your group no matter how honest they were. Some of the Hired Guns in the story started out as studio musicians then became full time replacement band members so the title is a little bit misleading. I also thought it was interesting for all these real rocker guitar players playing pop songs just to earn a living and get there foot in the door for music they really want to play. I actually really admire that, I am sure your street credit would probably go to crap if you were playing for Madonna, Mandy Moore, Katy Perry or Pink but for these struggling musicians just trying to make a living that was probably the big break they were looking for. I also liked how one of the musicians said it wasn’t an easy life, one minute you could be playing a European rock festival in front of 100,000 people then the next unemployed making peanuts. I would rate this 5 stars but it easily could have been longer with more substance. Focusing on some other genres of music like R & B, Jazz, Blues but had good content for what it is.

history.title: King of the Underdogs
history.review_title: Captivating documentary about a great director rarely recognised outside of Hollywood.
history.text: It is a very interesting documentary on the films of John G Avildsen's primarily his 2 biggest ROCKY and The Karate Kid movies. The documentary film is very honest and open with all the actors and people he worked with. The interviews from the actors are all fascinating. I especially found the movies John passed on or was fired from incredibly interesting. Unlike Steven Spielberg John didn't kiss Studio heads butts and winded up being passed over from several large films that he could have had. Seeing raw footage of John Travolta in Saturday Night Fever was pretty cool, one of those films John wanted to do but didn't get the chance to or the film Serpico which helped cement Al Pacino as a major movie star. Politics do come into play in the film industry just like regular society when John was dating an actress who's old boyfriend had studio ties and he was fired from doing a movie. Also the film features early casting calls with Sigourney Weaver before she was a well known actress along with Mathew Mcconaughy and a few other actors,That would later become huge movie stars like Daniel Craig who was the villain in The Power of One, John seemed so happy that his actor has gone on to great success as James Bond. The documentary touches on some of John's other powerful films such as "Joe", "Save the Tiger", "Lean On Me", "The Power of One". Not all of these films were massively successful but they are all memorable and captivating films you won't forget. I loved the scene where John meets Frank Capra his idol and asks him how he was able to do all the films he wanted and he tells him you have to make the bosses or the studio heads "make them think it was there idea" That seems so true in real life. Some times you have to know who to impress/kiss ass or do a favor for to get ahead. Of course the bulk of the film is dedicated to ROCKY and The Karate Kid his most famous films focusing on underdog characters. The director is correct when anyone talks about ROCKY it almost always centers around Sylvester Stallone and not on the director John Avildsen. I really enjoyed seeing John's Oscar acceptance speech I wish the movie would have played the whole speech and not just a snippet of it. Mr. Magi's character is as iconic as Darth Vader is to the movie business. Both ROCKY and The Karate Kid stand the test of time and are great movies to this day. I actually believe that The Karate Kid 2 never really receives its due for being such a great sequel. One of the best sequels in movie history in my book. The film also cannot be understate how powerful Bill Conti's musical score was to both movies. The music is dramatically powerful and instantly recognizable for both pictures just a few bars and you know exactly what film it came from. I would easily rate this film 5 stars I could have watched another hour or more easily about John's other films. I thought more of the film would have been strictly about ROCKY and The Karate Kid but found the film interesting non the less. If anything some parts of the film seemed rushed and I would have liked to have seen more about the impact these 2 specific films had on Hollywood. It seemed like there were countless duplicates and clone films of these films that were never done with the effort and style of John's movies.

history.title: It's A Wonderful Life (Two-Disc Collector's Set)
history.review_title: Bottom line: Best DVD yet for this wonderful movie
history.text: First: Most importantly, there is only one thing new to this edition: the colorized version on Disc 2. Which, if you're open to colorization, is pretty amazing. I, for one, am on the fence about it. I love old B&W films, and It's a Wonderful Life looks beautiful in B&W, but it's nice to have this color version to show my kids before they have to be in their twenties to appreciate a B&W film. Anyways, back to this 4th (?) DVD edition of the movie, and 2nd by Paramount. If you didn't upgrade to last year's 60th Edition from Paramount and still own one of the older (Silver Screen or other) copies, this would be the one to upgrade. I did a side by side comparison of my Silver Screen DVD to this one, and the new black and white transfer is a massive improvement; the difference is easily noticeable. Or, you can wait until Paramount decides to re-release it again, which they most definitely will. Only question is, when? IMO, this was the DVD they wanted to release for the 60th anniversary, but maybe the colorization wasn't finished and so they rushed out a branded "60th Anniversary Edition" just to cash in. That's 100% speculation, but it sounds pretty logical, doesn't it?

history.title: Oasis: Lord Don't Slow Me Down
history.review_title: Dissapointing movie; Special Features are worth the price
history.text: I've been an Oasis fan since 'Morning Glory was released and even own all of their singles/B-sides, so I was really looking forward to this tour documentary. But I was really disappointed in the film. It's boring. If you're not watching the band do awful interviews between shows, you're watching them play a damn board game or some other time killer. With all the footage the director shot, this was the best he could put together? They were on this tour for a year, but in the film, you don't get that sense of a year-long tour at all; there's never an indication of what city/country the band is in, or the dates of the shows. The fact that it's all in black and white doesn't help. Oh, and the handheld-NYPD Blue-style technique gets old really fast. Now on to the good: The Special Features: 1. The audio commentary by the band is pretty humorous, especially having Noel and Liam taking fun-hearted jabs at each other, while watching each other on screen. 2. The Q&A between Noel and fans is pretty intriguing, as Noel is in a great mood, answers all questions honestly and thorough, all while cracking jokes. It's only audio (with more footage from the film), which is a bummer, but it's still very good. 3. The concert on Disc 2, of course, is a great feature. And it's not in black and white! So if you're a huge fan of the band, you like audio commentaries, and want (another?) live concert of them, then this DVD is for you.

history.title: Ultimate Westerns Collection [DVD]
history.review_title: Excellent Collection, with Special Edition versions
history.text: 13 films, 20 discs. history.title: Superman/Shazam!: The Return of Black Adam [Blu-ray]
history.text: First thing: The Blu-ray is actually a Blu-Ray/DVD combo. Amazon does not indicate this at all, nor does the case, but the Blu-ray is a two disc set. Now let's go straight into the controversy surrounding this release: 1. The only brand new film is indeed a short film, the Superman/Shazam film (which is definitely more about Captain Marvel's origin, than a full team-up feature). About 20 minutes long, and is now my favorite of the short films and is WELL worth the price, alone, in my opinion. The animation is terrific and personally, I don't think Superman has ever looked better in an animated film. The voice cast is great, including George Newbern, who played Superman in the Justice League Unlimited series. 2. The other 3 shorts were all released on the previous special editions of the recent DCU features, but these are slightly extended and the blu-ray has a commentary on each. 3. Another VERY cool special feature are the four animated episodes, each featuring a character from the shorts: Jonah Hex (in Batman Adventures), Captain Marvel (Justice League Unlimited; the one in which he and Superman have a huge brawl!), Green Arrow, and The Spectre (Batman: The Brave and the Bold, "In the Chill of the Night" - probably one of the best episodes of that series, featuring Mark Hamill as The Spectre, Kevin Conroy as the Phantom Stranger, and Adam West as Thomas Wayne!). As far as I'm concerned, this collection is well worth the price.

history.title: How Do You Know

But when Owen Wilson is the best part of a movie... something's wrong.) I'm a fan of the entire cast - Reese, Paul Rudd, Jack, obviously - but their characters' huge flaws made them totally unbelievable. It's not funny. It's not romantic. It's just a bad movie. (and not the good kind)

history.title: Mickey's Christmas Carol, 30th Anniversary Edition (Blu-ray/DVD + Digital Copy)
history.review_title: Decent Upgrade, but a Bit Disappointing
history.text: I have an 80" HDTV, so older/unrestored films/DVDs really show their age. Before playing this new blu-ray of Mickey's Christmas Carol, I watched a bit of the same short film on the Walt Disney Treasures: Mickey Mouse in Living Color Vol. 2 DVD, since that's shown in anamorphic widescreen. I am happy to say that the Blu-ray is indeed an obvious upgrade in video quality. I did notice some shots were a bit soft and some scenes did look overly cropped, as one of the top reviews here mentioned, but for the most part, I'm happy with the upgraded video quality and glad I own this on Blu-ray. One major disappointment - aside from the price: this is easily a $14.99 Blu-ray - although not really that surprising, was the omission of the original making-of documentary that is also available on the same Walt Disney Treasures DVD mentioned above. Was it too much for them to restore that special in HD? The other shorts are fine, especially the classic Pluto's Christmas Tree, which is also now in HD. But I REALLY wish Disney would do on Blu-ray what they did on VHS back in the 80s and put out a full "Walt Disney Christmas" with all the Christmas short films on one collection.

history.title: Star Wars Trilogy Bonus Disc (2004)
history.review_title: Easy purchase for the Marketplace price
history.text: Well, first off, I shouldn't even be REVIEWING this DVD, because 1. It's just a Bonus Disc from the original Star Wars Trilogy DVD Box Set and 2. all of these bonus features (including the main feature, the two-plus hour documentary "Empire of Dreams") should have been included on the Blu-ray Star Wars Saga box set. So I give ONE STAR to George Lucas who CLEARLY hates his fans... But for the SUPER cheap price of this on Marketplace (between $1.00 to $3.00), this was an easy purchase for me - a big Star Wars fan and bigger fan of behind-the-scenes documentaries - and I'm happy to have it on my shelf. I gave it four stars because it's a DVD - if it were a Blu-ray, then I would indeed "LOVE IT". If you're like me and are replacing your original Trilogy box set with the Blu-ray set, but want to keep those Bonus Features, this is the solution.

history.title: Bugsy Malone [Blu-ray]
history.text: Just a quick review about the iTV Studios Blu-ray... As another reviewer mentioned, the movie and commentary play fine, with a 5.1 soundtrack that sounds great and the picture quality is great as well, but none of the Extras will play at all, due to the UK format. I don't think it's PAL though, but maybe 50i? I'm not an audiophile, so I'm not sure of the format. But if you want this film on blu-ray, it's worth $16, IMO, until Paramount finally releases it in the u.s. But even then, I would seriously doubt that these extras would be included. Just a hunch. As for the movie itself, it's really a film for those who grew up with it, like me. In fact, it's the first film I ever remember seeing in the theater (I was 4 years old :-). Because truthfully, I'm not sure this film holds up for anyone seeing it for the first time, now. For example, a friend of mine saw it (even several years ago) just laughed after it was over and called it "corny as hell". And the acting isn't really great from all parties - specifically the actress who plays Blousey Brown. Terrible performance. In fact, if I'm totally honest, she basically ruins every scene she's in. However the other main actors are good enough, especially young Jodie Foster of course. Overall, though, I love it. I love the splurge guns. I love the fact that it's an all kids cast acting as gangster adults. I love just about every song from the uber-talented Paul Williams, especially "Bad Guys", "Fat Sam's Grand Slam", "So You Wanna Be a Boxer", "Down and Out" and the finale "You Give a Little Love". This is one of those movies that takes me back to the place in my life when I saw the film, and in this case, I was an innocent 4 year old boy. :-)

history.title: Arrow: Season 3

Turning the second most important character, Diggle, against Oliver. -- The CORNY finale! The finale shot - won't ruin it for anyone who hasn't seen it, yet. I was seriously hoping The Flash would arrive, turn back time and retcon the whole damn thing.

history.title: Let It Snow
history.text: While I'm a huge fan of Christmas movies, I'm not a huge fan of Hallmark Christmas movies. And although this one follows the same formula: boy meets girl, opposites attract (country boy vs. city girl), they get together, they get in a fight, they make up and live happily ever after... This one is pretty good, though. My wife and I caught it on TV and enjoyed it all the way through, even with the predictable ending. The performances are decent, the story isn't exactly UNIQUE (executive wants to tear down a family-owned lodge and build a corporate, not-so-cozy resort on top of it), but for some reason, it just works. Maybe it's the fact it all takes place in the snow, with a cozy lodge as the central "character". It's also fun to watch Kirk Cameron's sister play alongside his former TV dad, Alan Thicke (who plays her dad in this movie). If you like Hallmark Christmas movies, I'm sure you'll like this one.

history.text: Super fun, colorful, with decent direction and sets. Casting is on the dot and the performances could not be any better. He too looks likes a million bucks and plays the role with style and confidence.

Was skeptical to buy this title and now I am soooooooo glad I did. This is truly one of those rare films that u don't see it coming. Truly a gem in the sea. It has a well written, almost semi perfect and balanced script. The topic is unusual and The casting is just on the dot. Wish there were more movies made like this. You get bored of seeing the big commercial films with over the top sets, customs, and an army of actors dancing to 10 plus songs every 15 minutes. This movie portrays the real life. The nonsense drama and tension in every average family, how the members react to it in their ways, how all of them are imperfect in their own twisted ways and how they deal with life. Many hidden gems in this movie for you to discover. The performances are the winning point. You forget your watching actors, they look real, show emotions that don't need dialogues to deliver. Rishi kapoor ( the chirpy grandpa) was just a delight. Loved his character and what he brought to it. The controlling mother, the insecure father they all do their roles justice. The little brother was pretty good too however the (Fawad Khan) older brother's performance shines through second to that of the grandpa. I have watched many of his works and am convinced this guy has range. Every character that he plays, he brings so much dept to it that you as the audience forget he is potrying a fiction on the screen. This is one of a kind actor that doesn't come along that often. He is like a fresh breath of air, never overacts or underacts. He looks effortlessly comfortable in every role that is given to him, not to mention super stylish, and painfully handsome in every single one of them. He is confident in acting and it sure shines through in each work of his. Mainly watched it for him and was not dissatisfied again. This is a must watch movie, just like the shark that you don't it see coming until it's one ft away from you!!! It's a beautiful work... .
