history.title: Chick Corea: Now He Sings, Now He Sobs [DVD]
history.text: Every now and then I wind up with a performance video like this where the director thinks he's clever with camera angles and editing and the results are completely distracting and truly annoying. Now, the music on this disc is great, just like you'd expect it to be with three virtuosi like this. The set list is mostly standards, only one tune from the original "Sings/Sobs" album so it's not as adventurous but it's all tastefully done and well played. But I wish I could just pop this in to the CD player to get the audio because the camera work is so gimmicky and useless. Unless, of course, you think that extremely tight close-ups of Miroslav's right hand and the back of Roy's head are helpful. I got the feeling that the director was inspired by Sergio Leone because of all the tight close-ups of the musicians' faces. And the hand-held camera guy standing behind Roy appears to have had a few too many at the bar before the set started because he zooms in and out and wobbles significantly. Oh, I guess that's "artistic". So is all the jumpy editing--no shot lasts more than 5 seconds. You can have a variety of camera angles without getting so gimmicky about it, you can back off enough so the musicians playing actually look like musicians playing instead of a lot of anonymous hands and feet flailing around. I base that on the dozens of other "in concert" videos I have where the director saw his/her job as communicating the experience of the concert rather than using the concert as raw material for a lot of self-indulgent second-rate cinematography.

history.title: Ulysses' Gaze [DVD]
history.review_title: It has its pleasures but ultimately...
history.text: I thoroughly enjoyed the cinematography and the director's pace, using long shots--many of which required some intricate choreography on the part of the cast. But I can't say I have the slightest idea what the film's about. Harvey Keitel doesn't really have dialogue, he has stylized recitations which make him appear to be mostly a mouthpiece for the director: almost like a single-actor chorus. He encounters women who instantly fall in love with him, but they're all played by the same actress so she's serving as some kind of archetype, I guess. I never figured out why the three reels of undeveloped film were significant enough to risk a journey into a war zone, or how they were to be interpreted in the context of war in general. I thought that at the end, when Keitel delivers a soliloquy, things might get tied together, but it left me more perplexed than before. Maybe I'll give the film another try at a later date, but I think I'll try a different Angelopouos film first.

history.title: Davis, Miles - Round About Midnight
history.review_title: Messy product that might have some value for diehard fans only
history.text: This disc is amateurishly presented and sloppily packaged (i.e. bootleg). It looks like it might have been taken from some Italian TV show; it's in black and white, though the picture quality isn't bad. There's a title block in the upper right-hand corner of the screen that remains through the entire disc that says "Miles Davis", just in case you forget for a moment who you're watching, I guess. There's no song selection menu and no chapter divisions, so you just have to play it straight through and fast forward it if there's a particular part you want to see. The song listing on the cover has no relation to what's on the disc and it has nothing to do with the album Round About Midnight. The song listing is: 1. Honky Tonk 2. What I Say 3. Sanctuary 4. It's About That Time 5. Funky Tonk 6. One Phone Call 7. Human Nature 8. Someting on Your Mind 9. Time After Time NONE of these songs are on the disc, except for Sanctuary. The disc is actually footage of the "Lost Quintet", i.e. Miles, Chick Corea, Wayne Shorter, Dave Holland, Jack DeJohnette, circa 1969. That is the only reason I'm not sending this disc back for a refund: I'm keen on getting any video of that group and the sound and cinematography on this disc aren't bad. But the idiotic editing is: the disc starts with what was probably the group's last song of the set (because it ends with "The Theme"), there's a fade-out, it resumes with another song, then another fade-out, then the group plays, as the last song on the disc, the song which would have been the opening song of the show (Directions). It's clear that the entire performance isn't captured here. There are some good shots of the interaction between the players and the director did a good job on setting up the camera angles. But it's a mess of a disc and you'd have to be obsessed with the Lost Quintet (as I am) to enjoy it. For anyone else, it will be a big disappointment.

history.title: Miles Ahead
history.review_title: Miles makes a wrong turn and somehow ends up in an action movie
history.text: Cheadle deserves praise for his attention to detail in portraying Miles--the vocal inflections, the facial expressions, even the fact that his fingering on the trumpet tracks the music. And there are a lot of small details that he gets right as well, including the fact that a lot of Miles' dialogue in the film consists of actual quotes. But then you have the action movie/buddy movie/blaxploitation part of the film that looks like a concession to the Hollywood money men. The sleazy promoter character who steals the tape was laughably cliche, the chase scenes and the final recovery of the tape were utterly standard and predictable and I found myself getting pretty bored about midway through the film. I have no problem with Cheadle not attempting a rigidly historical portrayal of Miles along the lines of "Ray" or "Get On Up". I've seen his approach described as "impressionistic". That's fine, I'm not a purist who's going to pick at the film's every little departure from "fact", but I don't spend money on action buddy films, either. It's a shame that Cheadle spent so much time and effort studying Miles only to weirdly use his life as a take-off point for an empty genre like this.

history.title: New Orleans Drumming (DVD)
history.review_title: The Heart of New Orleans Drumming
history.text: I bought this set back in the '90s on VHS tapes. I re-watched them recently because there appears to be a lot of interest in New Orleans drumming, including street beats. That means there are a lot of people giving instruction (like on YouTube) on New Orleans street beats, a lot of it inaccurate. This set will give you the real deal--a lot of history and tradition--and it will show how the New Orleans parade rhythms were adapted into other settings (like Ahmad Jamal, Dr. John, the Meters, even Patti LaBelle). All of the drummers here talk about (and demonstrate) specific examples, but also show what is the general the New Orleans "feel"; this can go a long way toward allowing you to adapt this feel into your own playing and not just limit it to a bit of Mardi Gras genre color. The drummers here all explain themselves very well and give good examples of what they're talking about. This set's been out for a while but it still holds up. It looks like Alfred Publishing has discontinued it but there are still copies floating around in VHS format or DVD on other web sites (like Musician's Friend). Highly recommended.

history.title: Knight of Cups [Blu-ray]
history.text: I've watched Tree of LIfe and To the Wonder as well as Knight of Cups. I found Tree of LIfe to be a great film but Knight of Cups less so. It's in the same style as Tree of LIfe but it seemed repetitive--here's yet another scene of the protagonist wandering through life with that lost look on his face, here's yet another scene of him romping on the beach with his latest girlfriend, etc. The voiceovers in Tree of Life were spare and, while a bit oblique, seemed like appropriate poetic commentaries on the characters' experience; here, the voiceovers are wordier, carrying too much of the narrative, even to the point of sometimes functioning as dialogue. And they're delivered in that solemn half-whisper that Malick seems to require, which here often seems a bit overdramatic for the content of the words. This film is more verbal than Tree of LIfe, which means it's a bit easier (not easy) to "get" the film's themes than it is with Tree of Life, but the visual and cinematic aspects of the film feel less remarkable (though they are nevertheless quite fine). Sometimes the whole thing starts to feel ponderous, which is something I haven't experienced in a Malick film before. I could watch Tree of Life any number of times to peel away its layers of meaning, but I don't think I could return to Knight of Cups. It's a decent Malick film, which means it's better than 90% of what's out there, but not up to his other films.

history.title: Don't Come Knocking
history.text: I loved "Wings of Desire" and "The American Friend", and after watching "Paris, Texas" I got interested in Wenders' take on the American West. I checked out his book of photography of the West and read his comments about the West in films. But this film has none of the meditative quality of other Wenders films and his take on the West is jam-packed with cliches. It might be that Wenders is playing with the cliches, a comment on old Hollywood Westerns, or maybe the cliches came from Shepard, but I find that kind of hip "meta" stuff to be pretty tiresome. The cinematography felt pretty jumpy, with lots of cut shots and reaction shots, none of the long, extended shots that I enjoy so much in Wenders' other films. There are some shots of landscapes and buildings that are very fine but Wenders doesn't linger on them like he has in previous films. The acting is uninspiring except for maybe one scene with Lange and Shepard. The music soundtrack is way too busy, it seems to be there all the time, getting in the way of the film just like the music in the bar gets in the way of the dialogue between Shepard and Lange. The ending was pretty insipid, not quite "they all lived happily ever after" but close. Not at all what I expected from a Wenders film.

history.title: Classic Musicals - 50 Movie Pack: Royal Wedding - Second Chorus - Stage Door Canteen - Breakfast in Hollywood - Hi-De-Ho + 45 more!
history.review_title: Good for Jazz/Swing, Other Bits of Interest, Can't Go Wrong for the Price
history.text: I bought this for 9 bucks last year and it's definitely worth it for that price. I'm not particularly interested in musicals but I do like old jazz/swing, and there are plenty of films here featuring such greats as Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Nat King Cole, the Dorsey brothers, Louis Jordan, Cab Calloway, Lena Horne, the Andrews Sisters, Artie Shaw, Lionel Hampton, and Sara Vaughn. The video quality on some of them is mediocre at best but it's a chance to see footage that doesn't get a lot of play otherwise. On the musicals side, there are a couple of Fred Astaire films and one with Judy Garland and Frank Sinatra. Admittedly there are some real dog movies in here, like "The Great Gabbo", "Sing, Cowboy, Sing", and "Minstrel Man", but some of them are so goofy and of their era that they're kind of entertaining. There are two to three movies crammed onto each side of each disc so don't expect convenient labelling, but there is an accompanying booklet that gives a decent amount of info on each of the films.

history.title: Whiplash [Blu-ray]
history.text: If you think it's realistic for a guy, just broadsided in a nasty car wreck, to pull his battered and bleeding self out of the mangled wreckage, stagger off to his gig and show his dedication by getting on stage to play with the band, then you'll find the rest of this movie plausibe. But it's full of caricatures, not characters, it's melodramatic, and underneath the melodrama there's a cliched success story with an ending that's telegraphed from the opening minutes of the film. For the most part the guy acting the part of the drummer isn't doing the actual drumming, which is fine--he's an actor not a musician and it's possible to do quick cut shots of him "playing" while the soundtrack has someone else doing the actual playing. (They could have at least mention the actual drummer in the credits, at least I didn't see any credit given.) In the scenes where the actor's actually playing--when he's supposedly practicing uptempo stuff--he's actually just banging around at random. I took this to mean that director doesn't acknowledge any difference between skilled musicianship and random noise, at least when it comes to drums. The "play till your hands bleed" stuff is just silly, and if the guy, out of frustration, tried to punch a hole through a real snare drum head, he'd probably break his hand before he'd have any success. But these are, I guess, the kind of minor details that might be labelled "jazz purism". So ignore the fact the movie's about jazz; this melodrama's still flawed in more fundamental ways.

history.title: The Trial
history.text: The visuals in this film are fantastic--the extravagant sets, the lighting, the camera angles--and make the film worth watching. Welles does a good job of creating a claustrophobic atmosphere as the film progresses. The acting--well, Anthony Perkins has some good moments and some other moments in which he seems kind of wooden, Welles isn't particularly into his part but he's always interesting to watch, Romy Schneider and Jeanne Moreau do the best they can with what are fairly strange roles, and Akim Tamiroff reprises his quivering (and somewhat annoying) character from "Five Graves to Cairo". The one thing that really bothered me about the film was Welles' habit of post-production dubbing in of the dialogue. He did that on a number of other films, rather than record the dialogue on the set. Maybe it was because of budget. But it gives everything a hokey feel when the ambience (or lack of it) of actors' voices doesn't match the setting they're in. It's not as bad as many dubbed foreign films but it's noticeable and annoying nonetheless. I wonder if some of the weaker moments of Perkins' dialogue didn't come from bad dubbing. And, though not having read the book, I doubt that Kafka ended his story the way Welles ends this film. Anyway, it's a visual masterpiece. I'll watch it again, maybe with the sound turned off.

I vacillated between five stars and one star, depending on the particular scene in this awesome movie. The main problem I had was that there are no English subtitles and at times the sound quality was too poor to make out what was being said, and then there were an equal amount of times that because of the accents, I couldn't tell what was being said. I teach English as a Second Language to adults and listen to accents all day every day, but this was just an incredible experience in frustration to me. I was hanging on every word and loving the premise, the acting, the scenery, the history...but then I would just have to accept that I would have to be content with only understanding about half of the actual dialogue. I want to buy this movie in the worst way, but without subtitles it's just too exasperating. Maybe I will need to read the book. What is it with subtitles that causes the person in charge not to include them? I suppose the bottom line is always money, but I just think this would reach so many more people if it had English subtitles. What a shame.

history.title: Apocalypse - The Second World War
history.text: My son went to the WW2 museum in New Orleans and couldn't stop raving about it. If it were a book, I would say it's a page turner. I didn't want to stop watching it until I finished; partly because I had the train of thought as to the series of events. It's very insightful and informational, without overloading you with information. So great to have it on a DVD cause you can stop and replay certain things that you weren't clear on; like "Where was this?" or "Who did that?" Can't say enough about this film. I will watch it again (not immediately) where I'm sure I will pick up more that I got the first time around. We take our freedom for granted in this great land of ours (USA). history.title: Monsters of Rock Live at Donington 1980
history.text: I knew this was coming out...knew the DVD portion was not the complete show so I thought OK still worth the shot. While the concert itself is pretty good (audio CD anways) the DVD is a let down. I mean it is only around 25 minutes and NO bonus nothing. You'd think in this day and age at least an interview of some participating members looking back or something! So lets begin, the audio CD represents the entire show I believe. The band start out strong. Eyes of the World, Since You Been Gone show just how strong the band are live and how good Down to Earth album is. Graham is in full force on Stargazer and Catch the Rainbow. He does an excellent job, and easily has the pipes to match Dio's gusto given to those songs. Lost in Hollywood is next, again strong performance, leading to the groups virtuoso skills. Keyboards, guitar and drum solos all intertwined with Difficult to Cure being played somewhere all the way, with Lazy being noodled out by Blackmore and the band. Graham returns for All Night Long, and vocally it sounds like he is loosing steam. Solid performance but again another jam segment for Blues. Will You Still Love Me is next, and Graham belts it out, leading to LLRNR, which to me is unspectacular really. Graham goes gonzo along with way and it just loses interest. All together a solid concert, definitely listenable repeatable on CD...the DVD however not so much. What erks me is the $20.00 price on this set. Definitely not worth that much.

history.title: Leviathan
history.text: This movie is all about greed, corruption, and how guy at the bottom is powerless to fight back. Kolya is a lives a simple life with his teen-aged son and his younger, beautiful, second wife in a small fishing village on the chilly, northern shore of the Kola Peninsula. He makes a living and by doing odd jobs and fixing his neighbors' cars out of a shed on his property. A property owned by his grandfather and his father before him (a significant fact in Russian culture). It has become a piece of prime real estate coveted for development by the village's corrupt mayor. Kolya refuses to sell, but the mayor decides to take extreme measures in order to get his hands on it enlisting a corrupt judicial system and the equally questionable police force. One person, however is willing to help, Kolya's old army buddy, Dima, who has become a successful Moscow lawyer. Dima uncovers the dirt on the mayor which he confronts him with, and which in turn makes the mayor uneasy. He seek counsel from the local Bishop who assures him that "All power comes from God", and since the mayor has the power, he should use it, and use it he does.....This movie has everything you would expect, deceit, adultery, and murder. Other reviewer has suggested that this is a reflection on Putin's Russia. I beg to differ. This movie is just as much a reflection of our own society as it is any other. The means of which the greed of the powerful among us is universal to all cultures.

history.text: Been a faithful can right up to the end Oscar season 13. What we're the producers thinking? Season 14 is reheated episodes from seasons 1-13. Without Michael Watley aka, "extra special agent Dinozo" the cast just doesn't gel or work. The writing is subparagraph, stories bland and uninteresting and the two new team members just don't fit. And what kind of diet is probie Tim on? He's gone from a normal sedentary squint type to a freakishly skinny anorexic looking Senior Agent with attitude. Denozo really held the team together. I liked grumpy but efficient Gibbs. Now I think his lack of speech might just be a way to make his part easier; he doesn't have many lines to remember, he just uses facial expressions, grunts and has other team members do the talking for him. And who thinks having Gibbs pull a Russian rocket launcher on a bad guy in close quarters is really dumb and stupid? Sorry guys but I'd bet there is no season 15. Bellasario has done great TV before and since Magnum and JAG he's made a lot of people rich and famous. NCIS was riding his coattails and doing well but they mucked the cast and crashed the show. I'm sad to see an end to what was a solid, entertaining, realistic and mostly technically correct military police show that's turned into something campy and banal. NCIS signing off.

history.title: The Vietnam War Ken Burns
history.text: I watched this twice bad Ken Burns has done some great history shows but this isn't one. Take for example the Civil War lots of good stuff put together by really good research or documents. Vietnam has a bias that bleeds through, it's very subtle but it's there because of the people who told their stories. Walter Concrite did a much better job of objective reporting in The Ten Thousand Day War. No interviews, just news clips and Walter's narrative. Burn's found people who wanted or needed to "heal" after their tours. That bothered me because to cover the spectrum of feelings and healings are much too big for interweaving into the outstanding g footage. I suspect a call went out for Vietnam vets and the one's on camera were chosen by people who had an agenda or slant they wanted to imprint on the "big war" America stepped into. There was a lot wrong with that war but there was a lot right about being in the military at that part of America's history and that doesn't come through. The Black Panthers, SDS and protesters come across better than the veterans and that's wrong. Now in 2017 a lot of the divisive environment America faced has reappeared. The country is divided by race, money, class, work, technology some of which were in play, some are new, but America is once again violently divided. Politicians in DC are pretty much worthless when it come to representing the taxpaying citizens in their Senate and congressional districts. Our system of regulatory bureaucrats and career politicians has held America back every bit as much as war or socio-economics has. We have protesters who champion race, money, Wall Street, banks, immigrants and other causes. I fear that the next big deployment of our military might be right here at home. As we saw from Eisenhower through FORD we had people in the Whitehouse that knew Vietnam was wrong but kept pouring men and money into a war we weren't allowed to win resulting in more than 58,000 soldiers dead and hundreds of thousands damaged. Today in 2017 we need smart tough leadership to turn our course around and once again become a nation of united states working for the good of the American taxpayers. I hope we can come together for a country of United States once again.

history.text: This is the most pretentious, insufferable, often incomprehensible film to ever crawl out of a comic book. On the other hand, I never liked the comic either (despite being a huge superhero fan), but bought this because of Benedict Cumberbatch, whom I believe to be one of the best actors around today. He's wasted here - partly because his American accent flattens out his performance, partly because he has so little to work with. I can't recommend this movie - it's just too cosmic for me.

history.title: Zootopia
history.text: Who would not love a movie about animals in which everybody at the DMV is a sloth? When I recently went to renew my driver's license, I unintentionally laughed in the face of everybody that worked there. It's worth watching Zootopia to see how this plays out. Even without the sloths, this is an extremely original, entertaining and delightful animated movie, filled with unforgettable characters and bearing an interesting and timely philosophy. If we as humans see ourselves as infinitely superior to animals, how do we justify the "wild animal" behavior we witness among humans in our daily lives? A great movie for viewers of all ages.

history.title: The Legend of Tarzan
history.review_title: The best thing in the film is Alexander Skarsgard
history.text: I began watching this on an international flight, and on that tiny screen, it looked interesting enough for me to purchase it upon returning to the States. The movie is actually disappointing - the story is flimsy, the script sloppy, the acting mediocre. The best thing in the film is Alexander Skarsgard, but I'd recommend turning off the volume and just staring at him. And would somebody please tell the CGI people that animals are not people in hair suits?

history.text: Bad, awful movie in the theater with too many flaws in plot, characterization and overly simplified stereotypes to go into here. Only gets worse as the screen gets smaller. A recent comment on this review has reenforced my review that the fans of this movie may never have actually picked up a book to give themselves a legitimate perspecitve on exactly how bad this movie is in plot and how badly derivitive it is.

history.title: John Wick [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD]
history.review_title: If you like Keanu movies, you'll love this one!
history.text: Let me start by saying I love Keanu Reeves movies (only the first Matrix movie, the next two were crap.) That being said, this one is awesome. A real bad guy who you want to love goes all bad-ass on some other not-so-nice villans that really do deserve what's coming to them. Just enough over the top action to make you say "Wow!"!!!! with those that have it coming to them getting their just deserts. Highly recommended.

history.title: Battleship [Blu-ray]
history.text: LOVE IT!!!! A very good take on an alien invasion movie scenario while tying it in with an (admittedly) simple childhood board game and blending it with a very plausable action/sci-fi movie theme!!! Yes, the plot and story line are a bit out there. But really, in what other movie can you say "Suspend my disbeliefe with Battle Ship Chains!!!" AND ACTUALLY MEAN IT!!!! Besides, a new generation gets to see what awsome impact a Battle Ship may have had/could have had/did have on history!!! (WW2, Korea, Vietnam) This impact is a fictional one, and yet I cheer at the top of my lungs for the USS Battle Ship Missouri for the sailors that served on it, it's actual impact on history and the fictional one EVERY TIME I SEE IT !!! :). ALL FEAR THE UNITED STATES NAVY!!! GO GO THE BIG MO!!!!

history.title: Here Comes the Boom [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: MMA fans and not-so-MMA fans take notice!!! A very good and entertaining film all around!!! A modern take on the ROCKY theme!!
history.text: Can't tell you how good this movie is. I am a fan of MMA and this film was a PURE JOY to watch. Also important to know, I am NOT a fan of Kevin James and yet I find myself cheering every time I see it. An inspiring movie that is (ok, maybe kinda out there) not so out there. Funny, entertaining, and enjoyable for everyone regardless of whether or not you know what MMA figthing is all about or not. There is some very realistic (and some not so realistic) simulated (sort of - watch the extras!!!) graphic violence, so be warned. Mark Cordia

history.title: Alien [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Timeless classic blending sci-fi and the fear of 'The Other' that hides in the dark. Or in this case, the dark of space.
history.text: Fantastic film that has held up over time. Wonderfully shot with beautiful use of camera angles to propell the viewer into the story and get a real feel for not only the human element cast so far out into space, but the vastness of the space and the loneliness that surely must have enveloped the characters and that will envelop future space travelers. As the film evolves, this gives the viewer a real sense the isolation of the crew adrift on the sea of stars with a (at the time of the original film) mysterious and murderous intruder in their midst; a genuine alien in all respects. Yes, the tech depicted is dated, but this is really minimal and limited to some flashing lights on control panels and monochromatic screen displays which are quickly lost in the atmosphereic and cinimatic treat that the film provides (and in some ways adds to the feeling of being alone and detached from warm, earthly things). Also, compared to other sci-fi films of the same era there are no glaring fashion and hair style gaffs of the 70's (Battle Beyond the Stars or Star Wars, anyone?) which is just as important in allowing the film to stand the test of time. The commentary by the cast and by the director Ridley Scott add fantastic insight into how and why the flim was shot the way it was and how a film from 1979 can outshine many (dare I say most?) sci-fi films and stories of this modern era. All-in-all a true Masterpiece that has its haunting beauty brought into the 21st century with Blu-ray remastering.

history.title: The Martian
history.text: Once the glow of watching Matt Damon's character use his brainpower to overcome his survival woes on Mars, the film quickly becomes Castaway in Space with the only difference being that eventually the people of Earth become aware of the survival of the Martian castaway. A fun soundtrack to listen to aside, the movie is too long with what become painfuly boring rescue scenes at the end derail what could have been a 5 star movie with some better editing.

history.review_title: More than just a clever title?
history.text: A very nice suprise as I had low expectations having been burned since the original in this franchise. A (mostly) tight plot, clever twists, well cast movie with a return of the 'original' terminator embracing more of the original depiction: i.e. no deliberate clever lines, no trying to be cute or clever. Exciting action sequences, of course, but more importantly character development. A must see if you are a fan of the Terminator series and perhaps the seed for a new 'genesis' of terminator movies?
Good intellectual bit of sci-fi.

The title says it all. Sort of. Women are funny, but female comics are not. The 'documentary' spends a lot of time with interviews and stand up footage, none of which is in the least bit humorous or funny (to me, at least). There is not very much investigative journalism, but to be fair I didn't expect it to be a serious documentary. Sadly, any film focused on comics and the world of stand up should at least make me laugh once, which this one failed to do.

So, I liked the cast. I also laughed out loud at some scenes. But the story has a meandering plot and different story lines that never weave together but travel near and far from each other. It opens with a wonderful and whimsical murder scene but devolves into the interaction of the principle characters that, again, never really mesh well. After a long middle section the ending does have a (mostly) satisfying end, especially the part about the priest/monk.

history.title: Parental Guidance
history.text: I am very disappointed after seeing this film. I have always enjoyed Bette Midler's work, and thought with her teamed up with Billy Crystal, the film would have to be funny. I was so wrong. The film is about three kids that are catered to 24/7, and all the adults in their world that spend their lives catering to them. The children are rude and disrespectful, and allowed to throw one tantrum after another because Artie, played by Crystal, DARED to try to impose any limits on their behavior, or to tell them NO. The youngest little cretin ruined a symphony performance, in only one example of his behavior, and still Artie was chastised for even implying that discipline would result. All the adults spent all their time apologizing to the children, when the children, specifically the youngest, were the ones that had done wrong, and should have been taught that they were doing wrong. Sadly, this kind of "non parenting" has become prevalent, where the children are in charge of the adults and the household, and it's doing no one any favors, least of all the children. I don't know how Crystal's character could have told Tomei's character that she was a "good mother," with a straight face. Non parenting, and allowing horrible behavior, is being the worst kid of parent. Bribing the children with cake and money was pretty bad grandparenting as well, and I didn't like how Midler's character kept ragging on Crystal for trying to discipline the children, and ruining her chance to be the "fun" grandmother. I did feel for the oldest child, who was being pushed into devoting her entire life to playing the violin. It is ironic, that the film was about "parents making sure that children are heard" yet no one heard that child. I guess that some people thought the movie was funny, if they like seeing horrible monster children being as horrible as possible while their mother looks on lovingly, and seeing zero respect for any adults exhibited or expected, and seeing all the adults crawling around catering to and placating the children. I didn't think it was funny. I gave the film one star because I can't give it less.

I find all the glowing reviews for a 'wonderful family film" disturbing, when it shows the kids having gross disrespect for the adults, especially Vin's character at least, and causing a woman to fall down the stairs at most, with no one saying a word about it. We have a little girl following Lt Wolfe around asking him personal questions, and then when he tries to send her off, she screams "disrespectful" and says she is "no longer interested" in him. Sadly I think that scene nails what is wrong with the film. The kids are in charge and feel that their feelings and wants are the only things that matter, and feel free to do and say whatever they want to, even when they hurt people. That is not a good message for a "marvelous family film," nor is it funny.

history.title: The Girl Who Spelled Freedom [VHS]
history.text: Just saw this film again on VHS, after seeing it so many years ago, and it is still such a good film. I too wonder why it is not on DVD. I also think that it is very important for American kids to see this, now more than ever, as kids' feelings of entitlement have gone through the roof. Linn is just heartbreaking, with her courage, spirit and amazing intelligence! The two things that bothered me, and I have seen this also in accounts of international adoptions from the 1970s, were that it didn't occur to the Thrashes to learn ONE word of Cambodian, in order to make even the most basic communication possible. There was a scene in the film where Mr. Thrash is learning the names of some body parts in Cambodian, but they had been there for many weeks by then, with no way to communicate, and it was done more as a game than as a basis for actual communication. People used to feel that English was the only language, and that those coming here had to learn it or lump it. I sincerely hope that people adopting internationally now have a more humane and accepting approach. The other thing that bugged was the Thrashes' daughter, who was absolutely spoiled rotten. She spoiled the movie for me the first time I saw it too. Even though she knew the level of deprivation and loss the Yanns had suffered, even though she knew of the courage and strength it took for them to come to a new world and try to survive, all she did was whine and complain about not getting new sneakers or because her mama wasn't there to see her cheerleading tryouts one time, as she continued to live in her comfortable home with everything she wanted around her. Poor baby!!! I wanted her parents to have a "come to Jesus" meeting with her but they never did, just went on coddling and apologizing to her. Otherwise, great film, and after Googling, I have learned that all the Yann kids went on to successful lives! YAY!

history.title: Ocean's Twelve
history.text: I think this is just a really fun film, and better than the other two. I think all the actors just had so much fun doing it as well, which makes it even more enjoyable. You can tell that the actors just really like working together. I have a couple of questions though, even though I have seen the film several times, there are things I apparently miss, and thought maybe someone could help me out. First, in regard to Linus' mother being the head of whatever international security organization she was with, how could she know that Linus was part of Ocean's gang, and not only not do anything about it but get them all out of jail? How could she aid and abet her son? Was she lying about being the Section Chief? The other question is similar, in regard to Isabel. She forged the arrest warrant for all of them, and got caught, yet there were no legal repercussions for her. Since I haven't seen "Lost in Translation," what did Matsui do to Linus? How in the world did Yen breathe in that bag for two days, and didn't he ever have to relieve himself? I also missed the reason he had to be sent in the bag in the first place. I really have seen the film, but I miss this stuff. The look on Danny's face when he walks into the hotel room and Yen is literally bouncing off the walls in his freedom, food everywhere, and Danny can't say anything, is a great moment.

history.title: Downton Abbey: Season 4
history.text: I was very anxious to see this new season on dvd, and have just finished it. There is some that is pretty good, some that is really good, and sadly, some that is not so good, but even with frustration with some of the plot lines, the acting is for the most part, excellent. SPOILERS..........................SPOILERS.......................SPOILERS......................SPOILERS.............................. There seemed to be some reversion to character traits of earlier seasons, which was unfortunate, since we had seen some development. I don't think it was just being with Matthew that "changed" Mary," but I had hoped, some maturing through the war, etc. All that is gone, and Mary is completely cold and self absorbed again. Even though Anna was expected to, and did, help her carry Pamuk's dead body to his room so that Mary's secret might be kept, and even though Bates left his job, his security, his happiness, to return to psychowoman, so that Mary's secret might be kept, when Mary was faced with the choice to keep his or not, what did she tell Mrs. Hughes? "it's a man's life, it's WRONG." She had no proof that Bates was the killer but was that ready to sell him out. ONLY when Bates yet AGAIN saved her family and the monarchy from another embarrassing scandal did Mary change her mind. Mary is loyal only to her position. Period. It broke my heart, and Carson's, when she was cruel to him. I am glad he got in the last shot. Nor did she tell Anna or Bates what she had done with the ticket, so Bates has to live in worry. I thought there were some layers of human complexity in Thomas last season, but that too is all gone. He is back to being "one note" evil, causing trouble for everyone for no apparent reason. Additionally, the thing with the Nanny was clunky. He was trying to get her in trouble, but she cooked her own goose when Cora heard what she said to Sybbie, which had nothing to do with Thomas. In contrast, the guy who plays him, from what I have seen in the extra features, seems to be a nice guy. He is good at being bad! I wonder what if it had been Tom who heard Nanny, and what he would have done to her. Sadly, there were probably many many children of "privilege" who were at the mercy of nannies and governesses like Nanny West, and even still. I thought it was too bad that both Robert and Cora seemed to suffer from extreme amnesia this season, to the point of seeming demented. First, when Thomas and Braithwaite were pointing fingers at Anna, saying she was being mean, they believe them, even though they know Anna is the sweetest person ever, and is never mean to anyone! They even speak to Bates about her. Totally wrong. It was the same in the scene where Thomas is complaining to Robert about the other staff and Robert said, "are you not liked downstairs?" Never mind that there were incidents of theft and attempts to frame Bates in earlier seasons, and what kind of person Thomas is, which Robert well knows. Amnesia, I say. Robert and Cora should have laughed Thomas out of the room. Why is he still working there? I was glad Braithwaite got kicked out early on, and loved her smackdown by Mrs. Hughes. Additionally, when Violet was questioning Robert about his wanting total control of the estate, I too was thinking, yeah, because you have done so well with that up til now!" Now Edith. She seems to present as a sympathetic character for alot of people, but she isn't to me. While Mary is not a nice person, she never did anything to really hurt Edith in the first season, yet what Edith did to her by telling the Turkish guy what happened to Pamuk, would have ruined Mary's entire life, if she had not married Matthew. She would have never married and even worse, have been shut out of the society she lived for. I thought it perfect karmic justice that Edith was jilted at the altar, losing her chance to marry, and now experiencing what would cause equal scandal for her. I wanted her to remember what she did to Mary, but the show didn't go there. I have to say that Cora and Mary were pretty blind to not know Edith was pregnant, since they knew she had a boyfriend,had to have started to show, and suddenly off to Switzerland for months. Stevie Wonder would know. I thought Violet's reaction was great.." I see I will have to take the slow path" but not judgmental, nor was she of Sybil and Tom. For all her clinging to the old ways, she was pretty down to earth with her granddaughters and matters of love and sex. It was funny how Robert chastised Dr Clarkson for saying the word "urine" in front of her! Tis a mystery what happened to Gregson. If the Nazis killed him, they would have found a body? They didn't have camps yet in 1922 I don't think. has he faked his death? Why would he give Edith his power of attorney? I didn't like Rose at all. She was a spoiled little rich girl who didn't give a thought to anyone else, but wanted what she wanted. No replacement at all for Sybil, who was a real person, with brains and a heart. I SO miss Sybil. Matthew was a nice guy but I loved Sybil. I wish that Cora's mother had been there when Sybil was dying. She would have thrown Sir I Know it All out the window, got Sybil to the hospital, and saved her. I absolutely think Dr Clarkson was right and would have saved her, had they listened to him. I agree with Cora, and didn't want her to reconcile with Robert, even though Violet pushed her to. It was completely Robert's and Sir Know it All's fault. I thought the Daisy/Ivy/Alfred/Jimmy adolescent posturings went on interminably, but Daisy and Mrs Patmore's relationship matured, which was nice to see. I got really tired of seeing Molesley whining and feeling sorry for himself. I liked how he stood up for Baxter though, helping her to feel better about herself, and hopefully telling Thomas to go jump in the lake. I see a relationship developing there, no matter what she's done. The pig stuff was dumb. When DID Mary learn to make eggs? Cora's mother and brother stuff was dumb and unnecessary. Also the cloak and dagger spy stuff in trying to get the letter back. If it was that important, maybe girlfriend shouldn't have had it in her bag and then left her bag unattended! What was REALLY good... Anna's storyline, and her acting. She brought it!!! I hope they have British Emmys, she should definitely win. I really wanted her to go to the police after she knew Bates knew though. I thought that she was selling him a bit short for being so sure that he would kill Green, and ruin their lives together. I LOVE Mrs Hughes, she is such a badass! I thought she was going to kill Green with her bare hands, and I bet she could have. Such great scenes with Anna, with Green, with Braithwaite, with Carson. ALL of them. It's such a shock to see her on the show and then how she looks in real life, a decade younger, like Mrs. Patmore. I also love Carson. He is absolutely old school, and is judgmental and rigid and everything else, but it is his job to make sure everything goes right. It was all on his shoulders. He does have a caring heart though. He adores Mary, though I am with Mrs Hughes on that, and I loved the scene with he and Sybbie. One of my favorite scenes was when he had just found out Mrs Hughes was okay, and he was singing and laughing while he polished the platter, so unlike him, but so sweet. The final scene of this season is right up there too, with Carson in BARE feet, wading, and holding Mrs. Hughes' hand for security! Others think they should be married, I don't know, but even if not, their friendship is wonderful to see. I don't think Bates is the killer. It would take alot of things to fall into place to take the train to another town, rent a car, find where the guy lives, follow him to where you would be able to hit him, with no one seeing it, or you, then returning the car and getting back on the train. It is possible he had someone else do it, but they would have the same problems. He was hit by a car right? I think it was an accident. I wanted someone to kill him, but slowly. I can only imagine how many victims he had. As vulnerable as women have always been to sexual assault, I feel sure that women and girls in service positions were especially easy to victimize. Tom matured this season, I thought. I didn't like him when he was with Sybil. He was controlling, willing to let her sacrifice everything in her life for him but gave up nothing for her,not wanting her to "disappoint him" I hated that, or to have ideas about their child that disagreed with his, and not even treating her family with the slightest respect, when they were sheltering him and even keeping his ass out of prison. I understood and agree with where he was coming from but he could have given Sybil that much.He was a jerk but did start to grow up after Sybil's death. I think maturity involves the ability to not only see your corner, but the other guy's as well, including the English, and he was getting there. It was such irony to see him dancing at the ball with monarchy. I wonder if the "troubles" are going to rear their head again next season, since one of the guys after Mary has a castle and holdings in Ulster, which I believe is in Northern Ireland. How would Tom deal with Mary becoming an occupier? I LOVE LOVE LOVE Dame Maggie Smith. I love her snarkiness and her wisdom. Her scenes with Isobel were gold. It was well done how Isobel could have gladly strangled her, yet when Violet was ill, wouldn't leave her side. Even sick, Violet had good lines! The scene where they are playing cards and having fun together is great. I had a sad moment though, in seeing her ill scenes, to realize she is nearly eighty years old. She is a treasure, and always will be. This show is a treasure as well, even with all its faults. It has stellar performances and often excellent writing. I don't compare it in any way with Upstairs Downstairs. This is its own entity, and it is awesome to see how many people around the world love this show.

history.title: The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel
history.text: This is such a good film. Others have spoken much on the issues presented of getting older, feeling obsolete, a bit frightened, as well as the feelings toward spouses, deceased and living, that went unspoken. It was awesome to see the courage of this group, who for the most part, as Evelyn said, not only survived, but thrived. I love love LOVE Maggie Smith and Judi Dench, and they were excellent here, though they seem to have a bit of pattern by now to many of their roles, Smith as sharp tongued and witty, Dench as motherly and warm. As a total Downton Abbey fan, Maggie Smith was not far here from Dowager Countess Crawley, but my goodness, Penelope Wilton, as a shrewish, bitter woman here, was worlds away from the strong and compassionate Isobel Crawley. At least with distant familial intermarrying, you don't have to change the monograms! I think it's a little unfortunate that the only character that refused to embrace her new surroundings was Wilton's character. We can plainly see that her prison is of her own making, yet I am sure it is true that a place like Jaipur might be too difficult, in many ways, for many people, and that wouldn't make them bad. To see Maggie Smith's character sitting on her hospital bed, exhausted, in pain, when she says, "I want to go home," hurt my heart. I loved her emotional and physical recovery. Another scene that broke my heart is when she is pouring out her heart to the woman who isn't understanding a word she is saying, and to see the emotional connection on the face of the woman "who no one else will even acknowledge." I had to put aside my American sensibilities with the scenes with Sunaina and her brother, when he was telling her what to do and listening on her phone. I know it's a male dominant culture but I still wish she had stood up to him and told him to bug off. It surprised me though that Sonny's mother was as controlling of him as she was. It would have seemed more accurate with a daughter. The tiny little things that bugged a little bit were when Evelyn saw Graham in the swing and just walked away. There was no blood or wounds, and you can't tell by looking a someone from feet away, whether they are living. He could have been asleep, he could have been unconscious and in need of medical help. Not the medical help from Sonny, who had problems telling living from dead. Sonny was awesome. The other thing that I wasn't sure felt very accurate was Graham's telling practically everyone that he was gay, even as a reply to "where are you going?" which seemed very odd, and not one person had a moment's problem with it, even though he had only known these people a couple of weeks. It was great to see that acceptance but not something anyone can count on, especially I would think, amongst older people. I also wondered, since Graham apparently planned to die in India, why it didn't bother him to make friends with these people, knowing he might drop dead in front of them, and not care at all about they might feel about that? Also Manoj's, whose life he just dropped back into out of the blue, unannounced and uninvited, and then drops dead. I suppose one could also argue that the pursuit of Evelyn by the other guy, I forget his name, was rather rushed, seeing as his wife wasn't even at the airport yet, but on the other hand, sometimes there isn't all the time in the world. But these are little picks. This is truly an excellent movie and has much to say about the human condition, caring about others and living life, no matter the age, or what your mother wants.

history.title: Captain Phillips
history.text: This was a gripping, chilling film, and Tom Hanks does a great job. The actors playing the Somalians kept the intensity on high throughout as well. I didn't remember hearing about this event so I did not know what was going to happen in the film. I agree with the posts asking commenters not to reveal full plots without using spoiler tags. I often will skim a few reviews prior to seeing a film to see if most people liked it,though with a Tom Hanks film, that's a safe bet, and therefore the comment that people shouldn't come here until after, is just rude and thoughtless. As angry as the hijacking all the way through made me, the most frightening scene in the film was the one in which the ship's crew of 19 have to hide for their lives, and Hanks as the captain, standing alone, watching in fear as four, only FOUR soulless cretins come tooling up in a boat the size of a bathtub, and take over the ship the comparable size of a mountain, terrorizing everyone on board. How can this happen and be allowed to happen? I don't know anything about maritime law but it's inconceivable to me that ships are sent into areas with high pirating activity, with no way to or right to protect themselves. The actual captain said piracy is a fact of life on the high seas and that may be, but having to face murderous thugs, unarmed and defenseless should not be. In my opinion, hostile forces should be permanently neutralized if they get within a mile of a ship. There was not the least bit of equity of force or power and there is no way these pirates should have been able to take over or even get close to the ship. The movie's synopsis states that both Phillips and the Somali captain undertake an emotional journey throughout the hijacking and kidnapping, but I didn't see this to be true. Muse was as much a terrorist at the end as he was in the beginning. I did see Phillips try to get the kid to give himself up and save his own life, which indicates a journey of sorts, and the kind of person Phillips was and is. I also didn't feel one bit sorry for Muse or any of the Somali adults. I know they have an impoverished country but a little money would have gone a long way to better their lives, and Muse refuses to take the money, then bragging about receiving millions for previous hijackings. Phillips asks him what he is doing there then, and to me the answer was that Muse and the others had no humanity, but lived only to hurt and kill others. I don't usually cry when watching films, but I was having a hard time when Phillips was in the medical bay, all right. Another powerful film for Hanks.

history.title: Watsons Go to Birmingham
history.text: I am surprised that some reviewers think the book is so much better than the film, since the book had, in my opinion, huge gaps in the story. For example, in the book, Byron, who is making a habit of getting into trouble and has zero respect for his parents, completely reforms on the very doorstep of his grandmother, with never a single word said again about him. Seriously, he says "yes Ma'am" and that is it. There is nothing at all about his or the family's experiences in Birmingham throughout the summer, or why he returned home with the family, when they had planned to have him spend the school year in Birmingham, or how or if his behavior changed. The book goes from the family's arrival in June, to the church bombing, to everyone, including Byron, back home in Michigan, in just that way. The film indicates that the bombing was in September, not during the summer, which in the book is confusing, and that tragic event should have been made clear, and the film indicates why the family was still there in September, which is also confusing in the book, since the younger two should have been back in Michigan for school. The book also contained far too much about the "wool pooh," which to me made no sense to begin with. I thought the film made cohesive sense. You see how Byron starts to mature and think about something more important than himself. I liked the part where his cousins are talking about fighting for equality at the costs of being jailed and injured, and you see the light bulb start to go on in Byron's head. You see how prejudice and segregation affected the family, which is not at all present in the book. You see Byron's and Kenny's growth when they are back home. The film is also gripping as it shows actual footage of the turmoil. The things I didn't like about the film are, for one, the casting of Byron. Byron was 14 or 15 in the book. There was no way that Byron of the film was 15. He looked 20, and his friend older than that, and both looked menacing, especially when they were roughing Kenny up. They looked like adults beating a child up. It made no sense to me in book and film that Byron's parents would choose to take a troubled boy who wouldn't listen to anyone, already committing small crimes, and heading for bigger trouble, to the rabidly prejudiced South, where the slightest misstep could get him seriously hurt or killed. Emmett Till was only 14 when he was brutalized and murdered for allegedly just whistling at a white woman. The other thing was Mrs. Watson's trying to keep her kids in a protective bubble while putting them in a middle of a war, where not knowing what to do could get them hurt. That seemed kind of insane to me. By the same token, Byron saw the conflicts on tv, and should have known about the segregation. I absolutely feel that the film is excellent, and much better than the book. Though, however, the four little girls were mentioned in the dedication, but I wish there had been an accompanying feature on them and on the church bombing.

history.title: Orphan Black: Season Four [DVD]
history.review_title: I think that Tatiana is brilliant in this season as in all the others
history.text: I think that Tatiana is brilliant in this season as in all the others, though I too am getting very tired of Sarah, and her never ending selfishness. But that is who she is. While I wish that the writers would at times go deeper instead of just bringing on new clones, I still think that this is an awesome show. The only thing not right, and may cause difficulties for others as well as me, is that the subtitling is extremely sporadic. There can be whole paragraphs of dialogue, often, with no subtitles. Since there isn't always really clear enunciation by all the characters, I can miss what is said. Other than that, LOVE it!

history.title: Call the Midwife: Season Five [DVD]
history.text: I have just come to the series, and while I wasn't sure originally how much I liked it, I have now finished season 5 and I love it. LOVE it. It is so interesting and beautiful and aggravating to see how people lived in times that are so different from the one we live in now, and the births of more than babies, but also of viewpoints and practices that turned out to have such profound impact on people's lives. Whether to feed with breast or bottle, whether what is new is automatically best, the ongoing issue of desperately poor people having one child after another that they can't feed or adequately shelter, illiteracy, hatred of people who are different, regardless of in what way, are still issues we grapple with today. It is also so interesting to see how things were then that are so different today, the ignorant but well meaning prescribing of or irresponsible taking of medication in pregnancy, the lack of technology, doctors making house calls, the constant smoking!!!!!!! I am not one to demonize smokers who do it responsibly, and i know back in the day they were just starting to know it wasn't healthy, and people did smoke everywhere, but to see people smoking in the hospital rooms, around sick babies, in the bedrooms, during birth scenes, everywhere, just is really revolting. You would think that people with medical experience would know that it wouldn't be helpful to anyone but they all puffed like chimneys. I give the series four stars instead of five because of the writers' tendencies to make some of the characters too saintly and perfect. Perfect people are boring. Shelagh is the perfect wife, mother, and office manager, and Dr Turner and Peter Noakes are the perfect husbands, even though wives and mothers working for fulfillment instead of economic need was not widely done at that time. Sister Mary Cynthia is so saintly, she has no personality at all. There was a bit this season in which she showed some emotion, for about three minutes. I do not care for the characters of Jenny and Trixie, since it seems very unlikely to me that two young, very attractive girls would choose to live in a convent with a bunch of nuns. The character of Sr Monica Joan is basically one note. Since the first season, all she has done is go for the sweets, quote poetry and moan about her physical infirmities. The additions of Nurse Crane, who is a loveable curmudgeon, and Patsy, who hides much pain, are much more believable. Sr Julienne often comes across as the all knowing, all wise, all gentle mother of the house, but we see her struggle privately, and Jenny Agutter portrays her with excellence. The other characters and performances that absolutely shine are Sr Evangelina, who says it like it is, often too harshly, but never intending malice, and knows what she is about. SPOILER............................. HER DEATH at the end of season 5 was heartbreaking. She was the best character, hilarious and genuine. Pam Ferris is stellar in this role. If there had to be a loss among the sisters, it should have been Sr Monica Joan. I also love Chummy. She also is humorous, incredibly poignant, and her coming to terms with her mother, and her feelings about how she was treated by her mother are such good scenes. Patsy and Delia's trying to live and love authentically when no one in the world wanted to allow them to do so also hurts my heart, and I love their scenes together. I am watching the dvds of the seasons, so is there deleted material of their scenes? I don't know.

history.title: A Taste of History-Second Season (Starring Chef Walter Staib)
history.review_title: With ATK the best-ever cooking show series
history.text: Beside [[ASIN:B002935GDW America's Test Kitchen]] Walter Staib's Taste of History is the finest cooking-show series ever produced. No kitchen gadgetry (at least motorized ones)! Simple honest food prepared the old-fashioned way in an open hearth. One thing I remember was the Chef remarking "People ask me all the time what the Founders actually ate, and all I can say is that I don't know but I do know what was served." (in that time everything was served family-style in big bowls that were passed from person to person each serve themselves). The only thing I wasn't crazy about was the sweetbreads (if you don't know, you don't want to know!). I guess back in the old days most people just couldn't afford to waste any part of the animal... What's unusual about this cooking show is the historicity of its settings. In each show, between courses, the viewer is taken out of the kitchen to some historic site for a short tour of the environment from which the food originated. One show featured a visit to a revolutionary battlefield where a meal was prepared "in the field" at a camp (bivouac). Another show featured George Washington's field tent from which he commanded the Continental Army (it has been preserved). Other notables who served as subjects of the show included Martha Washington, Betsy Ross, and Thomas Jefferson to name just a few (I've not yet watched all the series so undoubtedly there are many others as well). Other places gone to include historic buildings, hotels, restaurants, etc. where the various revolutionary principals discussed and planned the war and the fledgling American government. At most of these places a knowledgeable guide or character actor narrates with the historical detail. In a few of the shows the Chef visits farms and gardens and explains what kinds of animals and vegetables were cultivated during revolutionary times. BTW Chef Staib runs the City Tavern restaurant in Philadelphia's historic district. The website has their menu posted on it, as well the Chef's other media offerings.

history.title: Dogfights: The Complete Series Megaset
history.review_title: Experience the battles...dissect the tactics...relive the DOGFIGHTS!
history.text: This series kicks ass! Nearly perfect in every respect. Each episode documents four or five historical air-to-air dogfights. Most segments feature combat from wars from WW1 through Vietnam (one segment deals with the Gulf (Kuwait) War and one with air combat in the Balkans in the mid-1990s. Fewer fights from WW1 are featured; most are from WW2 through Vietnam). Most of the presentations are done in CGI, but this is CGI done so well that it displays near-photographic quality. Although Dogfights aired ten years ago, you wouldn't guess it from the quality of the computer graphics. The accompanying music is also first-rate. The CGI presentation is enhanced with short inline segments of commentary from some of the pilots involved in the combat, many even from WW2. Many episodes show archival footage of the actual aircraft and men during the war. So-called "ribbon" diagrams are often used to showcase the maneuvers and tactics that the aircraft executed in their dogfights. This is supplemented side-by-side comparisons of the capabilities and advantages/disadvantages of each aircraft in the fight. Often the view from the pilot in the cockpit is shown to give his perspective on the aerial situation. Every episode is introduced with an explanation of the historical context of the war in which the dogfight takes place, and the starting circumstances of each dogfight. Most of the episodes focus on American fighter pilots and combats involving allied pilots (like the British and Israelis). Very few of their Axis/Korean/Vietnamese/Russian opponents are portrayed in such detail. One exception is the episode "The Luftwaffe's Deadliest Mission" which documents the mssions of Sonderkommando Elbe which was ordered to bring down Allied bombers by ramming them. Two of the Luftwaffe pilots who survived after ramming their targets (Heinrich Henkel and Klaus Hahn) were interviewed. Watching the episodes dealing with the Vietnam War (among them The Bloodiest Day, AIr Ambush (Operation Bolo), and Hell Over Hanoi) the viewer would be led to believe that the USN and USAF totally ruled the skies over Vietnam; however, this was hardly the case. The last disk contains the 90-minute "Dogfights of the Future". Naturally the Fifth Generation F-22 and F-35 aircraft feature prominently. A scenario is presented in which they square off against the air force of some unspecified rogue state equipped with Russian Migs and Sukhois, along with some French Rafales. The moral of this story is that stealth technology will rule the skies and that all non-stealth aircraft are only helpless targets. The writers of the episode do make the point that the swarms of enemy Fourth Generation aircraft will likely deplete the limited missile-carrying capacity of the stealth 5th Gen fighters, and that other solutions may be necessary like the proposed Boeing (Rockwell) B-1R, which is a B-1B modified with the F-119 turbofans of the F-22, an AESA air-to-air radar and fire control system, and racks for dozens of AIM-120 antiaircraft missiles. (note the latest proposal for an F-15 variant doubles the number of air-to-air missiles carried). The writers of the episode do point out that enemies may contrive some anti-stealth technology like low-frequency radar, but it's not likely to upset the overall balance of power. Also better surface-to-air missile technologies built into integrated air defense systems are likely to threaten future air campaigns over enemy territory. And then they go on to point out that eventually America's enemies will develop their own 5th Generation competitor aircraft that will necessitate further advances in technology. Finally, the arena of warfare will expand into space and threaten America's dependence on satellite assets in Earth orbit, and this will spur the deployment of hypersonic aircraft capable of fighting in this new realm of combat. I've watched every episode at least three or four times and never tire of it. I ordered two copies just in case my first one wears out! Dogfights has got to be History Channel's best series, except for perhaps [[ASIN:B0015XASV2 The History Channel Presents The Best of Modern Marvels]]. It's the fightinest! * * * * * Five stars easy!

history.title: Modern Marvels: Welding (History Channel)
history.review_title: An interesting look at commercial welding
history.text: Chapters include skyscraper construction welding, underwater welding, explosive welding (fusing together of metal sheets with explosive charges), spot welding robots in auto manufacturing, and ultrasonic welding of plastics in manufacturing (including those all-so-exasperating plastic packages for retail merchandise). As usual with the Modern Marvels presentations, each segment supplies interesting historical background and explanations of the subject. The first segment showed how the beams of buildings were fastened with rivets before construction welding was developed by Lincoln Electric in the first decades of the 20th century. How the welds are protected from atmospheric gases is explained. The segment on robotic welding showed how the robot is programmed and how it senses where to place each weld. I liked the way the supervisor of the underwater welding station explained that everything inside has to be kept extremely organized because space is so tight and "there's alot of things in there that can bite you". Very informative. Only thing I would have liked to have been included would be shipyard welding (especially submarines with their special steels (even titanium)) and the welding for the pipes in nuclear power plants (carrying radioactive water -- those welds have to be x-rayed to pass inspection).

history.title: Arrival
history.review_title: A thoughtful story, only not very well thought out
history.text: I wanted to like this movie because I'd heard it was more like [[ASIN:B004L9GMBC 2001: A Space Odyssey]] than [[ASIN:B00008G8M4 Independence Day]]. We sorely need an antidote to the rash of mindless space-sci-fi shootemups that have been flooding out of Hollyweird in recent years. Sad to say, Arrival fails to fully qualify for this category, though the story premise was promising. The production design and cinematography are pretty good and the acting is okay. These are the reasons for the three-star rating, which is generous considering all the problems with the story / plot / script. The movie is actually pretty good if you don't bother to think about it too much. Twelve alien spacecraft touch down around the world and (apparently) make no attempt to communicate. No mothership capable of interstellar flight has been detected (apparently). They evidently possess antigravity technology since their craft float above the earth effortlessly, with no detectable emissions (implying they are tapping some form of zero-point energy or otherwise piping in energy from another dimension. The lack of waste heat is, however inexplicable with current physics). The story centers around attempts to establish communication with the aliens (heptapods). They make indistinct whale-like sounds which are indecipherable. They only attempt to communicate by drawing abstract circular figures in their "air" with a black smoke-like substance. They make no attempt to use human symbols or pictures / photos / drawings. This strongly implies that they have made no effort to study humanity from space before landing on Earth; nor (apparently) have they studied the volumes of radio and television broadcasts being beamed into space, which are detectable out to a distance of several lightyears at the least. The essence of the story is that the study of the alien language somehow endows the Banks character with the ability to see the future, because the heptapods experience time in a non-linear fashion (they directly experience the block universe in which all spacetime exists coterminiously). The aliens are offering their language as a "gift" to humanity to enable humanity to see the future because the aliens hope to enlist humanity's help (for some unspecified reason) 3000 years in the future (according to the heptapod Costello).. The alien word for "gift", however, is misinterpreted by the human linguists as "weapon". Banks argues that they might actually mean the word "tool" instead. Then news comes from the Chinese landing site that their heptapods conveyed the sentence "use weapon" rather than "offer weapon" as the Banks team interpreted. So the Chinese CINC issues an ultimatum to their heptapods, several of the other nations with heptapod landing sites follow suit, and tension rise as the aliens withdraw to a higher altitude and change the attitude of their ships ("shells") from vertical to horizontal (attack mode???). Then Banks receives a vision of the future in which the Chinese general conveys some personal information that convinces him to back down and share his linguist's information with the other landing sites (this happens when Banks steals a cell phone and breaks security by phoning the Chinese general with the unknowable personal info). Need I continue with this plot description? By far the biggest hole in this swiss-cheese story is that no explanation is given just how learning a foreign language can endow a human with the ability to see the future. Furthermore, the visions of the future that Banks experiences are only have to do with her future daughter, which has nothing to do whatsoever with the situation of the alien visitation. Then, just when it's most convenient for the plot, the one coherent vision she has is that of the Chinese general giving her exactly the info needed to defuse the rising conflict among the nations hosting the twelve landing sites. All this is too contrived to comprise a satisfying story. One might argue that since it's actually an alien language rather than a merely foreign one, somehow it has a supernaturally profound transformative effect on the mind of the linguists. Yes, I did consider this perspective. However, here is where the eminent Dr. Charles Darwin enters the picture. The heptapod minds and most especially their brains (or what serves as such) evolved in an entirely different "alien" environment. It requires certain anatomical adaptations, selected for by life (and especially death) experiences. Which no human could possibly experience. Sapir-Whorf notwithstanding, merely learning how to decode a different language, even an alien one, could not possibly account for this. And if it could, I sure would like to hear an at-least plausible explanation. None is offered or attempted except the off-hand reference by Banks to Sapir-Whorf. Insufficient! Besides, the aliens do not behave like beings possessing technology for interstellar transport and antigravity. So four stars for aesthetics and two stars for story. Three stars overall. I did enjoy the experience but for me the story has to cohere logically. For those viewers less cerebral than I, they would probably like the movie more than I did. Too bad, I think this was a 5-star story idea but the execution by the scriptwriters just fails to measure up.

Further, at least two representatives of the US government (Senators John Mccain and Chris Murphy) personally whipped up the anti-Russian mobs in Kiev with rousing speeches, giving the coup activists reason to believe they would have the backing of the US. Although Nuland serves the democratic Obama administration, she actually is a neoconservative working for the big-business interests of corporate America and Europe. history.text: Good documentary that speaks of the world's current and future needs of energy and the dilemma of nuclear energy's low carbon footprint versus it's waste and hazards. Professes that there are nuclear reactor designs safer than what is currently used. Also suggests that wind, solar, and hydroelectric sources are insufficient by themselves for the long term to meet the world's needs. Renewables are viewed as not an on demand source. Some of the technologies they suggest are limited by material science. Others, they suggest are limited by fear. Whether you agree or not, it's good insight and worth a dicussion.
