history.review_title: OK 1980's supernatural film with an inconsistent ending.
history.text: 1980's movie The Hearse was interesting, but, also confusing. The premise is a woman goes back to her small town where she lived with her aunt as a child to reclaim her aunt's home after the aunt died. The local towns people give her the cold shoulder because they believe that her aunt was involved in the occult or something like that. Even the county Sheriff is strange and rather gruff and hostile toward her. Soon the woman starts having encounters on the road with an old 1950's hearse that almost hits her car or runs her car off the road. The hearse is driven by an unfriendly looking white man in a black 1950's chauffeur's uniform. After a run in with the hearse, a handsome young man wearing a 1950's style suit and driving an old 1950's sedan stops and offers her assistance. She invites him over and they develop a relationship. To provide much more information would ruin the story. However, after the story behind the hearse is revealed it starts to unravel. There are a lot of plot holes and inconsistencies that take place near the end of the movie that make no sense at all. All in all it is an OK movie. They just go off the deep end at the end of the movie with inconsistencies. Worth about 3 stars.

history.title: Life
history.review_title: A great concept that was derailed by a lame script. None of the good actors could save the film's bad script.
history.text: I did not see this movie at the theater. I purchased the 4K Bluray disc because the previews looked really good. The movie revolves around a space station crew that retrieves a satellite that has taken samples from the surface of Mars and has returned to the Earth. The samples are found to contain a single celled organism that they stimulate with an electric current to activate and start to grow and multiply at an incredible rate. It soon becomes a blob of tissue that reacts/responds to it's surroundings and stimuli (like the doctor's finger reaching toward it). This is where it started to get really hokey and lose believability. All of the crew members are smiling and encouraged by the tissue reaching for the doctor's finger. Yes, he's wearing gloves that are attached to holes in the container that the tissue is growing in. But, still it seems really stupid for him to tempt the blob of alien tissue to touch his gloved finger. It also seemed really stupid that none of the crew members were the least bit concerned that they don't know what this thing is and they should be willy nilly playing with it with someone's hand (finger. Even the one crew person (CDC Doctor) who is their biologist and is responsible for biological security protocols is smiling at the tissue that is reaching for the doctor's finger. Really? Long story short, the touchy/feely close encounter with the E.T. blob doesn't end well for the doctor. Come to think of it, that scene did remind me of the scene from E.T. where the kid touches E.T.'s glowing fingertip. Things go from bad to worse up through the ending with all of the crew members doing stupid things (that make you think this is really, really stupid; why are they doing this?) that result in them being killed by the E.T. The surprise ending was no surprise at all. I knew exactly what was happening and was totally expecting the ending they had.

history.title: Wrong Turn 6
history.review_title: Completely changes the storyline from the 1st two movies and has an absurd plot.
history.text: I saw the 1st and 2nd movies in this series as well as half of the 4th one on cable TV. The 1st and 2nd movies were OK and both seemed in line with the story line of a family of inbred mutants residing in the back woods out of sight and scrutiny of civilized people. The 2nd movie furthered the storyline with an explanation for their mutation (besides being inbred). The 2nd movie indicated that tainted drinking water caused their mutations. Seemed a reasonable enough explanation. I missed the 3rd movie. The 4th movie I only saw the second half and it made no sense whatsoever and seemed to be an unnecessary addition to the series. Actually, the only reason I watched any of these movies after the 1st one was to see if/how someone was going to kill off these degenerates. Didn't happen in the 4th one, which brings us to this 6th one. Yeah, I missed the 5th one as well (I really don't like these movies because they never kill off the mutants). This 6th movie was ridiculous and absurd and changes the storyline. Instead of being mutated through tainted drinking water, they were all mutated through inbreeding. Not only that, this movie comes up with the absurd revelation ..... caution...SPOILER ALERT: The original family of 3 mutants residing in a shack in the sticks has been discarded. Now we have a whole community of 10 or 15 mutants residing in a shack in the sticks who have been inbreeding since civil war times and they built a large, expensive luxury hotel where several presidents have stayed at. Yeah, that's right, a bunch of inbred family members (at least the normal looking ones) built a large, expensive luxury hotel that rich and famous people stayed in. More SPOILERs: Not only are they inbred mutants, but, they are aristocratic, snobby inbreds that are looking for a long lost inbred pure blood (to further their pure blood line) who grew up in the big city (he didn't know his parents or where he came from) and he was depressed and tried to commit suicide because he didn't fit in. Yet, he was fairly well off because he was involved in the stock market and he has a girlfriend and snobby friends. SPOILER ALERT over. Anyway, the guy finds out he has inherited this old hotel and goes to see it with his snooty friends. The manager and his sister/girlfriend (they make no bones about this relationship with the guests either) are eager for the new owner to take over and start grooming him for the job. As expected, the 3 mutants from the title of the series start bumping off the guy's friends and he becomes a loser of a friend. One of the rules of any decent, quality horror movie is for the writer, director, and the actors to make the innocent characters likeable so the audience cares if they live or die. Like a cheesy, low/no quality Z grade movie, the director and writers don't make the characters likeable with the exception of the fat guy with glasses (don't remember his name because I didn't care) who at least tries to save the others and the skinny guy who follows his friend to look out for him. This movie is totally absurd. A large, luxury hotel (it is in need of some remodeling but is still a luxury hotel) that is having guests stay there and the mutant trio kills a few of the guests and no one notices except for the Sheriff's Office that posts "Missing" posters at the convenience store? At the beginning of the movie the mutants kill a couple out bicycling on the property and then an old rich lady staying with a group of old folks. Later they kill ....SPOILER ALERT......... a Deputy Sheriff and run his car off the road. No one ever comes looking for the missing Deputy or his patrol car????? By the end of the movie they have killed the young couple bicyclists, the old rich lady, the Deputy Sheriff, and the 5 friends of the main character, and the main character takes over the hotel and no one comes looking for any of these missing people????? SPOILER ALERT off. Anyway, the absurdity of the events and the storyline make this the most ridiculous of this series. I probably won't be watching any more of these because I don't think they will ever kill off the mutants (which is all I want to see). The cinematographer was great. Great cinematography, terrible plot and storyline. As I mentioned before, a good horror movie (even a low budget one) will make the characters sympathetic to the audience. The majority of these characters were not sympathetic and I didn't care whether they died or not. What's the point? Seems like the director only wanted to make a movie where the characters were nothing more than a means to show gruesome murders and nothing more. That's a total waste and pointless. I used to watch the old Friday the 13th movies just to see how they were going to kill the Jason character at the end. They did not kill off all the characters and kept you in suspense to see which of the characters were going to survive because some did and usually the ones (not always) you were rooting for. I don't like movies where everybody dies. That's pointless. You get to the point where you know that everyone is going to die, so why watch it in the first place?

history.title: The Autopsy of Jane Doe
history.review_title: Starts off with new ideas and some creepy scenes, but, then devolves into stale, predictable been done many times before ending.
history.text: I read the positive reviews and decided to buy this movie. It started out OK. This seemed new and different and was looking like it had a lot of potential. The characters were developed and the events were set to create a scary atmosphere. However, it started to become predictable after a half way through the movie. The last 15 minutes were very predictable and I figured out exactly how things were going to play out. That's where this movie falls flat. I've seen the events taking place in the last 15 minutes in many, many other movies. That's where this movie became stale for me. Even the ending was totally predictable. The main characters came up with a theory as to what was happening. But, the reason for the "characteristics" of the corpse (which I can't divulge as it would ruin the movie for those that haven't seen it) as well as it's condition was never explained and remains a huge plot hole. As I stated the movie starts off and seems like an original idea. But, later devolves into low budget cheesiness with a predictable, worn out/stale ending.

history.title: Alien: Covenant 4k Digital 4K UHD
history.review_title: Better than Prometheus, but, still a huge disappointment with huge plot holes and stupid characters.
history.text: I've seen all of the Alien movies from the original Alien to this one. I have to say that Ridley Scott should have stopped with the original "Alien." Prometheus made little sense and opened up a can of worms as far as questions. This movie, "Alien Covenant" does answer some of the questions that were created by "Prometheus." That was the good. The first part of the movie (after the lame beginning sequence) wasn't bad either. The bad is everything else about this movie. The movie has the colony ship "Covenant" traveling to a distant planet that appears to have the conditions for human colonization. The colonists are in suspended animation for the 7 year trip and the ship is run by the synthetic human, Walter, who is another version of the synthetic from the previous movie Prometheus. There are 2,000 colonists in suspended animation with over 1,000 human embryos. The ship encounters damage from a solar flare, killing the captain in his suspended animation tube and putting another crewmember in charge after they are awakened from their suspended animation. They pick up a signal from a nearby planet that is something that has earth origins. However the crew is not familiar with this planet and their scanning for a suitable earth like planet for colonization somehow totally missed this much closer planet. That is plot hole #1 that makes no sense at all. They decide to head to the planet to investigate and possibly colonize it if it is suitable, as opposed to going back to suspended animation for 7 years risking another incident. They land a team on the surface to investigate the signal and the suitability of the planet to colonize. The movie was great up to this point. Then is all goes downhill into mindless stupidity. The crew members encounter totally different "Aliens" on the planet than the ones from the "Alien" movie, which supposedly takes place 20 years after this movie. Yet the planet looks totally different from the 20 year later "Alien" planet. Landscape is totally different, the location of the crashed alien ship is not in the same place. The other misgiving I have for this movie, which I truly wanted to like (they had sense enough to carry rifles), was the total and abject stupidity of everyone of the crew members. They do stupid things that a child would ask "Why is he or she doing that?" Most (not all) of the crew member's deaths was avoidable. Several times I found myself yelling at the characters on the TV .... "You idiot!" And .... "How stupid!" Any director knows that he has to keep the audience sympathetic with the characters and caring about whether or not they live or die. I was starting to lose sympathy with most of the characters because of the stupidity that they displayed. I found the ending to be very predictable and I knew what was coming. Because I knew what was going to happen I didn't care. I lost any sympathy or interest in those characters. That is the jist of the movie. Also, there are a lot of gigantic plot holes that if revealed would give away too much of the plot. If you're like me and wanted to see the threads (and explanations) between this movie, Prometheus, and the original Alien movie, then you'll be sorely disappointed as I was. The plot holes are just too big to ignore.

history.title: Wind River [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Similar to Val Kilmer's "Thunderheart," except that it's vastly superior to "Thunderheart" with a much better plot and climax.
history.text: I saw the preview for this movie and it reminded a lot of the Val Kilmer movie "Thunderheart." I thought "Thunderheart" was so-so and had a typical Hollywood cheesiness about it that I didn't like. The previews for "Wind River" didn't give off that cheesy vibe that "Thunderheart" did. After watching it I have to agree that my intuition about this movie were spot on. The plot involves a young American Aborigine girl found dead from exposure in the wilderness on a reservation. Jeremy Renner is a Fish & Game predator hunter that comes across the body while hunting for a family of cougars. The FBI is contacted and send a relatively inexperienced field agent form the nearest office to assess the situation and report whether an investigative team needs to come in for a formal investigation, if she can find proof of a crime. There are signs in the way of sexual assault, but, no proof that the assault led to the death (which even the coroner says is obvious, but, he can't put that on the death certificate). The inexperienced agent teams up with the Fish & Game officer (for his tracking skills) and the reservation Police Chief of police, played by well known character actor Graham Green. The movie does take the time to flesh out Renner's character and his emotional connection to this crime. It's a little slow because of this, but, well worth it to explain the climax at the end. And what a climax it was. Pretty exciting climax that was unexpected at first, but, started building as the scene started and culminated with a very satisfying ending. I really enjoyed this movie and only wish they had released it on 4K UHD instead of only Bluray.

history.title: Bananas
history.text: I've seen this movie when it was released decades ago. It's Woody Allen's best movie. His second best movie was "Sleeper." After that one was "Take the Money and Run." I stopped watching his movies after this one because they weren't funny anymore. Back to Bananas. There are some classic, hilarious scenes in this one. Like the Subway scene where some thugs get on the subway car that Allen is riding and start harassing the passengers. Allen shove them off the bus and the doors close on them, then opens up and they get back on. The main thug is easily recognizable as Sylvester Stallone in one of his earliest movie roles. The movie is about Fielding Mellisch (Allen),a neurotic man who doesn't know what he wants to do with his life and he meets and falls for Louise Lasser's liberal, anti establishment character that wants to go to a South American country to protest for a revolution that's taking place there. They break up and Allen goes to the country by himself and ends up joining the revolution by accident and then becoming their president. The scenes in the South American country (actually Puerto Rico) are the best in the movie. This movie was sup[posed to be released on Bluray, but, all that was released on Bluray was a Region B (UK) disc, this one, so I ordered and received it. Fortunately I have a player that is region free. The movie played well on my player and was shipped expeditiously by the seller. I'm not a fan of Woody Allen's later movies (everything after Sleeper and Take the Money and Run) because they just lacked the slapstick humor of his earlier films. This one is his best work.

history.title: The Mummy (2017)
history.review_title: The Mummy starring Tom Cruise playing his childish, immature character from Top Gun. Dissappointing.
history.text: I ordered this movie because the previews, especially the transport plane scene looked pretty good. However, the movie itself was somewhat lacking. Tom Cruise's character was in the Army in Iraq and he and his buddy were archaeological/antiquities tomb robbers that have a map to a secret hidden tomb in an ancient city in Iraq that happens to be located behind insurgent's lines. Tom Cruises isn't my favorite actor, but, he does good work, sometimes. As example, I liked his work in his two Jack Reacher movies, his movie Edge of Forever, and most of his Mission Impossible movies as well. Other times he comes across as a snotty, immature teenager. The lousy, childish movie "Top Gun" comes to mind. Unfortunately, I got the snotty, immature, childish Tom Cruise from the Top Gun movie here in The Mummy. The movie is also inconsistent and does not have continuity or sense of time. For example, while in the insurgent village they almost die, call in an air strike (which happens almost instantaneously even though they are only two men who aren't where they were supposed to be - against their orders and without explanation), which an explosion opens up a collapsed area in the sand (a depression about 10 ft. that exposes the top of a statue). Yet, their commanding officer arrives minutes later and gives them two hours to check it out before they depart the village. Next thing you know they are descending by rope down a gigantic cavern (that wasn't visible a minute ago) with a huge opening at the surface and I was wondering "what happened to the statue that was partially exposed and no sign of any hole, much less a cavern?" Now, they only were given two hours to depart, yet they explore this giant cavern, locate a huge sarcophagus, and manage to lift the huge sarcophagus out of the huge cavern and load it onto the transport plane in that two hours?? On the transport plane they just barely take off from this village in Iraq. Cruise takes a nap and wakes up to an attack which ends up causing the plane to crash a few minutes later in ............. England????? Iraq flight with a prop job transport aircraft to England is almost 2,000 miles. I don't think they could make that flight in the time it takes to take a nap. I don't think a transport plane could even make that trip without a stop to refuel. The other bit of nonsense is Russell Crowe's character. STOP READING. SPOILER ALERT. Apparently Russell Crowe's character is Dr. Henry Jekyll and he uncontrollably turns into Mr. Hyde with the need to inject himself with a weird 1800's looking version of a futuristic syringe, to reverse the metamorphosis. Dr. Jekyll is the leader of some secret, British, organization not unlike the organization form the British TV series "Torchwood" with all of their monsters and creatures that they deal with. I'd use an emoji to show my eyes rolling about now if I could. SPOILER ALERT OFF. Anyway, with the introduction of Russell Crowe's character, this movie turned into a cartoon, only with live action ....... silliness. I've seen the first "Mummy" movie with Brendan Frasier and did not enjoy that movie and did not bother with the subsequent sequels. I saw this Tom Cruise movie and thought that this was going to be a semi- serious movie. But, alas, the only serious Mummy movies outside of the Universal Studios Mummy movies starring Boris Karloff or Lon Chaney, Jr., you will find are those cranked out by Hammer Films starring Christopher Lee. I liked those movies, but, I'd like to see some modern Mummy movies made with current day themes and technology that are not silly, live action cartoons.

history.title: BITTER/SWEET
history.review_title: One of the Best Romantic Films
history.text: This is sweet, romantic movie about a coffee buyer who travels to Thailand on business and falls for his travel guide. Complications arise when the company owner backs out of deals made to growers, including the guide's family. The buyer's problems worsen when his fiancée travels to Thailand and he must decide what direction his life will take. Relationships between family and friends add color to the story. Bottom line is, a movie is only as good as its acting. And you must like the characters in it to like it. This movie is a winner in both regards. It has a great cast portraying very likeable characters. It is also relaxing seeing the beautiful scenery of Thailand. My only criticisms are for the opening song and the DVD cover art. Normally, I would give 4 stars to a movie of this quality. However, it's rare to find a romantic movie as good as this. So I rate it 5 stars.

history.title: Secret Garden
history.text: A mesmerizing romantic comedy of a poor stuntwoman who is mistaken to be a movie actress by a corporate CEO. Once they discover the mistake, they part. But the CEO cannot get her out of his mind. Several love triangles develop (real and imagined) with them which include a fading pop star (the CEO's cousin), two directors and others. The story revolves mostly around the stuntwoman and the CEO and highlights the differences between the cultures of the poor and the privileged. There is a bit a magic in the story when they sometimes switch bodies. And there are many subplots during the 20 hour story. Everything about this is near perfect including the story, acting (especially the 4 leads), casting, directing, and pace. A story is only engaging if you actually like the characters in it and I did, with the only exception of the mother who was meant to be an antagonist. I found the story to be addicting and watched all 20 episodes twice in a 1 month period. I only wish it was dubbed in English rather than having to read the subtitles.

history.title: Something Happened in Bali [DVD]
history.text: This kind of drama falls into the catagory of tragedy. Three people meet in Bali and hire a tour guide. They seem bored with the trip and return to Korea, which is the location for most of the series. Each has a host of problems which are their own making. That is why it was difficult for me to care about the charactors. After watching 4 episodes, I had little interest in seeing the rest. But I did watch the last one and had no problems understanding or following the ending. If you like slow paced tragedies, you will enjoy the show. It was well acted. I guess I was looking for something different.

history.title: You're Beautiful
history.text: Clearly from the reviews, many people like this series. However, if you are over 20, I doubt that it will appeal to you. I only watch episode 1 and parts of 2 and 3. Rather sophmoric. But I can see how it would appeal to young people.

history.title: Sector 7 [Blu-ray 3D + Blu-ray ] [3D Blu-ray]
history.text: This is an average sci-fi monster movie about a drilling team on an offshore rig that are attacked by a mysterious creature. Their options are limited because a storm hits and they have limited weapons. The mystery is what is the creature and why is it there. Overall, the movie is enjoyable - but I am a big sci-fi fan. The movie was recorded in Korean but there is the option to listen to a version dubbed in English (rather than watch the Korean version with subtitles). I am very grateful for that because I get tired reading subtitles. However, the sound quality is not as good in the dubbed version. In particular, some of the subtle background sounds seem to be missing. And the voice inflection is not as good as in the Korean version. So I actually enjoyed the movie more in Korean. The movie is in 3D. But I cannot comment on that because I do not have a 3D TV. Overall, the movie was enjoyable. Yes, there are some flaws. But that is true with most sci-fi movies. I give it 4 stars for the Korean version and 3 for the dubbed version.

history.title: National Parks Exploration Series - The Grand Canyon: A Wonder of the Natural World
history.review_title: Nice video of National Parks of the Colorado Plateau
history.text: This video covers the following US National Parks of the Colorado Plateau Grand Canyon NP Painted Desert/Petrified Desert NP Arches NP Canyonlands NP Canyon De Chelly National Monument Bryce NP Zion NP Mesa Verde NP Lake Powell National Recreation Area So most parks only have about 5 minutes of video. But since I visited each, it was nice buying only 1 video to cover all of them. The video mostly concentrates on the geology of the parks. And there is a section covering the Colorado Plateau as a whole. It is not a travel log like some other blu rays. Overall, not bad. But there were some disappointments which include: 1. Canyonlands is a beautiful park. But instead of showing views of it, they talked about Indian petro graphs. 2. The best views in Bryce are from the Navajo trail. But it did not include video from that location. 3. All the views from the Grand Canyon are from the south rim - none from the north rim. 4. The commentary from the geologist, park ranger and historian were nice. But they should have showed views of the parks when they talked rather than showing the person. 5. The video had nice background music. But it was stopped when the geologist or ranger or historian talked. Overall, not bad and a good value for the price. But if you want a video only of the Grand Canyon, then this one is not for you.

history.title: Scenic National Parks: Glacier Banff & Jasper [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Terrible - Very Little Time on Scenic Views
history.text: When I buy scenic DVD's/Blu Rays, I expect them to show beautiful scenes of what I experience on vacation. In particular, I prefer some scenes of common tourist stops. This video has very little of that. Instead, it is filled with shots of people, railroads, hotels, close-ups of nature, and a lot of bad black and white vintage video. It has some beautiful shots of mountains from the air. But only a few fleeting views from popular tourist spots. Some of the best views only last a second or two. I honestly do not understand why anyone would give more than 1 star to this blu ray. I would give it 0 if I could. I now must decide whether to keep or toss this item. (I like my home videos of these parks better, even if they are more grainy.)

A charming movie about a couple who meet and share and evening together in Hong Kong. A year later, by chance they meet again, clearly attracted to each other and question if they should continue. The conversation is light and draws the viewer in. The chemistry between the couple is there – the actors married later in real life. Part of my enjoyment of the film is because it does a good job capturing Hong Kong’s scene & atmosphere and brought back memories when I met my wife there. Hope to see it on Blu Ray soon.

history.title: Major League Baseball Presents 2016 World Series: Chicago Cubs
history.review_title: Perfect for Die Hard Cub Fans
history.text: I believe this is what all die-hard Cubs fans will want, if not now, then in the future. It is probably best to buy now because I doubt the price will go down and because eventually they will no longer be sold, except for outrageous prices. Years ago, I purchased a set of DVDs of the 1985 Chicago Bears games which included the Super Bowl game. I thought the price was high but bought them anyway. I am glad I did because, to Bears fans, they are classics now. And I own some DVDs of old Cubs games too. According to the description, these DVDs/Blu-rays are complete games of all seven 2016 World Series games. Some games were boring, others were exciting. I hesitated when I saw the price of the collection. But I figure, no one knows for sure when the Cubs will win another. I know I will enjoy watching them in future years. And highlights will not be enough for me.

history.title: Hallelujah!
history.text: Christ missing From Christmas In fairness, I am writing this review based on the 60 minute version televised on PBS. The DVD is 81 minutes. One expects a Christ centered program from a Christian church. And although the show does have a few well performed Christmas carols like “Of the Father’s Love Begotten”, it does not draw one to the manger in Bethlehem. There is too much secular material for me. But the biggest disappointment was that about half of the program talked about the composer who wrote Handel’s Messiah and how performances of it helped the poor. The emphasis was on Handel and the poor – not on the Christmas story. Also, short performances of a few songs from The Messiah were tied into the people of the time, not the Christ Child. It would have been better if they sang the full versions of the Messiah songs and cut out the narration. This year there was no reading of the Christmas story from the Bible. Compare this with the 2006 Mormon Christmas Concert with Renee Fleming. In 2006 there was a bigger focus on religious songs. There was a reading of the Christmas story from the Bible. The stage was lavishly decorated. The stage in 2016 was drab by comparison. I have seen every one of their shows on PBS since 2006 and none equals the quality of that year. (I own the DVD from 2006 and would purchase others if they were as good.) The show isn’t terrible. But it could have been so much better if it were more Christ centered. I guess I expect more from the LDS church.

history.title: Pawn
history.text: This is an older movie, but one that I just happened to stumble upon recently. I really had no idea what to expect from the movie and had only seen the trailer once. I mostly chose it because it starred Michael Chiklis. I loved his work on The Shield. This turned out to be something altogether different though, in a good way. I will admit, the first thing that struck me about the film was Michael Chiklis having a cockey accent, which was a bit funny/distracting at first but he did a pretty good job of it and I was buying into it within a few minutes. The great roster of actors in this film also stood out, each of them giving A+ performances. Rat Liotta was especially outstanding in his small part of the film. Without a doubt, the standout part of this movie is the script though. The story is presented in a very non-linear fashion, jumping from one point in time to another and leaving you to figure out each of the character's true motives as if the film were some sort of puzzle. The quick back and forth between scenes reminded me a bit of Lock Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, minus the funny parts. Everything about the plot and the characters reveals itself in a very well paced manner leaving you sitting at the edge of your seat until the very end. It is definitely a movie that sucks you in and forces you to think about what is going on. Although the movie was apparently made on a shoestring budget, it certainly came off as an excellent production with some great acting, thrilling tension and characters that always have you guessing as to what they may be hiding and what is going to happen to them next.

history.title: Rock the Kasbah
history.text: The first 30 minutes or so of this film was pretty good, but then it suddenly shifted gears from a well-paced, light-hearted comedy to a humorless drama that seemed to drag on forever. It's like they took two different scripts and tried to splice them together somehow. Bill Murray's performance was really the only thing that held the movie together from beginning to end. Probably the most puzzling part of the movie to me was how they wove some hilarious parts with Danny McBride into the storyline and then just suddenly disappeared his character. Honestly, there were no big laughs after his character disappeared and after that the movie just seemed to drag on and on. Bruce Willis' part started off amusing enough, but then just swerved into a lame drive-by performance as well. Kate Hudson... Unconvincing and DOA insofar as humor goes. If you are a HUGE Bill Murray fanboy this might be worth your time. If you are expecting a comedy I would definitely avoid it though. It's a movie that had a lot of potential, but just ended up dying a slow, humorless death.

history.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming [Blu-ray]
history.text: To say that Marvel Studios has dropped the ball with the Spider-Man franchise would be a huge understatement. Spider-Man is arguably Marvel's most enduring super-hero, yet he can't seem to catch a break when it comes to the big screen. In this latest reboot, Marvel takes another stab at incarnating Spidey, using one of his most infamous foes as his foil, the Vulture. A funny thing happened to Spider-Man on his way to Marvel's latest incarnation... His character has pretty much lost all of his original roots. Other than Captain America, all of the original Marvel characters have had their time lines fast-forwarded to originating in the 21st century. Spider-Man is no exception. A few other things have changed as well. The new Peter Parker is not a scrawny weakling, but some super-buff athlete who looks like he does sit-ups in his spare time. His aged Aunt Mae is no longer a grey-haired, frail widow, but a busty 90's movie star. He is no longer interested in photography, but uploads his videos to YouTube. It's enough to make any die-hard Spider-Man fan sick to their stomach. The one bright point in this entire reboot fiasco is the performance of Michael Keaton as the Vulture. Although the Vulture himself has undergone some revisions, Keaton is captivating in his role as Spider-Man's arch enemy. After being unceremoniously dumped as the original Batman, Keaton shows his incredible flexibility as a bad guy who you can't help but feel a little bit sorry for. Keaton totally steals every scene he is in, making the rest of the cast seem awkwardly out of place at times. During most of the movie, Keaton's character has little interaction with the Spider-Man part of the story, which makes for an odd clash when they finally meet on screen. The comedic Spider-Man facing off against the dead-pan performance of Keaton is like mixing oil with water. They just don't seem to blend together that well. Going back to the whole revisionist history thing, making Spider-Man some some sort of geeky kid that Tony Stark can boss around doesn't really make a lot of sense and makes the character come off as weak and immature. This is a cruel irony for anyone who actually grew up reading Marvel Comics, just to see their characters get turned inside-out. Honestly, the story here is weak. The backstory is pretty much non-existent. The acting (besides Michael Keaton and Robert Downey Jr.) is just passable, at best. The jokes fall a bit flat and the film itself runs way too long. Sorry to say, but this latest reboot doesn't exactly leave me begging for a sequel.

This movie promised quite a bit, but can't help but disappoint. The backstory is quite rushed and there is no real chance for character development before we jump 90 years into the future. Once we arrive, things just get more confusing. It seems like the main characters are simply running around in circles most of the time. The lead role is played by an actor that does an excellent job of playing a robot. Maybe a bit too convincing. It is hard to have any empathy for a character that is basically a walking toaster. As such, it is impossible to get very attached to his character. The female lead role is exactly the opposite. Perhaps even a bot TOO human. She is an emotional wreck that seems to cry at the drop of a hat and has zero life skills. If she did, she might have noticed that this supposed human she was hanging out with had no memory, never ate, never drank and had the emotional response of a houseplant. Yet, they are trying to sell her as some kind of female Rambo who has somehow managed to survive when every other human on earth seems to have perished. John Cusak's role seems like a walk-on, who never actually interacts with the main characters. My guess is that he did all of his scenes against green screen and spent no more than a week on-set. Since the film has no other bankable stars, I'm guessing that he probably made more money on this movie than all of the other actors combined for a lot less work. His performance is lifeless, stiff and mechanical. He could have easily been replaced by robot himself. The movie has some really nice CGI and decent production values, but it is not nearly enough to make up for the convoluted plot, nonsensical drama and lack of believable emotions. The script just isn't convincing and nothing in the movie seems very well thought-out. Save your time and your money. This movie is definitely worth missing.

history.title: Atomic Blonde [Blu-ray]
history.text: I must say that the main reason that I decided to write this review was due to some of 1 star ratings this movie is getting here and I really feel that it is unfair. Charlize Theron delivers an incredible performance in this cold war period thriller that pits her against a dizzying web of agents and double agents in Berlin in 1989. Both the soundtrack and the movie itself give fairly accurate portrayals of the time period as well as the tension that existed between east and west at that time. John Goodman also delivers an excellent performance as the CIA's contact with Britain's MI6 and interrogator of Theron's character. I am not going to get into any spoilers here, but the movie starts off a bit confusing, with the rest of the film filling-in most of the backstory, but does not perhaps answer all of the questions that it should, which is why I wouldn't quite give this picture 5 stars. I'm guessing that the answers to some of the lingering questions ended up on the cutting room floor to trim down the running time of the movie and perhaps to not slow it down too much. Speaking of which, the movie paces itself quite nicely with plenty of action scenes and just enough time to catch your breath between them. While some of the minor story details may be missing, the story line in general makes complete sense, especially as things start to unravel in the final scenes. The mystery of who is on whose side should keep you guessing until the end. It's also one of those endings that seems obvious in retrospect, but not that simple to decode while you are actually watching it. Direction, stunts, effects, acting, production values, etc. were all first-rate and it is a very entertaining movie that I plan on watching again. I think that the film probably suffered from some bad editing that leads to some of the plot confusion that some reviewers had. It wasn't a problem for me though and was one of my favorite suspense films of 2017.

history.title: Mayhem
history.review_title: Mindless Humor and Horror At It's Best
history.text: Based upon my personal experience as well as the other reviews you will find here, I ca n pretty confidently predict that you will either love or hate this movie. So far, there are no 3 star reviews. You are someone who either "gets" this movie, or you don't. If you like bloody zombie humor that is fast paced yet has a story worth telling, then this is the flick for you. This isn't just another dumb zombie movie. This is an exceptional, dumb zombie movie. O.k., I guess that people in the movie don't exactly become zombies, they just go temporarily insane and start killing each other until some sort of antidote starts circulating through their air conditioning system. Oddly the antidote takes exactly six hours, to the second, to begin working. It reminds me a bit of The Purge, only in this movie people are killing other people (mostly?) involuntarily. The script, direction and acting is all first rate, unlike a lot of other campy horror movies you will see. This is definitely no "Sharknado", which itself gets an "A" for humor, but the plot to that movie is ridiculous, the acting is horrible, the production is cheap and there is really no character development or even a point to the story. On the other hand, Mayhem has some great acting, sympathetic characters and a decent message to it at the end. It's definitely no Citizen Kane, but for what it sets out to do, it absolutely succeeds.

history.review_title: No Spoilers, Based On a True Story
history.text: American Made is a fascinating movie that follows the life of CIA asset and professional pilot Barry Seal. While Hollywood generally takes quite a few liberties when it comes to making films "based on a true story", this movie tracks pretty darned close to the historical facts as we know them. Every once in awhile you will find a true story that is crazier than any Hollywood writer could possibly come up with and the story of Barry Seal happens to be one of them. Seal was recruited by the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency during the Reagan administration to do recon work in Central America and eventually ended-up doing double duty as a drug smuggler for the likes of Pablo Escobar in Columbia. This odd mix of allegiances leads to a lot of problems between the likes of the CIA, DEA, FBI, Secret Service, The White House, U.S. Customs, The State of Arkansas and local police. A number of complications arise from a potentially explosive mix of the law, politics and family issues, which Cruise has to navigate through throughout the movie. Speaking of whom, Cruise does an excellent job with this role and gives one of the most underrated performances of his career. While I wouldn't quite call this an action movie (which Cruise is normally known for) there is plenty of drama and suspense. About the only disappointment I had with this movie was the fact that all of the illegal activity that Seal was involved in happened in Mena, Arkansas, right during the time that Bill Clinton was Governor of the state. Oddly, his name only comes up once during the movie and that is pretty much in passing. The film also neglected to mention the mysterious deaths in Arkansas connected with the case and were almost certainly tied to the operation in Mena. I'm guessing that these details were left out to keep the movie's mood more upbeat and to keep all of the corruption going on squarely blamed on the Reagan administration. There are a few other decent performances in this movie, but Tom Cruise pretty much steals the show. It's definitely an entertaining movie to watch and tells the story quite well. You could definitely find much worse ways to spend 90 minutes of your time.

history.title: Valerian and the City of A Thousand Planets [DVD + Bluray]
history.text: To say that I was completely blown-away by this film would be an understatement. Having not heard anything about it at all beforehand, I was pretty much expecting just another direct-to-video sci-fi flick that I would quickly forget. It turned out to be what will hopefully become a future cult classic. While the script is definitely not your average shoot-up movie and can be a bit difficult to grasp at times, it totally falls within the realms of possibility for the sci-fi world. The movie seems to take a lot of inspiration from earlier classics such as The Fifth Element, Star Wars, Blade Runner, TRON, Avatar and even Who Framed Roger Rabbit. It's style is uniquely its own though, with a lot of emphasis on humor and chemistry between the two leading characters played by Dane DeHann (Valerian) and Cara Delevingne (Laureline). Speaking of which, I had never seen or heard of either of these actors before I saw this movie. From reading their bios, neither seems to have taken on this large of a role in a major film before and I must say that I am quite impressed by their initial performances. The Valerian character comes across as sort of a smart ass who is difficult to generate much sympathy for while the Laureline character comes off as extremely bright, witty and beautiful. And while CGI can certainly be given a lot of credit for the absolute beauty of this film a lot of credit has to go to this actress as well. The movie has plenty of action, suspense and surprises and keeps up quite a good pace. The action is occasionally interrupted by the love story developing between the two lead characters, but without it there wouldn't be that much of a plot. Herbie Hancock's role was short, but well done. I can't seem to recall him ever acting in a movie before, unless you count Blues Brothers 2000 (I won't hold that against him though). While the movie obviously includes quite a bit of CGI it does not throw it at you to the point of being obnoxious and unbelievable. This movie has some of the best CGI effects I have ever seen, but they flow quite naturally into the movie much as they did in Avatar. At some point you just stop noticing the difference between effects and live action. Of course, most of the credit for this movie has to go to Luc Besson who is one of my favorite all-time directors. He obviously took a lot of inspiration from his previous classic The Fifth Element when filming this, which just made it even more enjoyable for me, as TFE is one of my favorite movies ever. This is definitely one of those movies that I will undoubtedly end-up watching over and over again. To pass this movie by would be a tragedy. Why it received such little attention at the box office I will never understand.

history.title: Hansel & Gretel: Witch Hunters (DVD)
history.text: This is a highly underrated film that flew beneath the radar during its initial release, but has gained some momentum on home video. While the plot is pretty much nonsensical, the writing, acting, special effects, music score, etc. are all first rate, with much credit due to Jeremy Renner in the lead role. The story starts out loosely following the original fairly tale, but that entire premise pretty much goes out the window after the first scene. What we are left with is a highly original story that is told much in the same fashion as Van Helsing and Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter. While those movies definitely diverged from historical facts, this one completely befuddles any resemblance to the timeline of human history by introducing inventions such at the Gatling Gun and the electric dynamo to the middle ages. Forget about suspending disbelief. You should pretty much expect anything to happen. While the plot may be nonsensical, it is just realistic enough to set the background for some great one-liners, special effects and stunt work that must have taken a miracle to pull off without someone actually getting hurt. This is basically a comedy disguised as a horror film and it works. It is a bit heavy on gore at times and has a bit more sex and bad language in it than I would want my children watching, but for adults it is a rollercoaster of fun that never takes itself too seriously or lets historical facts stand in the way of a good story. If you liked Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter, Van Helsing, Pride, Prejudice and Zombies or even the Blade series, you will most likely enjoy this. If you didn't then I would skip this movie entirely, because you obviously have no sense of humor.

history.review_title: Sucked Less Than I Had Expected
history.text: I'll admit it... I really enjoy cheap, corny, ridiculous sci-fi and horror films. I have a taste for movies so bad that they are actually good. This movie had "trainwreck" written all over it and I was prepared to watch the entire thing come apart at the seams and descend into complete suckage. However, a funny thing happened... This movie did not suck nearly as bad as I had expected it to. Gerard Butler puts in a semi-decent performance as a disgruntled ex-scientist who is drafted into service by the government to save the world. The plot is pretty thin and the premise ridiculous, but between the action scenes, mystery and great CGI work it somehow holds together as a "real movie", as opposed to something you would find on the SyFy channel at 3 in the morning. Some of the acting in the movie, especially the part of Butler's Brother, was horrendously bad. Almost to the point of making me LOL during the more dramatic scenes. There are some brief, decent performances by Andy Garcia and Ed Harris, but Butler gets about 90% of the screen time in the movie and plays it just convincingly enough to keep the whole production from swirling down the drain. This movie reminded me a lot of the film Armageddon, with a similarly ridiculous plot and out of place "hero" figure somehow stumble into saving the planet with seconds to spare. It's all rather silly, but the movie doesn't take itself too seriously and neither did I. There are definitely much worse ways to spend 90 minutes of your life. Try it. You might actually enjoy it as I did.

history.title: Ranma ½ - Set 1 (Special Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I have been a fan of Ranma 1/2 since the days when I could only find the odd VHS tape in my local movie stores. Mostly it was the dub, but sometimes I was lucky enough to find a tape in the original Japanese. Those were very different times for anime fans in America. Now, 20 years in the future we have the sets that we never could have imagined, but that the series always deserved. The show has never looked better, and I doubt it is possible to improve on what we have been given. Not only does it look beautiful and pristine, however, but the masters have not been tampered with. Gone are the American title cards of the old DVD sets, and they are replaced with the original Japanese shots with soft subtitles. I may be mistaken, but this set doesn't seem to have a single hard subtitle in it.. and for a fan of animation and the purity of the original material, that is a dream come true. This is a set that will please both the hardcore anime fans, and the casual viewer who isn't necessarily interested in the minute details. The extras are nothing to sneeze at as well. They are very well represented with this set, and a welcome addition for the animation historian. Finally, the packaging is absolutely gorgeous. It goes for that strong Chinese theme that is prevalent throughout the series. It fits and looks great on my shelf. Highly, highly recommended.

history.title: House of the Long Shadows
history.review_title: SHAMEFUL TREATMENT FOR A ONCE IN A LIFETIME FILM
history.text: For a horror movie fan this is a must-have: Vincent Price, Christopher Lee and the great Peter Cushing in the same film with John Carradine as the frosting on the cake. This is the only film in which the star of the Edgar Allan Poe films teams up with the signature stars of the Hammer classics. An extremely enjoyable film RUINED BY A CORPORATION THAT COULDN'T CARE LESS ABOUT ITS CUSTOMERS. The aspect ratio is full-frame, which is a slap in the face to any DVD buyer. The print is not remastered or color corrected in any way - blacks are a grainy green and the overall quality is slightly better than a home VHS of the movie recorded from an HBO broadcast. As mentioned in another review, there is even a 2 second FRAME MISSING message on a white screen 20 minutes into the movie as well as a couple of slight tape glitches here and there - not what you want to see when you're watching a DVD. I bought my copy for about half the asking price and I still feel cheated. NO MENU. NO CHAPTER SELECTION. Warner Archive limited release DVD-Rs are worth buying, but STAY AWAY FROM LIMITED RELEASE MGM DVD-Rs! THEY SUCK!

Sometimes you can see plot points coming from a mile away, but that doesn't spoil the overall effect of the film. The cgi triffids look very believable and they are carefully designed and animated. Although I think this production takes 2nd place to the BBC version it's still satisfying and well worth your time.

history.title: Dark Obsession
history.text: If you're looking for the movie with Gabriel Byrne and Amanda Donohoe, this is not it. Low budget production soft porn crime melodrama. I don't think the script is as bad as the other reviewer has described. Just when you think you're going to a real groaner of a cliché the next line is better than you thought it would be. The actors aren't horrible, either. This was probably shot in a week in real locations, so you get what you pay for. I've heard worse dialogue and seen worse acting in big-budget major releases. Still, the other reviewer is right about the packaging - the front of the DVD even has a photo of Sadie Frost from the Byrne/ Donohoe film. Sadie Frost is not on this DVD.

history.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 1 [Blu-ray]
history.text: I purchased this set on release date. I finally got around to watching disc 4, except that I was unable to view the programs. I was unable to get the disc to load on my Samsung BD-P1500. I was up to date on my firmware. The disc at first would spin and spin and lock up the player. I e-mailed Image to report the problem and received no response. Another update was available from Samsung and I updated the player again. The disc would spin and give me a written message that the disc was unplayable. I again e-mailed Image and still no response. Since Image is slow to acknowledge the problem and offer a solution, I returned the set for a full refund. I really wanted to keep this set as the visual quality is stunning. I cannot support a company that refuses to admit a mistake and offer to correct it.

history.title: Saboteur
history.text: Years ago when I was first discovering Hitchcock and all of his wonderful films, I happened upon this gem. I guess this was about 30+ years ago and I probably saw them on TCM. I was familiar with Robert Cummings from Dial M and some comedies he appeared in. I was also a big fan of St. Elsewhere and was excited to see that Norman Lloyd was featured in this. I had never seen this film before this time. I was amazed at how caught up in the story I became. I could see that this was dealing with one of Hitchcock's favorite themes, the "wrong" man. I wansn't looking for plot holes or any inconsistencies, I was just truly enjoying the film for the great yarn it is. It has remained one of my favorites and I am glad I now have this on blu-ray. Such a nice looking transfer of a very entertaining film. Glad to add this to my collection. Will be trying to add most of his films when I have the finances. Enjoyable film.

history.title: Psychic School Wars: Movie [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A Pretty Trainwreck of a Film
history.text: I'll start with saying this: this movie is pretty. The colors and visuals are great to look at. But just looking pretty doesn't make this a great or even good movie. The plot is a mess. Characters do things for reasons that aren't explained very well. The movie also doesn't seem to know what it wants to be. A light slice of life? A school romance? A mystery that the heroes have to solve? It has all these things yet when one scene is light and comedic then immediately followed by drama it gets jarring to say the least. The movie also expects to just already know things about the characters and backstory. Does some elements of the plot need to be further explained? Yes. Does the film explain why or how? Of course not. You should already know, duh. The film is based on a book to my knowledge and it has been adapted before, so maybe those other iterations have the answers this telling ommits? Maybe, but this story should stand on its own without the need to look into previous established lore in alternate versions. I should at least try to summarize the plot, too. There are a trio of friends, the generic male lead, his female childhood friend that is obviously in love with him yet he never notices, and her big breasted friend whom the male lead is in love with for reasons that aren't established. Then a mysterious transfer studint, who is totally not Kaworu from Eva, shows up and weird things start happening to their friends and other classmates. There is also some plot device about cell phones that goes no where. The characters are bland. Like really bland. The main lead has no interesting personality or any uniqueness. The childhood friend is a run of the mill tsundere trope, getting angry at lead boy but pine for him in secret. The big breasted girl, well has big breasts. And is, like, totes nice. And Kaworu is there too. Oh, wait, no I forgot, he's totes NOT Kaworu. Should you buy this film? No, I don't think so. It's worth a rent, I'll give it that, mostly for its pretty visuals.

history.title: Engaged to the Unidentified [Blu-ray]
history.text: Might have minor spoilers. If you're scrolling through Crunchyroll and are in the mood for a totally bland, boring series, then you've hit the jackpot! Engaged to the Unidentified is a bad series. It's boring, unfunny, not romantic and after finishing the series you're unlikely to remember any scenes or moments from this monitinous drag of an anime. The story centers around a generic 16 year old high schooler, like countless other anime heroines, who is to marry a mysterious person from her past. I'll just spoil the twist since it doesn't really matter and the series never uses the premise in any interesting manners. So the person that anime girl is engaged to is like a dog person. Or something like that. Cool, right? Not really, since this character is beyond boring and hardly ever speaks. If you think you're going to get a charming anime romcom; look elsewhere. The two leads have zero chemistry. There are of course, the whacky side characters such as dog person's annoying little sister (Who is clearly there to be the OMG Kawai! character) and anime girl's older sister, who has a little sister... fetish? And is the best character in the show; although she does get tedious at times. There are other characters as well, but none are particularly important nor memorable. The show tries to add some supernatural elements to the standard slice of life romcom anime but does so poorly. The fact that anime girl is engaged to a shapeshifting dog person is never explored in detail. Nor does the anime use that for comedic purposes. If the show never utilizes the bizarre nature of the situation, then what's the point? It just becomes an anime about a girl and a boy who can also shapshift, but never does. That's extreamly entertaining. Throughout the series the two leads never bond aside from dog person constantly saying he loves anime girl, but that's just lazy writing. I don't think this the worst anime of all time or anything but it certainly is not good. The show is just so generic and run of the mill without any outstanding personality that I can not in good faith recommend this anime. If you are looking for a similar anime that does a romcom far better than this, then I'd recommend School Rumble.

history.title: Plastic Little - The Adventures of Captain Tita (Essential Anime Collection) [DVD]
history.text: Plastic Little, an anime film that knows it's bad and relishes in that fact. The 'plot' follows Captain Tita, a 'pet shop hunter', as she comes across a girl, Elysse, on the run from some shady people and desides to help her out. The plot doesnt really matter in this anime as its main draw is its fan service (And there is a good amount!). The animation is good and fluid; looking like old school anime, or at least mid-90s anime. The characters aside from Tita and Elysse get very little to do, but with a run time of about an hour, I don't mind. There isn't much substance in Plastic Little and I doubt anyone involved with the project thought they were making the next Akira, but they did succeed in making a short, fun adventure anime. So if you're looking for something to watch and willing to turn your brain off for an hour, then Plastic Little won't let you down. The nudity is an added bonus..

history.title: Princess Jellyfish - Complete Series - S.A.V.E.
history.text: Princess Jellyfish is an enjoyable yet short anime that follows the daily lives of a group of nerdy, geeky women (Dubbed the Sisterhood) who live in the same apartment complex. Their lives get turned upside down when one member of the sisterhood befriends a charismatic male crossdresser who then decides to visit her complex. I would recommend this anime to anyone that enjoys whacky comedy as well as some romantic moments. The characters are all unique and have their own identity, be it loud and boisterous to quiet and timid. Princess Jellyfish is a very unique show and my summarization doesn't give the show justice. The animation is great, the characters are interesting, the general plot is good and the show has a very fun atmosphere. The only real issue I have with the show is that it leaves things very open ended. Like Berserk, one would have to pick up the manga to continue the story. That aside, I highly recommend this anime.

history.title: Love Chunibyo & Other Delusions - Heart Throb
history.text: The sequel to Love Chunibyo and Other Delusions, Heart Throb does not add new plot twists to the previous story and it continues along with the same slice of life formula of its predecessor. There is one new character, a girl that Yuuta knew in the past and may harbor feelings for him. There is a love triangle thing that occurs in this season, a few one off episodes dealing with the other main characters and that's about it. The relationship between Rikka and Yuuta is still trotting along slowly (A bit too slowly, but hey, they're new to this) there aren't any big romantic moments between them but they are still pretty cute together. Heart Throb is more episodic than the previous series but doesn't have such a confused vision of what it wants to be or what its message is. At its heart this is just a cute romcom anime with quirky characters and is a good watch for a quick pick me up. If you liked the first Chunibyo then you'd likely enjoy this as well. Just don't expect too much.

history.title: Shiki: The Complete Series [Blu-ray]
history.text: In Shiki residents of a small secluded village in Japan people begin dying off mysteriously after the arrival of a suspicious family. The village doctor Toshio Okazi tries to find the cause of these deaths and put an end to them even if he has to do some shady things in the process. Shiki is a slow show. Like really, really slow. I almost dropped the show multiple times but I convinced myself it would get better. It does get better in the second half as the story kicks in and the slow build pays off. The towns people start to fight back against the Shiki, vampire like creatures that were the cause of the random deaths. The show tries, however, to make the viewer sympathetic towards the Shiki by going over their own inner monologs and povs. It is hard to feel sympathy for them when they were the ones who attacked first. The show tries to make the viewers question the morality of both sides, human and Shiki. I don't think it works if you paint one side as villainous and evil only to then flip flop and say otherwise. The show's pace is slow and may be a turn off for some viewers and I completely understand. I would say watch a few episodes before you judge but you'd have to watch a lot to do so. I hesitantly recommend Shiki, but maybe read the summaries of the first few episodes as the show takes a while to get going. If you like these kinds of shows, and don't mind the snail's pace the show starts at, then by all means pick it up.

history.title: Dragon Ball Super: Part One
history.review_title: Retread of Battle of Gods with lower budget
history.text: If you've seen or own both Battle of Gods and Resurrection F then you can honestly ignore the first 2 arcs of Super. Unless you really want to watch Goku fight Beerus again (Only now with cheaper animation) along with a lot of filler, then go ahead and pick up this set. You're better off waiting for when the US releases finally get to the Universe 6 arc, or even better, the Goku Black arc. Super starts rather slow and it takes a while for it to pick up steam, but the show does get better and is now almost on par with the original DBZ in terms of action.

This is by far the best season of Pokemon since the original Kanto days. The animation is more stylized and doesn't look as generic as the previous seasons of the show. This series also has a more laid back tone, taking a more slice of life approach rather than having one continuous arc. I've watched episodes both in the original Japanese and the dubbed English and both are fine. There are some more mature episodes as well that surprised me and the drama wasn't put aside for unnecessary jokes. This a fun show and is the first Pokemon series to actually feel like an anime.

history.title: Boys Be... Box Set
history.text: This anime is a mess. Boys Be... is a romantic/comedy anime that follows 3 boys as they enter the world of dating. There are a variety of girls that the boys interact with, some resulting in romance, some in heartbreak. That so far is fine, but the issue is that there are far too many side characters that the main trio are overshadowed and left underdeveloped. For the first few episodes it's like a new girl every episode that simply disappears in the next with no mention of said character. The animation itself is poor at best and frequently the characters are off model. The ending too is not an ending, rather the series just stops. There are no resolutions or any real feeling of growth for the characters (Two in particular are especially infuriating). The show would have benefited with more episodes and less side characters. I don't particularly think this is an anime that absolutely deserves a purchase, but if you want a series that builds then abruptly stops, then you may like this anime.

history.text: I saw 7 men from now when I was a kid then several times in the 60's with always the same passion. Then this chef d'oeuvre disappeared and became a much sought after for all the western fans all over the world. At last, this great film is available on DVD and in a glorious edition, carefully restored and with lots of fascinating bonus. What is amazing me the most for a film dating from 50 year is its sheer modernity and the masterful work done by all involved, whether director Budd Boetticher or actors Randolph Scott, Lee Marvin or Gail Russell. Dont miss this masterpiece at any rate!

history.title: Piche Entre Ciel Et Terre
history.text: Ce film épouse avec un grand bonheur toute la complexité d'un remarquable destin humain, celui de Piché, héros de l'aviation civile, soudain détruit par le retour de son passé et qui, à la force de sa volonté, se reconstruit. Justesse de ton, magnifique interprétation de Michel Coté et Maxime Leflaguais, très belles scènes d'avion... Un grand film québecois. Il serait bon que pour nous autres "Français de France" et sans doute les Canadiens anglophones qui veulent parfaire leur français, les films québecois soient systématiquement sous-titrés en français. Ces grands films québecois sont étonnamment méconnus en France et jamais ou presque disponibles en DVD Zone 2. la faute en est certainement à la France qui ne s'intéresse pas suffisamment à ces Américains pourtant cousins mais n'y a t il pas aussi une autre politique plus dynamique à l'export des responsables du film québecois. Un film comme Piché n'est nullement un film "régionaliste", il résume les aléas de l'ame humaine et devrait plaire à des spectateurs du monde entier.

history.title: Gangster Squad
history.text: I am surprised that apparently no one has noticed how this "new" gangster film is so influenced by some 1940's serials, particularly the great William Witney serial classic "G-Men vs Black dragon". In many scenes, you find blatant modernisations of some of the most memorable twists and turns from the serial. Josh Brolin has even the look and the hair style of Rod Cameron who starred in "G-Men". When you understand that filiation, Gangster squad is a very enjoyable film on his own, of course very different from the contemporary gangster films. The only drawback is Sean Penn's grotesque mimicks.

history.title: Four Fast Guns
history.text: This little known B-Western (in Scope and Black & White) adds to a classic plot a very dramatic edge. The false town tamer (James Craig who had killed the real one and takes his place) has to wipe out the town from a crippled saloon owner who seems to hire any gunslinger in the whereabouts. Usual western script... where we see Craig killing one by one all those supposed to kill him. Until the last one who happens to be his one kid brother (Brett Halsey)! Of course William Hope whoever he is ain't Anthony Mann who would certainly had made a masterpiece out of this script and this small budget western. But this is anyway a strong enough little western that should be seen by hardcore western fans. Sound and image are average. For foreigners, note that this series are zone free and with english subtitles.

history.title: The Borgias: Season 3
history.review_title: Remarkable series! Abnd more: this series is very ...
history.text: Remarkable series! Abnd more: this series is very faithfull to what really happened as far as we know of course. Well, whatever we can think about how the plot had to be handled in this fourth season, it must be said that The Borgias was for the most very faithfull of what we know of the history of Italian Renaissance in general and The Borgias family in particular. Some facts have of course been eluded, romanced, some characters don't appear in the fiction (There were two more Rodrigo Borgia's sons who also had a part in the rules of Rome) but overall it's remarkably faithfull to the real story. One thing anyway: some people were shocked about the incestuous affair between Cesare and Lucrezia but there were more than that: Giovanni, Lucrezia's baby, was said to have been The Pope's son for we have strong suspicions of an incestuous relationship between Borgia and her daughter...

history.title: Vikings Season 3
history.review_title: Good epic but not so historically accurate
history.text: As good as this series is as an epic drama, it should be known that there area lot of historical inaccuracies: Odo is of course Comte Eudes who will defend successfully Paris against the Vikings' raids and will launch a new dynasty of Kings of France, the Capetiens who will reign until Louis XVI and even Charles X (1830). Rollo (Rollon) in historical reality has nothing to do with Ragnar and he effectively will obtain a territory of France but in 911 after marrying French King Charles le Simple's daughter and being baptized as well as all his troops comprising Vikings and Saxons alike. He will become Robert and only his great grandson will be crowned Duke of Normandy in 987, vassal of King of France. Their descendant William the Conqueror (Guillaume Le Conquérant) will conquer England in 1087. As the first season of Vikings starts in 795, all those historical events are mixed a lot...

history.title: Vikings: Season 4 Vol 2 (us) [DVD]
history.text: This series about the Saga of Ragnar was largely remarkable until Season 3 with great filmings, actings and mostly accurate historical details about the life of the Vikings (although the chronological events were certainly not accurate!). Unfortunately, the first part of Season 4 was not that successful despite a great moment during the Seine's battle between Ragnar and his brother Rollo (of course Rollo wasn't at all a Ragnar's kinfolk and lived almost a century after Ragnar!). And now this Season 4 Volume 2 is a big let down. It drags interminably before the death of Ragnar that occurs during the 5th episode and many characters come inexplicably from nowhere, adding nothing to the very dragging plot. Moreover, with the exception of Bjorn, Ragnar's sons seem to come directly from the fountain soda of a teenager party and actors are really poor, particularly Ivar the Boneless who perpetually winces to make sure he is a very very mean man. Lagherta makes her revenge but becomes unexpectedly a lesbian (?) while Floki seems fascinated by Algesiras'Mosque in a particularly grotesque scene. The final battles are way better and bring at last some driving action to the series. As the authors of those Vikings (Seasons 1-3 are very good) are for a 5th and 6th Season, let's hope it will be much better than this mostly poor 4th Season.

history.title: Ocean's 11 (50th Anniversary) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Beautiful high-definition picture for this remastered blu-ray. Gorgeous color and just new-looking, feels like it actually takes you back to 1959 and 1960, when this film was made and released, respectively. Everything seems so current as to viewing it-- while the cars, clothes, and other styles are still clearly from those bygone days. I won't comment on the plot and production values since many others have done so, just wanted to note that this Blu-ray picture quality is amazing.

history.title: The Beverly Hillbillies: The Official Fourth Season
history.review_title: Beautiful, new-looking picture quality; and has English subtitles
history.text: Picture-perfect-- beautiful picture quality, vivid color; an extremely sharp, clean picture, thus BRAND-NEW-looking episodes. Also, they have very accurate English subtitles, unlike Season 2 (which has no subtitles), which I'm currently watching also. The only negative for this Season 4: most of the episodes this season have thin plots and aren't very funny or interesting. The exceptions would be the two about Possum Day/Granny running for Possum Queen, which were quite funny. Beautiful Sharon Tate, tragically a victim of the Manson Family murders in 1969, appears as a bank employee in the first two or three episodes of this season (and was in quite a few episodes in the preceding seasons, mostly in that role but also in others). As to Season 4 plots: on the other hand, they are superior to those in Season 2, which as I'd noted above, I am watching simultaneously, and the acting is more loose and relaxed in Season 4, esp. from Max Baer as Jethro and Irene Ryan as Granny-- resulting in funnier delivery of their lines and overall better episodes, I feel. Highly recommend.

history.title: The Rodgers & Hammerstein Collection [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Beautiful Hi-Definition picture quality, simply amazingly so on OKLAHOMA (the Todd AO version)
history.text: Beautiful hi-definition picture quality, simply amazingly so on OKLAHOMA (the Todd AO version). THE SOUND OF MUSIC and SOUTH PACIFIC also have beautiful hi-definition picture quality, although the longer SOUTH PACIFIC disc has numerous playability problems on my Sony Blu-ray player, making it useless. Oklahoma's alternate version is of decent hi-def quality, but nothing in the same ballpark as its Todd AO version. THE KING AND I, CAROUSEL, and STATE FAIR look excellent as to their hi-definition picture, though a cut below the unbelievably brilliant-looking OKLAHOMA Todd AO version. THE SOUND OF MUSIC doesn't have the additional disc of extras that comes with the Blu-ray version bought alone (I bought that one a couple of years ago). Recommend this blu-ray set.

history.title: Commitments, The
history.review_title: Excellent picture quality, even on a high-def TV! (2004 2-disc version)
history.text: Note: this review is for the 2004 2-disc version, which is the best DVD version of this film. Unusual, excellent movie about a 1960s soul music band put together in the 1990s by a young local in Ireland, and the working-class band's ups and downs, along with his own personal travails. The band has more than 10 members, incl. 3 pretty female backup singers (2 of whom occasionally sing lead), so various subplots and tensions play out. Extremely entertaining, constantly funny, and if it weren't for the unnecessary persistent use of foul language and an arguably gratuitous sex scene (where no nudity was shown), this would be a great movie for the entire family. Very funny, quite enjoyable, very musical, keeps your interest the entire time, and lots of great 1960s American soul music is played throughout by very talented people. This is the definitive version of the DVD to purchase, and I own several different versions. This one shows the movie in anamorphic widescreen (unlike some other versions in 4x3), and has been remastered to have an extremely sharp picture, yes, even on a high-definition TV. The Blu-ray is about to be released, and I'm curious if they can get the picture quality appreciably better than is seen here, because this is really an excellent, sharp, colorful picture for DVD, even on a high-definition TV set, which ordinarily makes DVDs look pretty mediocre (I always prefer Blu-rays when available, which are made in Hi-def because they are intended for Hi-def TVs). This 2-disc set has the most extras available for any DVD version of this movie (it has 2 or 3 on the making of the film), and is the definitive DVD version. UPDATE 5/02/2017 - The picture quality of the Blu-ray is essentially identical to the above 2004 2-disc DVD version. As much as I prefer Blu-rays, it's virtually impossible to see any upgrade in picture quality for the BR when comparing both versions on a Hi-Def TV, unfortunately. The bit rate of the Blu-ray is higher, but my eyes don't really see any better picture.
