history.title: Passengers
history.text: I didn't know what expect from a romantic sci-fi, but anybody could enjoy this! I took a risk buying it before I saw it, but I'm really glad I did! I thought the acting was superb & it was easy to get invested in the plot. Very creative and heartfelt!

history.review_title: So glad to own this one!
history.text: I love this movie!! I love the characters, the music and the beauty of the ocean, the beaches, The rich colors of trees, flowers, etc. The story kept my interest and there were many touching moments. It might just be my favorite Disney movie!

I chose this for movie night with my husband. My husband only watched a half hour before he went to bed. He couldn't take Denzel's ridiculous ranting and raving any longer. I watched the whole movie. Watch Fences if you want to see Denzel Washington play the part of a mysogenist, narcissistic, selfish father and husband. He was quite the ugly character. And poor Viola Davis' character. I was hoping her character would develop from enabling doormat into something empowering. She stands back and watches her son be bullied by his dad through the son's whole life.... and then bullies that son into attending his dad's funeral. There was nothing redeeming about Denzel's character. And Viola Davis' character was delusional. I don't think anyone grew in this movie but maybe the son through no help at all from his parents. I don't recommend this. If you read the positive reviews and feel like you relate more to those reviewers, give it a try.

history.title: BEAUTY AND THE BEAST
history.text: I am giving this movie three stars because it was an emotional experience watching it. I liked the backstory added in about Belle's Mom. It was heart wrenching watching the candlestick, teapot, clock, etc. turn into lifeless objects. I like how they showed them coming back to life after the spell was broken. Kind of a Toy Story 3 moment. It was touching! What I didn't like was Emma Watson's portrayal of Belle. In another review, someone said she was playing herself more than Belle. That was the feeling I got. I felt like she held back from showing emotion giving a flatter, awkward performance. For me, her performance was detached from the feelings she was trying to portray. Her singing was SO processed with auto tune that it was distracting. Her singing (on this movie) also lacked range and depth. I like Emma Watson as an actress, but Disney's choice in casting her was a mistake in my opinion. I love the actress Gugu Mbatha-Raw in other movies and think she would’ve made a great Belle! She came to mind because was in Beauty and the Beast as the feather duster. I know a woman of color would likely be rejected for this role, but I just thought her performance would have been more compelling. I wish I had rented this movie instead of bought it.

history.title: Southside With You [DVD]
history.text: This was a bit hard to get into. I like this couple, and I liked watching Michelle finally let her guard down by the end. It was a let down, personally, because it lacked heart. Boring, stilted, formal dialogue. Very serious. Lack of chemistry. Barack seemed to be analyzing Michelle to see if she was First Lady material. I'm sure he wasn't thinking that in real life, but this movie's version of their first date seemed like one big test to see if Michelle would fit the mold. Barack's character was more likable, and Michelle's was defensive and so serious. I have to think they can let loose better than that in real life. This movie was interesting for the info learned about their first date and their early start. But there was nothing special.
I really loved this! It was very moving & I loved watching Lee's testimony unfold. A meaningful movie!!
This was a ridiculous waste of time.

Poor acting, average looks & just trying to rip off the 80s. Unless you really just having nothing to do & want your brain to rot, this is the movie for you.
It was a good fun movie. Had some good laughs, Dolph was good at the lead. It didn't try to be PC/SJWish (like almost other movie out there), just a plain ol' good horror movie.

history.title: Stonehenge Apocalypse
history.review_title: Pretty good end of the world movie.
history.text: While nothing super great, it was pretty good. pacing was pretty good and they tried to make semi-plausible. The productions values were decent, especially for a SCi_Fi Channel movie - back when they made decent movies.

This is one of the best Sherlock Holmes I have ever seen. The scripts are excellent, the story interesting and the actors portraying Holmes and Watson have the characters down pat. Highly recommended.

This is one of the worst movies I've ever seen ... and I like shlock! There is no actual acting anywhere in the film. It's as if the people hired to play parts are reading their lines off cue cards. Lines are delivered with almost no emotional content and what there is tends to be completely wrong. The screenwriter needs to wake up and take a hard look around. Many of the actions taken in the film make no rational sense. While I completely understand the need for literary devices, they should at least have some grounding in the real world. I have no idea why some reviewers gave this movie high marks. Perhaps they watched a different film. If I could have, I would've given this movie zero stars.

history.title: Burlesque
history.text: If the critics hate something, that usually means I would love it. This movie follows that rule nicely. It is 2 hours of pure escapism with wonderful songs, marvelous dance numbers and a reasonable plot. Cher comes through like the trooper she is. It's hard to believe she's 65 years old! The real surprise for me though was Christina Aquilera--such a big voice in such a small package. I hope to see her in other movies. To the critics who hate this movie let me say this, remember the old adage about opinions. It certainly applies to you.

history.review_title: Almighty Thor? Not by a long shot.
history.text: I agree with K. Harris, a very poorly conceived movie done in a technically awkward manner. Hardly worth the $4 rental price.

I had several problems with this movie. First, the entire movie was filmed with a soft focus. I can understand something like that for dream scenes, but not for a while movie. Second, the main characters seemed unable to work at a burger joint let alone as a specialized team searching for survivors in an area contaminated with a deadly toxin. The team leader showed no leadership ability at all. The other three members were completely unable to follow simple orders. Third, the movie made little to no effort to explain what was happening to the team and the ending made no sense. Now some people like movies that leave most of the details to the viewer's imagination--I'm not one of them. Finally, the movie is incredibly slow paced. A lot of screen time is given to scenes that added nothing to what plot there is. In one scene, a character took over two minutes to search a small three stall restroom. Of course in the middle of the scene we were treated to him deliberately peeing all over one of the toilets. That added so much to the plot of the film--NOT! If you enjoy movies like this one, then get the popcorn ready. For those who don't, save your money and your time and give this one a miss.
This might have been a good movie except that I missed a lot of it reading the subtitles. That seriously detracted from the experience.
Let me clearly state that I did not watch this movie, the 1 star rating is based solely on the rental fee. I will never watch any movie that costs $150 to rent. That is a ridiculous price.

history.review_title: Good movie for taking a nap
history.text: Saying that this movie is slow would be an understatement. Molasses moves faster. I'm usually a bit leary of films written and directed by the same person and in this case I was right to be. Somehow I managed to watch the first 40 minutes without completely falling asleep. After that I started fast forwarding. As one reviewer said, it's an interesting concept done with very poor execution.

history.review_title: Most boring movie I've ever seen
history.text: I rented this film based on reviews from other viewers. Alas, it wasn't for me. It is slow, really slow until the last ten minutes when things pick up. Also, it was presented as a SciFi movie but what science there is in it is mostly wrong. I won't go into detail as that would be the equivalent of spoilers. If you've got a couple of hours you don't mind losing you may enjoy this film.
I love it!

targets.title: Led Zeppelin: The Song Remains the Same (Two-Disc Special Edition)

history.text: 5 Golden Globe nominations? Really? This was like watching paint dry. There is one - count them, ONE, scene worth seeing in the whole movie. The rest is just dull and dry. It's made even more so by the awful sound track. Whoever did the sound has no ear for pacing, mood, or emotion. The music was so distracting- like nails on a chalk board. And is it a rule that every Affleck movie set in the Boston area has to have ten f-bombs per minute? It's so excessive. I used to live in Boston and people don't talk that way.
Too many f-bombs. Jeez. Is that really necessary? Affleck always looks like the same character in every movie. He's kind of whiny and pathetic. He doesn't make a strong "hero."

history.title: Beyond Borders
history.text: This rates a solid 3 1/2 stars for me. I thought it was a unique story, but it fell a bit flat in the storytelling department. Actually the "telling" part is what kept it from being better. I felt I was being led by the nose when the story was good enough to just let me get there on my own. The love story dwarfed the aid story. Had they been more intertwined, I think that would have made it better as well.

history.title: Snow Flower and the Secret Fan
history.text: This is a story of the deep love between girls and women. I wanted to love this. I think there were some things that were too subtle while others hit you over the head unnecessarily. The movie jumped around a lot making it hard to stay connected as well. It jumped a lot between Chinese and English too. While I appreciated that it wasn't entirely subtitled, language makes a difference in feeling and so many other things that I don't think it was a great choice. Anyway, it was really different so I am glad I watched it. It left me with a lot of questions and thoughts. I like movies that do that.

history.title: The Crown: Season 1 [DVD]
history.text: The series is well done. The interesting part is that it's about real people. The dull part is that it's about really dull people who have absolutely nothing to do with the real life of 99.99999% of us. I mean the main character is a woman whose sister even says she has no character and she says she has the type of face that, if she's not smiling, she looks cross. It's like watching an automaton. Do you care what happens to an automaton? It's so unrelatable. It just feels like celebrity peeping or reality tv on a different social level. I was ready to turn it off before the series ended.

history.title: Line of Duty, Series 4
history.text: Brilliant writing. After 4 seasons I expect ideas to get stale, but this doesn't disappoint. It covers a wide range of humanity and gives lots of twists and turns. It stayed "edge-of-your-seat" fun until the end.

This is a light, modern look at the themes of Jane Austen. In the story, a present day woman in her 30s is infatuated with Austen romance. She uses her life savings to go to an emersion resort to live in the Austen days and be romanced by an actor. She gets the cheap package while two other guest have the Platinum experience. Our Jane gets to really experience the life of the Jane Austen characters who never had any money. It doesn't turn out to be all its cracked up to be, but the experience leaves her and the viewer completely enchanted. The writing does a good job of showing the Austen themes in modern romance. It also blends a bit of realism with a huge dose of comedy. The actors did a great job. I'm smitten!

It took me a while to join the GoT bandwagon. I found it hyper sexual, violent, and the characters weren't all that likable. Once I got past that, I loved all the twists and turns. There was so many surprises. The characters were deep, complex, and experienced growth. No one was safe from the ax. Season 7 is good, but it's definitely a kinder, gentler version. It feels really different. The others had a flow to them. You knew that episode 9 was going to have a big explosion and episode 10 would bring it all together, but also have a cliff hanger or teaser. There are only 7 episodes in this season, so that's the first shocker. Jon's a broken record. He bangs one drum, "The walk walkers are coming." He has always been a sort of one hit wonder dullard, so I suppose that's no surprise, but he has a lot of screen time in this one so it does get old. The surprise romance (I won't say between who) is not all that hot or sexy. No chemistry. It's predictable, but not an "ooohhhh! moment. A lot of banners change sides or are annihilated. Nothing all that dramatic there. Many characters meet their demise. There are no cross bow on the toilet "gotcha" moments. They are original but not the stuff you talk about the next day. Bran is now a dullard too. The Three Eyed raven has no personality. Bleh. This season is good, but it feels like it just tidied up a bit too quickly. It feels like a rush to the end of the series instead of simply telling the tale. It's like checking boxes: what happens to X, Y and Z. And it feels like most of the characters are war weary and old. They've lost a lot of zest. Where is the fire? Still good, just a kinder, gentler version.

This is a solid movie that suffers from a horrible title. I avoided this because the title seemed so "blah." The story is solid though. It's long, but you don't feel the time pass. You aren't sure what is going to happen, but it all seems plausible. The suspense is there right up until the end. It's well acted and well done. Bravo!

history.title: Victoria & Abdul [Blu-ray]
history.text: Great story. I found it interesting from a human interest perspective and also a historical perspective. I can't imagine what it must be like to have zero privacy and surrounded by haughty people you don't like. Abdul (like Mr. Brown before him) must have been a breath of fresh air. Good for Victoria for saying to h*ll with convention and letting herself enjoy life. The on screen chemistry between Dench and Ali was wonderful. You can so totally see how the queen could have been captivated by him.

history.title: After Armageddon
history.text: It kept me entertained. The movie touched on several issues, including the risk of serious infection from a small cut to vigilante justice. It's sure to raise some hairs on the back of your neck without scaring you half to death. If it sparks the viewer to contemplate their response to such a scenario, then the movie has done it's job. My only complaint is that it wasn't long enough. Considering the subject matter, it easily could have been extended another 30 minutes or more.

history.title: Manor House
history.text: Were it not for Lady Anna, Sir John, the cook and Edgar the Butler, this series may have flopped. Each of those four characters, though hated for it, adhered to Edwardian rules of the era. They demanded the same from all house staff, much to the staff's displeasure. What I found most interesting was the joy and laughter the overworked and penniless house staff attained during their hardship. The rich master and lady rarely smiled as they fulfilled their stuffy roles as a filthy rich Edwardian couple. All-consumed with putting forth the proper image to friends and associates, the parents had no time for Guy, their youngest son. Guy found love, happiness and comradeship in the basement with the "lowly" house staff who, no matter how burdened they were with work, always had time for the boy. We enjoyed this series very much. It's a DVD we'll watch over and over.

history.title: The Book of Daniel (DVD)
history.text: The sound quality isn't good, nor is the lighting. I needed to apply the captions to understand what was being said. The entire picture was darker than it needed to be. The acting is good, but the story moves at a snail's pace, jumping from the present to the past. There is very little action. The actors do little more than sit or stand in one place and deliver their lines. The movie actually put me to sleep a couple of times. It's an OK film, but I'll never watch this DVD again.

history.title: Children Of Men
history.text: If there is a redeeming quality to this depressing mess, I missed it. I keep wondering why anyone in his right mind would write this, produce it or act in it. It's mankind's futuristic plunge into barbarism, violence, filth, misery, despair... and the only glimmer of hope for humanity is a newborn baby who won't stop its agonizing crying once it's born. The sudden cessation of war when soldiers stopped killing everybody long enough to bow down and permit the newborn miracle baby to safely pass was laughable at best. After wallowing through almost two hours of blood and guts, shattering gunfire, screams, blood gushing out of heads and chests, grimaces and a non-stop wailing newborn that I wanted to strangle into silence, the movie suddenly ends. It's one of the most depressing movies I've ever seen, and it had absolutely no point.

Since when is the life of our president, or anyone else for that matter, worth more than America itself? If the terrorists kill our president, we'll all boo-hoo the moment, then we'd go elect another. Big deal. In Olympus Has Fallen, Asian terrorists were unknowingly invited to the White House. When the attack began outside on the lawn, the American president and his secret service, against protocol, brought his guests into the president's underground safety bunker. That's exactly where the Asian terrorists wanted to be. Oh, brother! Our government, national security and military looked like a bunch of clueless buffoons who were outmaneuvered, outgunned and outwitted at every turn. The standing president (Freeman) is faced with obeying terrorist demands which will save the president's life, but sign America's death warrant. Pah-leeze! This movie rates a zero on the believable scale. I give it two-stars for the acting. If you love violence and high-tech weapons that rip people apart and splatter blood and gore all over the place, this movie is for you. It's all action, brutality and tension. Unfortunately the plot is as old as dust... so if you enjoy a plausible story line, as I do, avoid this movie. I give it two stars because of the decent acting.

history.title: The Homesman
history.text: This film is mostly a slow mover with too many rape/sex scenes. One-scene in particular is very disturbing due to the manner in which a newborn baby was murdered. You'll know the scene when you see it. You'll never forget it. Meryl Streep didn't appear until that tail end of this movie about three insane women being transported across the plains by "desperate-for-a-husband" Hillary Swank and grisly, loner Tommy Lee Jones. The duo encountered several obstacles along the way, but the encounters were boring and nothing we haven't seen. Towards the end something shocking happened that I hadn't expected or anticipated it. Suddenly Jones was thrust into the lead roll, and for me, the movie soared after that. I'm not sure why. Maybe it's because Swank was as dull as the desperate and plain Cuddy character she played. Maybe it's because Swank's character held Jones back. This certainly isn't a great flick, but it's worth a watch. I doubt I'll ever watch this again.

history.title: Three Kings
history.text: According to writer and producer David O. Russell, Three Kings is a true story. That seems far-fetched, but who am I to say it isn't. I enjoyed it whether it's fiction or fact. Three Kings is the perfect blend of drama, action and comedy. Clooney, Wahlberg and Ice Cube are in top form as gold hunters turned humanitarians.

history.title: Star Trek: The Original Series - The Complete Series
history.review_title: Impressive, but there's No English Subtitles for the Hearing Impaired.
history.text: This is the first time I’ve noticed the brilliance of colors on the control panels and walls of the Star Trek set. The picture is vivid, sharp and clear. Even when I increase the picture to “widescreen”, very little clarity is lost. It’s amazing what they've done to this old TV series. The audio is perfect. The discs are all silver and plain, but I’m sure that’s what helped keep the costs down. Each episode runs approximately 50 minutes, the standard time for an hour-long program in the 60s. Younger viewers will notice footage that’s never been shown in the television repeats today. Any Star Trek TV fan would be honored to own this set. So far I’ve only watched the first two episodes, but I’m thrilled beyond measure with this purchase. I bought my boxed set at Walmart. It's unfortunate that the producers chose to ignore America's hearing-impaired population. The subtitles are only in Spanish and French.

history.title: The Classic Sci-fi Ultimate Collection (Tarantula / The Mole People / The Incredible Shrinking Man / The Monolith Monsters / Monster on the Campus)
history.text: Monolith Monsters is the reason I purchased this set. Loved it when I was a kid. Love it now. As soon as I saw that big fish, I remembered Monster on Campus. It scared me when I was a kid. It entertains me today. The special effects of Tarantula and The Incredible Shrinking Man are amazing. Boy, what they did with light and shadow back then, not to mention camera angles. Beautiful workmanship. I don't remember the Mole People. That's probably because it was as boring back then as it was today. I didn't care for it. The picture and sound quality are wonderful. Fans of the old SciFi movies won't be disappointed with this purchase.

history.title: Roger Corman's The Wasp Woman
history.text: The picture and sound quality are dreadful. The storyline is OK, but there are much better sci-fi productions from the 50s and 60s. Wasp Woman is predictable and boring, and it's almost impossible to hear what's being said. Maybe if the movie were cleaned up and enhanced it might pass for a decent flick. Look around for a better DVD. This one is like cracking open a colorful egg on Easter morning and finding it rotten.

history.title: Black Swan
history.text: This movie had a lot of chances to get things right, and messed up most of them. 1.The dancer's life. Nina is a dancer, sort of. She doesn't seem to have any passion for it. Where _A Chorus Line_ or _Billy Elliott_ had you rooting for the poor dancer to make it because of the passion felt for dancing, Nina just seems to show up. She wants to WIN, she wants to get the part, but she doesn't seem to want to dance. So I can't root for her there. 2.The plot of _Swan_Lake_. Uhm. The Black Swan is not the slutty Bizarro world White Swan. The Prince falls for her (Odile) because he thinks she is the sweet Odette. It's a pivotal part of the movie, and it's all wrong. 3.The dialogue. Dear god, I don't know if I've heard anything this stiff and overwrought since _The Brady Bunch_. Marcia Marcia Marcia! I pity the actors that had to say these things. 4.The costumes. Again, obvious and overdone. Nina in pink and white, even wearing a white feather scarf? Really? 5.Basic medicine. Dancing well with glass in your abdomen is unlikely. OK if you want me to suspend my disbelief and just go for the creepy otherworld feel, you have to give me a character to feel for, and there isn't one. But I liked the soundtrack. The soundtrack was an excellent blend of classical and modern.

history.title: Barbie: The Princess & The Popstar [DVD]
history.review_title: Be true to your glitzy self.
history.text: When I get a Barbie adaptation of a story, I am not expecting a faithful retelling. But I don't think it is too much to ask for them to get an inkling of the basic message right. This retelling of Prince and the Pauper misses the point that being poor sucks. The princess and the pop star are each well-off, gorgeous, blah blah blah. It is really more of a City Mouse, Country Mouse than Prince and the Pauper. Gritting my teeth at the changed message was bad enough: this has got to be the worst written song collection I have ever experienced. "When I was young, I played for fun..." Listen. That doesn't rhyme. The approximate rhymes are atrocious. Let me remind you that this is for an age group learning to read, and approximate rhymes hinder the learning of that skill. "Here I am!!! Burning like a spark!" (A spark isn't burning.) "Spark! Light up the DARK again!" (Sparks don't light up the dark.) Lazy, lazy lazy. The usual Barbie message of "Be true to yourself, as long as you are well-off, tall, slender, and white" is intact. Goody. My daughter, who got this out of the library, is tall and blonde and therefore can't see how insulting the message is. So she happily dances around the house singing the horrible songs. Two stars for the sheer enjoyment my target-audience daughter experiences.

history.title: The African Queen
history.review_title: Hardly seems worth adding to the praise but it earns it!
history.text: I saw the movie, read the book, then saw the movie again. Probably, now that I have the context, one of the top ten novel-to-movie adaptations ever. The changes they made in the story for the movie were mostly for the good: Rather than trying to make Bogart learn a cockney accent (accents were not his thing) they made the character Canadian. Works fine. They happied up the ending a bit--not much, really, if you read the book the ending is kind of open, but this is inarguably happy. Don't know why they insisted on Robert Morley for the brother--that was a misstep. He's great, really, except the book does make more sense, wherein he is as scrawny as Rose, and dying of disease before the Germans arrive. A great touch in the movie is NOT providing subtitles for the Germans. (In the book Rose spoke German, but since in the movie she does not, avoiding subtitles makes most of us as clueless as movie-Rose when the Germans are talking, which is a lovely device that unites us with the protaganist.) After Charlie and Rose consumate their relationship--did they or didn't they? they DID--the dialog is so funny, and altered cleverly from the book. Rose realizes after calling him "dear" that she doesn't know his first name, finds it out and reacts. In the book it's an internal dialog, "She thought 'Charles' was a very nice name indeed," and in the movie she smugly says, "Oh, that's a NICE name." Hilarious. (Hmm. Wouldn't have thought Hepburn for a champion of hook-up culture. ;) ) The special effects (1-D mosquitoes, model boat on river) didn't fool my eight year old, but that's OK. This was a long time ago. The couple's delight as they each find joy in being with another person is so fresh and beautiful--as if neither of them had ever realized it before. That's great acting, putting life into it beyond that in the book and better than the script itself.

history.title: The Wiggles: Taking Off
history.text: My child is old enough to give up the Wiggles, and frankly, I thought the new line up would facilitate the break up. It isn't after all, the organic coming together of a few Early Childhood Ed students, as the first line up was. Surprise! We like it! Simon's booming voice is great! Emma, in the yellow shirt, takes the wheel and is not regulated to "token female" in what they give her to do.Lachy is, uhm cute, and it is clear they all really like children. (Emma gave an interview wherein she said there was no audition; the original Wiggles picked the replacements by watching how the chorus people interacted with kids at concerts). BEST of all, they've returned to their roots--by this I mean, thank goodness, REAL SETS, simple and easy on the eyes, and the group back to interacting with children on camera. (Those glitzy years of green screen and adult dancers took a toll on my child's affection for the group.) A couple quibbles--they are whiter than ever--this in a country with a high Asian population and Aboriginal population. Dorothy the dinosaur has been considerably slimmed down. And no, sorry, ONE female is not enough. In the new lineup it was high time for a group that more closely resembled the world's population. But good enough, entertaining enough, kind enough, educational enough, that my child who can already read and write likes it, a lot.

history.title: Free to Be...You and Me
history.text: I was in grade school when this came out, and our music teacher had us watch the special in class. I liked it so much that I got the 8 track and played it incessantly for years. Now my daughter is old enough for it. And it is pretty good. But in a lot of ways "Free to Be . . . You and Me" doesn't stand the test of time. In some ways it's a victim of society's changes. "William's Doll" was revolutionary at the time this came out, but my 8 year old doesn't see why a boy having a doll is such a big deal, and anyway kids are not allowed (thank heavens) to chase each other around yelling "sissy!" these days. In some ways it isn't progressive enough, Mommies and Daddies are people? Well, that's kinda binary. There are so many people in families that aren't hinted at in this special supposedly about how everyone is great. Also, the racial inclusion is kinda forced. If the piece isn't specifically about inclusion, this isn't especially inclusive. The "boy" and "girl" puppets voiced by Mel Brooks and Marlo Thomas are pretty darned white. Atalanta remains great, the art, the story, the voice acting. "When We Grow Up" is sweet, even though it enforces, rather than blasting, gender norms. In general, the pretty good messages are obscured by dated visuals and you are better off getting the CD, which also allows you to hear some of the great parts not animated for this special.

history.title: Frozen
history.text: Because people were doing so many backflips over this, I didn't expect it to live up to the impossibly great hype. It has been billed as the feminist Disney film, the one we've all been waiting for, entertaining! musical! Fun! Quibbles first: If going for a pro-female demographic, well, uhm, try harder next time. The only females with lines were the sisters. Yeah, I know, they are the principals. But as soon as that quota was filled the script went back to Everybody That Matters Is a Guy. Guy reindeer. Guy that runs the trading post/sauna. Guy good snow creature. Guy bad snow creature. King, not Queen, gets the lines. Grandfather troll (although the female trolls did get to sing). [spoiler] Speaking of the grandfather troll, he's the Glinda of this movie, not bothering to point out that the right application of love could have controlled the problem from day one. THANKS, dude. And why did the mountain man have to be a big blond Denmarkian rather than an Inuit? Oh. Cuz everybody that matters is a WHITE guy. OK. OK, you'll see I did give this 4 stars, so now that the complaints are over, here's what I loved about it: The music, and especially the lyrics, are unexpected and lovely. Nice balance of songs to dialogue, and songs that really advance the plot. Great development of relationship between Kristof and Anna. Nice complicated personality in Elsa. Nice turncoat of initial hero. Wonderful gay moments in the sauna, when the owner waves to his family. The plot is as thin as an onion skin, and owes very little to the Snow Queen referenced in the credits. But the relationships in this movie are wonderful and ultimately loving and freeing. The look and feel are gorgeous. And the two 8 year olds I saw this film with loved every minute of it.

history.title: Scooby-Doo (Full Screen Edition)
history.review_title: Scooby Doo meets Into the Woods
history.text: It was great. Calculated, clever, and great. Knowing that the audience would probably be a lot of adults who enjoyed the cartoons as kids, the writers combined things we love about the cartoon with the obvious flaws: what would Fred REALLY do for a living if the gang broke up? What would a Velma journey of self-discovery look like? Best of all, they took the most hated SD villain of all time (and I don't mean the Black Knight Ghost) and finally gave him what he deserved. Matthew Lillard is perfect as Shaggy. Linda Cardellini is near-perfect--a tad prettier than I imagined Velma to be, but she somehow mimics a cartoon character while authentically actin, not an easy task. Sarah Michelle Gellar acts perfectly as Daphne even if physically she isn't a just-right fit--leaving us with Freddie Prinze, who is not bad as Fred. His acting and voice are perfect but not his physique. The producers wanted a real-life couple for Fred and Daphne so that's who we got. Although Rowan Atkinson is a good villain, the part seems to have been written for someone else--and was. The very different Tim Curry was cast but bowed out after he found out who the real villain was, illustrating how passionate we are about that character. Not as wonderful as SD 2, Monsters Unleashed, but witty, well-performed, and worth your time.

history.title: Mirror Mirror
history.text: Please, Hollywood. Stop hiring Julia Roberts. I have never seen her act, yet. All she does is recite her lines. A wry, high energy retelling of Snow White, recasting her as the heir apparent and a hero and the Queen as self-serving gold digger. The characters work fine--the dwarves have individual personalities, nice relationship between the prince and his valet. Lily Collins is radiant as Snow, and has a pretty good story arc, grows fairly believably in her fairy tale world. Julia Roberts does her usual posturing, uneven accents and what-does-this-line-that-I-am-saying-mean? As I watched I was recasting in my head: Meryl Streep (who also postures but somehow makes it work), Julie Walters, Vanessa Williams, Celia Imrie, anybody, please! save me from this Acting I student. It was made the worse for Mare Winningham's stellar supporting role. Funny thing with the costumes and sets. All the royal were done so we got the idea the queen had spent too much money--what says EXCESS?? So we flitted from Versailles to Victorian England to some Renaissance or Medieval costumes and sets with aplomb. The village of the peasants was pretty much medieval, which was OK. It's fun enough to watch again, and not too scary, so my young daughter can see it, too. But not perfect. Still, pretty good is, pretty good.

history.title: Sesame Street: Monster Manners [DVD]
history.text: With a Sesame Street vid, you have to judge on three qualities: educational, entertainment for the kids, and entertainment for the adults. Great, non-preachy manners guide. Addresses how kids can be so excited they forget their manners (Rosita pushing Baby Bear because she just CAN'T WAIT for her turn) self-regulating, forgiving people who try to be polite but just don't have it down yet. Very entertaining for my young child. The celebrity cameos were uneven. In a horrible miscalculation, they had some of the celebs film their bits in front of green screens, separate from the muppets and even the other actors. This led to a stiff acting style which prevented interaction with muppet performers. You didn't see the green screen line around the people but you could tell the actors were trying to remember where the muppets and set were. I understand the money-saving necessity of the green screen to save on set building (especially when they are not using the set but only standing in front of it) but when it hampers the performers interacting it becomes extremely irritating. David Hyde Pierce was the highest billed celeb, and he had what should have been a wonderful skit as a cookie expert visiting Hooper's Store and running into Cookie Monster--trying to teach him to be classy. He's being Niles, of course, but it's off. Was he tired the day of filming? Niles's prissy fussiness was always funny because DHP performed it with a spark of irony, joy, even--and that's absent here. He's just fussy, not ironic. But the SS actors, Alan and Chris, are warm and funny. The best celeb cameo was Zach Efron, who actually DID interact with the muppet performer, and seems aware that he is talking to kids, and seems to love them. Colbie Smulders and Henry Cavill were also good, by which I mean they conveyed that manners are a way to interact meaningfully with people, rather than a dictate from mean ol' grownups. A little sophisticated for the preschool crowd to understand (they cover putting your napkin on your lap!), but entertaining enough that from that age to even age 9 could watch it and find it interesting.

history.title: Lilo & Stitch
history.text: When I first watched Lilo and Stitch, it rubbed me the wrong way. When I saw a review that said it was more like Spirited Away than like Sleeping Beauty or Cinderella I GOT it. Watch this and expect singing mice and you are bound to be disappointed. Watch this looking for the humanity or worth in everyone and you'll say AAAAHHHHHHH. No singing mice, few pretty outfits, only a hint of romance, weird little damaged protagonist, a jumble of stories going on at once, real and painful results from catastrophe after catastrophe before a satisfying ending: it's really a Miyazaki movie set to Elvis music. I have some trouble with how real the sorrow is--the older sister getting more and more desperate to take care of her sister, and the realistic battles between them, but it is so well done. Great movie, just don't watch it expecting all sunshine.

Could barely see what was happening at times. Would have loved to see more of the actors faces. Thought I was going blind. Not a big fan of this dark dark filming technique - too much of a strain to watch. There is nice bonus material on this DVD and subtitles are available for those who appreciate having that choice.

history.title: Penny Dreadful: The Final Season
history.review_title: A IGNOMINIOUS END TO AN INTERESTING SHOW
history.text: If you're a fan of Seasons 1 & 2, you will no doubt feel compelled to buy the 3rd Season, but you will probably be very disappointed. Clearly the show was cancelled in a peremptory manner, since the third Season adds several new characters but never gets to develop their plotlines, including a woman who mysteriously appears and befriends our leading lady (but we never learn anything about her); we are introduced to "Dr. Jekyll" (but the show ends before he has time to become "Hyde"); and we finally meet "Dracula," who (in the stupidest, most unbelievable plotline imaginable) has apparently spent a year working at the British Natural Museum simply to initiate an accidental meeting with Miss Ives! [He might just as realistically have gone to work in the shop that does her hair!] Truly, the third Season is an embarrassing mess which (like Dr. Johnson's horse) charges off "in all directions at once" but (tragically) has no where to go. [As for the very beautiful Mr.Carney, the show quite literally leaves him alone in his mansion completely adrift from the rest of the plot. One thing is clear: Whoever pulled the plug on this show in such a precipitous manner certainly had no regard for its fans.

history.title: Birth of a Nation
history.review_title: A FILM BY ANY OTHER NAME WOULD BE ACCEPTABLE
history.text: This posting is simply an expression of contempt for a film-maker who would usurp the title of the single most influential film in the history of American cinema for a modern film that could have been released under any number of names. The original BIRTH OF A NATION may be a horrifying celebration of the Ku Klux Klan and its message may be (and is) despicable; but it's unarguably the single most important film in the history of American cinema. Heaven help the naive film student who reads about D. W. Griffith's masterwork and mistakenly orders this film. The director and the producers of this film should be ashamed of themselves. I can only wonder that a film-maker could have such brazen contempt for our cinematic heritage. What's next? A comedy about teenage pot-smokers called GONE WITH THE WIND? A Bill Murray re-make of CITIZEN KANE? Please spare us!!!!!

history.title: Absolutely Fabulous
history.review_title: STICK WITH THE ORIGINAL SERIES! THIS FILM BARELY MERITS A "P.S."

Enjoy the first three seasons of the TV show and let sleeping dogs lie. John Cleese did the right thing: Give it your best, then stop. This is AB/FAB on life-support.

history.title: Finian's Rainbow (1968) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A PALE, SHODDY TRAVESTY OF THE ORIGINAL SHOW
history.text: This film ranks with PAINT YOUR WAGON as one of the truly criminally inept film adaptations of classic Broadway musicals. A particularly unfortunate failure because FINIAN'S RAINBOW is one of the true gems of the American Musical Theater; but because of its subtly brilliant satire of race relations in America, it's unlikely anyone will ever produce it as it was originally written. Even the Broadway revival a few years ago was a badly butchered dumbed-down travesty of the original.

history.title: Esteros

The scrupulously PG script could NOT have been more than three pages long. If you you want to watch two pair of attractive young men eyeing each other and splashing about in the water for two hours, this piece of cinematic wallpaper might satisfy you. But if you expect a film to have an interesting story, you might want to look elsewhere.

history.title: This Sporting Life (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.review_title: AN UNPLEASANT FILM ABOUT AN UNPLEASANT MAN
history.text: I find it puzzling that Richard Harris should have been so highly praised for doing what is so obviously a sustained imitation of Marlon Brando as he appeared in both STREETCAR and ON THE WATERFRONT. Harris even reprises a variation on Brando's famous cry of "Stella!" Is it possible that so few British critics had seen the Brando films at the time that they thought Harris was doing something novel? In any event, (Brando-impressions aside) this is a very unpleasant film to watch. Great dramas like LONG DAY'S JOURNEY and DEATH OF A SALESMAN may require our serious attention, but we realize that we're watching something worth attending to and that we will remember. All this film offers us is the opportunity to spend two hours with a brutish Neanderthal with whom I would not want to spend 5 minutes in real life. The only positive element in this film is a remarkable, restrained performance by Rachel Roberts. But even her final scene is marred by one of the most intrusive, stupid Expressionistic images I've ever seen. As a young gay man, I loved IF... when it first came out. I enjoyed its sheer audacity. But after seeing more of Anderson's work, I can't help but think he was a very limited talent who had an enormous amount of solid support from his friends in the industry and the great good luck to create IF.. at precisely the moment he did. Timing like that is a gift from the gods.

history.title: Live In New Orleans
history.review_title: A RIDICULOUSLY PRICED RIP-OFF! SAVE YOUR MONEY!
history.text: This ridiculously priced DVD is a heavily edited version of the original broadcast with a VHS quality picture. A more complete version of the telecast is readily available from IOFFER.COM for 12.95. This version is a real scam.

history.title: A Quiet Passion
history.review_title: AS FASCINATING AS WATCHING PAINT DRY
history.text: If you love Emily Dickinson's poetry - or remain (as I have) intrigued by it for many years - you might hope that this film would give you a long-awaited cinematic portrait of the lady and her life. Think again!!! It is a typically self-indulgent, inexpressibly turgid exercise in Terence Davies' peculiar form of film-making in which nothing is expressed in one minute than can be prolonged to ten. In the end, you'd be better off sitting down with a volume of Emily's poems and simply spending the time with her. To paraphrase a remark one said about the composer Francis Poulenc, "When Terence Davies has absolutely nothing to say, he says it."

history.title: Double Indemnity
history.text: A superfically perfect noir thriller with flaws that are not immediately noticed by the viewer. The first flaw is that Walter goes for double indemnity on Dietrichson. This is sure to make the insurance company suspicious. The second flaw is that Lola, the daughter, is brought in like a deus ex machina to discredit Phyllis and wise Walter up to her real personality. The third flaw is that Nino Zachetti, Lola's boyfriend is brought in as a fall guy that both Phyllis and Neff want to take the fall for the murder. So the basic characters, Walter, Phyllis and her husband, were not enough to fill out the plot. Wilder and his writers had to bring in more characters whose role is dubious, when we consider that Walter and Phyllis kill Dietrichson, Phyllis shoots Walter, Walter murders Phyllis, and is caught by Barton Keyes. Lola and Zachetti are clumsily brought in to hold the structure together, and the result is the opposite. They make the movie seem contrived. Edward G. Robinson as Barton Keyes is the real glue that holds the movie together. His implacable intelligence, his growing suspicions weave a web around Walter and Phyllis that ultimately destroys them. Finally, I wonder what the censors thought about the fact that Nino Zachetti was having sexual relations with both Lola Dietrichson and her mother. I suspect there was trouble. What redeems the movie is the mood, the great acting, the complexity, which allow us to sit back and enjoy it without thinking about the flaws. It was not a box office success, but it is a classic.

history.title: Alien(Spanish)
history.text: This movie could almost be seen as a comedy. "An alien life form -- let me reach out and touch it!" Then they bring it into the ship with only Sigourney Weaver protesting. It has covered Kane's face and breathing for him. "Let's cut through one of its arms!" The acid penetrates several decks of the ship. Now that they finally realize it's dangerous, "Let's go after it with a butterfly net!" Possibly the stupidest scene is Harry Dean Stanton looking for the cat while the monster stalks him. "Here, kitty kitty kitty.." Unintentionally funny. In the end, of course, they all die. Except Sigourney Weaver, who does an effective strip-tease in the shuttle before realizing the alien is in the shuttle with her. Using clever controls of vents, she blows the monster out into space, and says into the radio, "This is Ripley, the last survivor of the Nostrum, signing off." This one scene is watchable.

history.title: Grand Illusion
history.text: In the Truffaut biography, someone said of Renoir, "He can make an armoire talk." Renoir was very proud of this, and indeed his genius consists in humanizing things we don't usually think of as animate. What I admire most in his best films is that you can feel the air in the room with the characters. The air is alive. There are many riches here, such as the soldiers dressing up as women in a musical comedy and the audience looking on in awe because all the soldiers are celibate. The tenderness and respect shown to Boildieu by the wounded Von Stroheim, burns all over his body, his spine broken, is very touching. Yet Renoir said of the movie, "That damned Grande Illusion ruined my career!" The movie typecast him and he couldn't make the films he wanted to make. Some call this the greatest movie ever made. I don't think so, it's too local, too specific. But it is a great movie, delightful to watch.

Jessica Lange allows herself to look ugly, to say ugly things in the courtroom, and for this she deserves some credit.

history.title: Fast, Cheap and Out of Control
history.text: After much thought, I realized that the subject of this lyrical documentary is behavior: the behavior of the lions, the behavior of the mole rats, the behavior of the robots, the behavior of the trees Ray Mendonça is trimming. But Erroll Morris is making a more subtle point: the behavior always threatens to elude Man's attempts to control it. From this we get the title "Out of Control." The protagonists relish the challenge they face, and are optimistic. Toward the end they begin to reflect on what will happen when they're gone. Will carbon-based life be replaced by silicone-based life? A tender mood ensues. But Caleb Sampson's end-title music is brave, forging into the future, but always with a touch of humor. "Boys and girls, count backward with me!" Says the ringmaster as the man is about to to be shot out of a cannon. To me, nothing Morris ever did compares to this quixotic fantasy.

history.title: Kiss of the Spider Woman
history.text: What hurts this movie is Arreghi's incomprehensible credulity. As a political prisoner he would immediately suspect that his homosexual cellmate is a spy, chosen precisely for his homosexuality. But Arrreghi alternates between spouting political slogans and berating his cellmate for failing to face reality. The pot is calling the kettle black. What saves the movie is that they both die. Arreghi is tortured to death while Molina, in a fine irony, is killed by insurgents because of his love for Arreghi. He is not politicized, he is a man in love with another man.

history.title: Dark Passage (Keepcase)
history.text: This is an underrated, highly symbolic noir classic. Throughout the movie Lauren Bacall functions as Bogart's mother and protector, though she is visibly young enough to be his daughter. This is nowhere more evident than when she removes the bandages from his plastic surgery. She is literally giving birth to him as a new person, a person she can love. Memorable is the metamorphosis engineered by Tom D'Andrea and his plastic surgeon friend. The only flaw in the structure is the 35 minutes that go by without us seeing Bacall at all. Bogart has to overcome his enemies, the most important being the feline, sibillant Agnes Moorhead (the real villain in the plot), before he can reunite with Bacall in another country. Very well made.

history.review_title: A TRULY MOVING, INSIDE LOOK AT ONE OF HOLLYWOODS MOST SUCCESSFUL ACTORS AND THE LOVE HE NEVER KNEW.
history.text: I purchased this video after buying Peter Ford's book "Glenn Ford: A Life". I have always been a huge fan of Glenn Ford and when I saw his son Peter had published a book about his famous mother and father (Glenn Ford's first wife, and mother of Peter, was actress and dancer Eleanor Powell from 1943–1959) I wasted no time in buying it. I want to first say this is not the typical book written by the spoiled Hollywood child trashing their parents just to make money on a book. It is evident throughout the book that Peter had a deep, heartfelt love for his father and spent a lifetime trying to connect to a man who, for the most part, was very narcissistic and self-indulgent. As a long-time fan of Glenn Ford, it saddened me to read how little he seemed to care about a very deeply-devoted wife who gave up her Hollywood career at a time when her income far-exceed that of her husbands, and how detached he was from a son who idolized his father and in return was virtually ignored. I couldn't help feel the pain of Peter as time and time again his father's career and lifestyle took precedence over any father-son time together. This is a beautiful movie that really highlights the inner beauty of Eleanor Powell and her devotion to her family. Peter was blessed to have had such a wonderful mother who gave him unconditional love throughout her life. And after reading Peter's book, one can only have the deepest respect for him and his wife and all they sacrificed in his father's final years to try and do all they could to help him at a time when he was being drained of his fortune by Hollywood bloodsuckers for whom Glenn Ford became nothing more than a human ATM.

history.title: The Flying Scotsman
history.review_title: A MOVIE MORE ABOUT THE HUMAN SPIRIT THAN BICYCLING AND ONE YOU WILL NOT SOON FORGET - TRULY INSPIRATIONAL!!
history.text: I happened to come across this movie while channel surfing and was immediately drawn to the storyline about a man setting world records in cycling while fighting the side effects associated with "extreme bipolar disorder". I never heard of this individual nor have I read his book prior to seeing the movie, but I was completely drawn into this man's struggle with mental illness. In addition to battling his personal demons, he is harassed by neighborhood bullies and a cycling organization that sadly does all it can to defeat him before he even gets on his bike! After reading a number of the reviews the general consensus appears to be the movie fell short of the book. Not having read the book, I can only say I thoroughly enjoyed the movie and I feel Obree is an amazing example of what the human spirit is capable of accomplishing in spite of overwhelming adversity. As a former competitive power lifter, I understand the personal sacrifice required to successfully compete in an individual sport such as this. I also understand all too-well what it's like to compete in a sport where everyone around you is using performance-enhancing drugs because they lack the intestinal fortitude to win through hard work. It seems everyone now days is taking drugs that have become so prolific on every level in every sport. This is a truly amazing story of one man's fight to overcome all the adversity that was dealt him and be victorious. What I felt was most shocking of all was the manner in which those making the rules for this sport behaved like children by making every effort possible to derail Obree from accomplishing his dream. Their adolescent behavior is juxtaposed against Obree's human spirit to win and it really shows how far some people have to go to overcome not only their own life challenges, but the challenges posed by others around you. What I found most satisfying was to see that Obree is still alive today, and with the help of mental health treatment has not only been able to live a more fulfilling life, but surprisingly still competes in cycling-related events. I recommend this movie as a great motivational tool for all!

What's particularly sad for this production - because it easily could have been remedied - is that Ms. Ball's make-up is so pathetically white under the lights.

Just not up to standards even of the day. This must have been an NBC intro for their '79 season but it falls short of interesting. The first season is fine, but the absence of Emmit Miller, (in his Entertaiment Tonight voice) makes the action flow and puts the emphasis on the work of genealogists. The stories are fascinating in both seasons (cannot wait for the third and more), but the value lies in the methodology of the pros who do this for a living. Genealogy is fascinating and expensive, particularly now with the introduction and relative affordability of DNA testing. There is still, at this point, no high tech method for the hard core grunt, paper trail work; which requires skill, diligence and dedication.

history.title: Finding Your Roots
history.review_title: Maybe I can determine my own paternity?
history.text: After witnessing the current role of DNA testing and analysis in the genealogical work of Dr Gates and his enormously talented and experienced team, I suddenly realized that I might be able to determine my own paternity mystery using some of the same methods. Maybe not as wide and deep, but it would be nice to learn my biological surname, at the very least, and hopefully the name of my biological father. Since I do not have ANY clues, DNA is a start. Thus, I am a little (maybe a lot) indebted to this series, for providing some hope. This series is, among the many knock-offs, a cut above, because of the rich and thorough historical context Gates provides to each of his guests/clients and the audience. It is so fascinating. I was so moved to see neurosurgeon, and CNN medical correspondent Sanjay Gupta so deeply touched, when he learned his ancestors deep Indian roots via centuries old scrolls maintained by holy men in India-- It is thrilling to watch.

history.review_title: Marketing & hype for sure. A sport in survival mode...
history.text: labels, spins, and looks for strategies to grow and remain relevant. Not sure this is the way to go; and not sure the upcoming players need or want this added pressure. Obviously, the "industry" of tennis needs these kind of players a lot more than they need the hype. I worry that tennis will collapse under the weight of its own insecurities. Why do these players need some media machine and hype to push them? Why not let the cream rise to the top organically and without fanfare? We know what happens when "sport" for its own sake, succumbs to sport for the sake of money and so-called development and growth, and it ain't good--off the chart endorsement deals for the ATP and the players, drugs, exclusion instead of inclusion and a palpable loss of the sheer joy and wonder of playing. All of these Next Gen Up and Comers, said not one comment about the sport and joy of playing, it was all about ranking, being the best, living out their father's dream, winning to deliver their families from obscurity, etc. Huh? If that is all they know, these Next Gen players will not last long.

history.title: New York Lately
history.review_title: Meh...nothing new, stories about coming to terms...
history.text: with the many challenges of trying to make connections, (career, romance, commitments, etc.) in a city full of opportunities, but in a city brimming with others seeking the same. When the connections work, they are great, but when they fail, the fall is spectacular as well. The setting in the film is New York, a lot a shots in Chelsea. We have a diverse selection of characters and a diversity of careers and levels of relationships. Some of these characters are connected, others become connected and others disconnect. My main quibbles are production oriented: Actors are so-so, timing is a bit off, there isn't a click or flow in scenes, i.e., they seem to take a bit too long, with the camera lingering too long as well, thus creating a longer film than necessary. Is there an editor in the house? The scenes are tedious, and a few should have been left on the cutting room floor, e.g., the scene with the ladies sipping wine and recounting previous romances--boring, awkward, poorly shot. There are numerous and better examples of films of this sort, (Happy Endings, directed by Dan Rhoos; Crash; 2 Days in the Valley, et al) editing is key and a clear thread must run through, with a compelling and satisfying denouement pulling all of the threads together into one abstract or specific cloth. That sorta happens here, but not really, not consistently and therefore, not well.

history.review_title: This ain't your daddy's Huxtables, thank goodness
history.text: Smart, hip, sexy, urban-- love the packaging. Though the ostensible theme ain't nothing new (folks seeking to do and be better), you gotta appreciate the creativity in offering viewers the perspective from a 30'ish black woman, Internet baby and her white sidekick in DEE-troit. Lots of current cultural references and digs (e.g., notably Kardashians), good music and good conversation. If they sustain the great vibe, interesting, but quirky characters and high production values, this could be a staple in my Watch List.

history.review_title: Good stuff, but I squirmed...A LOT!
history.text: I'm seeing this episode in the wake and ongoing public discourse regarding sexual harassment, and this episode pushes all the buttons...all the wrong buttons, sexually speaking. The waiter having sex with a "customer at work," the supervisor making light of the inappropriate touching of the group home resident, and don't get me started on the musical anthem--this is fodder for those who say, "she asked for it." Just simply over the top inappropriate given the current national discussion. But is the content interesting? Yes. Was the production first-rate? Yes. Is the inclusion of marginalized characters positive? Hell yes! It's (pardon the cliche) a bit groundbreaking. Should the production team step back a little given the current climate on sexual harassment? Possibly, maybe, not sure.

history.review_title: Sweet, good performances, ode (eulogy?) to NYC
history.text: Just got back from NYC, so many of the images and that "Autumn in New York" feel are still fresh in my senses, and this film--the photography--easily evokes those warm feelings. It is a fine production, NYC is usually a sure fire context and set, good performances (good music, I am the original Simon & Garfunkel fan of the 60's) and a truly layered, woven, interesting and compelling story. To say more would be criminal. Watch it and just let it unfold. Make no mistake, this is no indy, art film. It is a bit Hollywood (particularly the 'happy ever after' ending), but every once in a while, even I have to admit...that ain't such a bad thing.

history.review_title: A Poor production.Lacking in depth and authenticity.
history.text: I love romantic stories, but this is so awkward...and frankly, embarrassing. The narration is annoying and amateurish and is a cop-out for creating scenes, editing footage, and writing a decent script that "shows" us, rather than "tells" us. Egregiously, they included a downtown shot (smog-filled) of the happy couple in the hills overlooking...Los Angeles. Huh? The restaurant and story is in San Francisco, remember? I'm sorry but, San Francisco and Los Angeles are two very different cities with two very different and unique skylines. This film is such a mess. The "restaurant" is a suburban townhouse, the kitchen doesn't even come close to a professional, look 'n feel, complete with controlled chaos.The photography is amateur hour as well. This is such a joke. While our star, writer, director probably had a good intention somewhere in this mess, the incompetence and poor production completely obliterate it. Wearing 3 hats requires such talent and skill and experience, Mr. Kellan should pick one. He is young, likable and has time to learn, but the last thing you want is a stinker on you CV, the first time out. One good thing in this production: Doree Seay (Gillian), she is a serious professional and I hope she gets other opportunities. Cannot recommend this. See "Burnt," w/Brad Cooper and call it day! And yes, I know this is an indy film with tight budget and all that, but an unlimited budget could not save this mess.

history.review_title: Many technical problems, plus muddled story
history.text: There are a lot of technical problems evident in this film that are obvious from the beginning: The story is a bit messy, I mean cringy messy. The editing is only fair to poor. The acting is amateurish. But I get it, it's an independent film project, with literally no budget and hopefully a lot of heart. But there is no evidence of the latter so far. So, 'ya make allowances...to a point and then you cut your losses. I am 30% into this movie and nothing compelling inspires me to continue.

history.review_title: Welcome diversity in theme & casting, a little too long
history.text: In these xenophobic days around the world (exacerbated by fake politicians), the backdrop, casting and humanity of this movie, is most welcome. Though not a die hard Apatow fan, some of his material has hooked me--e.g., Forgetting Sarah Marshall comes to mind. In the comedy moments of this film, the effort was miss and hit for me. Loved Holly Hunter in Broadcast News, but that's it for me. Her acting persona (all big, very little subtlety) is one note and can be grating for me. The dilemma of first generation immigrants, i.e., how much to assimilate, is real and unrelenting. No one wins--particularly in matters of politics, religion and love. Either you follow your heart, and risk losing immediate family, or retain traditional values and risk losing yourself, if you truly embrace or desire to embrace the notion of human individuality and destiny above all. Can there ever truly be a happy ending. Well, this film tests your mettle on that point by droning on and on and on and it is as if it will never end. Overall, it's o.k.

history.title: The Complete Story: World War I
history.text: If you are looking for a DVD set on WW1 this is the best place to start. I remember watching this in reruns in the 70's as a kid, and was into it every time I saw it on. Watching it again now 35 years later it holds up very well. Robert Ryan doesn't put a whole lot of emotion into it at the beginning but his subtlety works as by the time you get to Verdun you can tell his voice is very cynical as he's reading the death figures and gains made. I only just completed disc one and it took me a couple of months of casual but regular viewing so it is an excellent value for the money. I learned in watching just the first disc about Herbert Hoover being the head of Belgium Relief and that the Germans had a cargo U boat that successfully made it through the blockade to America. Both things were never mentioned in the much newer World War One BBC set [...] I guess to write a review that would help other buyers here, I would like to say that I really enjoyed the newer set and watched it almost straight through, but if you were looking for the best set, I vote for this one. It's got a lot more content to it, plus since it is an American production and was done by CBS news during the 60's (Walter was the head newscaster then, very prestigious outfit at that time), it takes a look at both sides more then the British series does. The newer set is more accessible to the everyday viewer (color and better graphics) but if your really into History this set is superior. If you are a big History buff you should get both, they compliment each other very well. 5 stars, and it's very reasonably priced, would make a great gift!

history.title: Dangerous Assignment: The Complete Television Collection
history.text: You could be one of two different fans of this show, a person who has fond memories of seeing it earlier in their lives, or a younger person who can appreciate the camp factor this series has. I am younger and like old TV series but I recognize how campy this show is as well. Know how younger viewers rip Star Trek for all the Red Shirts dying in the series, well if you grew up on the show you probably never saw it that way until you heard it recently and it's true! Well here the camp factor with Dangerous Assignment is of all the episodes I've seen, all of Steve's allied agents get killed. If the Commissioner said that I was to work with Secret Agent Steve Mitchell, I'd turn in my Secret Agent ID and gun and resign! The production values are good enough so it's still good to watch and whether you are into it, or laugh a little (or a lot), it's all good entertainment. Donlevy is not nearly as "wooden" here as many of his critics say of his movies and being a Brian Donlevy fan myself, I enjoy watching this series I had never heard of until recently. Donlevy comes across kind of like an older American Roger Moore's James Bond if you will, and it saves the show as the humor is much needed to make this show still work. The DVD prints are clean by the way with only a trademark brand shown briefly during the intro. 4 of 5 stars.
