history.title: The History Channel Presents: The Revolution [DVD]
history.text: The main problem I have with this documentary is the following: I believe the History Channel should be ashamed of themselves for portraying George Washington as an ambitious, calculating and even incompetent man. Where much documentation exists of people testifying to Washington's humility and general desire to be a Virginian farmer as opposed to a politician, they dismiss this... even insinuate that his "pretended" sense of duty was some great plan for military and political ambition. They mentioned nothing of his connection to "Providence"... how he prayed regularly- and was seen so doing- nor how he insisted that his men prayed also. They've taken a humble, great man and tried to turn him into something completely different. If you'd like a true picture of this wonderful, God-inspired man, please read the following book: [[ASIN:0880800143 The Real George Washington (American Classic Series)]]. Secondly, the discs have a tendency to freeze; so they are not of the highest quality.

history.title: Super Sentai: Denji Sentai Megaranger - The Complete Series [DVD]
history.review_title: If you're looking at this, you're probably already going to buy this.
history.text: Of all the Super Sentai series sets that Shout Factory as produced, this one (so far) is the best acted. While the villains and comedy was Carranger's biggest strength, Megaranger's cast is their strongest suit. Every character feels developed, which is saying something for a Sentai series. This also is a show that really uses it's female cast members instead of just having them there to fill out the team, another rarity. So all-in-all it was a refreshing change from the direction Zyuranger-Carranger was doing, as the Sentai themselves can sometimes be one-note in these series. The premise of using emerging digital (90s) technology as a weapon is pretty good, and nostalgic if one lived through that era. The villains use a mixture of magic and inter-dimensional alien science, so it's a good contrast. I can't say the villains in this one match Carrangers (the previous show), but the overall theme and characters make up for it. Sometimes the mecha battles can re-use that stock footage a bit much, as well. For a show that doesn't have a lot of transformation mechs, it seems like summoning the various mechs take FOREVER. But then again, I'm not a mech person. I can appreciate a good mech battle, but sometimes a big dramatic story that seemed resolved get somewhat ruined by a pointless mech battle that adds nothing. Part of that is the story it's in, the other part is stock footage, and lastly pacing. But those are my only negative comments. Overall... buy this. Support Shout Factory and lets keep these Super Sentai releases coming. I can die happy if we ever get to Gekiranger, Shinkenger, and Gokaiger. If you're a Super Sentai fan, you're going to buy this anyway, but buy it! Megaranger, on it's own, is just a wonderful edition to the series, well worth the price on it's own, never mind it being Super Sentai. It's an outstanding show. You need this. YOU NEED THIS!

history.title: The Marx Brothers TV Collection
history.review_title: Interesting if you're a Hardcore Marx Bros Fan.
history.text: ...but only IF you're a hardcore Marx Bros fan. This is the TV years, well after their glory years. It's like watching Paul McCarthy now. You appreciate him as an artist, but...yeah. Harpo and Groucho come off a little bit better than Chico does in these TV spots, but it still feels like the Bros are retreading some of their great bits for a nostalgic public. It's nice to see as a fan, don't get me wrong, but if you're coming into this thinking you're getting movie-quality Marx Bros comedy...sorry. The best parts about this collection is the home-videos and documentaryish aspects to home life of the real men. The children and friends of the Marx Bros provide some footage and insight on who these guys really were. For that alone, it's worth the money. This is a great value as well. The first disc alone is over 4 hours of content... all worth watching. When they say over 10 hours, they aren't lying. Literally everything the Marx Bros appeared in during that time-period is here, even if it's a strange company advertisement for a magazine (only to be seen by employees.) Aside from the Marx Bros themselves, this is a weird look back into how early television was, which for someone who didn't grow up with it, was interesting. It's like a time capsule in some way. If you're a casual Marx Bros fan, I don't know if you'd like it on your own. But with everything I mentioned above, there are levels of enjoyment to these discs. You can enjoy it as a television historian, or as a semi-documentary, or just enjoy watching the brothers preform once more. Hardcore fans need this in their collection though. So buy it. You'll thank me later.

history.title: Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith (Widescreen Edition)
history.review_title: Needs to be seen by all, but.......
history.text: I guess if you are like me and have followed this story from the very start - yes I waited in lines to see the original - you kinda of have to see this one to fill in the remaining gaps and bring the story full circle. I have no issue with the concept or the overall story arc. But truth be told this movie is atrocious. The script looks like it was written over a weekend if that. It's obvious that a lot of the movie was laid out before the script existed, but that understandble to a point in a movie that ends a previously defined arc and the final installment of a trilogy. The whole thing was pretty much laid out in 1976. My problem with the film is that it's so poorly executed. Here we have a movie a cast of fine actors (with the exception of Hayden Christensen that is) and none of them seemed to be into or maybe even aware of their characters at all. The quality of the performances was embarassingly terrible. It was amusing to watch parts of the bonus materials showing Lucas atttempting to teach Hayden how to act - it didn't work. He still used the same dull monotone in each scene regardless of whether he was fighting or kissing. It may be the over reliance on CG. I'll bet that 99% of the scenes were filmed on greenscreen thus giving the actors no anchor to the scene in which they were performing. Maybe the current CG trend is just asking too much of human actors. Possibly this is the case since in my opinion the only character that showed any kind of believable expressions or emotion was Yoda and he wasn't even real. Star Wars III distilled to its essence was just a big loud cartoon with humans. The CG scenery ws beautiful but also sterile making it look too much like CG despite the photorealism. The movie was not all bad and there were several wonderful and moving scenes, but they were the exception. I hope that this movie wakes up Hollywood a little and sparks a trend towards slightly CG and special effects. When the day is done we go to see the story and the performances. Otherwise we are just watching a flesh and blood version of a Japanime cartoon. This movie was way too much like one.

history.title: 24: Season 4 [DVD]
history.text: I thought seasons 1-3 were masterpieces of cliffhanger style suspense. I don't know if it's just me or not but this season seemed very predictable. I was able to call way ahead of time just about every "surprise" this season. The other bothersome thing is the 2nd plot element about the Dobson device. The very concept it beyond ridiculous. For all the resources the producers had they could have hired at one nuclear engineer to tell them how silly the idea was and how it would practically ruin the enjoyment of the series. How could you take it seriously when they were talking such nonsense about the Dobson Override and its "capabilities". It was so idiotic it almost turned the rest of the season into a comedy. I was never so happy to see a plot segment finished as that one. It would have been more credible if they had the terrorists using a Star Trek transporter to beam nuclear weapons into government buildings. Thats about the level of the Dobson device. It was just silly and stupid and I was very disappointed with this segment of the plot. I was never so happy to see a plot segment finished as that one. It was even sillier than the Secretary of Defense pulling a Chuck Norris "Missing in Action" stunt even though Devane made it a little bit believable - but only a little. I almost would have preferred to see the S2 cougar back again. Fortunately the series got back on track after they found the override and we were back into an area where 24 excels - good old fashioned action/suspense. There were a few holes here and there, one of stretches of credibility and a more than a few spots where you wonder why Jack with all his skills and experience would do <spoiler deleted> and <spoiler deleted> but overall it was rolicking fun. It was also great to see a few familiar faces from previous seasons. In addition to the thrills and chills there are a few comedic aspects; the new President Logan gives a terrific "Bush look" confused and clueless while telling everyone he's in charge and he's the boss. He even looks a little like W, especially with the "W" patented "deer in the headlights" look every time something happens. Overall it was a 4 star season, but the last two DVD's were 5+. It was the 2nd half of DVD 2 and all of DVD 3 that dragged the rating down. My ony bitch is the final element with the Chinese could have been so easily dealt with, it was obvious yet they chose the hard way and that was a bit unrealistic but essential to the ending we we can forgive. It did set up what promises to be a very surreal and exciting Season 5!

history.title: Nowhere Man - The Complete Series [DVD]
history.review_title: More proof that TV is not a lost cause - 5 stars squared
history.text: More proof that TV is not a lost cause - Firefly is supporting evidence. Nowhere man was a milestone in American TV. It is the US version of the UK series The Prisoner. I am not so surprised that it was cancelled after a season, I am more shocked that it made on the air to begin with and lasted the season. This is a very thought provoking and cerebral story. This is not for the average "Entertainment Tonight/Desperate Housewives" TV viewer. This show truly meant something and communicated it's message on a variety of levels. Elements of this show were exciting and in-your-face while other plot elements went deeper and were revealed often hours after you have seen an episode only after it sunk inand your brain absorbed the sublties. There was not a single bad, dry or slow episode in the whole series. Every one was important and added another piece to the puzzle. Plus there was absolutely no clue as to where the thing was headed until very close to the end. This was spectacularly well done and Bruce Greenwood was magnificent in his role. This show so intrigued me I wrote a script for it. The show was cancelled before I presented it to the producer. I was sad when it was cancelled but pleased that they were able to hastily put together a wrap for the story that while a little cryptic, not as surreal as the ending of The Prisoner. I think The Prisoner is one of the true masterpieces of artistic TV production, and Nowhere Man is easily it's equal. I can't wait for the release. I have to have this set. I made room for it right next to my Prisoner Megaset.

history.title: The Accidental Tourist [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The Accidental Tourist - the Subtle Mid-Tier Film We Do Not Have Anymore
history.text: This is one of the 80's true gems. A Lawrence Kasdan classic, it comes on the tail end of the high watermark of William Hurt, who by that point had appeared in five Oscar Best Picture nominees: The Big Chill (83), Kiss of the Spider-woman (85), Children of a Lesser God (86) - he should have won his second Oscar for this, Broadcast News (87), and The Accidental Tourist (88), after a major turn in the neo-noir Body Heat (80), netting three Best Actor nominations and two wins. The film is a mix of light humor (witness Travel Writer Macon Leary's eccentric family) and rather dark drama, as Hurt and Body Heat co-star, Kathleen Turner, endure the destruction of their marriage after the loss of a child - until Hurt's life is re-ignited by a romance with a near-perfect Geena Davis, just prior to The Fly (86) with Jeff Goldblum. The eighties were a magic time in cinema. The seventies had pushed enough boundaries that pushing boundaries for the sake of that alone died out in a way, and we were left with a mature cinema that gave us The Right Stuff (83) and Amadeus (84), Dangerous Liaisons (88), among countless hyper-competent lesser luminaries. This sort of mid-budget drama could never be made in today's era of explosively budgeted special effects vehicles obsessed with creating shared universe franchises and we are all the worse for it, as is film. Bill Pullman is also excellent as Hurt's "modern" agent. Hurt was the Pacino of the 80s.

history.title: Friday Night Lights - The Complete Series - Blu-ray
history.review_title: The BEST Sports Drama TV Ever Produced
history.text: Forget "The Sopranos," which was wonderful in many ways, along with "Breaking Bad," and much of the so-called HBO-driven golden-age of the TV series as a true writer's medium, and embrace this all-too-often unsung character-driven classic, the dirty little secret of which was that football only served as the backdrop for one of the finest examinations of a community, here: rural Texas, ever filmed. "FNL" had the panoramic reach of a realist Balzac novel. You see every social class, race, type and people - and none of it veers toward cliche; when the final season strikes, and we find the Coach coaching the cross-town, under-budgeted, nearly all African-American rival, you have a moment worthy of truly classic storytelling in which the hero is reborn on the opposite side. The performances and direction are complete A-list. When the current (Bronze Age of TV) winds up, and the history of the show-runner as driving force is re-written, expect this seldom sung classic to rise to the top. This is TV's version of "Million Dollar Baby," and "Rocky."

history.title: 100 Years of Olympic Films (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: An Immediately Cinematic Genre Distilled to the Most Comprehensive Olympic Visual History Available to Date
history.text: This is an unimaginable historic archive. Not one I would have seen coming. Milos Forman and other high caliber talent filmed these games, reaping art from what French filmmaker Eric Rohmer (his beloved body of work nearly lacked dynamic physical action) thought sports a genre that almost immediately yields dynamic visuals. This set is representative of Criterion's ever-increasing commitment to cinema history, with non-standard fare included (they could have, for example, limited this solely to films and eras already marked in textbooks). There is also a strong argument for categorizing films prior to 1920, and simply collecting it in as restored form as possible. Like many, I desire want a Blu-ray of Joe Frazier and Muhammad Ali (in Rome) - as well as Eric Heiden, and Nadia Comaneci in their most iconic moments. Michelle Kwan alone has an Odyssey in Nagano and Salt Lake City. Boxing as well is a sport I've studied since a lad when the great Hagler, Hearns, Duran, and Leonard exchanged greatness over and over, but we see these athletes in nascent stages, often away from their collective primes. The price may seem high but not for a set this comprehensive - post discounts. Target has it for around 266.00 and change now, slightly above a 33% discount; Amazon often cuts prices closer to release date, as public demand and awareness shifts.

history.title: The Party [Blu-ray]
history.text: I like "Being There," but Sellers turn as an Indian movie actor tearing down a posh party is the brightest gem in his career. It is comedic gold. Today, strangely, it would be a little film. Its wit and sense of abandon are second to none. They do not make this type of film anymore. Perhaps Mike Myers came closest, but he retreated from film too early and existed in a very different Hollywood in which someone like Blake Edwards would be side-lined in favor of expensive extravaganza. What a shame this is - essentially the lack of tonal diversity in our films today.
Possibly my favorite show. It wars a bit with This Is Us.

history.title: Batman & Superman 9-Film Set (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Great Fub Gets its Due - No Darkness Here
history.text: I'm the contrarian. Most people I talk to and most critics I read really dig the Richard Donner cut on “Superman II,” the classic of the Christopher Reeve Superman tetralogy (yeah, I went there.) Now, I don't know whether it's nostalgia or fine memories of eating popcorn with Goobers dumped in and Twizzlers and coca cola wiring me like Times Square on the side. Those were the days. But I still love the original lighter cut. The cast is perfect. The bit with the trucker when Superman surrenders his powers is a classic moment in 80s cinema, as well as my childhood, right up there with “Star Trek II,” “Empire Strikes Back,” my beloved “Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom,” the supposed “stinker” of that series - well, wait until people see “Crystal Skull” and redefine “Indiana Jones stinkers with a blindingly bad low. “Superman III” has Richard Pryor, the audacity of that simply kicks ass. “Superman: The Movie” made me believe a man could fly, had a wildly all-star cast with Ned “Deliverance” Beatty and the always great Gene Hackman who even saves (for five seconds) the nadir that is “Superman IV” - “Nobody wants war Superman. We just want to keep the threat alive." (Too bad Nuclear Man wasn't a villain in the DC canon) - imagine some B-lister like Toy-man essayed by Martin Short, and you have elevated that spectacle by Kyptonian miles. The whole however sent me to Seven-Eleven spinner racks to add comics to my Big League Chew order. The whole began my life-long love affair with Smallville, Kansas, Lois Lane, Lana Lang, and Big Blue in general - not to mention Reeve who revealed himself as a legitimate hero in life; all we needed was Lori Lemaris and the briefest Super-boy bit, and I would have been rapt. Hell, I was rapt anyway. The Burton Batmans are both great, with Michelle Pfeiffer's Catwoman every bit as beautiful as she could be at that time and place (and still is, talk about aging with grace): the woman who made The Fabulous Baker boys swoon, along with every other red-blooded male in the nation. And in Stephen Frears’s “Dangerous Liaisons” and “Age of Innocence” by Martin Scorsese she proves her acting chops match the good luck of her biology. “Batman Forever” is simply good fun.

history.title: Wild Wild West
history.text: I rented this out of a sense of nostalgia and for its steampunk elements. I saw the movie during its theatrical run and, sad to say, it was nearly as bad as I remembered it. Given the concept and the strength of its cast and crew, it's genuinely a shame that this was the best they could do.

history.review_title: A genuine classic, and it looks great in HD!
history.text: This film impresses me for what it was able to accomplish given the era when it was made. Like another of Wells' story-to-movie, The Invisible Man, this is an enjoyable translation and an absolute classic. Rod Taylor's performance as The Traveller was as well done as fans of his work might expect. It's much different from the Guy Pearce film, but seeing this should explain some of the influences it has over the remake. This is a better adaptation of the original story, and still a treat to watch so many years after it was made.

In terms of a remake, this is a far departure from the original. In terms of something new, it's well-imagined and adds some ethereal quality to the horror genre. It would've been interesting to explore the characters further, but for what this film was, it was worth the price of a rental.

history.title: The Wolf Man: Complete Legacy Collection [DVD]
history.text: A diverse collection of films, including two that didn't star Lon Chaney, Jr. There are some great commentaries and bonus features, especially on the Abbott & Costello film. A great gift for fans of the Universal Monster films.

history.review_title: A quiet, haunted tale with charm.
history.text: This was a surprise for me, as I wasn't sure what to expect. The setting and small cast made it feel more like watching a play. Still, it was an enjoyable film with a convincing lead. It isn't spine-tingling, but there are a couple of good jumps. Mostly it's a character piece for Anna Walton, and she did a fine job.

Admittedly, this one isn't going to appeal to people who aren't fans of the Universal Monsters or their behind the scenes legends. I happen to be a huge fan of Jack Pierce's work, given the times and technology that he became famous in. That said, this was remarkably bad! It isn't a documentary, but a recording of a one-man play of someone pretending to be Jack Pierce, giving an account of his life. It seemed as though it could've been recorded on a VHS-camera with a tripod. Also, it would've helped had we not been able to see that the actor was reading his lines from the book in his lap. It may have picked up in the second half, but I'm not sure. I stopped watching due to the quality.

First off, I've never been a fan of the zombie genre. Maybe it's the imagined smell, the biting and hygiene, or maybe my disbelief isn't as willing to suspend itself quite as far as it did before. I gave the first season of iZombie a chance on a streaming rental service (with a really bright red screen). Two episodes in, I was hooked! The show takes a lot of liberty with the attractiveness of its zombies--which is appreciated. The cast is top notch, and series lead Rose McIver is doing similar bold, wide-sweeping work that Orphan Black's Tatiana Maslany is praised for. Yes, it's cute and quirky, but she takes on a different persona in each episode while never wholly surrendering the issues she's struggling with as one of the undead. She also has great chemistry with the ensemble, all of whom have evolved beyond one-dimensional characters. Also, I'm a bit dumfounded by how much the recurring love interest looks like the love child of Scott Speedman and Simon Baker--right down to the charm! This has the same heart as Buffy, Veronica Mars, and Once Upon A Time...sadly, without their fanbase.

history.review_title: An enjoyable and gentle Christmas movie.
history.text: I watched Back to Christmas simply because I'm a fan of Kelly Overton's work. I've often felt she takes on roles that are quietly downplayed, but instantly likable. This role was no different, except it allowed her to exercise some physical comedy that really made the character come to life. I was never really sure who the "stranger" helping her was meant to be, or how it happened that she found herself in the places/moments, but overlooking that, it was still an enjoyable movie. I'm not sure where this was debuted, but it reminded me of the ABC Family-style of Christmas movies. The supporting cast of familiar faces/voices managed to bring their characters to life, without their stories getting in the way of the main plot. Michael Muhney turned in another dependable performance of the "guy you love to hate." There was nothing offensive or unlikable about the movie, but I'd like to have seen more scenes to show us what/how things came to be.

history.title: Choose
history.text: A quiet, atmospheric horror story with a surprisingly brutal concept. Mostly, this is a showcase for the talented Katheryn Winnick. I believe this was made before her role on Vikings. As usual, she delivers an intense, credible performance. It was also nice to see Kevin Pollak, who pulls double duty as the lead cop and the worried dad. This'll appeal most of all to fans of Ms. Winnick, Mr. Pollak, and the shock-horror genre.

history.title: Café
history.review_title: Enjoyable, easy-going film that touches lightly on some sensitive subjects.
history.text: Not an earth-shattering film by any means, but a slice of life with some questions that scratch at what's beyond the surface of that everyday living. The performances were all quality, nothing felt phoned-in, which is sometimes the case with these smaller budgeted films. Some of JLH and Jamie Kennedy's most understated and credible work, but the movie really belonged to the other players in the ensemble. Familiar faces like Alex PenaVega, Madeline Carroll, Katie Lowes, and Michaela McManus lend support to lesser known performers who infuse the story with colorful and curious characters. It has an optimistic outlook on life and the sort of ending that cynics will hate. As for the DVD, I'm not sure who thought putting a red-band trailer as the opening preview to this particular film was a good idea. Judging from the availability of all the films previewed--all of which are owned by the same production house that made the film--I'm guessing it was intended as catalog advertising

Having now watched it, I can only conclude that the people who were telling me this are either 1. Very new to anime. 2. Devout Naruto Bleach Z fans. 3. Giving season 1 a rating that later seasons earned. or 4. Huge fans of Shinji from Neon Genesis Evangelion or god forbid, Cko from Project Ako *cringe*. The Amazon Prime streaming offering of Season 1 is actually only ep 6 and ep 12. If you want the series buy it on disk.

history.review_title: A phoned in script made out of cliches and dumb.
history.text: The prime streaming of Goliath was smooth and all the episodes were there. As for the show itself it is just plain bad. Pick a badly written lawyer movie and cast Billy Bob Thornton. It is fun to watch Billy Bob Thornton even in a badly written piece of drek. It would probably be fun to just watch him drink on a park bench. Where this goes wrong <spoilers of course>: You have a god attorney who no longer does real cases because (/writer reaches in to the cliche' bag) he got a murderer off and that guy killed again. Fact is as a god attorney you probably get several murders off each year and some kill again, so this is terrible writing. Through out the series god attorney loses his legal abilities for drama reasons. This is like a wizard who can't use magic because the writers need something stupid to happen. As it is it just hurts when people do documented illegal things to him and he sits by helplessly. God attorney has less than a lay person's knowledge of the law. In her a phone call to the ICC could have made things amusing.. it didn't even occur. He has a 0 experience dolt of a new attorney help run his new big case. I think we have seen this dead horse beaten enough. He has a substance abuse problem (this one pretty much falls out of the cliche' bag if bad writers look the bag and wonder "how can I add depth to my character?"). In the end it is just a big bile of rehashed cliche's and terrible writing mechanics, slapped together into another bad legal movie. On the positive side 1. Billy Bob Thornton 2. If you have a lawyer (say in GITMO) and you need to get information out of them, then forcing them to watch this will make them talk in a hurry. On the negative side. 1. sometime the stupid is so strong that it can cause you physical pain.

As a scifi fan I have to say this was a terrible piece of garbage. The idea is that Earth is in trouble and there is a new colony out in space that has just been founded. Knowing that water is incredibly important to humans they set it up on a desert world that in plausibly only has water below the surface. No, it is not a cold world where the water is frozen. Once on the planet people hallucinate and go to their deaths and yet they do not pick another planet. Yep, super dumb. Then there are the colonists. If the colony has to survive and you have billions and billions to choose from.. Well in this case they pick colonists from other scifi they have seen. The drug dealer, the bad cop who plays by her own rules, the gruff obese driller, the obese botanist, any cliche characters that you can take form other series and movies. It is like they do not understand that it takes money to haul weight into space and so we will not be seeing fat astronauts, not to mention all the other bad hires who fit a cliche but not common sense. The newest member is the last person you would send, a priest. A priest who smokes like all the other cool priests you have seen in the last 20 years. Why a priest? Well they are hamhandedly trying to make it look like the colony founder has found god on the possibly living planet. Yep.. So you can guess that in the future this will be the Faith and Spirituality scifi series that makes Star Trek 5 look good. I would love a new scifi show, just not this show. If Amazon plans one, please go with the stereo type that nerds love scifi and that nerds are smart. With that in mind, hire smart writers instead of morons who just want to rip off everything they have seen, than fill the rest of the show with drama bombs based on idiocy.

This is the opposite of Better Off Ted. I watched the whole thing, towards the end I was just hoping for a smirk by the end. No dice. Do you remember that kid in Jr High who though he was funny because his mom once told him he was? Do you remember how everyone else told him to shut up and that he was not funny? Do you remember how after everyone laughed at one of the funny kids, how unfunny kid would try to step in and be funny? Do you remember how he wouldn't shut up and you began to hope he would actually die? At least he finally got that mentally disabled kid to laugh at his jokes, so the 2 hung out alone and didn't feel such a need to bother the rest of humanity. Yeah, this show seems to have been written by that kid. It is like someone with no comprehension of humor tried watching shows they were told were funny and then tried to copy them. So this show tries to copy other stuff you have seen but fails to copy it in a funny way. In the end I was angry and wanted those 30 minutes of my life back. We need a term for comedies that offer up 0 laughs, or grins or even a smirk. I'd suggest "Cancer" but getting cancer was WAY funnier than this show.

history.title: Passengers [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Stupidity for drama's sake. Please keep your brain locked in the off position.
history.text: So glad I borrowed the Blu Ray rather than buying. WARNING: Some light spoilers here that may have been in the trailer. This is just a "trapped on a desert island" set in space with painful acting, stacked on top of writing that would shame a mediocre writer, and horrify anyone who passed Junior High science. This is the story of people going from Earth to a new Colony world on a ship with no redundant systems or backup plans to deal with malfunctions. So this is completely unbelievable and should be to anyone who has ever heard the word "parachute". This story also depends heavily on the deplorably stupid idea that by the time we can travel between the stars, that the human life span has not been extended at all from the modern day, even with the magic medical technology that the ship has. This amazing medical tech is a single machine for ~5,200 people and can only be used by approved crew members, so if you find someone who needs real medical help like defibrillation (like those machines on the walls at your work, next to the band aid box) and you are not a high level crew member, that person is dead. Yep, the medical tech is magic amazing but too dumb to do medical on its own, that defib at your work will pretty much handle itself after you slap the pads on someone and hit a button. Space ships will use all available space because to have more internal space means having to build more surface area. Yes, we get a pretty ship but it is an insanely stupidly designed ship. Also when it comes to surviving a malfunction caused by damage, planting trees in decks and such just dooms the ship/passengers. Now for the "romance". In this movie a really good looking man revives a good looking woman to keep him sane as he travels awake to a colony world where he will be about retirement age when he arrives. So for no good reason they talk about dying of old age before getting there (they are traveling at half of C). She complains about how he murdered her.... and then they live happily ever after. Now to get an honest idea as to what really happened imagine the guy was hideous because in the future they cannot extend human life, so maybe they can't make you better looking. If the guy was gross, this would be a horror film but it is a romance because he is good looking. Yes, his needing to wake her up also depends on less entertainment technology than we have today. We already have people who live out their lives on line and in games, with future AI I would doubt that players know who is human and who is not. There is also the assumption that he cannot "Netflix and booze" his way all the way to the destination, while viewing hundreds of years of the best entertainment humanity has produced.

history.title: Arrival
history.review_title: Five stars for what looked like a one star movie.
history.text: I borrowed the Blu Ray and I'm glad I didn't buy this as it is a single viewing movie. Any additional times you view it will be to show it to friends. The movie starts and in the first seconds you are saying "Please do not use this cliche again" with in the next minute or few you are saying "I wish you didn't do that but I knew you were going to". From there the movie trots out piles of dead horses to beat. It is a painful trudge through dumb moments and bits that have been recycled more times than you can count. They were stupid the first time they got written and every time after that that they got stolen and reused... But then they throw in a clue or two here in there that make you ask "Hmm, what's up with that?" the end reveal is too slow in coming so it loses "The Usual Suspects" impact. Like "The Usual Suspects" this is a single viewing movie. This is a three to four star movie but earns its last star(s) for the bravado of the writer/director making a film to directly ridicule the audience's stupidity. Embarrassing and making fun of your customers, few have the guts to do that. For those who do not understand how the writer/director is making fun of the audience, I will hide the spoiler as best I can by putting it in comments. This is your end twist, so if you have not seen the movie and plan to please do not look in comments.

history.title: Ghost in the Shell (2017)
history.review_title: Worst movie of the last few years.
history.text: I'm so glad I rented this rather than buying. If you are unfamiliar with the Ghost in the Shell anime or anime in general then this is just a bad movie. If on the other hand you are a fan of the Ghost in The Shell anime or manga then this movie is an abomination. This starts with with casting a movie star who is best known for having her derriere in the center of the frame when the director can justify it and not for her acting ability, in the lead roll. White washing is not the issue, anime hit it huge in the US because most of the people thought everyone in anime was white despite their Japanese names. People really have a hard time believing that characters like Sailor Moon are actually Japanese and not Norwegian or Icelandic. So white washing is not the problem. The problem is that when people complain that their are no strong female character in film, often characters in anime are held up as a contradiction to the statement, among these Motoko Kusanagi is front and center. Not in this movie however. After it gets Americanized: Motoko Kusanagi's genius gets stupidity washed. It is like the writer heard the complaints about the original movie's English dub being dumbed down and said "hold my beer". Motoko Kusanagi's strength gets weakness washed. Motoko Kusanagi's top level hacking ability gets "How do I start emails?" washed. Motoko Kusanagi's confidence gets insecurity washed. Motoko Kusanagi's presence gets cringing emo washed. Systematically the writers attack and destroy everything that makes Motoko Kusanagi, Motoko Kusanagi. If Deadpool was an anime, these writers would have his character being a mute, vegan, pacifist by the time they were done making the live action movie. Once they have done that they just tack in some iconic scenes from the original movie and call it a day. With the exception of Takeshi Kitano the rest of the casting was bad but lets face it, you could cast Takeshi Kitano as the lead in Heidi and it would still seem like a good casting choice. I have no idea what they were thinking when they cast Batou. Fans will also notice other terrible writing choices like swapping out Togusa's iconic Mateba for a new Chiapa. Not that the Major's team gets much screen time to begin with. Well until Hollywood decides to make a live action Akira or Cowboy Bebop movie, this piece of garbage reigns supreme as worst film adaptation of an anime or manga... but lets look to the future and imagine Michael Cera playing Spike in Bebop or Shia Labeouf as Kaneda in Akira!.. Wait, lets not look to the future, I have changed my mind about that.

history.title: Barry Lyndon (Amazon.com Exclusive)
history.text: Movie 2 of 1975 and 23 overall in my journey through films of my lifetime. In story telling I have a personal preference. Actually I'm not sure that it is considered preference but maybe a "right" way of telling a story. If the way I prefer is indeed the correct way of telling a story then Kubrick can work wonders. His approach to "Barry Lyndon" was not uncommon. In fact it is a style that is used in a very popular contemporary show called "The Walking Dead." The style of which I speak I call "reactionary." That is that the main character(s) overcome a series of, commonly unfortunate, events until they can no longer endure or "arrive" at some conclusions for good or for ill. The opposite of this would be a pro active character(s) that set out to accomplish a goal. It seems like a slight difference but it's actually quite important to making a point in a film. The person that uses the later method the best is Roman Polanski. If you look at his films the main protagonist is not facing a series of challenges that come to him or her. Rather they are seeking something quite aggressively. Whether it is a man authenticating a book or a Detective getting to the bottom of an artificial drought his characters gather no moss and are seeking something out. This is not the way "Barry Lyndon" plays out. It is, mostly, a series of events that happen to the main character. When something isn't happening to him, like thieves on the highway, he is getting lucky, like meeting the right woman at the right time. The worst part of this methodology is that one can't tell what the main point is typically. It's merely a series of events strung together. As a result the audience is left looking into the rear view mirror as it were and the ending just sort of happens. It may be a very good ending that even dovetails, like "Barry Lyndon" but they are usually left asking what the point was. Theme is much easier to come by, in fact almost mandatory in a proactive style. "Barry Lyndon" is mostly reactionary and does suffer in terms of theme. That said I would be a fool to not recognize its greatness. This was a very well told story and I loved it. I was skeptical when I read about it because every description kept saying it was beautifully shot and was an authentic period piece. I expected to be bored. Well it was all of those things except I was rarely bored, it was a great story. I was aware of its reactionary nature from the get go but it never bothered me because it was just compelling. I imagine only Kubrick could pull something like that off. I want to be clear that I have seen as much Kubrick that I can get my hands on so part of me was rooting for him but I don't believe I'm biased here. It's a unique and well told story albeit in an inferior style in my opinion. Pros -perfect music (typical Kubrick) -great acting -authentic period displayed in costumes, hair, environment, language, and everything -that great Kubrick style on full display -a great story told by an expert Cons -I prefer proactive story telling -occasional slow pacing, but with purpose -lacking in a larger point beyond what is staged Well 1975 is off to an incredible start! Two amazing works of art from the get go. Can it keep it up?

history.title: Citizen X (DVD)
history.text: When "Citizen X" is at its best its creepy, dramatically powerful, intriguing, and politically compelling. At its worst its repetitious, melodramatic, and poorly directed. Even though I only gave it 4 stars I actually recommend the movie I just can't look past some of its technical issues. Some examples I can offer: some of the murder scenes are clearly staged, the dialogue is a little too clever and not real enough, the movie oozes influence from silence of the lambs which I find was not best for its setting. Other than that final critique the movie also excelled in some of these areas and that makes for a good enough film as far as I'm concerned. The movie's lows are never that bad and it's highs are actually quite exceptional. One particular scene comes near the end that I won't spoil but suffice it to say that the main character's long hard suffering did not go unnoticed. He truly was a hero even if he didn't feel like it, VERY POWERFUL! It also connected well with the antagonist who also suffered in a lonely way. I'm not sure if this relationship was intentional on the part of the film makers but I must say it's nothing short of brilliant regardless. As far as a theme or a main point "Citizen X" offered some deep insights. Before I get too far into that I'd like to say that as an American I was drawn to the process a Soviet investigator would have to go through to deal with a serial killer and in that regard the film did not disappoint. The politics were very melodramatic but they were also very interesting. Which leads me to a point on theme. A friend of mine who identifies himself as a "moderate" believes that just because communism failed in the past does not mean that it can't succeed in the future. Haha not a moderate position in my opinion but I digress. My answer to him is that the reason why it has failed whenever it has been tried (I use the word "tried" because it has never been fully and successfully implemented) is due to it's inaccurate philosophical anthropology. It assumes the adequate or even good nature of mankind. I think "Citizen X," while under the guise of a flawed Soviet system, demonstrates the doomed reality of centralized government. The further a bureaucrat resides from a problem, either by physical distance or emotional, the more likely they are to become part of the problem or at least exasperate it. Appearances to authorities is all that ultimately matters and in a centralized system what matters differs greatly the further one is removed from a local problem. I actually think "Citizen X" is timely as media attempts to make the past 8 years of politics (2008 to 2016) in America sound like good things have happened when voters went out and demonstrated that it was only good for a centralized minority. The issue that the main character deals with, namely the bureaucratic red tape, are the very same ones an average person has to deal with now when getting health care or a college loan among other things. The well intentioned imbeciles think that centralized government can actually work going forward. It cannot and "Citizen X" does a good job of giving an example of why it will never work. No one cares about your problems more than you and those closest to you. In the final act a man beats his head against a tree as the murderer victimized a relative of his and that moment punctuated the need for a real solution not one that only looks good on paper. I imagine an unintentional point but a good one none the less.

history.title: Phoenix Forgotten
history.text: In the interest of full disclosure a relative of my wife has a bit role in this film and that's why I watched it, well that and some reviews I have seen. If not for those factors I would have never seen it because I have next to no interest in "found footage" movies. I prefer great originality and I don't tend to think the same set up and premise could yield much deviation in terms of story telling. In fact the first and only found footage movie I have seen was "The Blair Witch Project" in theaters which I enjoyed. After that why see basically the same thing with a different skin? I similar feelings for super hero films but I'll just leave that there. Some of my fears about the sameness of "Blair Witch" were realized in "Phoenix Forgotten" and there were some pretty contrived scenes as well. My complaints end there though. Other than the fact that this is not the original "found footage" movie I'd say that this is superior to "Blair Witch" and in almost every way. The final half hour of the film honestly felt far too similar to "Blair Witch" to me and seems to have confirmed my bias against these kinds of movies. However, again, these are my only complaints. In truth this is a dynamic movie with a non linear plot that will lead to enjoyment upon repeat viewing. There was some compelling hints peppered throughout that I thought was a really nice touch. The film makers didn't think I was a dolt. They treated me like a sophisticated viewer that can think for myself and I appreciate that. This movie is somewhat like a puzzle and fragments of dynamic media apparatuses bleed into the narrative rather than just a straight shot to the end. I have no problem with simple, linear story telling (I enjoy almost all of Polanski's films) but it takes guts and skill to tell a story the way "Phoenix Forgotten" does and they pull it off quite well. Now that I think about it I do have one more minor quibble which I will leave vague to avoid spoiler territory but at a pivotal point in the story they give you too much information. I really would have liked it better if everything had been kept a mystery. One of the strengths of the movie is the tight rope it walks between extraordinary and mundane but it violates this at one point with a clear image that spills answers all over the place. That's too a bad and a missed opportunity in my opinion. In its defense I will say that it sets you up for this and that was pretty good but not as good as if I had been left with a sense of wonder which is much better than a sense of closure. As to why so many people don't like this movie I have some speculation: they may have had their fill of "found footage" movies, in a sense you are watching a movie that is a faux documentary about a home video which contains news real footage (yeah that's a little complicated), they may have expecting a horror film (I expected nothing and got a compelling mystery movie) and didn't really get that. My conclusion would be that this is best entered with the mind set that it is a mystery and it is attempting a different spin on the "found footage" genre and it accomplishes this with moderate success. If the goal was to tell me a great story I would say that they succeeded. Lastly, I am in the middle of a retrospective where I am watching about ten movies form every year of my life that I have missed. "Phoenix Forgotten" has showed me how far our culture has come in terms of unique story telling today as compared to the 70's. One of the best films I have seen from my retrospective is "The Texas Chainsaw Massacre." It was so unique for its time and so well done. I hope that someone in the future that had never seen "found footage" movies before sees this instead of "The Blair Witch Project" because I think they will be blown away. No one ever perfected what "The Texas Chainsaw Massacre" did, not even Tobe Hooper, but Justin Barber absolutely has put the icing on the cake of this genre. Now let's hope this genre dies for it has been exhausted in my, admittedly, partially informed opinion.

history.title: The Stepford Wives (1975) [DVD]
history.text: Movie 3 of 1975 and 24 overall in my journey through films of my lifetime. I timed "The Stepford Wives" in conjunction with Halloween and it wasn't really until the 3rd act until that choice paid off. I always heard about this movie/story and it came off to me as a horror trope. Indeed there are ways in which it is just that. The idea of losing control is maybe the supreme horror axiom. "The Exorcist" and "Night of the Living Dead" are two that come to mind. I'm not saying that "The Stepford Wives" is that level of horror or quality but it had its moments. The third act is when it really takes a turn into the macabre and that was quite enjoyable. While I don't usually appreciate politics in my movies (although sometimes it is unavoidable) "The Stepford Wives" is clever in its implementation and I actually couldn't imagine the story told without some of its feminist elements. Perhaps I find older feminism more reasonable but I'm not sure. I will say that there were moments where the movie does hit you over the head with its allegory but that didn't detract from how well ingrained it was into the story overall. The main character is well acted and compelling. Her relationship with her husband is played very well and there is a time where the film makes her seem crazy in the eyes of the husband and you can't blame him. I'm not sure a modern version of this would have done that so it was refreshing to see the husband humanized rather than being a feminists caracture of a male which is usually what you get these days. I'd like to take a moment to compliment the music. It was perfection. I actually, personally liked none of it but it worked and was appropriate. The best scene in the movie comes near the end when we see a "malfunction" of a stepford wife and a rather than show circuits and smoke we hear robotic music, really cool. BTW that malfunction scene was as good as any I have vertigo seen in a horror movie. I found myself smiling at its creepy camera angles and unnatural disposition. It was as if the director wanted to plunge you into the uncanny valley and he did and did it well. Some elements suffered from just being an older movie. The film quality was not even as good as some of its contemporaries like "Barry Lyndon." Today, with digital, it seems even the lowest budget film will have decent looking quality. Now for "The Texas Chainsaw Massacre" the low quality film stock gave it that "Grindhouse" look that so many directors strive for. That didn't work for "The Stepford Wives." It needed a clean look, a polished world of perfection that reflected the whims of its antagonists. It needed to look like a compelling place to be so that when the ugly truth was unearthed you would feel duped. In conclusion, I liked it. I'm not sure it was a horror film but it was a good movie to watch on a Sunday night with my wife. Pros -well directed (especially the final scene in the grocery store, complex blocking and camera movements in one take but done flawlessly to great effect) -powerful third act (although a main character is discarded too hastily) -good comedic moments -music was well done -worked as a political satire (a rare exception IMO) Cons -low film quality takes you out of the experience -relational resolution between the husband and wife was unsatisfactory -a little slow toward the end of the second act

history.title: The Babadook
history.review_title: What!? No jump scares and easy answers!?
history.text: (spoilers via implication) I'm not sure if the Babadook was real or if this woman had just gone crazy. Perhaps the Babadook was a manifest of her unnatural regret from losing the "wrong" person. Guess what: I really don't care. I'm no postmodernist but I am grateful for much of the art it has produced. While I think some movies need clear resolutions and concrete answers I think some are better served by making us ponder. I own several movies that I have watched my whole life and will watch the rest of my life because they are bigger than the screens I have watched them on. They require dissection and cerebral work and I love it. "The Pabadook" is not meant to be watched passively, one is to really dive in and wrestle with its images and intellectual content. As I arrived closer to the ending I began to worry that the film would disappoint me and we would see the main character in a psych ward or it would be a dream or some political metaphor. Instead I was treaded to a tale that respects me as a participant not a mindless drone looking for a cheap thrill. Besides those cheap thrills are present in most movies being made these days. Thankfully "The Babadook" is much more. From a technical perspective I thought it was equally brilliant. Many wonderfully creepy scenes that I thought came close to rivaling those in "The Ring." The story took some cues from "The Shining" and a good story teller doesn't always have to reinvent the wheel. The acting was superb! I'll say that the music and sound were equal to the prowess of every other element of the movie. The only thing that turned me off to the movie is that some scenes that were meant to be scary were funny. Also the movie shifts from the book and visions of the Babadook to the mother and her internal struggle. That shift, although not forced, still lacked a clear logic. As a postmodern work I understand that will happen from time to time but there is still a sense of transition or emotional momentum that ought to be present but the shift in focus just sort of happened and it was a little empty. I didn't think the main character's inverted motives that worked against her own interests as the tension began to ramp up was moments that were entirely earned. I didn't see a reason for her to "side" with the Babadook. Yes one could conclude some form of possession but even that would seem hasty and cheap. So the movie tried but it failed in my opinion. Regardless I highly recommend "The Babadook." I watch one horror a year for Halloween and this one definitely made it a memorable one!

history.title: The Passenger
history.text: Movie 4 of 1975 and 25 overall in my journey through films of my lifetime. 54:27 was the third time I checked how much time was left and considered turning this movie off. I really, REALLY, want to enjoy and soak up every minute of every one of these movies along the way in this journey. I will not, however, allow my time to be wasted by a bunch of freaking amateurs! My process when I watch a movie is with good will and appreciation for the efforts it took to get a movie onto the screen. In fact most movies I watch, provided they do at least the basic things right, I assume will be five stars. Maybe that's not the best way to go about it but I love movies and that's just how I see them. I have a rule: if I have to rewind something to get information that I missed it's my fault. If I have to rewind a second time I really need to make sure I'm alert, get a cup of coffee or something. The third time I have to rewind I don't bother, because it is the goal of the film maker to deliver the information to me and at this point they simply don't have the skills to keep a person of good will toward them invested: it's THEIR fault. Was I bored watching "The Passenger?" You bet. Was it more boring than "Serpico?" Nope. Then why did I watch all of "Serpico" and not this? Because the effort and skill was there in "Serpico." I would not insult those film makers by comparing their movie to this piece of garbage. In fact I will give "Serpico" another shot one day now that I have had time to think about it. I can guarantee you my mind won't change about this filler. That's right I said it: FILLER. This movie wasted my time to show me filler. Would you like to come to my house and see my pictures from Lake Tahoe circa 2000? Sound interesting? If so then "The Passenger" is the movie for you! 30 minutes in when we finally get to the plot point of act 1 I thought "who was the editor of this movie and how did he or she fail the process of film making so badly?" I mean it is clear that the first 25 minutes is almost entirely unnecessary. If, by the end of the movie, it was necessary it would have only required no more than 5 minutes of what I saw, and rewound, and saw, and rewound-well you get it. I looked up the editor on IMDB just to see if they had ever improved. Fortunately they degenerated into soft core porn where they belonged. Nobody minds long, uncut, meandering scenes in that industry. I actually have the fortitude to finish this heap of crap but why would I allow such worthless bores to waste my time? Folks this movie is so bad, so amateurish, that they have you read on many occasions because they can't tell a story with pictures. I thought I was watching a movie, why are you having me read?! Really?! I understand that sometimes reading is acceptable in a film but not this much, not to supply information that you aren't creative enough to convey. Some things we read are also entirely unnecessary. Don't get me wrong I love to read. My favorite book is "1984" and I'm convinced it could never make a good movie because what makes it good is abstract and can't be boiled down to concrete images. The fact to the matter is that "The Passenger" at 54:27 is basically about an identity thief with unclear motives that gets in over his head with some arms dealers and will likely find himself in the middle of a family mess and a civil war and I really don't care. By the time we get to any story at all I am fuming and have no good will left in me toward this movie and its creators. Pros -start of a bright future for a bad editor in the porn industry Cons -I won't make an effort at a con list since the creators of "The Passenger" couldn't be bothered to create anything above filler themselves. -okay fine I'll offer filler in my cons list: hey I used to have a dog named "Feathers." I would wake her up when she was old because I thought she was dead. Buuuuut she was just asleep! Whew! Imagine how relieved I was every time I woke her! This was exactly the kind of movie that I feared I would see by watching 70's movies. Thank goodness there has been some treasures so far.

history.title: Love and Death [DVD]
history.text: Movie 5 of 1975 and 26 overall in my journey through films of my lifetime. As my third Woody Allen film I was beginning to think he was pretty much over rated. I found myself rather surprised at how funny "Love and Death" came off to me. I have made a career out of philosophy and it is an intrugal part of my life since I was able to begin thinking. Any effort to embrace philosophy in film is always greeted warmly by me. In this case much of it was just gibberish: strings of technical vocabulary with no real meaning though it appeared to posses as much. It's not hard to do actually I'll make one up now: prima facie affiliation must be, and cannot otherwise be, constructed of and by constituent components that cannot be resolved by hitherto cerebral methodology and thus count as efficacious in circumscribed* explanatory tautologies (*the circumscription is a necessary ontology and is not subject to infinite vicious regress). If you have seen "Love and Death" you will note a very important difference between my gibberish and Woody Allen's: his is actually funny (and a clever play on real Russo philosophy). That really gets to the core of what I like about this movie, it's genuinely funny and smart. I have always heard that Allen had a sophisticated humor. Well that may be a bit overplayed but he is no run of the mill comedian either. One method that is employed by Allen is a sort of shotgun methodology. In other words he's going to throw a lot of jokes at you (Mel Brooks style) and some of them are bound to hit pay dirt. I can also see why he liked working with Diane Keaton. She was beautiful, funny and a very talented actress. I guess I would add that one way you can tell if this movie is for you is that although it is a period piece Allen, anachronistically, wears his trademark glasses the entire time. Although that may seem shallow it's an easy mark to miss as far as jokes go. The reason it tells you something about this movie is that there is a lot of similar humor in this. I think that's why it's not entirely fair to say Woody Allen's films are high brow or sophisticated, to a small degree they are but he is above nothing. What I think actually mattered to him most was being funny. Of course I don't really know his motives but it seemed that way to me and that's definitely a compliment considering this is a comedy. I should note that there are jokes that are clearly meant to be parades of other works or history and some of that went over my head. He makes it clear that's what he's doing by his skilled directoral style but I didn't always know what the joke was actually about. Don't let that scare you off if you are considering this one though. There are so many jokes at such a rapid pace some will hit and some will miss. In my opinion most hit and made me laugh to my surprised delight. Pros -a funny comedy that usually hits its mark -a rare nod to philosophy -a rare nod to an often ignored part of history -Diane Keaton -unique Cons -very little familiarity, not a comfortable film to watch. -the middle gets a little slow in terms of pacing -story is muddled (not a small con but certainly story was not the main point)

history.title: Gilmore Girls: A Year In The Life (DVD)
history.review_title: Only for completionists and huge Gilmore fans
history.text: In terms of quality of writing you may have noticed a dive toward the bottom in the final season of the original run of "Gilmore Girls." When I heard the original creator Amy Sherman-Palladino and her husband Daniel were returning for "Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life Of" my hopes could not of been higher. Those hopes dwindled as this revival went on. I noticed that in the original series there were many cute elements. In the revival they were rarely able to be funny so they just went with cute. That's mainly true for the first episode. I actually liked the second episode and it was giving me more of what I had hoped for but a huge sticking point remained: it was pointless. I have noticed that other reviews have mentioned this and their warnings should not be ignored. As we enter the third episode it starts strong but tries to become a musical and it's really just filler. The third episode shows that Amy Palladino has lost her edge. Another huge factor was that a major character was missing. No, not the grandfather. No, not Sookie. The character that was missing was Lorelai Gilmore. All I can say is that Lauren Graham failed the fans of the show in dramatic fashion. She could not seem to muster the spunk and spirit that the character possessed before. She was simply not up to the task. I guess she didn't believe in the project or perhaps age caught up with her, or maybe she was having personal issues. I'm not sure but you should know that the main character of the show is MIA in this revival. She is there in body alone. She looks great but she is a shell of her former self. What is more, they go political. The original series had done this several times but it was at a minimum. There are multiple times where their ignorant, backwater views are shoved in the audience's face and it greatly diminished my goodwill toward the show. I hope they never make another episode of "Gilmore Girls, " it is dead. Let it rest in peace.

history.title: Farewell, My Lovely
history.text: Movie 7 of 1975 and 28 overall in my journey through films of my lifetime. I was only going to give a movie five stars if it met an important criterion: it must have re-watchability and I could recommend it with the confidence that I would with all of my absolute favorites. If a movie met this standard my mission to find a gem from the past would be complete (although that's not the singular goal of my journey). While "Farewell My Lovely" didn't actually meet either of my criteria I do believe I have a found a first gem in my journey. I love PI movies/stories. A friend of mine pointed out that all of my stories that I have written have a place for a PI in almost all of them. I hated to admit it but he was right. I'm fascinated by this kind of character and can't turn away. A major assumption that was possessing me as I watched this was that this was a homage to classic noir films of the past. Mitchum was in many of these movies as a younger actor and this type of film was trending at this time as I was understand. So I think my assumption was safe. If that is what was intended in this film I must say that I have nothing but supreme appreciation for the project. In later times these films have been parodied like "The Adventures of Ford Fairlane" or twisted in creative ways like "Angel Heart." As a Gen Xer I have to say that they didn't sour my taste for this in the least. I was smiling from ear to ear with great pleasure at every bit of dialog and action scene and betrayal, yes delicious BETRAYAL! Today it should come off campy but in truth I think it was meant to come off as a tip of the hat to an era gone by and camp was just fine if that's what needed to happen to make it authentic. Robert Mitchum's performance was just perfect. He didn't deserve any awards or anything his personality and presence was an advantage. The noir elements were fantastic and actually not heavy handed. There were scenes I think David Lynch would have LOVED from a repetitive, lonely dog barking in the background to a brothel and a drug induced abstraction that comes out of nowhere and could not have been more welcome. This movie hit all the right notes. The music was outstanding and proves, to me anyway, that 70's films could have had more appropriate music that actually sounded good, set the mood, or reflected it. Pros -noir perfection visually and not too much of it -hard boiled PI to a T -gritty story with the scenery to boot -pitch perfect music Cons -some elements will seem campy to modern viewers (bad ADR, off sound effects, etc.)

history.title: The Devil's Rain
history.review_title: FINALLY a positive spin on the Salem Witch Trials
history.text: Movie 8 of 1975 and 29 overall in my journey through films of my lifetime. So have you ever thought, "What if the victims of the Salem Witch trials were actually guilty?" Yeah I know, I haven't either, and it is the most meager element of "The Devil's Rain" but probably one of its best moments in terms of quality of camp. I'll go ahead and say that this is one you should watch with friends to get a good laugh. Watching this alone was not great. It had its moments. The opening was exciting and funny. After that it takes a turn for the boring and was never scarry. I'll give credit to the fact that it took place in a ghost town that gave it a western horror vibe that was unique. The term "vessel" was used many times and I thought this was referring to William Shatner's character, whom oddly acted almost exactly like James T Kirk. The surprise to me was that it was actually referring to a macGuffin that housed the souls collected by the devil. While the movie was focused on Shatner's character it was actually pretty good, but that was given up for an infomercial on Satanism. There would be a Satanism craze in the eighties that horrified many parents so I'm sure this would have been perfect in that time but I'm not sure how it played in the 70's. In the middle of the movie came a look at the cult's existence during the Salem Witch Trials. I'm thinking that the film makers were assuming they had found a universal enemy to couch the cult to make them look cool. It really added very little and muddied the plot. Ultimately "The Devil's Rain" was aimless and confusing. It also didn't satisfy as camp as well as many other movies like "The Room" or "Firestorm" to name a few. Pros -some unintentionally funny moments -unique elements -strong beginning -all star cast list Cons -not campy enough -too slow at times -disjointed and confusing

history.text: Pretty standard Lego fare for DC comics. A reasonable story with elements from the DC past. Braniac collecting worlds and this time, the Justice League needs to stop him. Braniac is a bit less than level 5 genius but who cares. Batman doesn't brood quite as much but is still in character. We get three members of the Legion of Super Heroes as a bonus, and the heroes in some time-travele altered costumes. That's fun also. And why in the world would you buy this without getting the Cosmic Boy character inside? That's part of the fun.
