history.title: God's Not Dead (DVD)
history.review_title: Christian students at a secular university
history.text: I am an evangelical Christian and a graduate of three secular universities, two of them nationally and internationally known and acclaimed. So, I think I know something about university life and about bearing a Christian testimony while studying and interacting in a secular university setting. I find the plot and story line in this film unrealistic and fanciful and the portrayal of university faculty inaccurate and insulting. A fairly widespread perception of university professors among right-wing evangelical Christians is that they will chew up and spit out tender little evangelical Christians and destroy their faith within the first semester on campus. After two masters degrees and a hard-earned doctorate, I simply have not met that type of professor. A faith that can be destroyed in a semester isn't much of a faith. The best advice I can give Christian students is this: On day one find a good, strong, campus student ministry and align yourself with it. Pray and study the Word with like-minded students and faculty. Nourish your faith, witness by the integrity and morality of your life. And find a good church in the city where you are and join it and participate.

history.title: The Big Gundown (Blu-ray + DVD + CD) Combo
history.review_title: Masterpiece of the Spaghetti Western genre.
history.text: Excited to finally see a hi def release of this most significant film in the long career of Lee Van Cleef. A cut down version of THE BIG GUNDOWN with faded color shown in pan & scan on the Encore Western channel cannot do justice to director Sergio Sollimas classic Western. Lee Van Cleef turns in probably his best performance as an egotistical lawman with political ambitions who engages in a brutal hunt for the Mexican peon Cuchillo (Little Knife. his weapon of choice.) Tomas Milian gives a very energetic performance here as Cuchillo. As a frustrated Van Cleef fails to capture his prey he begins to doubt his abilities, a dangerous development for him as he must soon face an eccentric Prussian gunslick (The Baron)who is determined to murder Cuchillo and is every bit as capable and deadly as Van Cleef himself. Also, in a too small role, is actress Maria Granada as Cuchillos wife and part time prostitute. Surely one of the most beautiful creatures to ever walk the face of this earth. Apparently this set has a (two?) CD soundtrack of the movie score, one of Morricones best, which makes the asking price more than reasonable. Hopefully there are other extras as well. Perhaps some other reviewers can reveal them if they are more knowledgeable about the product. If you are a collector who can appreciate great films don't even think twice about purchasing this product. Just do it!

For it's age this movie looks great, the subs are very good as well and it packs more action into it's last 20 minutes then THE MAGNIFICENT SEVEN (Itself a remake of SEVEN SAMURAI) did in it's 2 plus hours. I had hoped for a little more Kung Fu, although there is still a goodly amount on tap, but in lieu of hand to foot action you get a slew of bullets and dynamite chewing up the screen. Also, this movie reminded me of another Hong Kong actioneer with Sammo (as star AND director) called EASTERN CONDORS which borrows liberally from MISSING IN ACTION and THE DEERHUNTER but still a great "Men on a mission"movie. Check it out if you get the chance.

history.title: Barquero
history.text: This is for the Kino Lorber blu ray released in April of 2015. Like THE WILD BUNCH this movie begins and ends with a massacre. However, unlike that Peckinpah classic, it eschews the gigantic blood squibs and slo-mo violence. The plot is simple and serviceable enough, although unusual. In the late 1800's there must have been thousands of these barges used in the west but it's the first time I've seen a movie specifically about their necessity. About the main characters. Warren Oates was a very capable character actor and here he portrays a bloodthirsty leader of a large band of outlaws. This is the kind of role he could do in his sleep however so he yells loudly most of the time and kills indiscriminately. There is an attempt at back story here that reveals how he became the boss but it's not that interesting. Still, it's Warren Oates so you can't help but believe he's nothing short of despicable. Lee Van Cleef was a different kind of actor. He never did get into that "emotion" thing very much because he didn't have to. With his hawk nose, squinty glare and growly voice he exuded charisma by the bucket load. In most of his spaghetti westerns he was dressed to the 9's in black and outfitted with every deadly weapon in existence. Here he is a barge owner in a sleeveless shirt, frumpy hat and levi's but still manages to look like the last guy you want to piss off. Forrest Tucker I think was best known for a ridiculous 60's sit com called F TROOP. Quite frankly I was prepared to dismiss him as a washed up actor hired because of some favor perhaps. Boy was I surprised. Here he portrays a local mountain man and Van Cleef's only capable ally. He's clearly insane though, and just as clearly enjoys killing and torture, often delivering a clever quip to his victim b4 he shoots, stabs or strangles him.. His performance possibly provided the template for today's witty serial killers like Hannibal or Dexter. I'm pretty sure Anthony Hopkins must have seen BARQUERO at some time Last but not least is Mariette Hartley. Smoldering hot even covered from head to toe in a floor length dress made out of a canvas tent, she could be the owner of a whore house and still make you think she's a virgin. She and Van Cleef provide the best sex scene in a western...ever. I'll describe it for you but it could be considered a spoiler so stop reading here if you prefer. At one point in the movie Hartleys doofus husband is held captive by the outlaw gang on one side of the river while the townfolk are on the other. Hartley knows that Van Cleef desires her and she uses that to her advantage. She promises him the night of pleasure he always dreamed of if only he will rescue her husband. It's a suicide mission and she knows it but she also knows Van Cleef cannot resist her. She plays the scene so well that few men could. Amazingly, Van Cleef succeeds with Tuckers help. When Van Cleef comes to claim his prize she sulks. No doubt thinking that most men would let her off with a kiss on the cheek, and that's the way it would be, in most westerns. In this one however, Van Cleef wants what was promised. In this (day) night scene Van Cleef is shirtless and apparently had a bit of a sunburn. With his red skin and evil smirk he looks like Lucifer raping an angel as he rips off Hartley's blouse revealing her lightly freckled milky white skin and her loose strawberry blonde hair. Later, after the capital act is performed. Hartley makes an attempt at shaming Van Cleef for his behavior but Lee, ever the anti-hero, just chuckles and walks back to camp and his cigar smoking Mexican girlfriend. It's a great scene and lifts the movie above the standard B westerns of the time. The blu ray here seems to be a bit sharper than when I saw BARQUERO on the Encore Western channel. It is probably as good as you will ever see this film. I enjoyed the movie quite a bit and wish there had been more extras but most of the cast is now deceased. An original trailer for the movie is provided. The action scenes are well filmed and realistic for the most part. The U.S. cavalry used single action carbines instead of lever action winchesters but that's small potatoes. There's a lot of lead thrown in this flick and good storytelling. You won't be bored.

history.title: Mad Max (Collector's Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Hard to pass this up if you are a fan.
history.text: This review is for the Collectors Edition from "Shout! Factory" released in May of 2015. The picture here is as good as you will ever see this film. Ditto the audio. I just watched the whole thing complete and the extras are quite good, being very informative and never boring. Mel Gibson has some good anecdotes and leaves no doubt that this is the "accidental" movie role responsible for his rewarding career. Joanne Samuel has plenty of things to say as well. Remarkably, she has the exact same hairstyle as she did 35 years ago during filming. There's quite a bit of David Eggby who talks at length about the perils of the production including the financial situation. (My latest VIDEO WATCHDOG reports the total cost at about $400,000.00 and since they never make a mistake I'll stick with that). Director Michael Pate makes a short appearance with a story about how he directed Mel in his movie TIM just before MAX was released. He bemoans the fact that after the release of MAX he could not afford to hire Gibson for another of his films so rapid was his rise to stardom. That gave me quite a laugh because if you have ever seen TIM, where Gibson plays a mentally retarded yard boy to Piper Laurie, you would probably believe, as I do, that Gibson would not have done another film with Pate no matter HOW much money he was offered. Finally though,, The best thing about this particular Collectors Edition, if you are a REAL collector, is that when you peel off the shrink wrap you can carefully take the artwork folder out of the see-thru plastic, reverse it, re-insert it and PRESTO!!! You have the original 1979 poster art for your disc. That's why it gets that 5th star and makes it worth the price, for me anyway.

history.title: Shaun the Sheep Movie [DVD + Digital]
history.text: So I was watching this on cable. Not bad, not great, but my animated taste runs to RICK and MORTY or ARCHER and this was a little 2 cutesy pie for me. Then, I met the villain. An animal control nazi who locks up animals in cages after capturing them with an electrified shock gun that looks like something Wile E. Coyote would order from Acme. He has shifty eyes, an evil laugh, smirks a lot. You know the drill. He obviously hates all critters, except sheep in women's clothes, who he is strangely attracted too btw. Don't worry folks, it's all P.G. here and I started to perk up and pay more attention to this oddball character. Suddenly he whips out his business card and presents it to a fugitive sheep (in women's clothes) and what is his name? "A. TRUMPER". What the heyyy? Are you kidn me? Did they manage to slip that into this flick & nobody notices it... Or have I just been watching to much politics on T.V.? Please somebody, set me straight. Was Donald Trump on the radar screen when they were making this movie? Is this a tongue in cheek slam at his supporters, or does "A. TRUMPER" mean something else in England? They obviously wanted the audience to see that this no goodnick guy was "A. TRUMPER' because his name was prominently shown on screen more than once. But, was Trump already being vilified that long ago? Right now (May 18 2016) Trump is a hot topic in the U.K. and is being heavily criticized by P.M. David Cameron & the new muslim mayor of London (although celeb author J.K. Rowling seems to think he's a great guy). So, are Trump supporters in England called "Trumpers" and equated with being cruel to animals? Are they universally disliked by most Britons? (Mr A Trumper winds up in a pile of bull poop at the end of the movie) Or...Am I just imagining this and it's some weird coincidence in political timing. Anyone know when this movie went into production... and where? Is this a U.S. flick made Hollywood perhaps? I gave the movie 1 star just to get your attention btw. It's not bad if you're into PG animation. I'm just very curious if this is a slam on Donald Trump supporters.

history.title: Hard Target 2 [Blu-ray]
history.text: I will give this flick 1 star for the great location shooting and another for Rhona Mitra. Other than that it is pretty poorly done and I have come to expect much more than this from Adkins. As others have commented, the people in the movie acted stupidly. Several times Adkins leaves the weapons of fallen enemies behind and when he finally does use a discarded M-16 he easily shoots down a dozen hapless soldiers with no effort whatsoever. The weapons action on display throughout this movie is actually cringe inducing. Unforgivably, the fights are boring as well. Not only are they short (the girl vs girl face-off lasts about 30 seconds) but lazily filmed. The final slugfest on the bridge is so poorly performed you can see the missed punches and kicks. This is not worthy of Adkins at all. I am not familiar with director Roel Reine, nor would I want to be. He is either lazy or incompetent, or both. I am, however, a fan of director Isaac Florentine ever since he helmed U.S. SEALS 2 lo these many years ago. He recently worked with Adkins on the flick CLOSE RANGE. This effort probably cost half of what was spent on HARD TARGET 2 and is a great example of what Adkins is capable of doing. Try that movie if you are looking to add to your collection. I am donating my copy of HARD TARGET 2 to the local Am Vets so they can check out Rhona Mitra.

history.title: Blindman
history.review_title: Finally. A solid release for this spaghetti western classic.
history.text: Stumbled across this recent release by accident a few weeks ago & quickly ordered it. Just watched it (12- 26- 2016) & pleased to report that this is a very good effort from ABKCO studios. First I've heard of them btw. I am a bit of a spaghetti western enthusiast & have been hoping that maybe Arrow Video would eventually put this gem in their Blu-Ray catalog & release it with some substantial extras. This particular effort is sadly lacking in that department unfortunately, as the only extra is one trailer. The print is very good however. This was a well funded effort at the time of its production with excellent interior / exterior set design & cinematography. There are literally hundreds of extras, all outfitted in period correct costumes, with the colors being bright & distinctive. The volume appears to be somewhat muted but I just cranked it up a bit & no problem. For western enthusiasts who are unfamiliar with this seldom seen effort, the movie is rated "R" (and earns it). Despite its comic overtones there is an abundance of nudity. The communal shower scene itself has dozens of attractive women wandering to & fro while completely naked and in later scenes there is a goodly amount of brutal violence (beatings, rapes AND shooting deaths) toward the female cast as well. All courtesy of the very capable exploitation director Ferdinando Baldi. Those cringe-worthy scenes, in addition to the rather large blood squibs used during shoot-outs resulted in BLINDMAN being heavily cut or even banned outright in 1971 when it was released. No doubt this explains its rarity on television. Do NOT let Junior & his friends get this on their laptops to show at school or you may be getting a call from the local police. Never mind the local schoolmarm. Indeed, if you are one of the many who have never seen BLINDMAN, or even heard of it, the quite eccentric plot involves a sightless gunman (Tony Anthony) tasked with delivering 50 mail order brides to Texas. Mexican bandits (one of them played by Ringo Starr) steal the women to auction them off to the local federales. The BLINDMAN character here is derived from the Japanese ZATOICHI series about a blind, tho very capable samurai warrior. However, the Eurowestern version provides Anthony with a few more advantages then Zatoichi had. One is a slightly modified Winchester rifle to use as a walking stick along with...a seeing eye horse! Tony Anthony also starred in THE STRANGER franchise as well. All 4 of those movies are available on disc & recommended, provided you are a spagwest fan. Anthonys acting style & character here (aside from his inability to see) doesn't stray too far from his previous efforts and is minimalist, to say the least. His laconic delivery of lines closely mimics Robert Mitchums sometimes "dis-interested" method. Additionally, regarding the cast, all of the ex-Beatles were still huge pop culture icons in the early seventies & Ringo Starr was actually the "big" promotional name in BLINDMAN. He's no Klaus Kinski here, with his portrayal of a psychotic, lovesick bandido, but he gets the job done fine. Starr is still active today & recently did a tennis shoe commercial I believe. A real missed opportunity that they could not have him do a commentary here with Christopher Frayling, or someone else of his caliber. (shameless hint to Arrow Video) So finally... If you think you can handle the lapses into hardcore violence shown towards women in this film - an unfortunate but necessary part of its charm & cult following - I recommend this product highly.

history.title: White Tiger
history.text: I almost disregarded this movie at first glimpse of the box art. A Soviet soldier armed with a WW 2 era PPsh 41 sub machine gun shown above an enhanced T-62 Russian tank from the 1960's cold war. It reminded me of the cover art on numerous grade "C" (mostly European) dtv war flicks released during the 80's video rental boom. I wish the manufacturer here had used the ORIGINAL cover art that is shown on the Region B case as I am one of those fussy collector types. Anyway, after reading a few reviews I picked it up mostly due to the price. Box artwork aside, I liked this movie. It's not a straight up war flick but the combat scenes are realistic & quite violent, with authentic equipment & vehicles throughout. There was even a nice touch where a Soviet major uses a German MP-40 sub. During the war these captured weapons were sometimes given to high ranking officers as perks, not necessarily because of capability, but because the build quality was better than their counterpart. Movies about haunted vehicles are not really a rarity if you think about it. KILLDOZER, CHRISTINE & MAXIMUM OVERDRIVE are just some of the better known ones I can think of right now. There was even a comic book about a WW 2 tank crew fighting in an M-3 tank possessed by the ghost of Confederate general J.E.B. Stuart titled THE HAUNTED TANK. The main character here in WHITE TIGER, an apparently indestructable tank driver, is suitably distant from the people around him, almost as if in a trance. His superiors are the usual bureaucratic types who cannot comprehend anyone being so "different". Amusingly they try to either ignore his eccentric behavior or send him to an asylum where he cannot intrude on their communist inspired group-think. The exception is a major from the intelligence section who has been ordered to destroy the WHITE TIGER. The crew he assembles for the task, the driver, a rakish gunner & an alcoholic Siberian gun loader, is just as odd as the assignment. The major is constantly interacting with an almost soulless caste system of officers while being witness to a deadly slice of supernatural warfare. He eventually has his outlook on life changed forever. Meanwhile, the driver becomes a kind of Flying Dutchman who vanishes in a tip of his helmet to Clint Eastwood's HIGH PLAINS DRIFTER. The final scenes are somewhat problematic & surreal tho, as we are treated to a speech (from a well known historical figure) that might have been better suited for that 1968 classic THEY SAVED HITLERS BRAIN. Despite that curious finale it was a straight-up original and entertaining movie. I'll watch it again with some friends. Recommended.

history.title: Unholy Four, The (1970) aka Chuck Mool (Ciakmull - L'uomo della vendetta)
history.review_title: Another home run for Kino Lorber.
history.text: In the last 12 months i have added BLINDMAN, REQUIESCANT, FACE TO FACE & DAY OF ANGER to my western collection. After so many years of neglect I am glad to see some studios taking the Italian/Euro western genre to top quality release status for fans like myself. THE UNHOLY FOUR looks great here in Blu-Ray. The night scenes seem to be imbued with a touch of Mario Bava gel lighting style and director Enzo Barboni kind of mimics older directors like Sidney J Furie or maybe Hitchcock with some neat gimmicky camera work throughout. The extreme close-up shots of rifles and revolvers going thru their mechanical motions during an ambush seem to make the action that much more intense. UNHOLY also has one of the best saloon brawls of any western I've ever seen, complete with a kind of Jackie Chan vibe to the proceedings. Woody Strode is the American ringer in this spagwest and tho he only speaks about ten words (not counting the church choir audition) he has great presence here. As for the audio...Italian with English subs or English dubbing. Both good. Take your pick. On the downside, I didn't care overmuch for the musical score as it seems to be styled after Hollywood movies instead of what you might expect from a spaghetti western. Not terrible but no Ennio Morricone either. Also, the only bonus materials on tap were trailers from 2 (excellent) examples of the genre, NAVAJO JOE and SABATA. Bottom line here is that this movie isn't in A FISTFULL OF DOLLARS league but it does have well filmed action scenes, a high body count and some attractive females. I also appreciate studios that produce a quality product worth purchasing & that's why I give this film 5 stars. Soooo..If you & your friends are tired of watching THE SEARCHERS on TCM for the 100th time, give this movie a shot. Your guests will appreciate it. Some Blu macaroni combat in the future would be sweet as well.

history.title: The Mercenary - aka A Professional Gun (Il mercenario) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Another terrific entry in the European western genre from Kino Lorber. THE MERCENARY, directed by Sergio Corbucci (THE GREAT SILENCE) easily slides into any top 10 Spaghetti Western list you care to look up. The fantastic cast stars Franco Nero, who I regard as the "Steve McQueen" of European cinema. He exudes coolness here as a deadly gun- for- hire with a cynical attitude toward humanity in general. Tony Musante was also a very well regarded actor who did a ton of television work in the USA including the eccentric prison series OZ that was produced by HBO. He portrays an ambitious peon turned revolutionary here and is also the target of comical verbal abuse by a sarcastic Nero. Honestly, in this story they are as memorable as Newman and Redford at their best. Jack Palance ( as usual ) is in a movie of his own as the ruthless, religious and insane villain Curly. Giovanna Ralli as the romantic interest and passionate revolutionary is wonderful as well. She is that rare female who looks more beautiful without make-up than with. You won't soon forget those beautiful brown eyes and marvelous facial expressions. The movie itself has a few continuity problems, especially at the beginning. The plot jumps from one plot point to the next in rapid succession leaving the viewer to fill in the gaps with what might have happened in between but the main narrative is always there. It's also made clear at the beginning that the movie is told as a flashback , up until the pivotal showdown anyway. It's a great showdown too. Absolutely unique! Surreal and intense with a rodeo clown in pancake VS a dandified psychopath watched over by an ambivalent referee. A great Ennio Morricone soundtrack plays as the clock ticks away. Really unforgettable. Violent and comical. Pure genius. The film looks great in Blu. The packaging is original theatrical release art which, as a collector, I am a sucker for. ( when will these movies get steelbooks?) The extras are mostly trailers along with some interesting MERCENARY production pictures. There is a quite good audio commentary by Alex Cox as well. Top notch all the way around !

history.text: Bruno Ganz is such a superior actor, and this is maybe one of his best performances along with Wings Of Desire. It's hard to say 'finest', as it is Adolf Hitler, and based on a lot of speculation and here say. But, I think Bruno puts his all into it, and delivers such a humane portrait of one of histories greatest monsters. Had Hitler's last ditch maneuvers prove victorious, he may have led Germany on to great heights of prosperity and decadence. Or, he may have become the paranoid zealot and order every German to stand guard at the border to protect his ruined empire? Either way, we see a leader at the brink. The moment of truth. The denial of remorse, and the seething hatred for collective and personal failure. And though 99.9% of the world to this day view Hitler as a twisted, cruel, megalomaniac - he was still just a mere man who had dreams. And I think the movie shows that ANY leader of ANY country could easily look like Adolf in the bunker being surrounded by the enemy. How could something so right and powerful become so defeated and judged? Hard to imagine America, England, China, or Russia ever being put into that corner - and lose. But if it could happen to Hitler, it could happen to anyone still to this day. And oh, the truth we would learn thereafter. Exceptional movie with an exceptional cast portraying the exceptional ending of a leader who loved to hate, Yet may have not hated to love. How to span the chasm created within ones soul?

history.title: Automata
history.review_title: A Lot Of Skin Around A Little Meat
history.text: I had high hopes for this movie, but was sadly let down. It has the makings for a thought provoking story of the birth and continuation of A.I. life forms, and humans fear and bigotry of such a new race of life. But sadly glosses over a lot of the finer details that could've given the movie more 'umph'. It either tries too hard to be like Blade Runner, or I, Robot. It does give some insight into the birth and restraint of A.I. and the insurance company that ensures reliability, and investigates defects. But if this was a movie about railroads and derailments, I don't think the viewer would appreciate Antonio standing on the tracks in front of a high speed train to prove they don't hurt anyone. And this is where the movie goes downhill, at least for me. Some interesting aspects, and considerations for an A.I. race to develop in a non humanoid form and language. But in the end, it's the usual stand off, shoot out, literal cliff hanger. And the possibility of a sequel ala Mad Max. Or if Antonio can't make it for that one, it can easily be explained from this as well.

history.review_title: And The Darwin Award Goes To...
history.text: This movie left me with a bitter taste. This awful pretentious air that the human race has populated to such an extent that the abundance just 'lives to eat'. And McConaughy is the bitter farmer after having been a failed test pilot. Yet, a mysterious drone appears over the fields one day, and dad suddenly whips out a laptop while getting the kids to drive them all recklessly chasing it down. What does it mean? Where is it from? And then weird happenings begin in the daughters room. Ghosts? A miracle? Wait, it's longitude and latitude messages! (Close Encounters, here we come!) And that leads dusty mumbling McConaughey and stowaway daughter to the gates of an area 52 secret base. Turns out it's NASA, and they could use a good pilot like McConaughey for this super secret mission to restart pig eating humanity in a galaxy far, far away. And from there, all farm tools are dropped, kiss the kids goodbye, and lets get this bird out into the unknown! With cute gal and expendable crew members and unusual robot helpers that could be the bastard love childs of HAL9000, Robbie the Robot, R2D2 and the Ice Man from Logans Run. And let the action and suspense begin! And for anyone who has seen the Star Trek franchise, 2001: A Space Odyssey, Forbidden Planet, to Gilligans Island and Lost In Space - you've seen this movie already then. Save yourself 3hrs, and stick with the nutty classics.

history.title: Ghost Story [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Shout! Shout! Let It All Out!
history.text: This is to me one of the true great horror films of all time. Horror in the way of suspense, ominous surroundings, and just shear surprise at reveals. For all the hoopla Kubrick took for doing The Shining the way he did, pretty well only using King's title as the basis for the movie. Ghost Story fell under the same scrutiny. BUT - I think Kubrick redefined the horror genre on film, and left us with a truly haunting and memorable piece of cinema in his own right. And I'd say Ghost Story is a darn close second. Of course, the prime attraction was all the big names appearing in it. Which surprisingly is only about a third of the movie. Craig Wasson and Alice Krige really are the main stars throughout. I'm so happy Shout! is putting this out. And hopefully will contain more than enough to keep the die hard fans of the movie and/or it's timeless stars happy. They are really beginning to rival Criterion with these almost forgotten gem's. And infusing them with all the history, trivia, and then and now addendum's to shed new light and respect on it all. Keep up the great work Shout! And can't wait for this release!

history.title: A Man in Uniform
history.text: Excellent character study by Tom McCamus as a struggling actor that takes the bit role of a TV police officer a little too seriously. Only to realize the 'real law' on the streets is more corrupt and abusive than he could've ever imagine. A bit jumpy in places, and maybe a little too 'sped up' in plot devices and transformation. But all comes out at just the right length for a thought provoking and enjoyable movie.

history.title: The Royal Tenenbaums (The Criterion Collection)
history.review_title: As P.T. Anderson Would Say - "There's A Father Born Every Minute..."
history.text: Call me a late bloomer, but my first introduction to Wes Anderson was with The Grand Budapest Hotel, which took a moment to warm up to. But it's fast paced fantasy via flip flopping through history and it's cast of characters won me over quickly. So then why so many copies of The Royal Tenenbaums going cheaply everywhere? Because it's truly a 'majestic mess' in a good and bad way. Like The Hotel New Hampshire, it's a strange movie that I wasn't really sure I had witnessed properly when I saw it. A family and adventures akin to a 23 car pile up in Des Moines right after Valentines day. Bodies, blood, and heart shaped boxes dribbling out chocolates amid the carnage. Justice to some, tragedy to others, And in a short time it will all be swept away so that traffic can resume normally and safely. Is it worth investigating? Was there a culprit or any real motive behind it? Any heroes who were sadly cut short in their valor? Or just cosmic irony and probability at it's peak colliding in the middle of nowhere? Fascinating, sad, unbelievable, and spiritually confusing. And to add insult to injury (pardon the pun....); is there any entertainment value in any of it? That's what The Royal Tenenbaums seems to set out to find in a jam packed jalopy of a great cast and an uneven road lined with lamentations. To some maybe a feast for the imagination and emotions. But to me, it serves as a primer to how Wes learned to tighten things up for The Grand Budapest Hotel. And some may argue that movie is TOO fast. But I'd still have to say for Wes, his talent and niche mantra should be 'speed is the key'. You may wish to adopt or not The Royal Tenenbaums. But shall always be a friend of the family to your Criterion collection.

history.title: Notorious Bettie Page, The
history.text: For the little I knew about Bettie Page beforehand, I figured she had been a sexy slut out to capitalize on taboo eroticism long before Madonna and porn stars. I was surprised to learn she was this innocent christian from Nashville that was hard working, intelligent, and proud of her beauty. Yet the film isn't totally devoted to being a biography of Bettie, but more so the awareness and business of 'glamour' for a underground fetish market. And the hypocrisy of a scantily clad Jane in a Tarzan movie, to a scantily clad Bettie acting out in a men's magazine. Alluring vs. enticement - or vice versa? Where the movie somewhat fails is what personal deviation (if any?) this may have caused Bettie's outlook on relationships, sex, and fame. A little too 'righteously naive' and 'escaping unscathed' for me to believe. But it's Lili Taylor as Paula Klaw that showed the more believable character in the end. That Bettie was a true beauty, and there was to be a timelessness for the work she and others had done that congress and the moral majority were never going to effectively stomp out and punish. Kudos to Mary Harron for always being so darin' to take the seedier sides of life and put some humanity to it. Whether we believe it or not, it all makes for a good story in the end.

history.title: The Killer
history.review_title: Talk About Getting Some Bang For Your Buck!
history.text: Much like what Sergio Leone did for ''spaghetti westerns', John Woo put his stamp on 'Sweet And Sour Easterns' with this film. Yun Fat Chow certainly has this coolness and likability about him. And Danny Lee as well, as the unrelenting cop in pursuit. As violent and sickeningly sweet this movie is, it's also quite funny in places. The photogenic standoff where the cop confronts the killer at the blind love's abode is brilliantly suspenseful and hilarious. And may well be the antithesis for Mike Judge's 'Beavis & Butthead' (Though in this, Butthead & Numb Nuts has a better ring to it.) Over the top, yes! Overly sappy, yes! Overly violent, hell yes! But also very touching, funny and sad in many places. All in all, a fun movie that shows the many sides to John Woo.

history.title: Forrest Gump: Chocolate Box Giftset (Widescreen)
history.text: I haven't even gotten to the second DVD yet, so I'm not sure what I'm going to get? But as so many others have said, this movie is a classic that to me supersedes Jimmy Stewart in Harvey. And I think the 'box of chocolates' packaging is a clever and respectful way to memorialize this great film. I'm usually not into 'bells and whistles' when it comes to movie releases. Action figures, trading cards, stickers, etc. But I have to say this set put's the viewer 'in the mood' for this film. I was pretty moved by the tragedy that happens throughout the movie when I first saw it. And it left me saddened and depressed for some time. Was Forrest to forever live on the splinters of his past...? But having the incl. feather and nice smell of chocolates at hand, is a more assuring and satisfying feeling I get now when watching this. So for those that were like me that came away feeling 'is pure luck forever doomed?' when the movie ended, I have to say the packaging to this otherwise great film can give new perspectives and more uplifting to actually have some small something to feel, smell, and remember Forrest forever with.

history.title: Osterman Weekend
history.review_title: The Ostricized Director And The Completely Lost Weekend
history.text: I'd say this movie reflects Peckinpaw's emotional and mind state at that moment. A fearless TV interviewer (Rutger Hauer) is commandeered by the CIA when they suspect a group of his friends that comes for a annual house party has been solicited by the KGB. Former KGB spy (John Hurt) now with CIA after they killed his wife is heading the operation, and infiltrates the house with cameras and video equipment to get evidence as to which one of these 'friends' has alluded himself to the KGB. Thus becoming a weekend of suspicion, paranoia, and friendly patience. It sounds like a good scenario, but gets mired in clumsy dialog, over acting, and unexpected and over the top heroism. Maybe in Peckinpaws mind, this is how he viewed himself dealing with Hollywood and friends in the trade. But as a movie, it comes off convoluted, nightmarish, and a golden glow ending. For a seasoned director taking on a Robert Ludlum book, I think Ivan Reitman or John Hughes could've done a better job with this movie. Very disappointing!

history.title: The Jungle Book
history.review_title: Better than I thought it would be.
history.text: I was pleasantly surprised with the retelling of the Jungle Book story. The special effects do justice to the movie. I'm usually critical how CGI is overused in movies today, but it gave the talking animals more of a realistic look. And the jungle scenes looked realistic and natural. My main criticism is with the young actor playing the orphan. He lacked the ability to convey depth or emotion.His performance was passable but I think an Indian actor with the correct dialect would have made it more convincing. Also I didn't care for the songs hijacked from the animated version. It just didn't work for me. And of course the word "cool" uttered by the main character sounded silly. I recommend this version, even with the flubs I mentioned. I usually don't sit thru a whole movie these days, but I it kept me involved.

history.review_title: Awful. Boring. Been done a thousand times before.
history.text: Mindless drivel. Bad acting. Bad directing. Preposterous dialog. I didn't expect Shakespeare, but hoped for more than this trite offering.

history.title: Arrival [Blu-ray]
history.text: Arrival is one of those movies with good production values, competent actors, except for Forrest Whittaker and a new twist to a visit by Aliens. The problem is that I walked away confused and bewildered as to why I stuck it out. It was free, so I suppose that answers the second question. I like the idea that for a change the Aliens are not out to rip us limb from limb or zap us into dust, but I hoping for a more coherent story line. I had to go to Wikipedia to figure out what I had watched. I found myself getting up and doing something around the house and then coming back to watch, and then getting up again and again in order to get thru the movie. Not a good sign. If critics are calling this film the best movie of the year, the movie business is dead. Not financially, but artistically dead. Having a female heroine save the day and humanity seems to be the trend these days, but it's getting a bit overused. I like Amy Adams as an actress, but I think her role in this movie wasn't that great. I didn't relate to any of the characters in this film.

history.title: DOCTOR STRANGE
history.text: I wanted to like this movie basically because I think Benedict Cumberbatch is fine actor, but even his abilities do not save this film. I wish I could put my finger on why films like this don't entertain me. The visuals are well done and the obviously the production values are high. The dialog and plot is predictable and unnecessarily complicated at times. Little or no character development and some of the actors are just there for the sake of a diverse cast. There is no talent displayed by the Director actors or the anyone else associated with the making of this film. The usual CGI effects galore and twists and turns that make little sense. I suppose thats what audiences are used to today and apparently eat it up. I confess to being puzzled as to why films like this make hundreds of millions of dollars. But it is what it is.

history.title: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
history.review_title: Not as good as the previous installment.
history.text: My impressions upon watching this film were partly based partly on the first installment of "Rise of the Planet of the Apes" . I usually rate a movie as to whether I will watch it over and over again, or watch it once and put it away. This is a one time deal for me. I give it three solid stars for production value and acting, specifically by the Ape characters. I found the human actors annoying at times and the human lead, the nice guy, irritating and wimpy. The story was slow and monotonous. Rise of the Planet of the apes was original and held my interest throughout. I've watched it several times and each time enjoyed it." Dawn" sort of moved along slowly and made me wonder if maybe they should have moved in different direction with the story line. Nothing too original. The humans being human and the Apes in turn acting as bad as humans. As with most films made today, they seem to dumb the movies down for the masses. By not making it too complicated they fill the theaters and make their money.

The newest installment of the star trek franchise tries , but fails to capture the Original TV series flavor. Visually of course the CGI is superior to anything the previous TV and early movies did. And the costumes and makeup are excellent, but I just don't relate to the actors. One scene in particular I found annoying. I'll just leave it to ones imagination which scene that was.

Silly idea. In 1869 America, that they would have a black secret service agent, even if it existed back then is preposterous. The film producers should have forgotten political correctness and stay true to the source material. Aside from that it is still a bad movie.

The original Star Trek series is something that has never in my opinion been duplicated. Many movies and TV productions later, make me realize that the original was the best. Except of a few poor offerings, I have watched each and every episode numerous times and have enjoyed them all as though seeing them for the first time. I don't care for the enhanced special effects nor do I like what George Lucas did with the original Star Wars movie. If it's not broke don't fix it. The original series had it's own charm and I have never been a fan of the movies or other incarnations of the series.

In my opinion the fourth season had it's highlights, but was the weakest of the previous three seasons. Episodes 20 and 21 were blatantly obvious references to mutucultrial diversity that is constantly being thrown around , and is something that Hollywood feels compelled to insert into everything we watch today. Scott Bakula is the week link. His acting style just doesn't seem to fit well into the character of Archer. Jolene Blalock showed more depth and ability in the fourth season. When she's in scene it's impossible to take your eyes off her. She has a look that's hypnotizing. The last episode was weak and anticlimatic.

history.title: The Mummy (2017) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Could have been a good movie if it had a story, decent dialog and direction. And John Steinbeck.
history.text: I watched this movie from start to finish. It was free, so I didn't feel ripped off and my time is not that valuable as to wanting 2 hours of life back. Tom Cruise is a competent enough actor when given decent material and the actress playing the Egyptian princess is probably the highlight of the film. She's exotic and beautiful to look at. The other actors, with the exception of Russell Crowe, were substandard. What frustrates me about todays films is how they can be so bad with almost unlimited budgets. The three things that a film should give the movie goer is the story, believable dialog and direction. And a fourth, good Cinematography. Why, I ask myself, is Hollywood pumping out films like these? I know the source material has been done dozens of times, but a good writer can make it somewhat interesting. It's as if the people making movies just don't care, as long as it makes money, or keeps them busy. Maybe creativity and ability are dead in the film industry. Maybe it's political correctness watering down the talent pool. Or maybe it's that all the really talented people are dead. Who knows? I usually judge a movie I enjoy by how many times wish to view it. This was a one time event.

history.review_title: this is a good episode but season 7 was too much like DS9
history.text: First off, I am wanting to reveiw sesaon 7 as well as this episode. I give This episode five stars because of the episode itself yet season 7 is a collective of far too many "within" episodes, such as Jordie using his virtual self to find his mother, Data's nightmare holodec self solving physical problems and so on. While these things could happen here, it is a star ship and supposed to be about "without" occurances as in dealing with aliens, and not about what happens inside owr souls, or in one case, the ship becoming an alien planet or the crew becomeing primates and so forth this is not a canvas for those type of stories, DS9 is, since it is not about exploring but a space station and human(or other being) occurance on the station itself. The Enterprise is a moving ship, not a station, and yet here(Season 7 as a whole) it feels like a station or some building on Earth. And Since this season came out at the beginning of DS9 the writers, I suppose, were so into spending time writing DS9 that it leaked out into TNG and STTNG was now a clone rather than a separate series. Now on to this episode. The occurance of the dreams(most of 7 was about dreams) can be good in one or two episodes so it is individually a good episode, and it goes deeper into Roxanna Troi''s character. As with Jordie's mother, it is about protecting one's mother, I relate to this particular episode and the one with Jordie's mother in the instinctive need to protect my own mother. Much with others, it is about wondering the corridors of the Enterprise in dream state but it works here much as a paranormal show would rather than a science fiction(which it is supposed to be). Like I said, I like it in some instances but all of the episodes(excpet the Gambit) are much this way and it's too much. Five stars for "Dark Page", but I can only hand out 3 stars for the entire Season 7 being a clone of Deep Space 9.

history.text: where to begin. Reason, because I did enjoy Empire Strikes Back which didn't come across as a cartoon as much as the 4th movie where Han steps over Jabba and Greedo shooting first and Han being some kind of virtuous "paragon" like Matt Dillon in Gunsmoke or Return of the Jedi as a whole especially Jabba's fortress with the muppets WAY over done and it was tollerable in 1983 but the 1997 crap is too Disney/Henson! I can't really complain about the saga but I can't really give it a good thumbs up totally and I reluctantly lower it from 4-3 stars.

history.title: Becoming Jane
history.text: Women were property and had no rights. A good marriage (money) was a woman's only way to have a comfortable and respectable life. Jane Austen broke the rules. She wanted to marry for love, not for money or comfort. When you break the rules you will be punished by society, because society holds on tooth and nail to the status quo. That hasn't changed but people ignore a lot of it today (sometimes at their own peril). A great love was lost because the lovers had no control over their own lives. In the end Jane never married, he did, of course, but their love was solid all the days of their lives (not that it did either of them any good). Society is a hard task master. This is a politically loaded movie. Depressing for sure...no happy ending. Having the love of your life name his oldest daughter, from another woman, after you, would not be considered a happy ending in the opinion of most people. Jane, however, seemed pleased. Basically, the man she loved was willing to run away with her and give up everything (or at lest try). But Jane, being "responsible," and deciding for both of them based on an ASSUMPTION, felt that he would resent her later if she took him away from caring for his parents. He tried, she just caved and let the love of her life go. No gold medals for Jane. He went on with his life and was a good boy. She wrote and kind of wasted away. At the end of the movie she looks frail and pathetic next to her sister-in-law who is about 10 years older than she is. It's not a beautiful film either. It's dark and dreary. Even the landscape is miserable looking. Drab...drab...drab. If the drabness was meant to show how people actually felt, it worked perfectly...miserable, dark, dreary and drab. Blah.

history.title: Sherlock Holmes: The Complete Granada Television Series
history.text: Brett IS Sherlock Holmes. He is perfect and each episode is wonderful. He's brilliant. His movements and facial expressions are part of the story. Watson, Mrs. Hudson...each and every character is dead on. Best Sherlock series EVER. Don't miss it. An icon brought to life in the best of ways.

Daniel Craig is a great Bond. In Skyfall he looks worn out and tired. He is wounded, out of shape, and living in a lush paradise somewhere, drunk and pretending to be dead. He looks used up and he is. But one morning, while at the bar, he sees something on the news that catches his attention. He gets up and goes home. Because he was "dead" he is forced to go through a series of physical and mental tests, to prove his readiness to take on the bad guys. And the movie takes off from there. He failed all of the tests, of course, but he doesn't know that until much later. There are some great action scenes and the relationship between 007 and M has never been better. There are a couple of slow parts, now and then, but the villain is wonderful and Bond's sidekick, in the opening scenes, turns out to be someone we know and love. The new Q looks like a 12 year-old geek and is very likable. There is a surprise ending, which means there will be some changes in the next film. Craig brings a complex heart and soul to the Bond character. He is interesting to watch. He's tough, guarded, does what has to be done, regardless of the cost, and yet he seems lost and conflicted. M tells him that "orphans" make the best agents...and maybe she's right. Craig is far less superficial than the other Bonds (although I love Sean). The villain garners our sympathy on some level. He has been severely damaged and abused by the Agency. The torture and abuse made him what he is. All in all it's a great film and Daniel Craig is an exceptional Bond.

history.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
history.text: I liked it BUT.... (spoiler) I wish the writers of this movie stuck to the story line. Only the prison scene was true to the story; the rest of the movie is an insult to the great works of Alexandre Duma's classic, "The Count of Monte Cristo". With the exception of using the characters names in the novel, the rest of the movie was completely re-written, and in some instances fabricated. Anyone who read the unabridged version of this great novel will be disappointed with this movie because the movie failed to include: the THIRD person who betrayed Monte Cristo, it changed the end results of his romantic love, it changed what the betrayers did to themselves as a result of Cristo's vengeance, and it failed to show (besides the betrayal of the 2 (really 3) betrayers) the real reason for Cristo's father's death. These altered events, as well as MANY other omitted events, led Cristo on a mission of vengeance, which in my opinion, best explained and defined how Cristo's character was molded. The makers of this movie should have said it was BASED on the novel by Alexander Dumas, or, give the movie a different title. From the true-to-the-story aspect, it gets zero 0 For the performances in this re-edited MOVIE VERSION of the story, it gets a 4, hence my 3 star rating.

history.text: The visuals, cinematography, sound/music score, and the suspense of this movie is hypnotizing. It held my attention from the beginning. It's the prequel to 'Alien'. The story builds on the scientists search for "who created mankind" only to find that their question should have been "why kill mankind?" The movie is slow but deliberate; teasing your visual and mental senses with boiling point horror and an ending that leaves you gripping your chair. This movie left me with questions (which are spoilers I won't mention) which also made me drop the score to 4.5 stars, but it doesn't take away from this very good suspenseful and mysterious movie. Hopefully the answers are fulfilled in a sequel (Please!). The cast of actors were excellent: Michael Fassbender, Noomi Rapace, Charlize Theron, Idris Elba, Logan Michael-Green, Guy Pearce! I'm so glad Ridley Scott picked the banner back up.

history.title: King Kong
history.review_title: Overblown, overwrought, overdone, please god, make it be over.
history.text: Tripe banal wasteful remake of a classic. This wasn't even as good as the '76 remake with Jessica Lange and Jeff Bridges, it wasn't even as good as 1963's KING KONG VS GODZILLA. Okay, it was slightly better than KING KONG LIVES which deserves the MST3K treatment but that's saying something. It's disappointing that Hollywood keeps churning out these overblown over rendered special effects (CGI) laden films designed to get teenage boys to see them four or five times to drive the box office. The real shame is that the general public continues to flock to these mediocre examples of pablum with little or no heart or story. The crime here is that Peter Jackson is allegedly a fan of the original 1933 classic. I understand the thought behind remaking that one; done with what at the time was state of the art technology you'd think we could blow that out of the water today, well it shows you that having something that actually exists as an effect, like a stop motion puppet, is vastly superior to anything a computer can generate. Jackson's never met an editor he liked so we get double the "fun" with this mess. Jackson completely missed the very most basic point of the original-- Kong is a more than a giant gorilla, he's the missing link. He's that creature between man and ape, so therefore he walks upright like a man. Having Kong as a potbellied silverback gorilla takes all of this away. We should have had an Ultraman sized Dian Fossey come out and talk to Kong with some sign language. The movie mercifully flopped at the box office, saving us from the threat of a Jackson helmed sequel. Don't waste your time on this steaming pile of monkey doo.

history.title: 007: The Roger Moore Collection, Vol. 1 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The Set to Get if you want to get a taste for Moore as Bond.
history.text: Roger Moore was my favorite Bond growing up in the 70s, then I matured and appreciated Sean Connery's original performance in the role, and Daniel Craig is killing it as the current Bond seeming to come right out of the pages of Fleming's books. But back to Moore. He's sillier and campier than Craig or Connery. He's better than Lazenby, Dalton and Brosnan, but only in the early ones. My favorite of his is either MAN WITH THE GOLDEN GUN featuring Christopher Lee as the villain or THE SPY WHO LOVED ME which is the most lavish of the series and features the great assassin Jaws. Truthfully, Carly Simon's theme song makes me cringe when I hear it, but I just fast forward through the credits. Also included on this set is Moore's first outing as Bond in LIVE AND LET DIE which is equal parts black exploitation film, creepy voodoo film and probably the straightest Moore ever was as Bond-- there are very little quips and silly parts in this one, but it's also a bit less fun because of that. Still, this is the set to get if you want to see Moore at his Best Bond.

history.review_title: Connery's Run Comes to and End with a bloated gasp.
history.text: The second half of Connery's run as 007. THUNDERBALL was about as big a Bond as Bond could get. By the time this one was made he was an institution and Connery was getting tired of playing him, and it shows in his performance. YOU ONLY LIVE TWICE is noteworthy for it's glimpse of 60s life and style in Japan, but Bond as a Japanese is ridiculous in a series that was getting more and more ridiculous. Connery's hairpiece and waist line seem to be suffering a bit but it's only worse in... DIAMONDS ARE FOREVER which is sort of like if your Uncle Ned played James Bond. Its hard to imagine a bloated middle aged man as suave 007-- it would be 40 years before middle aged Daniel Craig would come along and show the world that age didn't matter where Bond was concerned.

history.title: The Daniel Craig (Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Craig will be remembered as the Best Bond
history.text: Initially I balked at Daniel Craig as James Bond. He's blond, he's short and he's not the classic handsome (at least in the early publicity stills) as I thought Bond should be. Boy was I wrong. Craig is as old as Connery was in Diamonds are Forever, but he shows that doesn't mean he's got to be paunchy and winded. Craig is the first Bond in the entire series even including classic Connery to look like he could actually do the things he's doing on the screen. This collection features all of Craig's Bond work with the exception of SPECTRE (and he says he's doing no more after that). These are much more akin to the original Fleming books. Gone are the quips-- Craig doesn't fire off a punchline after killing someone, he takes this business seriously and the series is refreshed and better for it.

history.title: 007: The Sean Connery Collection, Vol. 1 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Connery's BEST as Bond in this set.
history.text: Until Daniel Craig came along, this was the penultimate Bond. Now loyal Connery fans please hear me out. I too think Nobody Does it Better (ha-- see the pun?) than Connery did in FROM RUSSIA WITH LOVE which is out bonded by GOLDFINGER a year later. If Connery had stopped right there with three films we'd have a clear winner. Dr. No is not a bad film by any means, but it's the slowest and most dated as Bond was just figuring out his ways. THIS is the set to get if you're getting only one. Sean Connery sets the standard as James Bond and GOLDFINGER is the best Bond film in the entire series.

One of the best serials of the golden age of serials. Buster Crabbe IS Flash Gordon-- if you've never seen these you're in for a treat. Sit back, pour yourself a cold one, and enjoy some whacky outer space adventures!

history.title: Batman: The Dark Knight Returns (Deluxe Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Mediocre Adaption of a Classic Graphic Novel
history.text: Frank Miller's seminal graphic novel THE DARK KNIGHT RETURNS is a brilliant story-- not just a brilliant Batman story or a comic book story-- it can stand with anything sitting with literature on a library bookshelf. I'm not sure what went wrong with this adaption which disappoints right from the very beginning. There are so many great lines in the graphic novel that are watered down and re-written here for no reason other than to spoon feed what we're seeing. In the book- there's a great exchange between Jim Gordon and his friend Bruce Wayne which goes something like this: "To Batman, I'm glad he survived retirement." The glasses tink together. "He didn't," Bruce responds "But Bruce Wayne is alive and well." "Well, he's certainly learned to drink. Spoken to Dick lately?" "Not in 7 years, you know that Jim. Let's call it a night." Look at that-- it's brilliant dialogue that moves the story along at a fast paced clip. Compare it to what's done here and the dialogue is done in that awful "let's sum things up for the viewers manner". Gordon has to sit and explain to Bruce (and us) that Batman wouldn't be accepted today, that crime is out of control, that the Mutant gang is worse than anything Batman ever faced-- all facts we LEARN in the graphic novel by seeing evidence of it-- so why sum it up so early in the film? The film makers also opted to leave out the first person narration from the book, which is understandable but regrettable. Some of the best lines in the book are ones Bruce/Batman delivers in his thoughts and we lose those here. The worst offense is the storyboarding-- the choices for shots for many of these are just bad anime compositions-- Miller did perfect storyboards in the book and adapting those would have been much more successful. In the book the race car scene which opens the story is handled in an abstract way so that we aren't really sure what's happening while here it's spelled out for us so blatantly as to make it bland and uninteresting. It's a terrific book, this is a mediocre adaption.

history.text: Agatha Christie was not much for character development, but she was a master of plot and surprise twists. I haven't read "Thirteen at Dinner" (originally titled "Lord Edgeware Dies" as a novel), but now I want to. It is impossible to imagine that she would telegraph the solution so quickly, so obviously, from the beginning. I wonder if that was another element that was lost (surprise) in the transition from 1930 to 1970 (complete with Poirot on a talk show hosted by David Frost). Dunaway as Lady Edgeware is very good and Lee Horsley is capable as her handsome co-star. Unfortunately, Ustinov as Poirot is, as always, so dreadful. I don't understand why dapper, overly fastidious and very intelligent Poirot is acted (in so many films) by the sloppy, rumpled, addled and inappropriately comical Ustinov. Why? He would be more convincing as Columbo's father than he is as Hercule Poirot. As a result, he spoils every scene he's in, even in the better movies like Death on the Nile. (A sad irony here is that David Suchet plays Inspector Japp). Such a shame. This is one to have on in the background, but not pay too close attention.

history.review_title: If you think atheists are evil, this one's for you!
history.text: Terrible movie, but might be useful for a classroom to analyze and critique (as a free Instant Video only--I wouldn't want to add a penny to the $40 million this offensive, laughable movie has already earned on its $2 million cost to make).. There are so many strawman arguments and cold, uncaring "non-believers" that surely there's got to be some way to use it to build critical thinking skills rather than succeeding at its goal of brainwashing. It's such a mess--and yet, apparently, so widely shown. The film begins with a college professor telling his students they can skip past a major portion of the class by just doing as he instructs and "admitting" that "God is dead" by writing just that on their paper and turning it in. (Even Kevin Sorbo, a very good actor, can't save this crazy atheist bully from the badly written script). One student refuses to write "God is dead", instead telling Sorbo "I can't. I'm a Christian." For this act of "defiance", the professor upbraids him before the class, makes him defend himself in an essay and at the podium in a debate (set up with various strawman arguments), and then Sorbo threatens him that, if that's really what he believes, "I'll do everything I can to make sure you never get into law school." This film is often shown by Christian camps to pre-college age teens and younger children.. It would be sad if young Christians--if anyone--would be afraid of college courses, believing that real life professors would act like this toward them just for being a Christian.. (If anyone's reading this, I promise you, in real life, this man would not have gotten this job to begin with--and if he had it and began acting like this, he'd be fired. If you're a Christian, you really don't have to be afraid to attend college. And in real life, atheists are often also humanists, very respectful of individual differences, including differences in religious beliefs. This guy's just a crazy bully, nothing more.) While Sorbo is making his Christian student's life horrible, another evil atheist, this one a businessman played by Dean Cain--(yes, Superman)--is dumping his girlfriend because he doesn't want to be bothered when she tells him that she has cancer, because... well, this movie truly believes that if people don't believe in God, they have no reason to be caring or nice. As the film tells us, "When you don't believe in God, anything is permissible." A scary thought, considering the world is full of billions of people don't believe in the Christian God (the only god that matters here), and many are atheists.. But this is a movie to teach intolerance toward everyone who doesn't share the filmmakers' idea of God, and "fear of differences" is a time-tested way to do promote bigotry and prejudice toward non-Christians, as this movie does.. SPOILER:...The closest hint to "why be a Christian" comes at the end, where the evil atheist professor is hit by a car. But luckily for him a Christian sees him lying in the street and knows just what to do--no, not call an ambulance, are you crazy? He needs to get a deathbed conversion from him. This gives the film its "uplifting ending" because the professor dies--but as a Christian. "God is Not Dead" at least tries to tell a story, and has decent production values. Unfortunately that story itself is shallow, intolerant, dishonest and insulting to Christians and non-Christians alike. .

history.title: WOMAN'S WORLD
history.review_title: Star-filled cast, interesting story. Good overlooked 1954 film!
history.text: I didn't know anything about this movie when I began watching and for some reason expected that it would be boring. It wasn't. To my surprise, it quickly drew me in. The premise is simple. Clifton Webb, the president of a big automotive company, brings 3 top men from branches around the country to NYC to interview (and compete) for a top management job. He wants to get to know them, interact with them, discover their character and talents. With this goal, he has them also bring their wives. We see them arriving and realize each of these couples has issues. As Clifton Webb sums it up after a couple of days, "Right man, wrong wife. Right wife? Wrong man." His wife and (adult) son also get involved in social situations that will help him observe and select a couple. \ Each couple brings significant star power to add to Webb's:dilemma. June Alysson and Cornell Wilde are from Middle America--wholesome, honest, in love, happy in their city with their three children. But she doesn't want to live in New York--and keeps putting her foot in it as she interacts with the sophisticated Webb. And Wilde shows himself to Webb as a very honest man--perhaps "honest to a fault" for the boss. Arlene Dahl and Van Heflin are a couple with marital tensions. He's a smart interesting guy --describes the kind of leader to Webb that he thinks he wants and then tells him he's not sure how he measures up himself. Meanwhile, his wife, a glamorous social climbe r and flirt, wants to move to NewYork and is willing to flirt with Webb in the hope of landing the promotion for him. Fred McMurray and Lauren Bacall are the third couple and their marriage is in bad shape. He's become a workaholic--with an ulcer--and she feels neglected and resentful. McMurray is the boring, safe choice for the job, a man who doesn't say much but knows how to tell Webb what he wants to hear. It's interesting to see the way Webb invites them to situations and observes them. The script is sharp and it isn't long before you start to care about these couples, root for one or the other of them and really become curious which it will be. The interactions between the men are well developed, very believable and the women's stories get interesting, too. It's filmed in a lighthearted way, but has some interesting ithoughts about what we really value.

history.review_title: Fun, Hip 60's movie with the Rat Pack trying to hit the big time with a Las Vegas heist
history.text: Not a great movie, but a good one of its type and one of the "Rat Pack's" best--plus a look at vintage Las Vegas. A real feeling of the 60s here (sexism and all), and everyone gets something to do. Sinatra doesn't sing, but Davis is so good with the title song ("Ee-O-eleven"). while Martin has his moment with "Aint that a Kick in the Head"--both from Sammy Kahn and Jimmy van Heusen. Peter Lawford, who brought the property to Sinatra, has one of the bigger parts and one of the most complicated--a suave 40 year old man-child who has lived on his mother's money all his life. He might be the least likeable of the 11 former army buddies trying for their big opportunity with a New Year's Eve heist at five big Vegas casinos (one, the Sands, where Sinatra actually had a real-life 9% interest). Angie Dickenson, Shirley Maclaine, George Raft and Red Skelton have small parts. I was particularly impressed by Cesar Romero who did an excellent job with what I found to be the most interesting character of the bunch--the once-poor man who had once been a gangster, now gone straight (more or less), was charming, very wealthy and preparing to marry Lawford's mother (his scene with Lawford was probably the most interesting in the film, character-wise). Romero not part of Sinatra's group of cons, but he brings his own brand of suave con-artistry to the part--I actually found his character more likeable than Lawford and more interestingly complex than any of the others, even Sinatra (the hip womanizer, former army sergeant, Danny Ocean who brings them all together for the heist). Enjoyable, good "buddy flick", but don't expect a comedy. And if you liked this one, I'd also recommend the even lighter "shady Rat Pack with hearts of gold" flick--"Robin and the 7 Hoods" (where Bing Crosby actually steals every scene he's in). This isn't the slick, fast paced Clooney remake, but for some reason, I actually enjoyed this one more.

history.text: Powerful and tragic.

history.title: I.Q.
history.review_title: "We squeeze the brain a little to make room for the heart"
history.text: This is a sweet whimsical romantic comedy with excellent performances. I sometimes tire of Walter Matthau in movies but he's so good here, surprisingly not hamming it up at all as Einstein. Nice message about enjoying life--and that having brains can be a big part of that (and smart people are -necessarily- humorless stuffed shirts!) One of my favorite photos of Einstein is that one of him at Princeton, riding a bicycle--so human, a genius, and so joyful. This film has a little of that innocence and Meg Ryan and Tim Robbins are a charming couple. Whimsical, fun with a bit of a nice hidden message, too

history.title: The Killers 1964 VHS
history.review_title: 5 Stars as a "B" movie--with Ronald Reagan's only "bad guy" performance--and his best!
history.text: I got this as a curiosity because of Reagan being in it and playing a bad guy for the only time in his career. It is also the first "made for tv movie"--so a part of film/tv history right there. But it was too violent for television of 1964 so Universal released it into theaters instead. This IS a violent movie, not that there's any blood and gore, but because of the ruthlessness of the killing that's at the heart of it. Lee Marvin as the aging main gunman looking for nothing more than money, is perfectly cast. Angie Dickenson gives a good performance as the love interest of several men, and a young John Cassavetes as one of her lovers--a race car driver--is also good. Reagan isn't in much of the movie until past the midpoint, but unlike some of his earlier films, his acting here is very natural and convincing. He's expressive, holding his jaw and lips in a tight, different position, but not afraid to smile, raise an eyebrow or wink. His line reading is perfect, without the sometimes over-the-top earnestness of his youth. If he hadn't gone into politics, no doubt he would have continued to have a big career on television--possibly, with the right role, in movies again, too. In his 50s he had really come into his own as an actor. Unlike his earlier movies, although this is 20 years before he becomes president, this is the Reagan of his presidency. He looks and sounds and moves the same and it is a little unnerving to see the President of the United States playing a tough guy who doesn't mind killing people who get in his way. To those who say Reagan couldn't act, I recommend you see this one. If he'd been given good scripts and directors, I think he could have done well, at least past mid-life. Good film (though the color are so "off" they probably should have just gone with the BW after all).

history.title: Sante Fe Trail 1940 B&W
history.review_title: Read something to learn the real history of John Brown, Jeb STuart and George Custer, but enjoy the film for its performances
history.text: John Brown was a white abolitionist who took up the cause of freeing slaves so deeply that he repeatedly risked his life to fight against those who would enslave them. His cause at the time was vilified in the South (pre Civil War days) and he was called a fanatic, and this film often descho ribes him as "terrorizing" the country. Other abolitionists argued about his methods, but agreed with his commitment to freeing slaves and his unwillingness to tolerate slavery or put up with the "compromises" that so many Northerners were negotiating with the South. (He particularly opposed the Fugitive Slave Act which meant capturing escaped slaves and returning them to captivity). After the Civil War, distinguished African American leader Frederick Douglass wrote of Brown, "His zeal in the cause of my race was far greater than mine—it was as the burning sun to my taper light—mine was bounded by time, his stretched away to the boundless shores of eternity. I could live for the slave, but he could die for him."[wikipedia] Here, John Brown is the bad guy--an unsympathetic fanatic--not only about slavery but also religion. The good guys here are Jeb Stuart *Flynn) and George Armstrong Custer (here, one of Reagan's best performances, as a more tolerant figure than Flynn, having several lines early in the film for freedom of speech. He's also his rival for Olivia and does well with the military lines, the romance and the humor as well). The history here is inaccurate and the film has no passion for ending slavery, elevating the two men who are no longer regarded as heroes. If you can ignore all that--and not hold Raymond Massey's performance against the real abolitionist Brown whom Douglass so praised--this is an entertaining western -- not much in the history department, but a well paced story with great stars who give soe good performances (including Van Heflin as the villain who sympathizes with Brown).

history.title: Kid Galahad
history.review_title: One of Elvis' Best --Drama, Comedy, Singing and A Great Supporting Cast
history.text: This is 5 stars as a "really good Elvis Presley movie", not 5 stars as "one of the greatest films ever". I had read a couple of the 1962 reviews--Variety, Bosley Crowther for NYT--and, after seeing the movie for myself, was really shocked how bad the reviews were, really unfairly so, imo. Maybe there was some envy involved because Presley is perfectly convincing to me as a former GI who is a mechanic roped into a big money local boxing match against a fighter b acked by the mob. This is his tenth movie, and his persona just feels so real. He's not surly and swaggering like James Dean or a taciturn tough guy like Humphrey Bogart who starred in the earlier version of this film. No, Presley is the breathtakingly handsome and likeable "nice guy"--polite and unaffected, genuine and kind, a little naïve, who falls in love at first sight and always is trying to do the right thing. He's in good contrast with Gig Young (the critics split on his performance but I thought he was excellent--the character who starts out as a charming weasel and has the most growth of anyone. Charles Bronson has a big part and is also good. There's other good support, including Ed Asner and some others you'll know from longrunning supporting roles. All real pros. It's a feel good film with a lot of attractive people and a plot that moves right along and, though not revolutionary, is never dull. Plus, yes, Presley sings! (Crowther thought a prizefighter would never be a singer, but he sells it so...why not?) If you like Elvis, despite Colonel Parker's negative effect on his career (making the choices all about money not art even though he clearly has acting talent, too), this is one of his best.

An excellent script about an important time in our history that is still relevant today. My favorite Woody Allen performance. Allen, Mostel and the plot gives it entertaining elements at the same time the dramatic points are being made. There's added poignancy with the involvement of so many who really -were- blacklisted, writer Walter Bernstein, director Martin Ritt, actors Mostel, Lollyd Gough, and Herschell Bernardi. I wasn't expecting that ending, but it was a great choice. Let's hope we learned something from that period of our country. These people eventually were able to work again but many great talents weren't, their careers ended by an ideological hysteria that should have been repudiated from the beginning as a violation of our Constitution. A great film.
