history.title: Life of Pi
history.text: "Life of Pi" starts pleasantly, though is confusing. It has the potential of being something quite thought provoking. But, the thing quickly degrades into a hellish experience that will leave scarred memories, images that may well remain with the viewer for some time to come. The mindless, idiotic fool that is the central character fumbles his way onto a life boat while intentionally wandering around on the deck of a ship that is struggling to stay afloat in typhoon conditions. There are zoo animals confined on this ship, which are depicted as drowning below deck while the ship is slowly doing down. People and animals suffer miserably, and you get to see it! While everyone in your living room is begging you to please stop this miserable agony of a "movie"; you hold on hoping this garbage will improve eventually. Then you get to see a hyena attack, and mutilate a zebra while the coward is standing in the lifeboat with a ten foot oar in his hands, just looking at the butchery with flies buzzing in & out of his cavernous pie-hole! I slammed the stop button on the remote, and found myself desperately wishing I could grab that oar and do to the fool what he should have done to the hyena! If you have children, or adults with sensitive demeanors in your family, be sure to avoid this ravishing torture at all costs!!

history.title: The Book Thief
history.text: This film is really two great movies in one! First off, you have Geoffrey Rush, (the guy that did such a wonderful job portraying "Wasingham" in the "Elizabeth" movies, & the lead role in the "King's Speech") doing another superb character in this touching, compassionate, and revealing story of a European family during the 1930's/40's. If you like shows that have adolescent issues, adoption scenarios, or warm family situations, then this is a show you will want to own for repeated viewings. But this film also happens to be set with the world of Nazi-dominated Germany with all it's associated trappings. It is not necessary to know everything about the period to enjoy this wonderful movie because the script is marvelously written, and has great narration to keep a non-history oriented viewer interested. But for folks like me, that are well-read on the period, it is just flat-out GREAT! I loved seeing the truth brought out this way. This stuff really happened the way the Director plotted it out. Truth is, the girl in the lead role steals the show. Sophie Nelisse is her name I think. She is as talented as Elizabeth Taylor was. Each facial expression, every moment she makes is just perfect as she "ages" in this tale that replicates the lives of so many good people that were caught in this maelstrom of evil that was the third Reich. I had never heard of her before, but she must have done a lot of acting somewhere to be this good! The "Mother" role is that charming lady that played Rocky's new love interest in "Rocky Balboa", which I also liked much. It is amazing how Emily Watson is able to alter the nature of her role in this show from a tough survivor true to the Germanic culture of the time, and yet be so very warm and likeable as she was in that good Stallone movie. I will watch this multiple times I am sure. The music of the movie is as good as the sound track of "Dr. Zhivago." It just takes you back to this period of time when the world was so different than it is now, (well everywhere except in the Ukraine nation where history seems to be repeating itself currently.) This show has that "magical" feel about it, kinda like "Gravity" does by making the viewer feel that he is actually there with the actors. Yet, it is not stark, or one dimensional ever. There are no battle scenes, blood & gore that might disturb young viewers, even though the subject matter would seem to pose this issue. "The Book Thief" is really a family drama that would be enjoyed by anyone!

history.title: Stalingrad
history.text: [[ASIN:1844081117 A Woman in Berlin]][[ASIN:B002ZQX090 Katyn [Blu-ray]]][[ASIN:B000YKT4BW Dresden]]Well, first off, the other reviewers are correct in their analysis of the English subtitles; laughable! I particularly enjoyed hearing the word "Coward" being interpreted over & over within the subtitles as "Sissy." Sadly, this is one of the high points of the entertainment therein this release of "Stalingrad." Most folks watching this show, ...having interest in such movies; are going to be relatively familiar with the circumstances of the uniqueness of the battle of Stalingrad, and the inhabitants of the city. Von Paulus, and the Sixth army get isolated from the Wehrmacht, and essentially freeze, or starve to death while desperately fighting valiant, terrified Soviet troops in ever increasing numbers thus heralding the coming German collapse in WWII. Between eighty to one hundred thousand German solders are forced into horrible gulags in exotic places such as Siberia upon the surrender of the recently promoted field marshal ultimately. Forget all that! The plotline here ain't got nothing to do with Von Paulus, Zhukov, Konev, Goebbels' propaganda, Goering's Luftwaffe, Hitler, or even Stalin. This show is about "love", and social drama with the need of a reasonably studied viewer relying upon his knowledge of the harshness of WWII urban battle scenarios, and the circumstances of forced relationships between "captured" women, and enemy officers. Actually, I thought the most interesting part of the movie involved the German Hauptmann & the Slavic beauty he had obviously commandeered. The actor portraying the German captain is the same guy that I saw in another similar movie, but ain't sure which one (maybe "The Pianist", or "Dresden") He, and the Ukrainian lady were both interesting, and obviously good veteran performers. If you have a Blu-ray version, and good surround sound, "alien" technology in your movie room; you will find all the latest directorial techniques currently used in similar WWII movies in evidence the last few years. Airplane crashes, digital enhancements, constant battle/boom ambience throughout the presentation, etc. But, that's about it with this show. The whole thing starts out during the 2004 Tsunami event in Thailand(?), and then recedes into the memory of a Ukrainian rescuer toward his father's war experience in Stalingrad. It never gets there really. This whole show could very easily, and probably would have been better set in another Soviet city of conflict, such as Kiev, Leningrad, or Minsk. Using the well-known city of Stalingrad as the movie's title was just probably an effort to get more attention to the show since it had been the setting of "Enemy at the Gates." RENT this movie, don't buy it! ANY five minutes of the masterpiece "Lone Survivor" currently out there would probably please anyone interested in this kind of subject matter more than the "Stalingrad Tales of Romance" found in this DVD! Your probably not going to watch this movie repeatedly as you would "Saving Private Ryan", "Katyn", or "Lone Survivor." I also recommend "Woman in Berlin", - IF you READ the book first! You need the background to really appreciate this one.

history.title: Zulu [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: One of my Favorite Movies of all time!
history.text: I am not going to write much here because there are already some brilliant reviews listed that actually describe the story, pacing, acting, and artists involved with this masterpiece. There is only one point that I really want to add to what has already been stated concerning "ZULU." The TENSION of impending attack upon a fortified position is better portrayed here than in any other release that I know of. This suspense lasts throughout almost all of the movie, and it is electric! Stanley Baker is as good in this show as Lawrence Olivia is in Richard III, or maybe Bogart in "Casablanca" ...maybe better. Michael Caine is perfect in his role, and does a great job as do all of the other primary performers. In "Saving Private Ryan", there is a moment near the end when Tom Hanks and his squad is about to defend a small French town against a possible assault of German resistance. Hanks and his men are waiting, and then the sound of approaching panzers is faintly discerned in the distance. The ominous roar of the overwhelming Axis force slowly becoming visible as they march across a large, sparse area of land in the distance begins to send shivers down the spines of the American troops, (and viewers of the show), who then realize how they are about to be swamped by such a massive force, ... It is this "moment of realized horror" that exists in the Hanks film that is literary amplified within the wonderful "ZULU" performance. I first saw ZULU at a drive-in theater in 1964 when the previews were all over the media as it was a big, new movie then. I still remember the shivers I got when the Zulu army appeared on top of the mountain range, or when they "trilled" war cries. Those sensations still come to me now, ...still when I watch this presentation, as I have many times in the years since. Spielberg, Hitchcock, or no other director in my experience has ever topped the majesty of "ZULU" for me. I seem to never lose the excitement I feel whenever I sit down to experience it over, and over again.

history.title: Copying Beethoven
history.text: Total surprise! When I saw the Ed Harris was in it, and portraying Beethoven, I had to give it a shot. I have really liked Ed Harris for a while now. His masterpiece was "Enemy at the Gates" in my opinion. Then I saw this show, and now I ain't so sure. In this movie, he BECOMES the character in the way that you want to believe is a honest interpretation of what the genius was really like in real life. There is no videos of the man, of course, but artists of that caliber always seem to be eccentric individuals with little patience for mortals in daily life. Ed Harris NAILS the role, and his talents perfectly suit the role as well. I ain't got no classical records at my house. I am afraid of it because I fear that I will like it too much. You hear bits of it at church, etc.; but it wasn't ever "cool" among my peers in the early years. But these days, more and more guys I know secretly have some Bach, Tchaikovsky, and other similar type CD's up underneath their other records. I guess they are starting to want a change from the Allmans, Eric, Elton, and Dolly. Anyway, this movie is GOOD! It is not a documentary, or biography; it is a very watchable, interesting story that is set in what a 19th century Vienna probably was. It has a very good cast that supports Harris very well. The second leading character is a lady that I had not seen before, but was VERY familiar to me. I convinced myself that it was that lady that starred in the TV show "The Medium" (Courtney Cox's sister-in-law), but my wife said it was not her. In any case, she provides a strong performance that rivals Harris's star power portrayal. A well-paced movie, never "dragging" and gets more, and more interesting with every few minutes. The music, the "Ninth Symphony" which has a significant part of it played in the movie is stunning beyond belief! In surround sound; this music is powerful, ...overwhelming! You completely "lose" yourself for a minute, or so. It is that emotional, or "fulfilling(?)." I don't know if all classical music is like that song, but I would rate that tune up above "Stairway", or even "Sweet Home Alabama"!! It is that good. This movie is one of those shows that "grips" you to where you just sit and stare at the credits at the end, not wanting the show, or score to end. You want to immediately start the DVD over, and watch it again.

history.title: Fury [DVD]
history.review_title: A Bit "Stunned", but I'm Glad to have seen it
history.text: I was impressed with the performance of the principle actors in this film. Each of the tank crew were very believable, (including Pitt), and the caliber of their respective abilities really added to this experience. It is riveting, and I stayed on the edge of my seat throughout the show. I must say that I had great expectations of the film, (thinking it may be another "Private Ryan/Band of Brothers" level of show), prior to actually viewing it and that may have contributed to my attention level. The tank life focus was unique to anything I ever saw, and not being an expect in the technical aspects of tank warfare, I was really impressed. What the movie did not do was include a good "foundation" of what was happening around them, (as Allied troops), both throughout Europe, and their immediate theatre of conflict in the same manner as "Enemy at the Gates", "Monuments Men", or the two examples I mentioned earlier. In this, I compared the show to the "Stalingrad" offering of 2013. Most of what occurs in "Fury" could have happened anywhere in Europe during the war, and anytime during the Spring of 1945 in Germany. So for me, this was a drama of an American Sherman tank crew and their individual experiences fighting WWII Germans that just happens to be in the waning months of the war. You never really realize that the events take place just weeks before Hitler's suicide, or Germany's capitulation a week later in May. I was a bit uncomfortable with a couple of scenes in the show. Nothing was unexpected, and everything was certainly present during that war, but the scenes could have handled differently with the same overall effect upon the viewer. It isn't easy to express my opinion of the show any better right now. I will certainly watch it again sometime in the future, but I just am not as enthusiastic as I was immediately after viewer "Private Ryan" or "Enemy at Gates." But if you like this subject matter - do watch the show! (I have been anticipating seeing it since I first heard about it months ago).

history.title: Unbroken
history.text: I get movies to enjoy. I watch documentaries, depictions of history, and biographies on the A & E channel, or history channel, or on whatever channel on TV when I stumble across them. This file is a missed opportunity in my perspective to really put forth a dramatic event that could have been an experience to enjoy more than one time. The previews mentions the 1936 Olympic games in Berlin. I figured that the film would have gone all out with images of Hitler, Goring, Goebbels, and Jesse Owens at the Sports Palace in Nuremberg with massive amounts of color with thousands of international attendees present. Well, none of the above mentioned historical figures were present in the film, and the magnificent arena, known for enormous Nazi rallies during this period, was decorated with hundreds of red swastika flags, was not evident at all! I think that was only one flag shown in the distance, and you had to be looking for that to see it. The whole scene just flashed by pretty quickly and really was just close-ups of the central character the whole two minutes as he jumped up and down celebrating a victorious foot race that was over very quickly. This movie is about Louis Zaperinni! An Italian immigrant family's son who had a hard life of being bullied by his school mates, and went on to become a heroic POW in a Japanese Prison camp. The whole show seems to have a micro-focus on this one guy, and all his hard times. No other characters are really developed well, and the historical aspects of the war around him are barely touched on at any point, though there were many, many other events occurring all around him that are mostly, completed ignored throughout the film. The lifeboat scenes are okay, nothing much different than what Tom Hanks, or Robert Redford went through though. A Zero attempts to sink them with strafing rounds at one point. Also, one soldier dies, ..... The villain in the prison camp was a bad, really vicious guy. He was nasty, but I think the Bataan Death March was much worse. Actually, the Japanese have been documented in many books, articles, and movies as having been as in belief that any enemy combatant that permitted capture was to be held, and treated with utter contempt. So I doubt that Mr. Zamperinni suffered much more than thousands of other allied POW's during this period. He is/was a hero for sure, but not unique enough to be the sole focus of a movie with this much fanfare. With all the money that was blown on this show, a magnificent WWII movie could have been produced that could have paid allegiance to this hero, and still have enough other plot development that included some other real-life characters, and occurrences to make the film much, much more entertaining, and interesting. I'm not taking anything away from the great devotion, and commitments expressed by this great man, but as a movie; this thing drags on incessantly. Why not show a little battlefield action, or a shot of the "Yamato" in the distance, the Japanese Emperor making a speech in Tokyo, or anything related rather than always having the camera concentrating on the central actor and his hard life in a cell, or mud pit?

history.title: Terminator Genisys
history.review_title: I might have to BUY a copy of this Masterpiece! It is too Good to see only one time!
history.text: I rented this because I like action movies, and this Terminator Series has always been very good. But, this one was a major surprise! It is EXCELLENT! Every aspect of this film is superior, and Arnold puts out his best performance to my memory. Actually, all the actors really are perfectly selected for their respective roles. The guy playing "Kyle Reese" is the same guy that does Bruce Willis son in that last "Die Hard in Russia" movie, but here in this Terminator; he is magnificent. He is good in the Willis movie; but he looks nothing like Bruce, and I think Father/son roles should be cast with guys that kinda resemble each other a little in family scenarios. Whatever, the new Sarah Connor is dynamite, and she had BIG shoes to fill. But she almost redefines the role, and it has become BETTER! I like the older Cop guy who adds some comic relief. AND the special effects are flat-out SUPERIOR! This show really makes use of the latest cinema technology to keep you holding on to your chair. Arnold has really surpassed himself on this one, ....and I thought the last Terminator show was downright good. It just wasn't as brilliantly written as this one is, and had nowhere near the optical explosive effects displayed. Strange, Arnold's "Maggie" effort was also a lot better than I expected it to be mainly because of his acting skill improvement. Whatever he learned during his time in the Governor's office really propelled his acting abilities!

history.title: Ritchie Blackmore Story
history.review_title: This Documentary is as good as you want it to be!
history.text: First, ...if you really like Blackmore, and are aware of his historically unique method of improvising electric lead guitar solos; then I say to you that you should not hesitate to get a hold of a copy of this documentary. I have kept up with all Deep Purple related materials since 1970, and did not really think this film would have much material that I had not seen previously in a book, or on a DVD. I figured it would probably have as much of Candice in it, as Ritchie himself. I was wrong! This is exactly what you want to see if you want to hear/see RITCHIE addressing everything from Mark ONE in the 60's, up to present day activity with a rather limited amount on Blackmore Night even mentioned at the end. He does bring up the Lord Sutch / Gene Vincent / Jerry Lee period a bit, but not as much as the Purple/Rainbow periods. No surprise there, but it is all new video, new interviews, new photos that you see. Now, he does NOT go into in-depth discussion of his methodology of discerning Baroque Classical scales with reference to lead breaks, and solos. A guitarist from Def Leopard does a short demonstration, but not Ritchie. What Ritchie does give you is a closer image of who he is, what he is like, ...his personality through constant narration of images from his life. He knows himself pretty good, I think. He must be the Boss in any endeavor he pursues. He gets the lion share of the income of his current project, which cannot possibly be as much as he made during the "Renaissance Period" of creative, progressive music in the 70's; but that music is not in vogue today. You can turn on any radio station in your town, and not hear a Deep Purple song all day in 2016. You could not do this in the 1970's. ALL three was on the radio in the Seventies was pretty good progressive music from the bands that were highly respected then, and now by knowledgeable music fans. Today, we live in the "Dark Ages" of popular music with literal noise being sold as music to many consumers, and with Baby Boomers largely preferring acoustic songs with pop vocals dominating the airwaves. That's where the money is, and Ritchie has quite a few mouths to feed each month. Of course, his acoustic music is FAR superior to what is played on radio stations in America today, but in this documentary; one is able to detect his appreciation for just how good his electric creations of the past were as well. If the 2016 Rainbow shows do well, financially, I expect he will add some performances. But, in this video, you get to actually hear him talk about the people/music/experiences of his life in about as much depth as you are ever going to hear him speak. I watched it twice immediately Be sure to watch the bonus "Interviews." You get to see new video of many folks that you NEVER expected to see in this show. I was so pleased to see about five of them comment at least one time during this documentary, and Interview section. (Not Gillan, but everyone else!!) Sorry to add this, ...but I really, really like Steve Morse, and love his work in Mark Eight! But, Blackmore is definitely the best lead guitar player in captivity today. In Hard, Melodic Rock - he is the BEST there ever has been. His personality is that of an English gentleman with a warped sense of humor; and I like him much. This video is not as long as the Tom Petty video. It does not include as much music as the Jeff Lynne video, and it does not go into the extreme depth that the Eagles documentary; but "The Blackmore Story" is very, very good! (I bought the documentary without the Rainbow concert.) If you want an extremely good concert performance, I recommend "The Black Masquerade" from 1997. Doogie White version of Rainbow was phenomenal! [[ASIN:B00DPH7QFM Black Masquerade]]

history.title: Memories in Rock - Live in Germany
history.review_title: Incredible Performance, ...Insufficent Superatives to Adequately Describe the Glory of this show!!
history.text: Can you imagine an American band, (classic, or current), that has such a catalog of brilliantly written, complex, musically challenging, compositions as the Blackmore material? There are very few "star" bands on this side of the Atlantic that could even handle the changes, arraignments, or execution of these incredible songs. There are many European groups that I have never heard of that seem to still play this type of material, but not in the US. This vocalist, Romero, is beyond description. He is so good, powerful, melodic, able to effortlessly handle these classic songs; it is unbelievable that he is not known throughout the world. (If this were the 1970's, he would be bigger than Plant, Mercury, or any other singer that was around). That keyboard player is mighty, mighty good, and adds so much to the show. He is said to come from Sweden, or one of those "ABBA" countries in the north. Never heard of him either(??). At least I know Bob Nouveau, or whatever name he is using these days. I did not know just how marvelous, incredibly skilled he was on Rock Bass. The drummer ain't Cozy Powell, but he is solid on keeping the foundation of each song exactly as is needed, regardless of tempo changes. Ritchie scored very high on band selections with this group. The show is marvelous, looks great on Blue Ray, and is so beautifully orchestrated that it flows from one song to the next effortlessly. The level of excitement is unlike anything I have seen in many, many years. These songs, ....masterpieces, ...are so much better than anything I have heard in a very, very long time. Romero takes ownership of a couple of them; "Spotlight Kid" & "Mistreated" are his to keep now. He defines them now - he is that good! I never thought anyone could sing "Stargazer" but the original, ..but this guy handles it with ease. Nothing is "forced" with this band, they do all very well, or incredibly well. The first CD is like a roller coaster ride, and you are ready for a break in excitement when it ends. I have not heard the second one yet, ...I really do not want to hear anyone do "Tokyo Woman" ever again, but will let it play soon anyway. Blackmore's greatest period, I think, was on the Strugartt CD in 1976, or pretty much anything he did that period of time after the "Burn" CD. The earlier material was good, but he got so much better in the later 70's that it is hard for me to listen to those "Machine Head" era songs now. With Elvis & Lennon gone, ...only Blackmore, McCartney and Clapton are left from the truly great innovators of pop/rock music when excellence was rather commonplace. It is a wonderful thing that he is depicted on this document in high definition so he can be viewed while he is still extremely good at performing electrically. He doesn't move like he did on stage back in the 80's, but he still plays the best improvisation out there. I did not expect this show to be this good prior to viewing it. I did not realize just how good those songs were back when they were first released years ago. That "16th Century Green sleeve" song is stunning with this band! The bass guitar just memorizes the infrastructure of the tune, and the band plays like they have been playing it for years! I really am speechless in trying to convey just how stunning this show is, and cannot imagine what it would have been like to actually have been there for one of those shows. Folks do not get that level of professionalism is performance these days, particularly by the silliness that passes for art in the USA now. I think it is very cruel, and selfish for the European "powers that be" to conceal the great musicians from the rest of the world. I never heard of this Romero guy, and he is "head & shoulders" far superior to any singer currently active in this country. I cannot imagine how the European Union keeps this magnificence locked in over there, ...but I now fully understand why Britain got out! If Blackmore bought this show to the USA - the stadiums would be packed with adolescents to elders wanting to just experience the majesty of true genius once again. It has been a long, long time since this level of performance has been witnessed in this land.

history.title: Dial M for Murder [Blu-ray 3D] [3D Blu-ray]
history.text: Haunting Alfred Hitchcock, Captivating Grace Kelly, Cunning Bob Cummings and Murderous Ray Milland may be correct or not but the film is haunting, captivating, cunning and murderous. The film was filmed in 3D but for some reason only released in 2D. The fact that after 58 years the 3D print was even good enough to rebuild is amazing. For those that think in today's technology, try to remember that this film was released in 1954 using the technology of the time. Cellular phones were first used in the 1960's and the first 15 inch color tube tv's went on sale the year this film came to theaters in color with wide screen CinemaScope. When you approach 60 look at your high school photograph and see if you look as good as you did even 40 years ago.

history.title: Leftovers: Season 1
history.text: Wow, what a truly awful TV series. There are basically two modes within its plot structure; Somber, depressed moods and strange moments perhaps intended to conjure a vague sense of meaning (but failing to do so). I came to this series expecting high quality writing because of Damon Lindelof and his work on LOST. I'm actually quite surprised at the overall poor quality. If you're looking for a meaningful, entertaining, intelligent TV series.... look elsewhere.

history.title: Blindspot: The Complete Second Season (DVD)
history.review_title: Blindspot hits the spot. An entertaining series!
history.text: One of my favorite new TV shows. A great mixture of mystery, well developed characters, and action. Blindspot is sometimes reminiscent of the classic J.J. Abrams series ALIAS (which is high praise). The plot device of unraveling the meaning behind each of "Jane's" mysterious tattoos allows the writers to introduce and explore a plethora of scenarios. As a result Blindspot is far more interesting and entertaining than a typical espionage (CIA/FBI) related tv series. Great casting. A talented and diverse ensemble helps to bring these characters to life. This isn't just a two character or two actor series. Lots of character development and progression! The first season wasn't without flaws and neither is season two, but by the time you reach the final episode of season one you'll be begging for more. And here it is, season two! You won't be disappointed!

history.title: Captain Power-Complete Series
history.review_title: Poor video quality (looks like VHS). Great nostalgia value.
history.text: Really surprised that the video quality wasn't better. I have old VHS recordings with somewhat better quality at times. Captain Power was originally intended to be a toy tie-in series marketed to kids. But, the combination of live action (instead of animation), quality production, and interesting concepts appealed to a wider age group. It's pointed out by the series creators that Star Trek's famous "Borg" characters came AFTER Lord Dread and other such similar characters and ideas in Captain Power. For a simple 30 minute "morning kids program" it really did manage to entertain and come up with some interesting concepts. Because the series was supposed to directly interact with the toys (via flashing pulses on screen) you'll notice a tendency for battle scenes to be directed in a peculiar manner. The toy line was not the success that Mattel had hoped for, so the series seemed to exhibit less "interactive" qualities as it progressed. The CGI effects are very low quality compared to today's standard, but at the time it was very unusual to have such effects in ANY series. The costumes and set designs are suprisingly good. If you're buying this as a nostalgia item, then you'll know what to expect. Only the video quality may disappoint. Viewers who are new to this series shouldn't expect too much, but it's fairly good for what it is. I'd suggest that you search for a few previews and trailers online before committing to a purchase. This DVD collection is packaged nicely with a cardboard slip cover and very nice 10 page booklet that contains series info, episode guide, and pictures. Special Features: The Making of Captain Power Cast & Crew commentary on six episodes Trailer Photo gallery Original TV Film; The Legend Begins (never aired in the U.S.)

history.title: ADVENTURES OF BRISCO COUNTY JR. (DVD)
history.review_title: A Western, Comedy, Action, Sci-Fi, Cult Classic.
history.text: Created by the late Jeffrey Boam (Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade) and Carlton Cuse (LOST). The Adventures of Brisco County Jr. is without a doubt one of the most enjoyable television cult classics of all time. High production values, perfectly cast, with campy, well written episodes. A series that should have enjoyed many more seasons beyond its 27 episode run (a single season). I doubt that I can add anything beyond what has already been said by other reviewers, I simply wanted to chime in with a five star rating and my highest recommendation. At the time of this review the DVD box set was selling for $25, a real bargain. I paid more than $50 for mine and felt it was money well spent.

history.title: The 100: The Complete Fourth Season (DVD)
history.review_title: Better than Season Three. But, only 13 episodes.
history.text: A very short season of only 13 episodes. Packed with plot twists, anxiety ridden adventures of survival, and a fair amount of character progression. Season four is a return to the higher quality, more character driven writing found at times in season two. My only complaints; The plot twists in The 100 are usually caused solely by characters making poor decisions. The writers definitely need to develop a more intricate plotline. Also, I would have liked more episodes in this season! I almost gave up on the series during the first season. I'm glad I didn't. Looking forward to season five!

history.title: Revolution: The Complete Series
history.text: Something to watch if you're desperate to pass the time. Horrible writing, terrible acting, and a poorly developed plot. It's rare for five minutes to pass without someone being punched, stabbed, or shot. Dialogue that often seems like it was written by a child. I'm amazed that this series lasted two years, it should've been cancelled after just a few episodes. This complete series box set contains season one and two in their original DVD packages with an outer cardboard slip cover.

history.title: Under the Dome: The Complete Series
history.text: As a fan of the TV series LOST, I've spent years trying to find other TV offerings that rise to that level of quality. In my opinion nothing has ever attained that same level of mystery and suspense. But, if you enjoyed LOST you'll probably enjoy Under the Dome, as long as you keep your expectations quite low. The first episode is very good and the premise is fascinating. From that point forward things begin to unravel. Some characters remain undeveloped while others evolve in unrealistic ways over a very short period of time. Dialogue often leaves much to be desired. A key character is eliminated at the beginning of season two in a meaningless fashion, then another key character just a few episodes later. Season two has its good moments (some of the best of the series) but the third season is mostly comprised of poorly written episodes. Very disappointing when you consider that a great premise was squandered. Under the Dome is a mediocre, but somewhat entertaining sci-fi series. Nine episodes were directed by Jack Bender, who also directed Thirty Six episodes of LOST. If you're going to buy the series I'd recommend this full series box set. Packaged nicely in a hard plastic clamshell case.

history.title: Supergirl: The Complete Second Season [DVD]
history.review_title: The best superhero TV series since Smallville
history.text: Everywhere you turn there's another horrible superhero movie or TV series. Usually loaded with CGI, non-stop violence, and zero character likability, depth or progression. Supergirl is different. This series has a HEART. It's fun, well written, and has likable characters. If you liked season one you won't be disappointed in the second season. The only complaint I have is with the very unrealistic retail price (at the time of this review it was $35 for the DVD version). I waited for a good, fairly priced used copy. I highly recommend Supergirl.

history.title: Odyssey 5 - The Complete Series
history.review_title: Great cast, well written, cancelled too soon!
history.text: This series was cancelled before the writers could offer a suitable ending or resolution to the storyline. Never the less, this is still a very enjoyable sci-fi series. At the heart of Odyssey 5 is a talented cast with great chemistry: Peter Weller is perfectly cast as Commander Chuck Taggart, a kind of Buzz Aldrin/Chuck Yeager hybrid. A great leader for the team and their mission. Tamara Marie Watson brings an intellectual charm and "girl next door" sexuality to the role of astronaught Angela Perry. A great actress who's character should have been utilized much more. Sebastian Roché very effectively portrays Kurt Mendel, a behavioral geneticist and something of a playboy. Great chemistry and character interplay between Weller and Roché. Leslie Silva delivers a solid performance as reporter Sarah Forbes. Although her character faces many personal struggles as a result of the main plot device, I think the writers could have done much more with her character. Christopher Gorham as Neil Taggart, Chuck Taggart's 22 year old son. Gorham plays well with Weller and adds much to the series. The pilot episode is outstanding. I'd rank it on par with the best of Star Trek. Not every episode is a winner, but most are filled with terrific acting, well written dialogue, and interesting plot twists. As some other reviewers have noted, there's some harsh language and also some nudity, which I didn't find inappropriate. I've never understood how some people are offended by nudity while almost never complaining about violence. Thankfully this series has very little violent content of a graphic nature. Series creator Manny Coto has said on many occasions that he'd like to revisit the series, giving it another season or at least a series finale. Fans are still holding out hope! Odyssey 5 is currently a bargain on DVD and is well worth a viewing.

history.title: Defying Gravity: Season 1
history.review_title: Very slow plot progression. Last 5 episodes are the best.
history.text: This series was cancelled after only 8 episodes. There were a total of 13 episodes filmed, but the network considered the series such a failure they chose not to air the remaining 5. All 13 episodes are contained in this DVD package. The storyline moves along at an incredibly slow pace without any real character or plot progression for far too many episodes. Everything FINALLY becomes interesting beginning with the 9th episode, which wasn't even broadcast. If the writers had simply picked up the pace early perhaps the series would have lasted. The final 5 episodes that weren't shown on TV are actually the best of the series. The last episode hits the highest point of all and will leave you wondering about the unrealized potential of this series. Worth watching. Don't pay very much!

history.title: Better Call Saul
history.review_title: Great actors. Somewhat dark view of human nature turned ...
history.text: Well written. Great actors. Somewhat dark view of human nature turned into entertainment.

Nice production values. The writing is formulaic and acting is stilted to match. There's no real grit here, just a bit of sparkle. I think they could have asked more of their creative team. The context is full of storytelling potential, but it comes off like an expensive soap opera, with good and bad guys and gals.

An artful political satire that goes into surreal territory in a weird and delightful way. Funny and disturbing at the same time, like the Twilight Zone crossed with Funny or Die. All the actors do a great job.

history.review_title: Watching this show is like being heavily sedated inside a tornado...
history.text: Watching this show is like being heavily sedated inside a tornado, like a time lapse explosion, like a scream under water, like playing guitar in a sand storm, like being giddy at a funeral. Well done, and looking forward to a second season.

history.review_title: The Dark Side of Matt LeBlanc
history.text: Zany and profane. Talented team of actors with the ego of Matt Leblanc as the hub. Everyone's self centered, obnoxious, and a little over the top, which makes for a solid, laugh out loud, adult comedy.

I think for anyone experienced in the tragedy of love this is a sort of touchstone. First let me say the actors, men and women, are phenomenal. The story is contrived, but so is Midsummer Nights Dream. It has the feel of an Altman flick. Camera work and production values are top notch. Some juicy, deep, emotions that touch on the real complexity of life and marriage. Romance is illusion, life takes wrong turns, and we only get one chance.

history.review_title: A tour de force performance by Susan Sarandon, and seamless support by Ralph Fiennes
history.text: A tour de force performance by Susan Sarandon, and seamless support by Ralph Fiennes, who provides an impeccable counterpoint to Ms Duke's complete and total self absorption and self importance. It is a dance between two individuals, performed with the flawed grace of real people living in an unreal world of unimaginable wealth and privilege. The performances are touching and the characters sympathetic, if far removed, from where the rest of us live. I have a new appreciation for the words Doris Duke Charitable Trust, which I hear daily on public radio.

history.review_title: Red Oaks Started Well and Quickly Lost Momentum
history.text: The first season established likeable characters and relatable story lines, and a couple characters you love to hate. The initial framework was then thoroughly abused in season 2 and 3 with weak character development, less interesting story lines, and felt like a driverless vehicle. Hard to say what happened, but the show lost its momentum and then died a slow death. The actors seem to be filling space without a real purpose.

history.review_title: Witty, gritty, underdog makes good movie. Favereau shone...
history.text: Witty, gritty, underdog makes good movie. Spot on family story with adult language, and real emotions. Jon Favreau shone, and seemed happy and in his element. And what a cast he assembled for this small scale production. The music was great too. This is like HBO meets Disney. I loved it.

history.review_title: Not the original version of the movie
history.text: This is not the original version with "I'm a Believer" on closing credits, and John Getz doesn't stick his cigarette in the stuffed pig's mouth...! The supplements reveal that digital effects and animation were used to cover up dolly tracks, light stands, and eliminate reflections and shadows of camera people. Lame. Classic films should be preserved in their original condition. Does it really affect the impact of the movie? No not really. But a low budget movie should remain low budget looking because that is what attracted me to it in the first place.

history.title: Breaking Bad: Season 05 (Episode 1-8)
history.review_title: What can you say, it's Disturbingly Violent and Bluntly Revealing
history.text: I wanted to give this 4 stars because of how much down the rabbit hole the characters go and how violently evil things get. But I thought about how true to life this is when people loose themselves to their own divisive moralities and self justification of what they do when they lack Godly foundations. Especially how Walter White fades away and becomes the facade to someone who's soul becomes more and more unredeemable. It almost hurts to watch but you can't stop because some how you don't want to give up hope that they will conquer by doing the right thing.

history.title: Tai Chi Zero
history.review_title: Odd combination of good story and questionable production
history.text: The story is interestingly good but it is inconsistent. You have a character that acquires super powers but is plagued from a side effect of that power. He then goes to seek a cure of sorts for his skills problem. When he gets to this place of masters he suddenly becomes a weakling idiot and his skills are diminished for no apparent reason. Then the story starts to jump between making sense and suddenly glorifying the characters of the story with increased abilities. Basically the flow of the story is not balanced and some of the parts are over dramatized with bad acting in those situations.

history.title: Man Of Tai Chi
history.text: This movie has some great realistic fight scenes (No wire work), a better than good story line and very good acting. Some of the fight moves were so fast it was hard to follow the strikes and how did they keep from really hitting each other? It was strange seeing Keanu Reeves being a bad guy but it was a nice change for him. I felt like the ending was to quick and seemed to be missing something but I just can't figure out what it is. Maybe a kiss on the mountain top, but then again I'm somewhat of a romantic. I say See it.

history.title: Falling Skies: Season 2
history.text: The series captured my interest from day one. It has many intertwining stories weaved into every episode that connect well to the next one without dragging the story line out into endless dialog that babbles on-and on-and-on. It also does not dwell on melodrama for very long which is refreshing. Although the series is based on a fictitious apocalyptic event with scfi space invaders it was made with realistic believable human reactions and awesome alien creatures and effects (Finally). The acting was above standard and the characters were very interesting. I thought the contrast between the non-aggressive and aggressive posture of some of the characters were to separated. I believe most people would have a have a mix balance with some extreme moments. Usually people with extreme attitude are not well accepted and are cast out quickly. It always amazes me how lax security is when unknown elements are present. The stupid things always make for problems and I find myself thinking that I would never do what the characters are doing in the story and It drives me nuts. Its great fun to watch.

history.title: Oblivion
history.text: This movie presented an interesting venture into SciFi with a bit of a twist on the human condition. I really liked the vision of advanced technology and aviation.

history.title: Tank Girl
history.review_title: Tank Girl a wacky retro movie
history.text: I love this retro movie with its silly punky cartoon style. It does have some sexually suggestive moments that young teens often flirt around. The plot is centered around a futuristic post apocalyptic style society in which the powers that be control the population by hording all the resources. Of course there is an under ground resistance and a rebellion but it is as wacky as Lori Petty can make it. I gave it 3 stars because of the naive way the theme develops and its implications of a casual 60's style, lack of a healthy moral code of conduct.

history.title: Cowboys & Aliens
history.review_title: A fun SciFi Western that challenges the norm
history.text: I kinda liked this out of the ordinary SciFi Western that the critics panned. It is great to see something a little different than the same OLD THEMES re-made over and over again. Doesn't Hollywood have any kind of creative imagination any more? There are tons of SciFi books that have been out there and loved by the readers for years, yet all we get are the same old stories that are maybe altered just enough to be a little interesting. OR maybe it is the limited scope of the movie going public that can't seem to grasp new concepts that lie just outside of their commercialized comfort zones. How shallow it that?

history.title: Breaking Bad - Season 03 (4 discs)
history.review_title: the Breaking Bad series, it's edgy, sinister and sucks you into the story
history.text: Who doesn't like the Breaking Bad series, it's edgy, sinister and sucks you into the story. But remember you need to start form the beginning of this story to get the true feeling of what happens and why. Having lived through the 60's I have seen people that easily fit into the characters of this story. It is scary that such people exist but life is full of viciousness and men that don't care about anything but their own version of how to live and treat other people. This is a story about people who teeter on the edge of both worlds and how they manage to slip off one side or the other and back again. You learn to hate them and to have sympathy for them but then realize it was their choice that lead them down the rabbit hole. Like dominoes, one thing leads to another and before you know it you are plugging yourself into the story line, good luck with your out come.

history.title: Monster Walks VHS
history.text: In 1931, Universal Pictures released "Frankenstein", starring Boris Karloff. Instead of joining Paramount Pictures, and other studios on the brink of Depression Era receivership, Universal thrived! Americans flocked to see the Monster. Poverty Row studios tried to cash in with their own "Monster" flicks. Thus was born "The Monster Walks", released in 1932. The story involves people in an old dark house on a stormy night menaced by a killer ape(see short man in gorilla costume). If extremely poor filmaking intrigues you, pick up this lemon. Otherwise, save your dollar. The sets are so cheap they waver, and threaten to collapse at any time.One bright spot is the performance of Mischa Auer, a Russian actor emmigrant in a small part as Hanns. One year later, he'd shine working for Howard Hawks in the classic "Viva Villa". "The Monster Walks" plods forward at a pace a snail could challenge. In fact, the Monster doesnt't walk, it crawls.

history.title: Demented Death Farm Massacre
history.text: Fred Olen Ray was a little-known producer of low-budget schlock-movies in the 70's and 80's. Today, he's, well, still unknown. But Ray deserves a niche' in the history of independent film-making of that era. Make it a tiny niche'.Here's a chance to see horror film icon John Carradine in a near final, if not totally curious, starring role. If you can call it that. "Demented Death Farm Massacre(1986)" is a 16mm, amazing color compilation of non-drama, B-movie regurgitation, and frankly, I don't know what. The only thing more odd than this movie is the history of it's production. "Demented Death Farm Massacre"'s opening scene shows John Carradine standing on a darkened backyard set, with a fence and bushes in front of him. He proclaims: "I am the judge of Hell. I see the evil men do. Some people think that they can get away with murder. But are they? Let's see if Judge Death can help them on their way to hell." "Death Farm" is set in the hillbilly part of the Carolina mountains. As a jeep with two men and two women drive throught the countryside, a radio is blaring a news report that tells us that the police are looking for four New York thieves who robbed $1 million worth of gems. The four are headed to Florida, but suddenly the jeep stops. "It appears that we are out of petrol" states Phillip, the gangleader. The four come across the home of moonshiner Harlan and his new and near jail-bait bride(in a fetching bare-legged skirt). When Harlan discovers that they are the thieves, he and his bride are overpowered, and the thieves soon decide that they want the hidden fortune that Harlan has made from his moonshine business. The murder and mayhem that follows is framed in pasty, red, Hollywood blood. The actors are pretty bad, and the screenplay is mostly talk, talk, talk. And yet, "Death Farm" has a totally on-location earthiness that's hard to describe. In a sex scene that's half rape and half seduction, it manages to show a topless woman in various poses, without much in the way of actual nudity.In 1985, producer Fred Olen Ray bought an old movie called "Shantytown Honeymoon(1971)" from Jeffrey Hogue. It was directed by Donn Davison. He could only view the last color-faded reel, but that was enough. He bought the picture for $5500, and retitled it "Demented Death Farm Massacre", and made a new master from the negative. Intending it as a straight-to-video, Continental Video said they would buy the U.S. rights for $15,000 if he could put John Carradine into the film. He did. Ray planned to re-shoot the titles, and insert John Carradine, his old friend, into new, added scenes. On December 14, 1985, Ray hired Carradine for the entire day, for $2400. His part would only take an hour to shoot, so Ray wrote up a series of additional scenes to shoot that would provide him enough footage to make three more John Carradine movies. He planned to use one scene for the future "Star Slammer", which he did, and another scene for "Frankenstein's Brain", which was never made. Other footage(about two minutes) was with Carradine as Judge Death, and was editted into "Death Farm'. Other footage wound-up in "Jack-O", in 1995. By then, John Carradine had been dead for seven years. In "Death Farm", Ray cuts in shots of Carradine intoning: "Love of money is the root of all evil. The lust that comes with wealth is the lust of death!". In the finale, Carradine proclaims: "Well, I see things turned out as planned. The evil were punished and the good rewarded. I like a happy ending, don't you?". The Carradine footage was shot at Movie Tech in Hollywood. Fred Olen Ray said later: "Carradine was reading from cue-cards, but I think he knew that different scenes were for different films. He was called a doctor in one, and a judge in another. We finished at three o'clock. Seven A.M. till three o'clock. I can tell you what Carradine had that day, because he had the same thing for lunch that he had for breakfast: a Spanish omelet. He always had a Spanish omelet!".

history.title: Kong: Skull Island
history.text: Two scientists convince the U.S. Army(somehow) to send a small tactical team to a remote South Pacific island at the end of the Vietnam War.They want to explore strange creatures, a super-power; a gateway to another world. In helicopters, the team descends onto Skull Island through blinding clouds and thunderstorms, and finds a remote, lost world ruled over by a giant ape the natives call Kong. As the helicopters drift down, Army commander Packard shouts: "Hold onto your butts" .Packard is played by Samuel L. Jackson, who used the exact same words in "Jurassic Park" twenty years before.A literate, fast-moving monster movie, "Kong: Skull Island" features dazzling, rolling pans through the islands and prehistoric landscapes of Oahu in Hawaii, Australia, and Vietnam. Respectful of the original "King Kong(1933)", and yet open to revisionist changes, "Kong: Skull Island" blasts into a world of ancient, throbbing, blood-thirsty creatures fighting Kong and the Army, all at the same time. Tom Hiddelston heads a good cast; but John Goodman and John C. Reilly steal the show.The original "King Kong" is a great classic. It will never be topped. But "Kong: Skull Island " is a different movie. It's new;its's updated. It's a fun roller-coaster ride all the way through. E-Ticket.

history.review_title: All it's cracked up to be.
history.text: When Hollywood remakes a 25-year-old movie, the result is almost always a flop. But "Beauty and the Beast" is no flop. Hardly. Belle(Emma Watson) is a young girl in a small village in the French countryside.Lonely, Belle loses herself in books; romance and princes. The villagers say she is "odd". Belle's father, Maurice(Kevin Kline),rides to the market to sell his trinkets. "I'll be back tomorrow" he tells Belle. But Maurice's horse gets lost in a dark, gloomy forest. Maurice takes shelter in a mysterious castle, where he is captured by a monster, a "beast".His horse returns home alone. Belle rides into the forest, searching for her father.Her big adventure is about to begin. Disney uses the original 1991 story, and spares no expense($160 million). Director Bill Condon("Gods and Monsters(1998)" and "Mr. Holmes(2015)" uses a tender hand to guide the fantasy, the classic music, and talented actors. Leading the way is Emma Watson as Belle. No longer the Harry Potter little girl, Watson is now a young lady; sure but wistful. Kevin Kline stands out as her father; old now; still damaged from the loss of his wife(the plague) so long ago.Also in support is Ewan McGregor, Ian McKellen, and Emma Thompson. Special effects include CGI, matte paintings, and rotoscope, which was used as far back as 1916, when Walt Disney himself was drawing cartoons.A heart grown cold, redemption, love, and maybe, too much sentimentality, "Beauty and the Beast" measures up. Way up. "Tale as old as time, True as it can be, Barely even friends, Unexpectedly. Certain as the sun, Rising in the east, Tale as old as time, Song as old as rhyme, Beauty and the Beast...."

history.title: Wonder Woman [Blu-ray]
history.text: At the June opening, "Wonder Woman" smashed all records to become the biggest weekend for a female director ever. Patty Jenkins directs "Wonder Woman", which grossed $100.5 million at 4,000 theaters."Wonder Woman" is a super-hero action flick starring Israeli actress Gal Gadot and actor Chris Pine.Princess Diana, adopted child of the Amazons, is a girl made from clay by the Queen Hippolyta with the blessing of Zeus.Diana grows up on a hidden island, and learns to fight for freedom; and the day that the Amazons will be called upon to save the world from the evil Ares, god of war.World War I pilot Steve Trevor crosses a vortex and crash-lands on the Amazon island.He is being pursued by the Germans. Steve tells Diana of the Great War that ravages the land. Diana hears her calling; it is time to save the world from Ares; he has returned and she must kill him. Diana and Steve sail to England, and to the Front. She must find the evil god; while Steve battles German scientists who want to poison the world.Gal Gadot shines from her first scenes in "Wonder Woman". She is a natural Hollywood leading lady. "Wonder Woman" characters live and breathe; they are happy;they are sad. They care. These characters you want to know. The Amazons are always warning Diana about men and mankind. They tell her: "They're not worth saving". But Diana has an answer for that. She says: "And you're right about men. They are selfish and cruel and weak. And everything you say. And so much more." She adds:"It's not about deserve. It's about what you believe". Before the movie opened, Ms. Gadot reflected: "Today I had a moment with myself when I was looking out the window at the clear blue sky and realized that I'm nine months pregnant and soon will have a new pup as an addition to our family....could not be more grateful to the universe. Sending you guys some positive energies..." During filming, Gadot was five months pregnant.

history.title: Making "The Misfits"
history.text: A boozy old cowboy, his friend, a washed-up rodeo star, and a lonely young woman. These are the characters caught up in director John Huston's 1961 "The Misfits". This 2002 documentary pries open the door on the making of this now legendary movie. An all-star cast was hauled into the Nevada desert for the shoot. Here is: Clark Gable(his last film), Marilyn Monroe(her last film), Montgomery Clift(he would make two more movies), Thelma Ritter, Eli Wallach, Estelle Winwood, and Kevin McCarthy, who has one small scene(McCarthy was a personal friend of Montgomery Clift). Clark Gable suffered a heart attack just days after shooting ended. He survived. But 10 days later, a second heart attack killed him. He was 59 years old. After "The Misfits", Marilyn Monroe was signed to star in 20th Century Fox's "Somethings Got to Give", directed by George Cukor. Late for filming, and un-responsive, Monroe was fired from the film and all shooting stopped. The movie was never completed. Thirty minutes of "Somethings Got to Give" still remains, and it can be seen on a DVD documentary, featuring Monroe swimming in a bikini, plus scenes with Dean Martin and Steve Allen. "The Misfits" film production was troubled. As the shooting continued, Marilyn Monroe became increasingly dependent upon pills. She had prescriptions flown in by her Los Angeles doctors and also received medication from other local doctors. She was taking three times the normal dosage of the sleeping pill Nembutal. The pills left her disoriented and incoherent. She couldn't remember her lines. Somehow unmoved, director John Huston spent the nights drinking and gambling in a Reno casino. He usually lost. Needing little sleep, he'd be up all night. "Making the Misfits" features interviews with the writer of the screenplay, Arthur Miller, actor Eli Wallach, members of the crew, and John Huston's son, Danny Huston. The movie filming was delayed and over-budget. Yet, out of all of this, somehow, a moving, wicked, film classic was made. Arthur Miller wrote a touching screenplay, and some great scenes for Marilyn Monroe, his wife at the time. The marriage was failing, but Marilyn's soft, sad performance erased her Hollywood spectre of the pretty dumb blonde, at least for now. Maybe her heart was breaking. Marilyn Monroe stole the movie. At the end of the documentary, Arthur Miller sums it up: " Artistically a wonderful experience. But so wrenching. Movies are a very mysterious business. It's a mystical effect on you finally. I can see where people devote their whole lives fiddling with this".

A pretty young American-Indian girl is found raped and murdered in the icy mountains of Wyoming. It is revealed that after the attack by a gang of oil-workers, she escaped and walked six miles in the snow before collapsing. She was barefoot. "Wind River" is a murder-mystery set on an Indian reservation. It's smart, well-written, and has some noble cinematography. Elizabeth Olsen plays a rookie FBI agent, who teams up with Jeremy Renner, a game warden.A smart one. Together, they devise a plan to find the killer. A god cast includes Gil Birmingham, and an outstanding performance by Graham Greene, father of the murdered girl. Deeply disturbed, he pledges to Cory, the game warden: "Find that guy, whatever you do. Find him..."Ben, the Indian father, fights loneliness and poverty; just as they all do. Ben's young son fights drug abuse, as well."Wind River" is written and directed by Taylor Sheridan, who wrote screenplays for the excellent "Hell or High Water(2016)" and "Sicario(2015)". "Wind River" is a complex allegory, a notion on the fragile human condition. In the end there is redemption. In the rousing finale, one poor soul babbles: "Living up here in the mountains is hell. It's awful.You can't leave. There's nothing to do. There are no women. Just snow. Just silence. And snow". "Wind River" was filmed in Park City, Utah. "Wind River" director Taylor Sheridan directed one other movie, "Vile", in 2011, starring Eric Jay Beck. I could be wrong. But I don't think he's done yet.

history.title: Erik The Conqueror (2-Disc Special Edition) [Blu-ray + DVD]
history.review_title: All the Colors of the Dark
history.text: A big bag of extras and a new Blu-Ray and regular DVD(2-disc set) nails it. Wait a minute. Nails him. The great film illusionist/color painter known as Mario Bava. In "Erik the Conqueror", a master Italian film-maker makes a statement. And a good movie. All at the same time. At the end of the 8th Century, the evil Sir Rutford(Andrea Cecchi) leads his English army against Viking settlers in the British Isles.A violent seaside battle leaves behind two twin brothers with royal brands on their chests. Twenty years later, they are Erik(George Ardisson), who is adopted by English royalty, and now a duke, and Eron(Cameron Mitchell), who is now a Viking leader. A massive naval battle brings the two brothers together again during a Viking invasion of England. The brothers identify each other; they now know their blood connection. And now they must join to fight a common foe.Suddenly, you are in Bava land, a world of swirling colors, and maybe, a little fantasy. In "Erik the Conqueror", vibrant hues of purple, blue, and green dance against another color palette; all shrouded in old-school, in-camera movie special effects. Here are miniatures, reversals, matte paintings, and a medieval castle constructed from a photograph from National Geographics magazine. I'm not kidding. "Erik the Conqueror" was released in the United States by America International Pictures(edited) and later in some rough VHS editions, including one from Sinister Cinema(sometimes seen As "The Invaders"). The first decent DVD version came from Anchor Bay in 2007. In 2017, Arrow Video has released a dual-format DVD, a new 2K-sourced presentation. The new DVD's(both versions) add more image information on the sides. They are better composed; darker, with the color palette showing more range. Extras include a new commentary by Mario Bava historian Tim Lucas, a telephone interview with actor Cameron Mitchell from 1989, U.S. and German trailers, a poster and stills gallery, and a Bava biography, and more. Tim Lucas points out Bava's camera magic; such as inserting a little waving flag into his matte painting to create a more believable hilltop castle. Tim Lucas' telephone interview with Cameron Mitchell is expanded to 63 minutes, and Mitchell glowingly relates the making of "Erik the Conqueror", and also notes from his two other Bava movies: "Blood and Black Lace(1964)", and "Knives of the Avenger(1966)". Cameron Mitchell died on July 6, 1994, at the age of 75. Still more extras include the featurette "Gli Imitaturi", a Michael Mackenzie short, which reviews "Erik "s connection to the 1958 "The Vikings". The first DVD pressing has a liner-notes booklet, and a new notes essay by Kat Ellinger. "Erik the Conqueror" is a direct re-make of Kirk Douglas' 1958 "The Vikings(Italians love remakes)". This is not Mario Bava's best movie, but it ain't bad.As stated, Andrea Cecchi appears as the evil English lord, Sir Rutford. Cecchi worked for Mario Bava before, in 1960. He played Dr. Kruvajan in an ever better Bava film. It was called "Black Sunday".

history.title: Kingsman 2: The Golden Circle
history.text: "Kingsman: The Golden Circle" is a spy-spoof based on the 2012 comic book "The Secret Service" by Mark Millar and Dave Gibbons. An all-star cast completes this sequel to the 2015 original hit movie.Returning for episode 2 is Taron Egerton(very good), Colin Firth, and director Matthew Vaughn. "Kingsman: The Golden Circle" features great location shot, Bondlike gadgets, wild action, and crude humor. Gentleman Eggsy(Taron Egerton) appears outside of his tailor shop spy-HQ in London, when he is suddenly attacked by an old Kingsman training reject, and his new cyborg arm. A terrific deadly fight continues in a taxi racing through the night streets of London.Later that night, a bomb destroys the Kingsman's tailor shop headquarters and almost all the agents are killed. The bombing is traced to an international drug cartel called the Golden Circle, run by the smarmy nut-job known as Poppy(Julianne Moore), who lives in a remote jungle surrounded by 1950's retro decor; guarded by a small army of soldiers and robots. A scandal for the American president blurs the story in the second half, as political demagoguery takes over. "Kingsman" also stars Mark Strong, Halle Berry, Elton John, and Jeff Bridges as Champ. Julainne Moore easily steals the entire movie as Poppy, the devilish, funny head of the the Golden Circle drug cartel. A few key scenes include Elton John in pink feathers playing his trademark grand piano, and a flashy sequence of an out-of-control cable car crashing down the snow-covered Italian Alps. Matthew Vaughn, who has already helmed 6 movies, has been announced as director of "Kingsman 3". At 141 minutes, "Kingsman: The Golden Circle" is too long. But it's funny, and as chic and sharp as Taron Egerton's new suits.

history.title: Janis Joplin - Janis Little Girl Blue
history.text: Five stars. Up. Way up. Janis Joplin was a country girl from Port Arthur, a little hick-town in Texas. She was fat. She had acne. Her face was round. It was the 1950's, and boys made fun of her. They laughed at her. They made her cry. Life sucked. Then she and some friends got to Austin. Wow! Music in the air. Fun. You didn't have to be a babe. And little Janis found out she could sing. Even bluegrass. Janis and some friends got to Los Angeles. A new world. Music. Nice people. You didn't have to be a babe. It was 1964. Back and forth, Janis traveled from Texas to California, back and back again. She went to San Francisco. She started singing in little bars. She smoked pot. She had a few drinks. The big break for Janis Joplin was the Summer of Love, 1967, 50 years ago. It was the Monterey Pop Festival. Boom. Janis became a star at age 25. A whole new world. Janis found out she was happy on a stage singing the blues. And all those kids sitting out there listening. They were happy too...."Janis. Little Girl Blue" is a sad, beautiful rock-and-roll love story. So well done. So real. Interviews and scenes with Jerry Garcia, John Lennon, Bill Graham, and TV talk-show host Dick Cavett. And more. Her friends. Her lovers. Her managers. She could not know that the road would be short. Blasting out at Woodstock and the Avalon BallRoom, little Janis could not know that she would join the "27 Club", a list of famous artists would died at age 27(Hendricks, Morrison, and Janis). "Janis. Little Girl Blue" is a rare documentary, a true story of a sad little fat girl, who did good. And then saw it all fade away. A tear will come into your eye. You'll realize that life is short. But it's a gift. A gift to be alive.

history.title: Titanic (Blu-ray/ DVD Combo)
history.text: The costuming was very nice and that is the only good thing I can say about the first part of the Titanic miniseries. One might say to give it a chance and see the whole series. I won't waste my time. After only the first hour of so, I turned away to something else. I admit that I was spouled with the movie. James Cameron poured so much money and beauty into his work. The sets were small and cheap. As for the acting, as my title states, it was a soap opera on the sea and I found that I did not care if they went down with the ship. I had bookmarked the DVD set to buy when it came out. I will save the money and now remove it from my list. Too bad, I had high hopes. The best words to describe this Titanic is; stink, stank, stunk, sunk. James Ellison The real story of the Titanic then, is it sunk at the dock. It was a clear night and the ocean was calm but it stunk like rotten sea weed. It is hard to determine which scene was the worst. Was it the scene where some of the male servants were tossing a woman's prized book in the air? Was it the scene where Mommy reminded her daughter it was late when she was out on the deck with a prospective beau? Was it the scene in the dining room when the scarlet woman was trying to sit at the dinner table with all the other married elite? What really sunk the Titanic? Was it the script? Was it the actors? Was it the director? Perhaps, the actors who had a really stinking, sinking, script really could not put their hearts into it. However, there was one thing good about this mini-series: it was a virtual reality trip that would make anybody seasick! Melinda Ellison

history.title: Rats: Night of Terror
history.text: This is one crazy '80's vintage Italian giallo film with some of the unintentionally funniest scenes and characters. Set in the far future, a group of Mad Max wannabees end up in a deserted town where they encounter a ton of rats...which don't seem very interested in them until the stage hands fling them at the actors! Also, these rats are having a seriously bad hair day which is odd since grooming is one of their major activities. Also, either the camerawork or some post production gave them the reddest eyes - almost fluorescent! I did learn some important safety tips like if you're covered with rats don't ask your buddy with the flame thrower to help you!! It has a twist ending that is also amusing. All in all a fun film unless you're a rat-a-phobe!

history.title: Red Dawn (1984)
history.text: A slam bang action film where a bunch of regular high school students team together to fight a Soviet invasion spearheaded by Cubans. It all seems a bit silly now since there isn't a USSR and we're normalizing relations with Cuba but it is still a good drama and war movie. In it's universe, it makes sense and the story flows right along with a lot of flag waving, scary moments, a bit of humor and war action. Surprisingly not that bloody a film compared to today's movies but it was strong at the time. One odd bit. In the movie, the American rebels have a Patriot rock that they carve the names of their fallen on. During my first tour in Afghanistan, I saw a very similar rock in the outback with names carved in Farsi. I was told it was from the Russian occupation...spooky. Anyway, great movie IMHO and well worth a look.

history.title: Theater Of Blood
history.text: One of my favorite Vincent Price movies! It's smart, stylish with a bit of mystery and macabre humor. It's a serial killer film but he uses Shakespeare as the means to an end. history.title: China Beach: Season 4
history.text: "China Beach" may seem like a latter-day attempt to recreate "MASH." It is enormously more persuasive as drama, however, more genuine as human experience. To accomplish this the writing and producing had of course to be different, but while throwing no stones at the casting of "MASH," that of "China Beach" is brilliant. Dana Delany is the key to a large cast, among whom there are no stars, but many regulars and much coming and going, which is just right for a Vietnam war setting. "China Beach" is the one series I have all of, bar the cartoons of "Top Cat."

history.title: Thames Shakespeare Collection: Macbeth / King Lear [DVD]
history.text: "Macbeth" is a claustrophobic play, tightly controlled in space and time, written for performance on an open stage with almost no scenery. I'm not persuaded that it can be done effectively on-screen, especially a television screen. This presentation in particular presents "the Scottish play" in a claustrophobic setting, which so circumscribes the drama as to make it difficult to watch, much less appreciate. The same is not true to the same extent with "King Lear," but the scale of the setting here is still wrong. It's too small. Both plays really need a certain amount of space to be played in, and in this case both are presented in settings that are too limited. I think the reason for this is that the major characters are written as very large-scale human beings, powerful but evidently more influential than their human limitations can legitimately support. That is finally what these two plays are about.

history.title: I COULD GO ON SINGING
history.text: Fat, fatuous, forty-ish Judy Garland, who had not long to live, starred in another semi-biographical film entitled "I Could Go On Singing" (1963). Sad to report, it was a disaster. Just two years earlier, she had performed her legendary solo concert at Carnegie Hall. But by the time of this film, Judy's commanding stage presence and camera presence were gone. Okay she was petite, less than five feet tall, but she couldn't manage even the most moderate high heels to complement her stature. Often doubled, she needed physical support most of the time. This woman danced with Fred Astaire in :"Easter Parade." She was the one and only partner who could steal the stage from him, She also danced with Gene Kelly, mentored him in his first film, "The Pirate," and again in one of her greatest, "Summer Stock." Among Judy's most amazing attributes was how she used her contralto voice. At full belt, in a whisper, or anywhere between, you had to listen. See and hear her in another of her best, "A Star Is Born." And if you've never heard the recording of that Carnegie Hall performance, get it. That's Judy Garland at her inimitable greatest, but it was also her swan song as a top star. In "I Could Go On Singing," she had lost much of her power and range. In every respect but the acting of her co-stars, which was excellent, the movie is fragmentary, even sloppy, hard to understand.

history.title: Electra [DVD]
history.text: Excellent, outstanding. This is no sort of comedy, but a thoroughly evocative film, especially when you know the background story. We now know that the Trojan War actually happened, and It is of course the very stuff of legend but there must be core fact also. In those days no distinction was made between historical truth and legend, because it was all story-telling, and this is wonderful story-telling. There is detailed realism in the telling, which will help draw you into it. I've seen Irene Papas do very good film work, in "The Guns of Navarone" for example. I've never been her biggest fan, but she is excellent here, as is the supporting cast. Well done!

history.title: True Grit
history.text: It's the Duke's Oscar film, and he deserved the award. Adorable Kim Darby stands toe-to-toe and trades lines with the legendary star. Glen Campbell doesn't seem quite clear about what he's doing, but that actually works in context. Maybe it was deliberate? Rooster wears an eye-patch. The Duke sees clearly through it. I see this clearly: the film is terrific.

history.text: It's Day at her best, but she was always at her best. It's Sinatra playing to stereotype, as he sometimes did. The two of them never really connect, so that when her character admitted she was in love with his character, I thought "huh?" Interesting to compare with "The Man Who Knew Too Much." There, Day and her co-star connected completely, and the result is a terrific film. This is a decent story but trivial. I can't think why this film or it's theme song were hits.

history.title: The Verdict
history.text: Newman often played to stereotype, though doing it very well. He exceeded that here, but not brilliantly as some reviewers suppose. Also stereotypical is the hero-wins-against-long-odds ending. Newman's greatest role? "Somebody Up There Likes Me." However, given that it's a send-up on the hard-boiled detective genre, I quite like "Twilight."

history.title: Strategic Air Command
history.text: Good stuff from the early cold-war era. The screenplay is old-fashioned also. Stewart is great as always, in a sort of unlikely role, and has a fine supporting cast. Great flying sequences as the jet-bomber age began. The world knows that Stewart was actually a bomber pilot in WW2, but it's ironic anyway. The world might not know or care that the first active jet bomber (B-47) was classified not as a heavy but a medium bomber. Then came the B-52, which is probably still flying somewhere after sixty-odd years in action.
