history.title: Star Wars-Clone Wars: Season 1-5
history.text: Let me start off with the most important part: IT DOES NOT WORK. I have region-free UK releases of Game of Thrones and Battlestar Galactica that work perfectly on every blu-ray reading device I own including an Xbox One and PS4. THIS ONE DOES NOT WORK. Now, for the exponentially less important things. As most will know, this is not the complete series. It doesn't include the theatrical film, nor Season 6 ("The Lost Missions") or the 2003-2005 Cartoon Network miniseries (which canonically meshes with this series and introduces two critical characters not introduced in this 2008 series). At roughly 40% of the price of buying each season separately or the US Blu-Ray collection, you'll get the cheapest blu-ray cases that, with two or three discs each, take up as much space as some 6-disc cases I have, and does not include the mini art books and inserts that came with the initial releases of seasons 1 and 2, but that may still be worth it to you if your player can read Region B discs. Episode guides are on the flip side of the cover insert, but at least Season 2 has episodes listed on two separate discs while omitting others. In short, unreliable, which is bothersome considering how messed up the chronology of the first three seasons was (In usual Star Wars fashion). However, the series is entertaining for kids and adults and the dark themes of Revenge of the Sith begin to show themselves halfway through the series, with several multi-episode arcs that are like watching an entire Star Wars movie. This is the easiest and by far cheapest way to get the "whole" series (To date, no set contains the movie and season 6 and they must be purchased separately) and is worth it if you're willing to deal with numerous superficial inconveniences and if your set happens to work in the US. Pick up the movie, Season 6, and the original 2003 series (in two volumes) and find an episode guide to get the correct order of episodes. Force knows you'll need it.

history.title: Logan
history.review_title: While a fully canon entry in the X-men series, ...
history.text: While a fully canon entry in the X-men series, I'm hesitant to call Logan a Superhero film. It tosses out all cliches and doesn't lean on past movies to tell a story that is, at its core, about family. Equal parts Superhero, western, and road trip movie, the film brings back Hugh Jackman and Sir Patrick Stewart for their final outings as Wolverine and Professor X, though as indicated by the title, these aliases rarely come into play in the deeply human narrative. They're joined by Dafne Keen as Laura, or X-23, a mysterious 11-year-old with a connection to Logan that both try to deny. Keen's performance is stunning. Not just as a first-time child actor, her talent blows other industry veterans out of the water. in the 90-minute documentary (broken into digestible featurettes) on the making of the film, it's noted that Keen understood her character so well, she was improvising with Jackman DURING HER AUDITION, and holds her ground throughout the film, never overshadowed even by a Knighted actor. The only negative thing about the film is that, while it concludes the Wolverine trilogy and even the majority of X-men films to date, it's come out before the series is completely finished, with the preboot saga and several subseries continuing. That being said, it does NOT depend on the other films to be a compelling story of what is essentially a family. With plenty of action and a bit of gore.

history.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past (The Rogue Cut)
history.review_title: Rogue Cut: Best of the prequels
history.text: As a relatively new fan of the X-men series, I've been a bit bored with the prequel series. However, Days of Future Past is a pivotal film in the series and brings things back to form, with the return of Director Brian Singer. After The Last Stand and Origins: Wolverine's questionable quality and First Class and The Wolverine's changes of form, it was nice to see the series return to its roots as well as prep itself for more films to come and in a way erase the unanimously worst two films of the series. That being said, as long as you've seen the first two films, you will know what's going on, though seeing all of them (In release order is best) certainly helps. Now, The Rogue Cut obviously brings the titular character back, and offers more of a sequel to the first three films, including a redemption arc for Magneto in its additional 15+ minutes. That being said, it doesn't drag on like some Extended Editions do. This is the definitive version of the film, and even if you own the original cut, I'd say it's worth throwing out in favor of this cut. If you end up hating the added scenes, the original version is included as well, on the same disc in the blu-ray version.

history.review_title: One of the best Scooby Doo movies ever made.
history.text: I have fond memories watching this repeatedly when I was younger, but didn't remember more than a few moments. I bought the DVD expecting it to either be amazing or a huge disappointment, but you know what? It was just okay. And that's fine. It's for kids. Classic Scooby Doo style with all the tropes and cliches and hallmarks of the franchise. And a plot that, for once, keeps you guessing. Despite a few plot holes. And of course the introduction of the Hex Girls, the goth band now recurring in the series. So despite having to wait more than two days for it to ship (Amazon has really spoiled us with that), it was well worth the wait and I'm glad to own it. Quite possibly the best piece of Scooby-Doo work since the original series ended.

Note: I'm talking about the red trim "Diamond Collection" version (which usually sells for less than the Golden collection. If you don't mind my following gripes, look for this version). The DVD is very bare-bones. The menu is just text on a black background with the DVD cover art in a tiny square off to the side. The case has all three discs stacked on top of each other like a multi-disc CD-ROM game. The discs themselves have very cheap pink markings that, with my package, were sticky as if something in the DVDs' burning process didn't set right. Still, the show is there for a VERY good price and I'll binge through it in under a week. I just wish there was at least a commentary with the living cast members.

history.title: 4 Kid Favorites Cartoon Network Hall of Fame Number 2 (DVD)
history.review_title: Need an episode list? Here you go.
history.text: If for some reason you've never seen these shows, here's a quick rundown. These are all from the first seasons of classic shows from the late '90s/early 2000s but they're suitable for kids of all ages, though Courage can get very eerie. The basic premise is evident in their titles, but here's a quick rundown anyway: SAMURAI JACK: A samurai is flung into the distant future by a shapeshifting wizard who rules the world. Jack has to return to his own time and stop the wizard from ever taking over. Light action sequences. COURAGE THE COWARDLY DOG: Courage lives with an old couple in the middle of Nowhere, where eerie visitors come to visit, with sinister plans for the couple. It's up to Courage to save them. Very eerie. Definitely not for kids under 8 years old. CODENAME: KIDS NEXT DOOR: A group of kids part of a global network of secret operatives save their neighborhood from rival factions with childish goals (Stealing candy, spreading lice). Suitable for all ages. (Obnoxious to me as an adult) FOSTER'S HOME FOR IMAGINARY FRIENDS: 8-year-old Mac has outgrown his imaginary friend, Bloo, and brings him to live at the titular organization. Mac must visit Bloo every day or he will get adopted out. They're joined in their hijinks by Madame Foster, her imaginary friend Mr. Harriman, her granddaughter Frankie, the lanky and friendly Wilt, the cuddly Eduardo, and bird-like Coco. (I disliked this show as a kid but love it as an adult. It teaches valuable life lessons and stuff) EPISODES: Samurai Jack: -The Premiere Movie (3 episodes) -Jack, the Woolies, and the Chritchellites -Jack in Space -Jack and the Warrior Woman -Jack and the Three Blind Archers Courage: -Queen of The Black Puddle -Everyone Wants to Direct -The Snowman Cometh -The Previous, wonderful, adorable, Lovable Duckling -Heads of Beef -Klub Katz -The Revenge of the Chicken from Outer Space -Journey to the Center of Nowhere -Little Muriel -The Great Fusilli Codename: -I.S.C.R.E.A.M. -P.I.R.A.T.E -L.I.C.E. -L.I.Z.Z.I.E. -T.H.E.-F.L.Y -C.A.T.S. -S.P.A.N.K. -S.U.P.P.O.R.T. -G.R.O.W.-U.P." Foster's: -The Trouble with Scribbles -Seeing Red -Phone Home -World Wide Wabbit -Berry Scary -Who Let the Dogs In? Actual review: I wanted something Halloween-themed for my classmates to watch in the background in animation class, but wasn't ready to commit to a full season of "Courage." Having watched Foster's as a kid and meaning to watch Samurai Jack for years, this seemed like a great opportunity. The good: -First 7 episodes of Samurai Jack, arguably CN's most serialized show ever -Buy the first two volumes of this collection and you get the complete first season of Courage -Foster's turned out not to be nearly as trashy as I thought it was as a kid. It was very enjoyable. The cons (Very small nitpicks) -Disc 2 of Foster's. You'll have to pay another $12 for the whole first season to get the other disc. -Disc 2 of Courage. Not a problem if you intend to buy Volume 1 of this collection. -Samurai Jack froze during episode 3 on my computer, despite being spotless. Played fine on my PS4 -DVD case just stacks all discs on top of each other like an early-2000s multi-CD PC game (Luckily I have some 4-disc cases laying around) -Honestly... Kids Next Door wasn't great. While it was a great hit of nostalgia, it just left me wanting to spend money on more Courage and Foster's (And I already planned to buy the Samurai Jack blu-ray collection). Not necessarily a bad thing. And a warning: DO NOT BUY VOLUME 3 OF THIS COLLECTION (Dexter's Lab/Kids Next Door)

history.title: Voyage of the Damned Combo
history.text: Many thanks to previous reviewers! I'm so glad I took the time to read through several pages of reviews and was finally able to sort out the ones ONLY for the 2013 Blu-Ray/DVD release version. I was able to learn that key scenes were cut out for some unfathomable reason and that this film version has been cut down almost 30 minutes on the Blu-Ray version. Why, oh why do some companies do this? So I now know not to waste my almost $18 on a incomplete version. I will keep hoping that a quality restoration company, such as Criterion, is able to take this movie on and bring us a full restored version for Blu-Ray. I want to have this film in my collection for my children to inherit so that they will never forget the things that took place during this time in history. Also still hoping that Amazon can make it easier to find the reviews for the movie version you have clicked on to buy. It is still very difficult to sort through all of the reviews, most of which are not for the version you are looking for, on the page you pulled up. Surely there is a more efficient way to do this?

history.review_title: I loved it! I've read scientists (I guess) complaining he ...
history.text: I loved it! I've read scientists (I guess) complaining he is too simplified or something, but I find it very understandable from the perspective of someone with little knowledge of the sciences. Plus the locations are just astoundingly beautiful. Filmed in many places around the globe, including Madagascar & Africa. I find Professor Cox very understandable & he shows a real love and wonder in all of his documentary series. Another great doc series thanks to BBC! Loving my CuriosityStream channel. Best one yet!

history.review_title: It did an excellent job of combining the historical information on these incredible ...
history.text: Not being a musical person I did not hold out much hope of finding this interesting. I was very wrong. The documentary was very well made. It did an excellent job of combining the historical information on these incredible instruments and the modern day attempts to unravel the secrets of how Stradivarius achieved the unique sound found only in his creations. While I found the scientific processes being used very fascinating, I was rather relieved in the end to know there are still some things we can't quite completely figure out.

history.review_title: I learned a great deal about the Vikings I had not known
history.text: Very well made documentary. High production value. Did not think I would find it nearly as captivating as I did. I learned a great deal about the Vikings I had not known. I had no idea their expansion was as far reaching as it was. Flows well, keeps your interest. Very highly recommended.

Light, very funny little series on exactly what the title says. I watched them all straight through and had a great time doing so. Looking to unwind at the end of a stressful day? This is a great show to help with that.

history.review_title: Looks to be a great series. The problem is why is there only ...
history.text: Looks to be a great series. The problem is why is there only one episode? With streaming we are now free from having to watch a series a week at a time. I will have forgotten all about it by next week. This is a view I've heard voiced by many friends who also do their primary television watching via streaming. We do so to be able to watch an entire season in one night. Better to wait a year and release it all at once than dribble them out one at a time. Even when watching my "regular TV" I record an entire season on the ever and then watch it all at once. Technology has moved past the limitations of weekly episodes. Please release an entire season or not at all. Thank you. The series could be a 5 star series, hard to tell from just one episode, but that one episode was quite good. The 3 stars is given for the sole reason that I will probably never get to see the rest of them having moved on to another full season release show.

history.text: No one does quaint village murders like the British. From Holmes to Poirot to Marple to Morse to Lewis, it's a long tradition. Midsomer Murders is right up there with the best. On I think at least it's 16th season it has a loyal and devoted following of which I am a happy member. Watch! You won't be disappointed.

history.title: Live and Let Die 007 (Dvd) (2012)
history.text: Has anyone who loves Live & Let Die ever seen another Bond movie? Where do I start with this extremely weak film? Other than the theme song, a cool voodoo/graveyard sequence and the alligator pond, this is one of the low points in the franchise. Short on action and exotic locals, but packed with ghetto slang, goofy characters and an overall lack of secret agent "coolness". The 1960's were at an end and this movie is just way too early 70's looking (and sounding). Overall it's more dated than Dr No (made 10 years prior) if that's even possible. The Spy Who Loved Me is the film that won me over as far as the Moore years go. This (for me) was a terrible start for Roger Moore. It's like a long episode of Starsky & Hutch....but boring.

history.title: Allied [BD/Digital HD Combo] [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: An epic romantic thriller by director Robert Zemeckis.
history.text: I knew Allied would at least be a competently directed film thanks to director Robert Zemeckis, but I didn't expect to be as drawn into the story as I was. This is a spy thriller (not an action film) and it has you on the edge of your seat through most of the running time. The story moves at a slow but well crafted pace, so if you're looking for a World War 2 action film, this isn't it. However, if you're after a romantic period thriller with beautiful locations, beautiful people and a little World War 2 action thrown in, Allied should satisfy your needs. This is one of the few romantic movies where I actually believed the two leads were in love, and that's no small feat. SPOILER: My girlfriend was sobbing by the end if that gives you any idea how emotionally invested she was in the film.

history.title: Anthropoid [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Anthropoid is powerful, tightly paced and unforgettable.
history.text: I won't recap the plot of Anthropoid film as that only serves to spoil an amazing true story that few know about. This is a movie that is best watched with little knowledge about the story being told. I will say that Anthropoid is a very well crafted spy thriller that honors some very brave men who had no problems taking on a suicide mission to help further the Allied cause. The attention to detail and "matter of fact" action scenes are harrowing and brutal. Anthropoid is shot with a gritty, documentary style and at no time do you not feel completely immersed in Nazi occupied Prague. I would love to see a gritty World War 2 movie like this come out every year or so to counter balance the superhero saturated box office.

history.title: The Island [Blu-ray/DVD Combo]
history.review_title: An underrated classic from the author of JAWS.
history.text: The Island is an intense action/adventure/horror film that attempts to offer an earthly explanation for The Bermuda Triangle phenomenon . Modern day pirates (descendants of classic pirates) have been surviving for decades by raiding ships, killing the crew and dumping the bodies in the ocean (more believable than the maritime alien abduction or magnetic portal theories). This was one of those movies that I watched every single time it aired on The Movie Channel back in the 80's. Having recently watched it again after 20 years I can say that it's still a blast and hasn't lost any of its charm. I saw that one reviewer claims The Island is "too violent", but I feel the violence is absolutely necessary to show how brutal and ruthless these pirates are. A sword or an axe penetrating a human body is going to be messy. and this movie isn't Pirates Of The Caribbean. I think this is a great Peter Benchley follow up to Jaws and director Michael Ritchie actually makes the audience sympathize with these cutthroats to some extent. If you want something different, intense and sometimes shocking, by all means set sail for The Island.

history.title: Tales of the Gold Monkey: The Complete Series
history.review_title: Every bit as fun as you remember! Maybe even better than you remember....
history.text: I revisit shows from my youth all of the time, and sadly most of them I find unwatchable as an adult. Tales Of The Gold Monkey is that rare 80's television series that really got everything right. The stories are fun, the characters are developed, the scenery is gorgeous and the show just seemed destined to run for several years. Unfortunately the series was cancelled after only one season and never heard from again. This is one of those rare shows that has been extremely hard to find since 1983 (except on the collector's market with poor quality VHS transfers). Much of the talent from Gold Monkey (including the show's creator) went on to work on Magnum PI, another show I loved that still holds up today. Tales Of The Gold Monkey has everything that fans of pulp adventure could want, including treasure hunting, killer apes, Nazis, Japanese warriors, headhunters, beautiful locations, snakes, temples, sexy women, spies, a volcano, a rousing theme song, campy dialogue and more danger than most 80's shows combined!

history.title: Yoga Hosers
history.review_title: Funnier than 90% of the recent comedies put out by mainstream studios.
history.text: Forget the negativity from humorless critics, Yoga Hosers is an absurd, silly, fun movie! This new wave of Kevin Smith experimental movies is a lot more fun than his rehashing of Clerks characters over and over. I can honestly say that I had more fun with Yoga Hosers than I did Dogma or Clerks II. PLOT: Nazi sausages attack a convenience store in Canada run by Kevin Smith and Johnny Depp's 15 year old daughters. Smith's wife and Depp's ex Vanessa Paradis also appear in the film. Yoga Hosers is truly a family affair and it doesn't bother me one bit. I grew up with Kevin Smith films, and while I still consider Mallrats and Chasing Amy his best films to date, Red State, Tusk and Yoga Hosers offer up a creative outlet that I'm really digging. Johnny Depp was pretty hilarious in this film, especially during the table scene when confronting the evil, Nazi scientist responsible for the sinister sausage attacks plaguing Canada. I wouldn't recommend this movie to anyone who doesn't have a weird sense of humor, but for ME it's funnier than anything mainstream Hollywood has put out lately (Ghostbusters redux comes to mind).

history.title: Conan the Destroyer [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A movie that has gotten better with time...
history.text: While not nearly as good as the original John Milius and Oliver Stone Conan movie, Conan The Destroyer is a fun way to spend 2 hours and watch Arnold reprise the role he was born to play. I didn't like this film when it was originally released because of the PG rating, large supporting cast and overall lack of a dark tone, but now I can appreciate it for what it is and not what I wanted it to be 34 years ago. Truthfully, if the original Conan film wasn't so fantastic, Conan The Destroyer would stand on its own as a solid epic. Because of the real locations, fantastic cinematography, no CGI and fairly grounded story, I think this an overall better film than any of the recent sword and sorcery epics (Hobbit, King Arthur, etc). Arnold Schwarzenegger looks like a Frank Frazetta painting in every scene and the Blu-ray quality helps make Conan The Destroyer worth revisiting with modern sensibilities.

history.title: Speed Racer: The Complete Series [Blu ray] [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Speed Racer finally jumps off the screen in full HD!
history.text: YES, this is the 1967 Speed Racer with the classic American voices we all grew up with. NO, there is no Japanese audio track on this Blu-ray set. Apparently the Japanese version is being released as a separate set down the road. This is not a surprise because some of the Japanese episodes of Speed Racer were edited for content before they were dubbed, and the Japanese voices would not sync up just by switching audio tracks. Now that we have that confusion out of the way, this is every episode of Speed Racer in full HD with colors that pop right out of you screen. You have never seen the show this clear and vivid. The audio is great and the show is formatted in the original full screen format for widescreen televisions (no switching screen formats on the remote!). This is a steal for 20 bucks and having 12 episodes on each Blu-ray will keep you on the couch for hours before switching discs! If you're a fan, buy it.

history.title: Battle of the Bulge [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Model tanks, historical flubs and aging actors come together for one of the laziest WW2 movies ever made.
history.text: If you're a fan of post World War 2 tanks, model tanks being blown up like an old Godzilla movie and an overall lack of quality, Battle Of The Bulge may be a war movie you'll love. However, if historical accuracy, competent film making and wicked battle scenes are your thing, you may want to look elsewhere. This movie was included in a World War 2 triple feature Blu-ray set I bought (with Defiance & Memphis Belle, both FAR Superior films) and I couldn't even finish it. I'll watch it again eventually, but after a a few drinks to make the model tanks and fake environments more entertaining. I had no idea that the US had Korean War era tanks in WW2!

history.title: The Exorcist (Extended Director's Cut & Original Theatrical Version)
history.review_title: This review is for the region free double disc Blu-ray set (with both versions of The Exorcist).
history.text: There's no need for me to give a review of the most iconic horror film of all time, so I will review the region free Blu-ray set that contains both the 1973 & 2000 versions of The Exorcist. The picture and audio quality is fantastic on BOTH versions, and there are several special features included along with the films. I'm one of the few that considers the original 1973 theatrical version of The Exorcist the superior (and only) version of the film. I hate the "happy" ending of the Director's Cut as it completely dilutes the horror show that came right before it. The nihilistic, 1973 somber theatrical ending with the priest looking down the stairs, turning towards the camera as "Tubular Bells" kicks in is far more powerful than a lighthearted discussion about free movie passes and Casablanca (the Director's Cut ending). I highly recommend this two disc set as it's one of the only ways to watch the original version of The Exorcist that terrified audiences in 1973.

Even if it ends up on Prime for free, ignore the obvious plants who offered 5-star reviews and let this "film" die its deserved death. What was Breaking Glass thinking?

history.title: Force Majeure
history.review_title: Pay little or no attention to those who had no ability to understand the film's point.
history.text: It's unfortunate that the average American watched this film and complained as if nothing happened. European cinema puts simple ideas on screen and then asks the characters in the story to deal with them, unlike American films which decided decades ago to use sound and visual effects in place of story and storytelling, asking nothing except reaction from character and audience alike. The central conflict involves a morality play - do you save yourself, or do you save your loved ones in the event of an emergency? Is there a correct answer? Is it unmasculine? Is it unmotherly? Is it inhumane? These are the questions put forth to a family on vacation in the mountains, who must deal with the consequences of choices made by instinct in the moment. Even more, the film doesn't shy away from the uncomfortable humor of the scenario or its aftermath, even as the family tears itself apart. If your far more used to turning your brain off for 2 hours, look elsewhere. If you're opening to questioning yourself and the ones you love, watching with you, enjoy this fascinating dark comedy and discover something about who you are underneath it all, and pity those who tell you to skip this film, inconsolable with rage at what they discover.

history.review_title: Prime doesn't mean it's worth your time, even if it's "free."
history.text: As I wrote for the DVD release, 2 stars is generous for only 2 acceptable shorts out of 7. If this is the best version of "Fun" that Strand and San Francisco Frameline could make, you'd be better off going out to Folsom in only your underwear because that is more fun than these boring sexless shorts! The only "fun" short out of 7 tries is the 1 that has subtitles called "Bald Guy," a musical from Scandinavia, and those subtitles are not even available in this digital version! However, all of the American shorts are tired, tired, and exhausted. I watched "Spooners" last year and while its trying to be charming and had the crowd laughing, the lead actor is a wet fish and the bearded boyfriend bearly saves him from ruining it. The other five films are not entertaining at all. They're shot poorly with standard bad gay acting. 1 short is just 2 guys talking in a beige kitchen and living room and that's it, another short is just 2 guys talking on a bland street corner in LA and that's it, another is supposed to be in Alaska but it may as well have been shot in Nebraska because its mostly indoors. Fun, right? I don't live in San Fran anymore but I wouldn't see the shorts programs there if this is what they liked or played, Outfest is soooo much better for shorts, lots come to mind easily. I'm just very shocked after some good shorts DVD releases in the last couple of years that this was so bad. I sold the DVD I had to recope some of the money I spent on it because 1 amusing musical isn't worth keeping 5 or 6 yawn-inducing ones. There's so much better on YouTube and Vimeo now anyway, way past the crummy gay comedies here.

history.review_title: The hubris of terrible filmmakers asking people to pay to watch an awful short
history.text: I had to laugh when I saw this amongst the options for LGBT films to rent. Not Prime, actually asking for money! This Cali filmmaker may as well be a walking desert because "thirsty" is the only way to describe him. He would play this film in a parking lot if he could, and he'd fly across the country or world if it played in that parking lot, just so he could take credit for making it. All one needs to do is go to the laughable Facebook fan page to see this guy in action! As for the film itself, I have to wonder who broke this poor guy's heart this bad to be thoroughly obsessed with supposedly shaming him for ghosting or dumping him. This drama-free meladrama has some of the worst acting I've ever seen. I'd be surprised if he could direct an actor to West Hollywood, much less how to speak on camera truthfully. The film was poorly edited, made no sense, and at 17 minutes, could be about 11 minutes shorter. The lead's grandma, who never says a word and has less than 10 seconds of screentime, gives him the self-esteem it takes to tell a mean ex off, in the most stilted phone exchange ever, and somehow makes him cry? The sheer stupidity of the screenplay will make anyone with half a brain supremely angry for having your time wasted watching it. It didn't even get into OutFest, where shorts of the highest caliber can't even get distribution, but this guy thinks you should pay to watch such drivel, as you can see from the number of planted friends giving 5-star reviews to fool you. So use the Freudian slip in the poster, which tells you what your answer should be to "Should I rent, or bother to watch, this atrocious short?" Nar. Not even if it's free.

As low budget gay indie films go, there are many, many, many worse than "Best Day Ever." These films must never make any money because it often feels they spent $500 making them. If I would recommend this film to anyone, it's to someone in need of a pick me up. This is yet another wish fulfilmment fantasy where the older guy ends up with a cute young twink, but in this case, the older man looks like handsome Mel England, and the twink looks like dad-bod strawberry ginger Tom Saporito. There is a sweetness and a familiarity by which these two find each other, as the older guy turns 50, worried as all men that age they'll end up alone. There's is a relationship based in friendship and sparks, so by the time these two are giving you the tried and true frontal shots and getting it on in bed, you're aching for them to get it going. It's not a hot scene, but loving and based in affection. This is a film in which many men will see themselves. Why do we wait until we're senior citizens to settle down? I wish the supporting characters were more memorable, and that the production values were stronger, but if this appeared on Logo, I'd probably watch it again on a rainy day. Beyond older men, I don't know if it would translate as well to others.

history.review_title: Don't judge it off of the first two awful minutes
history.text: Actors who make shorts where they play the lead, direct, produce AND Exec Produce are about as fun to think about as actors who write and star in one-man shows. You'll probably want to avoid 4 out of 5 of them. Shawn Ryan, the actor/director/producer/exec producer in question here, probably qualifies among the majority. However, his film "Charlie" indicates there maybe is more to him than just annoying actor tendencies. It would be easy to dismiss this short after 60 seconds given the shrill family we first meet. Ryan, as Charlie, comes off like a rich simpleton but harassed like a idiot criminal. Bizarre and unbelievable circumstances puts Charlie in the backyard of a family at the opposite end of the spectrum, so nice they're all beyond reason or belief, on Christmas Eve. It's here where the films best moments happen, albeit at sporadic moments. Ryan must be connected to the casting of "Parks & Recreation" because Jim O'Heir and Mo Collins play the family's warm and inviting parents. They're involvement outshines everyone involved. Collins displays a maternal instinct that allows her to play more than just her normal outrageous comedic side. She's quite compelling at moments. As for Ryan, there isn't much to praise. Playing a mute character renders him mostly as furniture, though one scene involving a shave gives him a solid expressive moment to play, and he does well there. Perhaps then Ryan would do better to pawn off some of those other roles besides actor if that's what he's trying to be. A real director might have a made short worthy of 5-stars, where the lead is the true focus, not the better known co-stars. As a Prime freebie, gay guys might enjoy a rare holiday-driven treat, even if it's very light on the gay. As a rental though, you might be disappointed.

history.review_title: There ARE subtitles, but you have to watch it on your computer to see them!
history.text: Ignore the 1-star reviews, which are almost exclusively related to Americans who can't be bothered to watch a trailer, or follow instructions, and would rather complain and wreck the movie's rating here for their own failings to figure out a mishandled situation by Amazon... YES, this is a foreign-language film. NO, they don't speak English here. YES, there are subtitles. NO, they are not automatically turned On (like they should be, Amazon). YES, you can watch it with subtitles! NO, I could not turn on the subtitles via my TV, another problem created by Amazon. YES, it will play on your computer with subtitles! NO, not automatically. Just press Play after you rent it, move your mouse over the screen towards the top right corner of the picture, and hover over the revealed icon on the left, which will allow you to choose to watch with subtitles! YES, you can alter the look and size of the subtitles! Just go to the Settings tab on the Home page (also near the top right), and change them there. And now that the users have made easier what Amazon and the distributor should have done in the first place... The movie itself has heart, a few laughs, and a subtle message about the way neighbors (including immigrants with Muslim names) can uplift and revitalize your life. There are dark elements, but smart kids and teens can still watch it with the family. It's not any darker than an animated film.

history.review_title: A pure cinematic experience for all of the senses!
history.text: What can one say about this unexpected delight called "The Handmaiden" without gushing? This is pure cinema and emotion at the highest levels one could hope to find. This twisty affair of lies, lust, greed, obsession, and many other sins begins as a tale of deception and becomes a love story of tenderness and awakening. Along the way there is political intrigue, pastoral scenery, impeccable costumes, gorgeous people, sexual indecency, ghost stories, a killer score, and a screenplay to die for. Had "The Handmaiden" been in the English language, like the director's last film called "Stoker" with Nicole Kidman, it would have been an Oscar contender. The acting from the entire enselmble brings this pulpy story to viseral life, and makes it an unforgettable experience. Yes, it is subtitled but please do not let that dissuade you from buying or renting this modern masterpiece. If you miss it, you'll only have yourself to blame!

history.title: The Heat
history.text: Both characters (good cop/bad cop) have obvious flaws but manage to find a way to connect with each other for the common good against the bad guys. Not an original plot but Bullock & McCarthy brought enough to the characters to create an on-screen collaboration that makes it work -- but this certainly wasn't my favorite movie. McCarthy's character in this and "Bridesmaids" was very similar - a loud, overbearing, trash-mouthed woman which, for me, is not her most appealing character but, overall, she did a good job with it. (Her best movie, in my opinion, was "Spy." Average Jane being put into extraordinary circumstances and dealing with them as most of us would, mistakes and all). Sandra Bullock was good as well but, again, the character seemed "repetitious" of other characters she's portrayed. Overall, the movie had fewer laughs than I expected from these fabulously talented women (however, some of the deleted scenes were hilarious. Not enough to warrant the cost of the movie but hysterical, nonetheless), which is why it only rates 3 stars for me.

history.title: The Descendants
history.review_title: If you're looking to be cheered up, move along...
history.text: I can certainly understand why I'd never heard of this movie before. Clearly not Clooney's best movie but I liked the diversity of the characters. The plot was interesting enough but the overall story, though realistic and plausible, was incredibly depressing -- even the parts that were supposed to be funny were depressing. If you need help with a good cry, this might be the movie for you.

history.title: Julie and Julia
history.review_title: ... this movie 3 times now and each time I enjoyed it as much as the last
history.text: I believe I've watched this movie 3 times now and each time I enjoyed it as much as the last. Based on real life events, it was done with a lot of creativity and I found it very entertaining. Though I was never a great fan of Julia Child, it was still fascinating to watch how her life evolved -- and I can say I have a lot more respect for her, now, seeing what she went through to accomplish all she did. Streep does a wonderful portrayal in this film. Adams, as always, was fun and quirky and brought a lot of life to her character. If you're, at all, a fan of good food, you'll probably enjoy this movie as well.
