You're better off downloading a free copy off the public domain.

history.title: The Revenant
history.review_title: Same old, old, old story... did I mention, 'old'?
history.text: This film might be worth watching, but only if you have absolutely nothing else to do for about three (long) hours. I am glad I didn't pay to watch it at the theater with teens behind me kicking my seat and chatting and giggling all through it, but even in the somber oak woods of my home theater ambience, I was almost - almost - bored. It's not that it isn't a finely crafted film (the bear attack scene is pretty good if you can hack the kind of screams and squeals that only L.D. is capable of emitting) but it's so predictable. In fact, the entire film is predictable. It is a composite of better films like, "Jeremiah Johnson", "Kill Them All and Come Back Alone", "The Patriot", etc. It's a formulaic screenplay that copies dozens of screenplay's before it, and they always - always - turn out the same.... Bad man kills good man's son. Good man needs to overcome overwhelming odds and obstacles to take revenge on bad man who killed good man's son... I'm actually boring myself as I write this. To sum up, 1) not a bad way to spend 3 hours if you've nothing better to do, 2) the CGI is unforgiveably noticeable - especially the bear attack scene, 3) if there is ANY good reason that I can think of for you to watch this movie, it's because of Tom Hardy. First of all, you will never, ever know that the antagonist, "Fitz", is Tom Hardy - this guy is a phenomenal actor - but the screenplay is at fault; it's perfectly predictable and though Hardy does an outstanding job (an I do mean, OUTSTANDING JOB) with what he has to work with, the role he plays is nothing special. In summary, think, good guy vs. bad guy - with a sort of half-way decent bear attack scene in the beginning...

history.title: Black Mass (Blu-ray+ DVD + UV)
history.review_title: BORING, PREDICTABLE yawn-fest. Bulger gets way with it again.
history.text: Growing up in the '70's and '80's I heard about the Winter Hill Gang, Whitey Bulger and his Senate brother, Billy... but this movie is a fart in a bottle. Don't you dare waste your money on this contrived film. It doesn't know what it wants to be.. a documentary? A biopic? It's just a very long yawn-fest that never tells you anything about the man. Yes, he's bad - but not as bad as Depp's nasal imitation of Jack Nicholson throughout. There is so much bad with this movie, I don't know where to begin... So let's sum up: 1. You never get to understand how and why Whitey turned out the way he did (and for that matter why his goody 2-shoes brother Billy-boy (allegedly) turned out the way he did... you know, the 'good son/bad son' thing... 2. Bulger was a gay hustler, spent time at Alcatraz, gouged out the eyes and pulled out the teeth of beautiful young women, and all we get is Depp in some serious caked-on flesh-colored makeup and fake blue contacts belching out the typical Godfather hit-man crap we've been forced to endure in countless better films on the subject before. 3. Have you yawned yet? 4. What the bloody 'a-HELL" is Jai Alai? It's a sport, right? - popular in Florida, right? - but you never get to know what attracted an IRISHMAN SOUTHIE GANGSTER to it. Money - yes, but what was the attraction? In the early '80's wouldn't cocaine and M-Jane have been the big draw? I was totally LIS on this one... and aside from the murders involved, you'll need the Robot and the Space Shuttle yourself to get yourself out of this one. 5. The film tries to make Whitley look so b-a-a-a-d, but it only ends up making him look hilariously cliche, like the scene where he strangles Flemmi's step-daughter and 'stokes' the face of the disgusted, poor Mrs. Connelly. The film's portrayal of these events give these scenes such unintentional humor... from both a writing and acting perspective. 6. Depp is a great imitator. He imitated Keith Richards for his role of Captain Jack Sparrow, Charlie Chaplin in "Benny and Joon", Crispin Glover in "Ed Wood"... eeeeesh... and now Jack Nicholson as Bulger. BORING! 7. How did the writer, director and producer(s) ever get a green light on this one? The back story to this alone would be a much better film than "Black Mass".

history.title: What About Bob?
history.review_title: HILARIOUS FUN - when is the Blu-Ray coming out?
history.text: I laughed all through this film the first time I watched it, and since then, I've watched it five times - each viewing with different friends and members of my family, and each time we find ourselves crying from laughter. I'm in my 50's and I've seen many comedies in film and on the stage, but this is one of my top five all-time favorite comedies. Richard Dreyfuss is absolutely perfect as the uptight and narcissistic psychiatrist who has just written a book that he believes is the answer to introverted psychopathic behavior, yet no one wants to read it (for instance, he has a library loaded with his unsalable books). Then comes along the real deal - a nice enough 40ish home worker with a germophobe complex and severe introversion, who is "passed off" on the Dreyfuss' character, "Dr. Leo". This is where the story takes off and what a story it is. Dr. Leo is about as uptight a man as you can possibly imagine. His 10 year old son dresses in black and has a death fixation. His daughter and wife are delightfully aloof and end up befriending Bob against Leo's demands. In a way, it's quite terrifying to think that a sick patient can worm his way into the family of his Dr., but in this film, it is all harmless fun. Living in New Hampshire, I found it a real treat when the film tales place on Lake Winnipesaukee.

history.title: Penny Dreadful: Season One
history.text: Total loser of a story. Took two episodes for me to finally get nauseated enough to give up the ghost on this contrived garbage. I guess all it takes now is to use composites of successful, original stories from 80 years ago - add a whole lot of fake blood, the C**T word, gratuitous cleavage, and a coffin-load of totally boring BS, and I guess you have a hit... A hit? Damn the hides of these writers, producers and actors to hell for the moronic foolishness of this idiotic series. The fact that there are so many fans is proof that sheep are always used synonymously with the human race. I worship the day when the world produces another Shakespeare. In the meantime, we get, er... this.

history.title: Stripes (Extended Cut) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Don't waste your money on the "Blu-Ray"
history.text: I was a corporal in the Army when I watched "Stripes" in a full theater of GI's as part of a double feature on my base in Fort Lee, Va, and my memory of it at that time was that it was just an "OK" movie. Not a lot of laughs apart from the John Candy scenes... It was obvious that Bill Murray was really hamming it up, and it all just fell flat. The other film, "Airplane 2" was a real screamer - lots of laughs and it was perceived as the better of the two films that night back in '82. Fast forward 40 years, and this "blu-ray" format of "Stripes" is a sad joke. If you have a DVD of it, you're good to go. The 'blu-ray" includes some additional "special features" that are truly yawn-worthy and utterly forgettable - even Bill Murray is bored out of his mind (when interviewed on site in Japan during the "Lost in Translation" film he was working on in 2003). If he couldn't give a damn about it, why should you? The extended bits (approx. 17 minutes) are boring and dumb - this is why they never made it into the final film and got left on the cutting room floor. The quality of this phony "blu-ray" is blurry and muted; to use a 'Murrayism" from the film, "there's NO WAY..." this should have been classified as 'blu-ray" or HD or anything other than the 32mm film it was originally photographed on. Moral of the story: you've got to be a super-psycho Bill Murray fanatic to get through this film. I dropped out after the "Aunt Jemima" scene, and tossed this disc out in the trash - never to be watched again. "St. Vincent" is a far superior representation of Murray's "talent", the best schtick he's ever done.

history.review_title: A personal look at a piece of the war
history.text: Any movie with Ed Harris would be on my watch list. Add the talent of Jude Law and you have to have a winner. Perhaps the name of the movie is too misleading and should have referenced the personal stories instead of highlighting the war. I do think we can get a good idea of the battle that waged between the stalwart Russians and the die hard Germans. Revenge. Is it sweet? Justified? Does it free you from the bad memories? This film asks these questions and more. To me, the culture doesn't make a difference. I became more and more involved as the story continued. By the of the movie I was on the edge of my seat, wondering what the husband would decide to do. I've never had a bad experience and met some interesting people over the years, so it's difficult for me to pass someone by. This movie does not change my mind. I started yelling at the black guy, to get rid of the white guy about 10 mins into the ride. I can't imagine that he would continue to go along with the story the white guy handed him. In addition, like some of the other reviewers, I don't see how it could end the way it did. Too many clues for the cops to follow-up on. However, I really appreciate that two people carried this whole movie. Liked the actors and was fascinated by the characters. There are just too many coincidences to make it believable.

There are many ways to evaluate this movie. Does it define faith. Is faith worth giving up your life, or the life of another. Is missionary work justified? Must we prove our faith loudly or can it be done quietly. Let me say I am anti any kind of religion. Won't go into why I feel that way, but I can say I have studied most of the "big" religions and some of the lesser known. One of my main questions is why so many religions don't accept others' beliefs as genuine and worthwhile. I think we can see, in this film, that the missionaries did not ask themselves that specific question. They went into Japan with a specific agenda and did not understand the culture and beliefs they would be facing. I don't think they would have been any more accepted, but they might have been able to go at conversion in a different way. Ok, back to the movie. Scenery, costumes and settings are terrific. It is slow moving, but there is a lot of thinking and soul-searching going on. I do agree with other reviewers that some of the scenes could have been shortened without changing the essence of the plot. Andrew Garfield is great as are the Japanese cast members. Niam Leesom and Adam Driver are almost non-existent. We may flinch at the methods the Japanese officials used to punish the converts or change their minds, but need only think of our own hostility and brutality toward unwanted faiths in the western world. This is a very heavy movie that does not have a happy ending, so don't sit down to watch this and hope to feel light-hearted at the end. You might come away with a better understanding of missionaries and more importantly, Japanese faith and culture. That is quite a reward for a couple of hours of your time.

history.review_title: Basic Knowledge leads to Better Understanding.
history.text: this is a difficult subject to tackle. Just finished the segment on Islam and I'm anxious to see the rest of the series. Some reviewers have complained that it is not an accurate picture of the religions being discussed. They lament that recent acts of terrorism or past atrocities have not been discussed. I see this series as a positive outlook on each religion. How each one begin and what are its tenants. To go into what is wrong with the religion or how their beliefs have been used to bring bad things into others' lives would defeat the purpose of this program. We all need to learn some basic facts about each other's beliefs and religious goals. How those beliefs have been twisted to suit individual or group dynamics is an entirely different discussion. I have attended many classes on different religions and read many books that describe and contrast the "big 3" religions. I think this program does a great job in the time given. I took some notes about things I wanted to further investigate. I agree with one reviewer that some form of this material should be taught in school. I am not a religious person at all, but it is important to me to understand how other people think and what directs their thinking about life. Religion is a huge part of our world, even if we don't participate ourselves.

history.title: Crown Heights
history.text: Having volunteered for several years in a max security prison I can really identify with this movie. Not that I believe that every prisoner who says they are innocent is, but that there are plenty of them who are or who have received unjustly, harsh sentences. The acting sets and situations are very real. I'm glad this movie did not go into the usual routine of prisoner abuse, sexual mistreatment and violence. There is plenty of that in prison, but here we are focused on the people not, so much, the situation. We all know that the prison system in this country is full of problems; too many to go into here. If we are to solve this situation, more people on the outside need to get busy and create a society that incarcerates as few people as possible. The determination and love shown this prisoner by his family and friends is not always available to a prisoner. It's easy, when those heavy, metal, clang closed behind you to feel lost and alone and give up hope. I didn't find this movie boring or slow. I could only watch and acknowledge how my patience it took for the wheels of our legal system to turn. If you think prison is THE answer to crime, please watch this movie and learn how unfair prosecution and penalty can be. I think you will find this film informative and, perhaps, open our eyes about how we punish people in this country.

history.title: Searchers / Wild Bunch / How the West Was Won (Triple-Feature) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Warner gives you three films here of high quality, all with good to great transfers. Right now the set is about 11 bucks with tax. There really is no better triple collection out there for this price. All three films are legendary for different reasons. The Searchers got an extensive restoration. This film defined a lot about what we love in traditional westerns and at a very high level of expertise. A John Ford masterpiece. How The West Was Won, here sans its smilebox version--which to me is too distorted for my liking on my 42 inch--is a wonder to behold for its set design and costumes. If nothing else enjoy the production values here. Stunning realization on bluray. The Wild Bunch could probably be improved, at the least in its bitrate, but it still is a solid presentation. Peckinpah's classic looks very good for its age, and any viewer only knowing the film from DVD will want the upgrade. The bitrates are overall a but low to average, but the films do not suffer tremendously from this, and most people will just see a hint of softness compared to the highest bitrate restorations on bluray. All in all this is a must buy recommendation for anyone interested in cinema and art of the period.

history.title: Who Framed Roger Rabbit: 25th Anniversary Edition (Two-Disc Blu-ray/DVD Combo in Blu-ray Packaging)
history.text: Bos Hoskins is just a magnificent actor in many of his roles. He left too soon. At any rate going back through some of his catalogue, you arrive at the pop sensation that is this film from Zemeckis and Co. in an age where CGI and digital trickery was in its infancy. And dear lord does the bluray finally do it justice. Amazing. That is about all that needs to be said. A nice layer of grain accentuates a not perfect but totally great transfer to bluray. It's almost everything you wanted it to be. Furthermore, it isn't some horrid trainwreck of DNR nor was much altering of the source even considered. For a film from 1988 it could hardly look better unless given the full 4K restoration. Even then the look of the film gels with the 1940s thematic elements. What you are stuck with here is a one of a kind film. Never before or since has Hollywood merged all kinds of different toons together with such whacky animation. And it's all surrounded by a great tale. Some doubt it will ever happen again. What you need to know is that this film has never looked even close to this good. Pick it up immediately. If you are not a fan it's at least worth it to see where Hollywood and Zemeckis were in this era, experimenting and wallowing in zany, disastrous glee. Toons and humans will never be the same. The humor still holds up. As I said at the beginning, Hoskins gives a remarkable performance as the hard drinkin' detective Eddie Valiant. A glorious release! Fully Recommended.

history.title: John Wayne: Film Collection
history.text: This is a really fine boxset with a couple caveats. The Longest Day has some DNR in it. It's not completely wasted but it's close. The other films range from decent to excellent transfers. Excellent clarity and grain structure: The Comancheros, The Undefeated, North To Alaska, and The Barbarian and the Geisha. Mediocre to decent transfer: The Big Trail, Horse Soldiers--The Big Trail at least was never in great condition to begin with. Needs major improvement: Sadly, The Longest Day comes from the time of the first version of Patton, where studios were experimenting with DNR. The image has decent detail, but the grain is gone and the film looks too soft and plain. A 4K transfer here would make the film look amazing. Way too many pasty faces in this one. Overall a fine set well worth your money. It's on sale for 20 dollars at times. Whenever they do remaster The Longest Day I will just put it in the case I guess.

history.title: The Bourne Identity
history.text: So it begins. We all knew this was going to happen. Studios barely care about giving catalogue releases new film masters from the negative, so do people really believe they are just going to magically transform every title in 4K and spend the money on 4K transfers? Haha, no. This film looks different from the bluray for sure, but it's probably worse. The transfer they used for this 4K edition, costing 20 or 30 dollars, is the same 1080p transfer you got on bluray. There might be a very small, barely noticeable uptick in detail, but it's nothing hardly anyone will actually notice. What is different is the reduction in color. HDR and the contrast have manipulated the image to be lifeless almost, and very much different from the bluray. I will leave the viewer to see the film and choose which they prefer, but for all intents and purposes I actually like the bluray better. At any rate the release is being sourced from not even a 2K Digital Intermediate. What is the point of this release? Much like many old and shoddy blurays, the point is to take your money. So who is this 4K release for? IDK. It's clearly not even in the same galaxy as something like The Revenant, which is amazing in 4K. This release at times looks worse than the bluray. So for 20 bucks you are getting basically the same thing you get for 4 dollars on sale. If it is worth it to you to have both masters in one release so be it. I know collectors will probably want both. But be warned: this is going to happen more and more. It happened to bluray from dvd in a LOT of releases, and doing 4K masters from the original negative is an expensive process that will not be used on the vast majority of films. To be honest this release is basically a cash grab. And there will be many more like it. And for a cherry on top the cover art is awful. It does have slightly better audio for those that care.

history.title: Ghost in the Shell: 25th Anniversary Edition [Blu-ray]
history.text: The release is cheap no doubt, and the video transfer is decent. But nothing is up to par like a film of this caliber demands. The subtitles for the Japanese track are all botched, with slang and grammar errors everywhere. Unreal. The 5.1 English track is missing sounds in many places as well. The video is decent like I said, but it's an old source, and it's letterboxed to a degree. I'm not sure who was in charge of this release but it's pretty much amateur hour throughout. I recommend the film. If you can find it for 5 bucks it's not a bad purchase, but you have been warned about its problems.

history.title: Romancing the Stone / Jewel of the Nile [Blu-ray]
history.text: Garbage-tier audio ruins the entire experience. The audio as has been noticed on bluray.com has basically just cut off all high frequencies. The DVD even has these, so the HD audio here is false and among the worst audio you will ever hear on bluray. Is it worth 7 bucks or so? IDK, that is up to you. I wouldn't buy this. The picture quality is decent, but I would just wait for a 4K scan. Romancing the Stone is the only good film in here, and the only one directed by Zemeckis. This is a very poor couple of blurays done in the infancy of the format.

history.title: The Land Before Time [Blu-ray]
history.text: I must have watched this so many countless times as a small child. Every theme in here resonates with growing up. There is death, life, love, comedy, and everything in between. An all time classic matched by few films. Unlike the Secret of Nimh, this release is in very good shape, and the resulting bluray might blow your mind if all you have are memories of the VHS. The audio is finally uncompressed and sounds crystal clear. They did a wonderful job with this one. A first rate recommendation.

history.title: Sicario 4K Ultra HD 4K UHD
history.text: Denis Villeneuve and crew are an amazing new force in film. His past films are amazing for the most part, and this one is no exception. I am glad Hollywood saw that this guy and his team can craft some really great films and decided to hire him for some bigger budget fair. His previous films in Enemy, Incendies, and Prisoners were all very creative and enthralling. But now he is on the BIG circuit, and one can only hope that creativity stays put. For Sicario it does. This is a somewhat quiet but mesmerizing thriller you might mistake for not being a big Hollywood production at all. But the acting is first rate here, there is a sense of realism lacking in worse action pictures, and the characters are fleshed out just enough to keep you interested in the main trio, always wondering what might happen to any one of them in the next scene. The script is micromanaged and assertive in its control of the reasoning behind each character's decisions, though, we are never truly privy to some of the past happenings in each of their lives. Blunt totally shines here as does Del Toro. Brolin as well puts in a quality performance as the veteran CIA officer. The three actors really bring out the details in the script, and the direction and cinematography as well the score are all spot on. This is quality film. I would rate it at 4.5 stars, but I guess I'm giving it the full 5 here.

history.title: Enemy [Blu-ray]
history.text: I'm kind of astounded at the low reviews here. All the players involved have terrific performances and the men and women behind the scenes do their jobs incredibly well. DV has directed another film in a closet full of them at this point, and quite honestly I really hope his Blade Runner sequel succeeds because he has the talent to make it happen. What does not surprise me at all I guess are the tepid and inane reviews by Amazon reviewers, who absolutely need most things spoon fed to them. Look, the whole point of this film was not to give you a history lesson, to outright make you believe in any one thing, or to control your emotions and wrap things up in a tidy soap opera ending. It's symbolism. The film leaves things open-ended for a reason. If you were given reasons and crucial points of exposition that explained everything it would totally ruin the entire film. I think it speaks more to this generation of "kids" than anything else.... in that people cannot be bothered to think beyond the first line of sight anymore. Ironically, the whole film has flashes of the theme of dictatorships and control that seem to explain what is going on if only people would, you know, control their attention spans for a quick moment or stop and think about what is actually going on before just giving up and in to their tendencies to be displeased on first sight of a problem. But no, a one star review and waste of time it is. Back to Hunger Games and comic book films! Enemy is open ended in that you can put your own thoughts and ideas onto its symbolism, though, there are distinct lines of understanding that beckon you to peruse their depths. There are ideas about spiders, women, sex, twins, mythology, government, et cetera. You are never too sure what exactly is going on, but the film encourages you to think a little bit, take in its source material, and then with the absurdly gorgeous direction and score you have something to ponder for a couple hours. Enemy probably doesn't quite live up to its ambitions in that it leaves a few too many things left unsaid, and that missing exposition or even symbolism does leave a bit of a hole in the film's complex, but it still is a great little indie that is way too underrated on this site. There are many themes about control in this film, and one only has to go so far to see those concepts played out in intelligent and creative ways within the short running time here. I never once looked at the time in a hurry while watching this. It's 90 minutes for god's sake, and the director is easily one of the most talented guys in the film business. As I said this is a quality film. I have no idea whatsoever why it is sitting below three stars. People in general have poor taste when it comes to difficult films. The Bluray looks very good for an indie and is shot in wondrously minimalist yet artful way typical of the director's other films. Totally recommended.

history.title: Nocturnal Animals
history.text: It's an unusual movie, with two parallel stories, a totally cheap shock beginning, which was supposed to show the values degradation which the main character despises but is well paid to promote. She is a successful gallery owner, who gets a manuscript from her ex-husband 19 years after the divorce. Again, a note accompanies it stating that the book is nothing like he wrote when living with her. She is trapped in an unhappy marriage and reminiscent of the previous marriage with a kinder man, who she left for being as "weak" as her current husband is driven and ambitious. Coming from the long line of "doers" to her, her ex's writing career career seemed like a fool's path, and even more so to her controlling mother. Now, at a critical juncture of her life, with her possibly cheating husband, she gets a glimpse of a dark side of the ex, which she had no idea about, who wants to pay her back in shock value for the shock she gave him in order to expedite their divorce. The acting is good, the time switches are mostly not too jarring. I would say that all in all, the movie was interesting.

Unexpectedly, an elderly woman arrives from London to Verona in reply to the letter, looking for her lost true love from old letter, whom she left waiting under "their tree" in 1950s, when she left for England, where she got married. history.title: Americans on D-Day
history.text: Very well done documentary. When I first saw this available, I wondered why a British chap was running around in American combat uniforms talking about World War II. After watching it, it is obvious it is because Mr. von Seibold has a passion for the subject, for story-telling, for accuracy and an appreciation for the American sacrifice and contributions in WWII. Documentary also includes veteran interviews, which are always a plus. I highly recommend this and look forward to viewing the others in the series.

history.title: Americans in the Bulge
history.text: I collect any DVD that has veterans interviewed, I would guess I have 200 or so about WWII, and this is a real surprise. It is very well done, from the soldier's interviews, to the reenactments, to the correct period gear, to the stories about forgotten heroes like 19-year-old James Hendrix. I also appreciated seeing the exact spots where history occurred and seeing so many of the monuments to American troops that exist. Throughout this 90-minute film, Ellwood Von Seibold zips around and shows his passion for history and his appreciation for the American contributions. Buy this DVD and the others in this series, I am aware of two others. I wish there were more. Well done, Mr. Von Seibold and colleagues.

history.title: I, Robot (Two-Disc Combo: Blu-ray 3D/ Blu-ray + DVD) [3D Blu-ray]
history.text: Amazed to read some others found the 3D conversion suitable on I Robot. I am using a top of the line blu ray 3D player and a new LG TV and I found I Robot to be a big disappointment and a very bad sign of where 3D (conversion) is headed -- studios using the cheaper conversion option and movies having little depth and no pop-out whatsoever. The funny thing about the I Robot conversion to me was the small on-screen menu that would appear when prompted was the ONLY popout in the whole movie and the sad thing about that is that it immediately and constantly shows you and reminds you of how the movie COULD have been. I do think the 3D version of I Robot is better than just the bluray experience BUT when you watch other 3D movies like Titanic and Avatar you'll see a day and night difference. At least I sure did. To all studios: I will be re-thinking future decisions on 3D purchases if this is what you'll be offering us. What I see in I Robot is not worth the $30 pricetag at all. It's an amazing and entertaining technology but you are going to miss your opportunity if this is what you'll be offering us.

However, with all this attention to detail you would think that the person responsible for costuming would do a better job. The problem is not with the Vikings, but rather the Anglo-Saxons. Why are they wearing identical outfits and why are some of them wearing helmets from the Renaissance? Maybe I nitpick, but this annoys the heck out of me. If you want to see what the Anglo-Saxons actually looked like, check out the BBC miniseries called "1066: the Battle for Middle Earth," which concerns the three great battles the Anglo-Saxons fought that year.

history.title: Olympus: Season 1
history.review_title: Give it a break. Relax and enjoy.
history.text: I enjoy this show. Long ago I stopped expecting the tv/film industry to portray the ancient myths or ancient history accurately. They simply can't/won't. Consequently, I bought the first season of this show with limited expectations. It is a great deal of fun. The way they arbitrarily give names to the characters cracks me up. The costuming and background sets are the usual scramble from Greek history and more. The Minoans are wearing what looks like Norse helmets, there are a number of correct Mycenaean/Minoan reproductions, but they also mix in things from the Archaic and Classical period. The mullet haircuts are funny. Anyway, the series is not intended to be taken seriously. Like ATLANTIS, it is meant for us to just have an entertaining time. Hey, sit back and enjoy. The acting, especially Medea's actor are pretty good. They do in a very broad way, relate the story of Theseus.

history.title: The Last Ship: Season 2
history.review_title: A Rogue British warship would be a tough opponent
history.text: WARNING: SPOILER I really enjoy this show. It has plenty of action, the characters are well developed and most of the action is plausible. As and obsessive Anglophile, it was hard to watch ships from our two countries fighting against each other. However, just as the series shows elements of American forces (Md. State Police) going rogue, the same could happen with a British nuclear sub. The show makes you question whether the military would be something the people could depend on for help in an apocalyptic setting, or would elements of it go rogue. Larry Niven and Jerry Pournell posed this question in LUCIFER'S HAMMER also. It is food for thought. I just wish the opponent was from another nationality. In a way though it is a compliment to the Royal Navy in that although these guys went rogue, they are tough, smart and fearless. I loved season 2.

history.title: Self-Massage with Finis Jhung
history.review_title: A nice personal touch at the end is when he lets ...
history.text: This DVD has 13 sections which I will break down for you below. In overview, Finis is alone in his apartment showing how to use the various physical therapy items, where, and what muscle groups they are for. Very personable, helpful to anyone struggling with arthritis or injury rehab. Helpful advice includes: "Every day is another day," and "Get up from sitting every 15 minutes." 1. Foam Roller: Hip flexors, quads, adductors, iliopsoas. 2. Air Filled Balls & Solid Balls: Glutes, trochanters, rotators, hip flexors, iliopsoas, adductors (the turnout muscles). 3. Air Filled Ball: Greater trochanter, glutes, piriformis, IT band. 4. Hand Tools: Hip flexors, glutes, IT band, quads. 5. Stretch Strap: Hamstrings, adductors, glutes. 6. Ma Roller: Spine, back. 7. Soft Ball, Hand Tool: Shins, calves, fibula area 8. Rollers, Solid Ball: Foot 9. Rubber Ball on Stick: Shoulders, neck, back, glutes, IT band, head, sinus 10. Stick (flexible): Neck, shoulders, glutes, greater trochanter, IT band 11. Thera-Cane: Neck, back, greater trochanter, glutes, IT band. 12. Tennis Ball in sock: Glutes, piriformis, back. 13. Door Bar: Full body stretches, also uses stretch strap for some of this. I am waiting for some of these items to arrive from Amazon, but the explanations by Finis are very informative and crystal clear. The DVD can be used for either instruction or work-along demonstration. A nice personal touch at the end is when he lets the viewers know that the whole video was shot in his apartment, and it is not only the first video of this type (rehab) he has ever made, it's also the first time for a father-son collaboration with his son Jason (who briefly appears on camera to say hi at the end). Cannot recommend this video highly enough, this is what I have needed for years.

history.title: Evolution: Darwin's Dangerous Idea
history.text: [[ASIN:B001PYD0RK Evolution: Darwin's Dangerous Idea]] The film starts off with a brief interview with the evolutionary philosopher, Daniel C. Dennett who wrote a book by the same name, Darwin's Dangerous Idea. He puts forth a most outrageous assertion when he says," If I were to give a prize for the single best idea anybody every had, I would give it to Darwin, ahead of Newton and ahead of Einstein". Why? Because, he says, Darwin managed to bridge the world of purposeless, meaningless, matter and motion, on the one hand, and the world of meaning, purpose and design on the other. What an erroneous notion, especially to anyone who knows about the history of science and how Newton's laws of motion and law of gravitation are foundational to modern physics and to modern technology. A very important question to ask is, how has evolutionary theory contributed to the advancement of science or to technological advance. I am sure that honest inquiry will come up with one number - zero contribution. Another unfortunate aspect of this film is its prejudice toward Christianity and to Christians, but this should not be a surprise since Darwin was himself thus prejudiced. He said in one place in his writings that the Bible was not to be trusted any more than the writings or utterances of a barbarian. He also wondered how anyone could wish that Christianity could be true. I should hasten to say that Emma Darwin, a Unitarian, is presented as a true compassionate Christian. However, the film takes a different view of three other Christians that are portrayed. The three presented are Captain Fitzroy, the naturalist Richard Owen who is famous for coining the word "dinosaur", and the physician who attended Darwin's daughter Anna when she was sick and lay dying. The film portrays Fitzroy and Owen as being close-minded and intolerant. The physician is presented as uncompassionate when Darwin is weaping for his daughter. This is a very biased view of Christians indeed and does not describe Christians that I know and those I have known for over 30 years of being a Christian myself. One just needs to consider the history of hospitals and to ask, who founded our hospitals? On the other hand is Russia, the former Soviet Union, and modern-day China where the state religion is atheism and evolution is the only accepted belief system. Countries like the United States become more and more like these others the more evolutionary theory becomes dominant and freedom of thinking and speech is not allowed (which is happening, please see Ben Stein's DVD: Expelled: No Intelligence Allowed). Darwin's Dangerous Idea has a rather lengthy segment on how the eye could not possibly have been designed by an intelligent designer; they indicate instead an evolutionary process. The flaws are apparently two major ones: the eye's photoreceptors point to the back of the eye instead of toward the light source, and the second is that in front of the photoreceptors, blocking some of the light, are blood vessels, nerves and ganglia. The ignorance of the evolutionist is astonishing on this point (and on many others) and also alarmng when you consider that some publish biology textbooks that are used in many of our public schools. Here's the real story that the reader is not likely to hear from evolutionists. The photoreceptors point backwards facing a pigment layer that supplies them with much needed nutrients and oxygen since these structures have a very high metabolic rate. Also back there is the choroid which cools the photoreceptors and prevents them from overheating. There is also a black layer comprised of melanin which absorbs extra light and prevents that light from bouncing around inside the eye. The ganglia and nerves that are placed between the source of light and the photoreceptors are practically transparent and block little light. And most amazingly this apparatus is pushed aside at a crucial place to allow light a direct path to the foveola and fovea where the cones are at a their highest density. this is why human vision works so well and images are so sharp. Man, with all his intelligence and ingenuity, has not yet been able to make anything approaching the marvel of the human eye. In one place in the film Emma is talking with Darwin and it is at this point, I believe, in Darwin's life that he is interested in artificial selection. (He himself bred pigeons in real life.) She makes a noteworthy statement when she tells him that he can produce big dogs and little dogs but he cannot produce a dog with feathers. [Today genetics shows us that the genome of an organism is limited in what it can produce.] She says further that he cannot produce a heart - only God,can. Emma was quite right. Evolutionary explanations go no further than explaining the varieties within a species. When it attempts to go further than this, and it certainly has, it is over its head and cannot rely on science to support its claims, not from genetics and not from the fossil record or any other area of science. It was the late evolutionary paleontologist Colin Patterson of the British Museum who asked an assembly of his colleages "What is one thing we know for sure about evolution". He got no reply from all that were assembled. I believe it was also he that said that evolution is anti-knowledge. As a science teacher for 30 years, I quite agree, though evolution has captivated many, it is the the arch enemy of science and scientific progress and the arch enemy of Christ and His Church.

history.title: Charles Darwin and the Tree of Life (David Attenborough) [DVD]
history.review_title: David Attenborough's Presentation of Darwin Questionable
history.text: Though the film provides stunning cinematography of the natural world, yet its shoddy presentation of science and its historical revisionism prompts me to give it only one star. Gregor Mendel is generally acknowledged in the world of science as the father of genetics whose laws of genetics are true today as in the day that he discovered them, so how can Mr. Attenborough say in his documentary that in Darwin's day, no one had the faintest idea of the mechanism of heredity or the rules of heredity except "perhaps" a monk named Mendel. Perhaps? I think Mr. Attenborough is attempting to excuse Darwin's apparent ignorance of Mendel. Likely Darwin was ignoring Mendel as other evolutionists were. At the same time that Darwin was working on his Origin of Species, Mendel was doing his pea experiments. Then Darwin published in 1859 and Mendel published in 1866. And Mendel did not publish in an obscure journal. That journal was distributed to 120 libraries including several libraries in England and in the United States (Ian Taylor, In the Minds of Men). At least a couple of authors suppose that since Mendelism was so incompatible with Darwinian evolution his work was ignored. Nelson Byron in his After its Kind quotes from Alfred Russell Wallace who expressed his concern that it (Mendalism) was "antagonistic to evolution". Ian Taylor in his book In the Minds of Men said that evolutionists could ignore Mendel because he lacked the stature as Louis Pasteur who evolutionists had vigorously opposed because of their belief in spontaneous generation (which Pasteur definitively disproved). What Mendel's laws demonstrated was the genetic basis for organisms reproducing after their own kind. In Genesis, God ordained that all organisms would reproduce after their own kind. To date evolutionists have not been able to break the species barrier even though they have attempted to do so. Darwin could not do so with his breeding of pigeons. And though in the 20th century evolutionists bred generation after generation of fruit flies, all they got for their their trouble was more fruit flies, and nothing else. Attenborough does not make mention of any of these difficulties that Mendel's laws posed for evolutionists. Professor M. Gyrtych who taught population genetics at the Polish Academy of Sciences has pointed out in the video Evolution: Fact or Belief that there is no genetic evidence for evolution in any of the world's genetic's laboratories. He says that evolution is not a science, rather it is a philosophy. If evolutionists had done their science honestly from Darwin's day, they would have given up evolution. Darwin said that if the fossil evidence remains lacking this lack of evidence could falsify his theory. Attenborough's presentation, like so many others we see today, glosses over the fossil evidence and presents none of the considerable difficulties. Attenborough gives us to believe that if one just could know the fossils in the sedimentary strata it would be obvious that evolution has occurred. But it is not so obvious. This is why Stephen J. Gould and Niles Eldridge came up with an alternative mechanism to Darwinian gradualism. They could not see any transition of one organism into another in the fossil record. In fact they described a stasis, that is, the fossils show no change in any particular layer. In a successive layer they may be replaced by other organisms or by another species. Gould and Eldridge called their theory punctuated equilibrium. The fossil record very much depends upon interpretaton. Rather than it demonstrating evolution, the theory is imposed upon it through speculation. Though Attenborough does point out the complexity of organisms in the Cambrian such as the trilobite which had very sophisticated eyes, he fails to point out that the fossils in the ancient layers below do not exhibit any plausible ancestors to the complicated organisms in the Cambrian. He mentions the Ediacaran fossils of Australia, but does not point out that even among these there are no ancestors for trilobites or other Cambrian organisms. The presentaton also fails to show the out-of- place fossils, or the fossils that are a bit of an embarrassment such as the polystrate trees which straddle many strata, supposedly waiting around for millions of years before they were buried. There is an important clue at the very beginning of the movie what Darwin's theory was all about. It provided people with an alternative to the Bible (and in the nineteenth century many were ready to chuck Christianity). It provided an alternative explanation for the complexity and wonder of the natural world. But Darwinism should properly be called a religion. As Professor Richard Dawkins of Oxford University has said, it makes being an atheist respectable. But Darwinism should not dress itself up as science, because there really is no scientific evidence for it. Dr. M. Gyrtych is right. As a postscript I would like to say that the newly made video Evolution vs. God: Shaking the Foundations of Faith (also available on Amazon) is very effective in showing that there really is no evidence for evolution. Four professors of evolutionary biology as well as students of evolution are inteviewed. The interviewer, Ray Comfort, asks the right questions, because he effectively shows that none of the professors or students is able to provide any observable evidence for evolution.

history.title: Uncovering the Truth About Dinosaurs (DVD Series)
history.review_title: Uncovering the Truth about Dinosaurs is a Signifcant Contribution to Our Understanding of Dinosaurs.
history.text: Protein and blood cells in dinosaur bones? No ancestors for the dinosaurs? A stegosaurus depicted on the column of a Cambodian Temple and a long neck dinosaur among the drawings left on a cave wall by an American Indian group? Yes. This DVD set produced by the Institute for Creation Research is masterfully done ( as are all its productions). The sciences of biology, geology, paleontology, and archaeology, as well as history and the Bible are used to show that the Bible is accurate about its depiction of Noah's Flood, a world-wide catastrophe. Scientists from a number of disciplines are interviewed including one scientist who digs dinosaurs for a living. Those who are as interested in dinosaurs as I am will find many interesting facts uncovered here that we normally do not hear about. I found particularly interesting the story told by dinosaur track ways found in North America that tell of these animals struggling to escape the rising Flood waters. These track ways yield quite a bit of useful information. In the DVD about dragons and dinosaurs, I found it interesting to see some familiar faces of dinosaurs among the depiction of dragons. I believe one was the velociraptor. The argument on this DVD makes it credible that people in history actually did see dinosaurs even though they called them dragons. In fact there is evidence that dinosaurs may have lived up until the Middle Ages. The name dinosaur was not coined until the 19th century. Some of the scenery used as a backdrop or for illustrative purposes is spectacular. The dinosaur animations are well done. This 4-DVD set gives glory to God as the creator who created different sorts of dinosaurs for his pleasure. Some of the design features in these animals are very unique. I want to watch this DVD set many times over. One of the most significant statements, I think, made in this presentation was by astronomer Jason Lisle who said that it was Christian thought that made modern science possible. I have seen this claim corroborated by others. For example, Rodney Stark makes this claim in his book The Victory of Reason: How Christianity Led to Freedom, Capitalism, and Western Success. Mary Midgley in her book Science as Salvation makes the same claim. This fact of history has been lost to us, I believe, in our public schools, and in education in general, because of the propagation of the false idea that there is a war between religion and science. This latter view favors the atheistic world view called evolutionism. As a science teacher in a public school, I will be using this as a resource to bring interesting science to my students. I can say also that all science rightly understood will help lead our young people to God. ( I don't include as science the atheistic philosophy of evolution which has absolutely no scientific bases and which has left our young people without meaning and without hope.) We read in Romans Chapter 1 that the visible things that can be understood will teach us of the invisible attributes of God including his eternal godhead. For sure our children need to know this great God given the perilous world that they live in. Our children need to know that they have value and that there is hope. Two other very valuable DVD packages from ICR that I would highly recommend are Made in His Image and Unlocking the Mysteries of Genesis. These also give glory to God and are full of very good and interesting science.

Reason: Ray Comfort starts by asking university students and one elderly gentleman if they are atheists. They say they are. Then he reasons with them by asking if a book could write itself and put itself together. Then he asks if our DNA could write itself and put itself together without an author. There is quite a lot of detail I am passing over here, but it's worth seeing the movie to see how Ray Comfort reasons with atheists and persuades them to reassess their positions. He also presents other aspects of God's creation for the students and elderly man to consider. By the end of the movie most if not all the atheists are willing to reassess their positions. One atheist prays with Ray to accept Jesus as his savior. Ray's approach is shown to be very effective and impressive. Ray Comfort's interviews are interspersed with stunning scenes of God's creation in nature. This too is a special part of the movie. history.title: Murder, She Wrote - The Complete Fourth Season
history.review_title: Lansbury does it again! Great season!
history.text: The radiant Angela Lansbury does a superb job again in this fourth season as she continues solving intriguing who-done-its during her exciting travels and in her quaint hometown of Cabot Cove. We follow our beloved and brilliant sleuth/mystery novelist as she unravels intriguing mysteries and always helps justice prevail again. From solving a murder during a glitzy Paris fashion show, to posing as a madam in a brothel shrouded in secrecy and death, to unraveling a grisly murder in a convent, Jessica always gets to the truth and ventures where others dare not go. If you like Murder She Wrote, this season is a guaranteed pleaser. I am happy to have this in my Murder, She Wrote collection!

history.title: Murder, She Wrote: The Complete Seventh Season
history.review_title: Another great season! Jessica is back to solve the mystery!
history.text: The incomparable Angela Lansbury returns again as Jessica Fletcher and viewers are sure to be pleased as our beloved sleuth from Cabot Cove unravels the clues and uncovers the truth behind twisted murder mysteries in this season of Murder She Wrote. It's always fun to "travel" with Jessica and try to solve the mystery with her, and like in previous seasons before it, Season 7 does not disappoint in the intrigue and fun category. I have always loved Murder She Wrote because it is just a pleasant show to watch. I can always relax and enjoy the show without ever having to worry about what cuss words I will hear, or what graphic/bloody images or nudity I will see. Each episode weaves a good mystery and Jessica Fletcher is a wonderful and likeable character. I think everyone could use a Jessica Fletcher somewhere in their lives. I believe it is truly sad that Angela Lansbury was never awarded for her work in this series, because she always played Jessica with so much sincerity and warmth. There were many episodes that I liked this season, but her performance in the episode "Thursday's Child" touched me. Spoiler alert! Jessica encounters a woman with whom her beloved husband Frank may have had a child with while he was away at war, and she has to learn if it is the truth or not. There were moments in the episode where Angela Lansbury didn't even say a word of dialogue and the look in her eyes made me almost cry. An emotional impact from just a mere look in her eyes and her deafening silence. That is the mark of a superior actor in this superior series.

history.title: Nomads [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A good scary flick from the 80s!
history.text: I love this product and I highly recommend it for anyone who craves a good supernatural movie. I liked it for its story about an attractive doctor (Lesley-Anne Down) who, after helping a dying ER patient (Pierce Brosnan), finds herself as an unwilling witness to his last memories of what happened before he died. Although not fast- paced like many thrillers, this movie has an almost "Twilight Zone" vibe to it, with a haunting, pulsating score that features fierce guitars by Ted Nugent and dazed, creeping imagery. The Blu-ray quality was excellent and I know you'll enjoy this movie. Watch it!

history.title: Dallas: Season 9

This has not happened with any of the other seasons I have purchased over the years. This was so frustrating, and is not becoming of an excellent show like Dallas. I sadly had to return it. I will purchase this season again hopefully soon.

history.title: Audrey Rose [DVD]
history.text: I first saw this film when it was on the Comet TV channel several months ago. I was already interested in it since I am an ardent fan of Anthony Hopkins. At first, I thought this was to be another horror film about frantic parents trying to deal with a disturbed/possessed child. The film features a disturbed child, but it is not by malevolent forces. Audrey Rose has been categorized as a horror film by several reviewers, but it is not a horror film. This is clearly a drama about reincarnation that is spiritual, thought provoking and sad. Marsha Mason and John Beck portray loving parents whose young daughter, Ivy, is experiencing moments of emotional trauma for no apparent reason. Enter Anthony Hopkins character , Elliot Hoover, who tries to convince Ivy's parents that their daughter whom they have raised and loved as their own, is in fact the reincarnation of his own daughter who died years ago. Ivy/Audrey Rose is suffering emotionally because she is supposedly reliving the last terrifying moments from her past life. The really sad part is that there are no winners in Audrey Rose, as Ivy's parents and Elliot Hoover must face the possibility of each losing their only child, as she is caught in a tug of war between them. Is Ivy really Audrey Rose or not is the question all three parents must answer. I loved this movie in how it was done, and how it effectively captured the haunting subject of reincarnation. I am glad I purchased this film, and if you are in the mood to see something a little different, I recommend this to you.

history.title: Marty
history.text: What a bunch of miserable, rotten people. I felt miserable myself after watching.

Perfect depiction of how the constant threat of going to hell, with any behavior outside the doctrine considered sinful, children become scared and paranoid that anything they say or do will send them to hell. Put that on top of freezing, starving, and enduring external threats, you have a remedy for driving children mad. Some of them could then follow with acting out because of the attention they're getting. These were extreme conditions under which they lived. I don't know what it is about this movie people don't get, being driven mad by radical doctrine and falling into a catatonic state accompanied with periodic terrors and hallucinations. It's so annoying when people stop watching after five minutes and they 1-star the movie for being overly dramatic... like hastily reviewing a movie they didn't even watch isn't overly dramatic?

SPOILER: No pay off at the end. We are simply a collection of our memories. Well, yeah, when we die. The end presumes we all at some time in our life stop making new memories and allow ourselves to be totally defined by our past. It's like our lives quit when the movie quits. Their ARE people who get squashed and never move on to grow, of course, and that is the dismal feeling I got from this uneventful and boring movie.

history.review_title: Dunkirk Battle was a series of events in the English Channel, not in Dunkirk!
history.text: Ignore the 1-star raters complaining about the story line. I almost didn't rent it because of that. There is no problem following the story. Music was appropriately grim and dark, much of it like an uneasy rumble. Gave an unsettled feeling like the men waiting on the beach would have had. Since the men on the beach were forced to wait, the movie is about a series of events in the English Channel. The different type of people and personnel that was involved, and events in which they were swept up. The Dunkirk Battle was not urban combat. The whole point is how troops were stranded on the beach, and the people in the English Channel who fought and made efforts to clear the way for their rescue.

history.title: Feasting on Asphalt - The Complete Second Season: The River Run
history.text: This series is the perfect confluence of Alton Brown's engaging foodie personality, motorcycling, and the open road. It's a smooth continuation of Season 1 and that's a good thing. Videography and style are pretty much the same. This season has 6 episodes: 1. A Strong Brown God 2. Fry Me A River 3. Soul Food Survivor 4. Take Me To The River 5. Mid-American Pie 6. Lutefisk Express Unlike Season 1, this season has no bonus episodes. Content is terrific; however, video quality is a B. It's 480i letterboxed widescreen, so resolution is a bit low once the frame expands to fill modern widescreen TVs. Actual picture resolution ends up being only 720x360. There also some noticeable black vignetting in the frame and a few pixels of junky picture content on all sides of the frame. Ebay is a great place to find this series--especially Season 2--at reasonable used prices.

history.title: Gulliver's Travels (Widescreen Special Edition)
history.review_title: Frame Content Deleted to Make an Artificial "Widescreen" Version
history.text: I should have read the reviews before I purchased this "Widescreen Special Edition". I incorrectly assumed that the movie was originally filmed in genuine widescreen and that the version I happened to see on TV years ago was cropped down to full screen 4:3. I thought I'd get the genuine widescreen version by purchasing this disk. In actuality, the movie was originally filmed in full screen 4:3 and to make this "Special Widescreen Edition", the remastering company cropped out--deleted--a portion of the frame to give the appearance of widescreen. Even this new "widescreen" version isn't a genuine widescreen but rather an odd letterboxed frame. On modern TVs, it'll likely project on the screen surrounded by black bars on all 4 sides rather than using up the available screen real estate (perhaps an aspect ratio flag isn't set properly on the DVD?). On my LG TV, I had to use the TV's "zoom" function to fill up the available screen area with the image. The actual frame size, once I took out the letterboxing, is 720x388 or 16:10...a weird aspect ratio somewhere between 4:3 full screen and modern 16:9 HDTV widescreen. In the attached frame captures, the picture on the left shows the original 4:3 frame content. The frame on the right shows the new "widescreen" frame content. You can see that a significant portion of the bottom of the frame is cropped out. In my opinion, rather than enhancing the film, removing frame content actually detracts from the film...literally. I recommend purchasing the original 4:3 version.

history.text: There are plenty of reviews for the film itself, so my review is limited to the Blu-ray upgrade. Bottom line: It's worth upgrading from DVD. The main improvement, of course, is the increased resolution. In addition, another significant upgrade is the reduced judder as compared to the DVD version. Overall size: 31.5 GB Overal bitrate: 37.6 Mbps Video specs: 1920x1080 progressive scan 16x9; Max bitrate 36 Mbps, 24 fps Highest audio quality: DTS MA Core, 2 channel (2 channel is the only audio available on the disk)

history.title: X-Files: The Complete Season 1 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Now Available in Widescreen. Amazing Quality Increase
history.text: Purchasing The X-Files on blu-ray is a no brainer. The quality increase is amazing and further lends to the motion picture feel of this weekly drama. Pros: - Amazing quality increase and much less judder over the DVD version. I'd estimate the increased resolution is 90% of that observed in modern 1080p video. That's pretty amazing considering it was shot 20 years ago. Additionally, the increased bitrate really smooths out motion and reduces motion blur. - Early seasons are now available in anamorphic widescreen. It's a genuine widescreen as well since the original was shot in widescreen and cropped down to full screen. What a difference over the old full screen version. Cons: - The blu-ray menus aren't as user friendly as I'd prefer. The two main menu colors--black and dark gray--make it difficult to determine what menu option is selected. MediaInfo reports the following video and audio specs. Average episode size: 10-12 GB Average overall bitrate: 34 Mbps Video: 1920x1080 progressive scan, 24 fps, 16x9 aspect ratio Best audio: DTS MA/Core, 5.1 channel surround, 48.0 KHz Watching the The X-Files on blu-ray is a completely new viewing experience for this series.

history.title: X-Files: The Complete Season 8 [Blu-ray]
history.text: This review is specifically about the "Black Crush" encoding problem in X Files Season 8 early production batches, and excellent Fox Customer care. While researching quality differences between the DVD and blu ray versions of X Files, I came across the website wwwdotxfilesvaultdotcom/features/Season-8-Black-Crush-Blu-ray-Problem/. It explains how early productions batches of Season 8 have an encoding problem that results in very dark "black crush" portions of the video. It offers comparison screen captures and a way to contact Fox Customer Care for replacement. I received replacement disks free of charge (including shipping both ways) in about 10 days and the new disks do not have the encoding problem. Kudos to Fox Customer Care for quick service. The disks are presented in the same amazing increased resolution and bitrate of previous seasons.

history.title: My Big Fat Greek Wedding 2 [DVD]
history.review_title: Not As Good As The First One. Odd Dialog Pace.
history.text: The movie had some funny parts, but I don't think it was on par with the original. - Plenty of jokes and funny parts. The writers tried to hearken back to key lines from the first movie (like "Why you want to leave me?") but some of the lines are delivered in an odd, unfunny manner. - Pretty much all the same cast. That was a nice carryover that welded the two movies together. - In a serious moment, one of the brothers--Angelo--comes out as homosexual. His family embraces his gay lover and welcomes him into the family. It was weirdly out of place and seemed to be a scene shoe-horned in to support the homosexual acceptance movement. - Dialog delivery timing was just...off...in many places. The pace of the dialog was just a bit weird which left the movie feeling choppy, and the choppiness interfered with the effectiveness of the movie's humor/jokes. - As in the first movie, this movie adheres to the "smart wife, stupid husband" storyline between Gus and Maria. - Part 2 is pretty much a smooth continuation of the first movie. The theme is largely the same, so the viewer isn't forced to adapt to a new world. That's a good thing. It's worth watching once, I suppose, but I don't think it has the attractiveness to garner repeat viewings like the first movie has.

history.title: Alone
history.review_title: A Couple Dozen F-Bombs Per Episode
history.text: I didn't like this season as much as previous seasons. It doesn't cover as much ground as previous seasons so it feels rushed and incomplete. There are no doctor visits (for regular on-camera health checkups) in this season, which added a lot of depth because we were able to see the medical side of survival. Also, participants don't develop their camps or survival methods as well as previous participants and the editing focuses more on the fighting and drama between participants rather than on development of survival techniques. Some of the participants have some pretty serious potty mouths with upwards of a couple dozen F-bombs per episode--"f***ing", "motherf***ing", "f*** me", "f***"...pretty much any way they can invent to use it. That gets old after awhile.

All reality TV shows suffer from a little bit of fake scripting. This one seems to have a little bit more than most. It's entertaining, but take the drama with a grain of salt. Pros: - Great scenery. - Likable characters who display a wide range of interests and skills. - There's a good variety of activities--hunting, fishing, repairing equipment, building, personal issues. - Gives some reasonable idea of what subsistence living is like in an isolated Alaskan town. Cons: - Nonstop, bleeped out profanity. - Fake sound effects. - Lots of high tempo drama music. - Some believability or credibility problems. For example, when Charlie complains about an intruder setting a trap right next to his line, the intruder's trap appears to have a lot of old wire wrapped around the trap and the bait, and the set pole end is cut but appears to be well weathered...conditions not likely on a "new" set. A lot of injected drama like "I'll fight to the death for my trapline." Really? You're going to commit murder for a trapline? In another incident, Courtney supposedly blows an ATV tire (complete with fake sound effects) 20 miles from home and says she would normally walk home but for her daughter. They supposedly spend the night in a little pine bough shelter, in the middle of winter, with a foot of snow on the ground. Twenty miles at approximately 2.5 miles per hour (the average pace of a healthy adult) over flat ground translates to 8 hours of walking. Seems questionable they would put themselves in such a dangerous situation without proper survival gear or tire repair kit. Plus, Courtney's husband conveniently shows up the next morning just as they decide to start walking the 20 miles home. What husband would just wait around the house while his wife and daughter were out in the middle of winter overnight in a known location?? It's just not believable. - The amount of pain inflicted on trapped animals should be unacceptable in this day and age, but all characters justify the pain as "a way of life" and "we respect the animal". None of them would consider purposely inflicting 12 to 24 hours of pain and suffering--and often freezing to death while hanging from a leg--on other animals like caribou or moose but don't think twice about doing it to trapped wolves, foxes, wolverines, martin, etc. Do a Google image search for "leg trap" if someone tries to claim it's "painless" or "comfortable." - The new couple, Chris and Jessi, are terrible actors. They don't behave or respond naturally in front of the camera, which is a telltale sign of scripted drama. In one incident, their sled dog races off and dumps a log out of the sled (on camera) she was pulling. Chris and Jessi go looking for her while lamenting how she'll die in the snow if they don't find her. Then they find the sled with the dog harness attached, upright, with a log in it. Manufactured fakery. - This season really plays up "the road" and "the intruders from the road". Despite the fact that the characters are all doing their resource gathering on public land--land that all U.S. citizens pay for and have a legal right to access--they feel entitled to it and they feel entitled to keep other U.S. citizens off of that public land. They even imply a willingness to use violence to protect "their" land. I get it. They've had near monopolistic use of public land and now they're upset that others are accessing it, too. That's understandable, but the implication that it's *their* land and that they'll use violence to protect it is immoral. It's entertaining, but I think the scripted drama is a little too much. When I watch it, I just keep in mind that it's "reality TV" and not a documentary.

history.title: Father Dowling Mysteries: Season 1
history.text: This whole series is really great. I watched them when they were on TV and this series holds up through time. The quality of the discs is great, they are made for small screen so you have to make them fit the size you want, but the stories, film and sound are great.

history.title: Centennial: The Complete Series
history.text: This was so good, I watched it when it came out years ago, and it has not lost any of it's interest. Very well made and history that I had never studied about Colorado.

history.title: A Family Man [DVD]
history.text: Great movie! A movie that needed to be made and I am so glad that Gerry Butler was the one to make it and star in it. All the cast can be very proud of a very good performance. Congrats to every one from G-Base to the actors and actresses. After watching this movie again, I want to add this comment. There are layers in this movie and I missed the one about the journey to integrity! Now looking back I think that is the main point.

history.title: Magnum P.I.: The Complete Series [DVD]
history.text: I love the series, the sound and pictures are fine, my problem is that Disc 2 of series 4 is unwatchable because it is scratched so bad even washing it will not make it play. That is as far as I have gotten with this series. There is no way to play all the discs within the period they are covered for exchange so that is a problem with buying a series in one box.

history.title: Agatha Christie's Poirot: Murder on the Orient Express
history.review_title: Best yet Murder on the Orient Express
history.text: I have seen most of the "Murder on the Orient Express" movies but my favorite one is David Suchet's version. Everything about this movie is first class. The lighting with the smokey look setting the time in the past, yet clear perfectly in focus for the actors in the spot light, that is when they are being questioned or finding clues. The feel of the cold with such magnificent scenery and the snow drift they are caught in. David does an excellent job of showing how tired Poirot is after having done a job where the guilty soldier kills himself, not being able to have his own compartment on the train the first night, when he is suddenly called back to England for another job with no rest. A real jewel of a movie!

history.title: LAST MAN STANDING: THE COMPLETE THIRD SEASON
history.text: This is an excellent series. We have watched them at least 4 times so far and we never get tired of the story lines or quips that are so funny. Great cast! Excellent writing with actually something important to say. Well done cast and writers.

history.title: Last Man Standing: The Complete Fourth Season
history.text: Excellent series, worth watching over and over. Very funny!

history.title: Last Man Standing Season 2
history.text: I enjoy this series, a family show with great values, very entertaining!
