history.review_title: Holy cow... what are people seeing in this movie?!
history.text: This review contains spoilers. To start off, I'm a huge Jack Lemmon fan. So far, have seen over half of the roughly 60 films he has been in. He was the reason why I watched this movie. That was mistake one. Jack Lemmon really isn't in this film that often. He is here and there and doesn't add much to the chemistry (who does in this movie?) and is wasted talent. The movie itself has a decent idea behind it, but really does wildly betray itself in the end. The end of the movie was intellectually unsatisfying. The guy who was hypnotized to love the witch finds out what happened, goes back to his bride. The bride has no longer has interest in him, so he goes back to the witch because he is in love with her... for really no reason whatsoever. Not a few scenes previous, he had nothing but distaste for her. The ending is so thoughtless and without craft, that is wrecks the film entirely. The movie isn't really funny, isn't really dramatic, isn't really anything, but boring and pandering. Ultimately, there is too much star power in this movie to be this bad a movie. It would appear that people give this movie a good review simply because it has Stewart and Novak in it. To me, that isn't enough of a reason to like a film that is a complete waste of time.

history.title: The Male Animal
history.text: This movie achieves much without much instigation. A professor wants to read a letter in a classroom. There isn't much more to it than that. Yet, events quickly unfold that make this event into so much more. The movie marvelously pits Collegiate Intellect against Collegiate Business, something which stands true today as much as it did when the movie was made. Then toss in the side-by-side story of this professor and his relationship with his wife. This film has intelligence, a bit of comedy and manages to deal with a significant issue of censorship in such a nonchalant, but very effective manner. The cast is great, the script solid. This film must be watched.

history.title: Anesthetize (DVD + Blu-ray)
history.text: To put it simply, this release is just remarkable. Filming, set list, editing, sound, it is all near perfect. What is incredible is the very beginning, during the Intro. It gives you the sense and anticipation of actually being at the show. For a minute of two of film, it does a great job of putting you there, not just in front of a television screen. The rise of Blu-ray has most certainly changed the atmosphere of watching a concert on television. You no longer feel as separated, instead you feel a lot more involved and the production of this disc does nothing to spoil that. The set list is great. The entire Fear of a Blank Planet suite performed together and then Nil Recurring with mostly Signify and In Abstenia songs mixed in. I remember seeing a concert with mostly this set list and Dark Matter itself was worth the price of admission. The only thing I missed was at my show, they did The Sky Moves Sideways, but truly, one can't expect everything. That was such a treat though. The sound is perfect and is nothing short of what Porcupine Tree fans expect to hear from a Steven Wilson project. Crystal clear and very dynamic. And of course, the band never misses a note. I purchased the Gray Special Edition through PT's site and am glad to have the CD's from this concert. If you like rock music, and have never heard of the band, this may not be a bad starting point to get the point across about how legendary this group is. The concert and Blu-ray production is nothing short of amazing and is a good representation as to the quality of this band.

Season One had potential. Much like Babylon 5, the first season seemed to be building the characters and the atmosphere. Season One wasn't blow your heads off great, but it felt as if it had something to tell down the line. The characters were interesting, the production pretty good. There was plenty of intrigue and questioning, you weren't too sure what would happen. Then they literally kill the series in the Season Finale, they would never recover. Problem with Season One is that it was exposition, with some suspense. It never developed into a must see thing. I gave it a chance, liked it enough (but didn't love it) to try Season 2, but the show devolved as many have said, from a much less impressive Season 2 to downright depressing Seasons 3 and apparently 4, 5. This show doesn't go anywhere. You won't get a Firefly feeling after watching the first season of this. Don't bother with this. Season One is pretty good, but it leads no where.

history.title: Anne of Green Gables: A New Beginning
history.review_title: The Batman and Robin of the Anne series
history.text: For a moment, ignore the Anne of Green Gables material. Forget the previous movies, the books, the Anne universe. If you do all this and watch this film ignoring all of that, you still end up with a pretty bad film. The plot suffers from fits and starts, from blunt plot devices to annoying just-so attitudes to what just happened? The film poses as Anne remembering the good ole days... ie stuff that doesn't really happen in the books. It's Anne of Green Gables meets Oliver Twist and its a mess. The acting is fine, but the plot and scenes are tried and sometimes nonsensical making you scratch your head.

history.title: Get All You Deserve [Blu-ray]
history.text: Simply put, this is just awesome. Typical Steve Wilson form. I dare say it rivals the PT Blu-Ray release. The music, video, style, form, presentation, set list. It is just as good as it gets! Wilson just keeps pushing his boundaries and developing evolving sounds and themes. What, you haven't bought it yet?! Just give them your money!

It's fun, it has everyone back for a final romp. My problem is that the key to Veronica Mars were the significant story arcs that last an entire season, but in no way did the plots move along slowly. The creator and writers continued giving out info and hints and all sorts of swerves all season long, making the seasonal arc intense and enjoyable. The movie? The venue of a motion picture doesn't allow for this, it is simply too short, so while an enjoyable ride, I felt almost cheated getting the resolution to the story so "quickly". The film itself looks great. I would have liked it better if the film centered more around something new to give us a feel where the show would have gone with the FBI angle. But you have to take what you get and what we got was pretty much the best that could be done with Veronica Mars being inserted into a motion picture length story.

history.title: Hand.cannot.erase
history.text: Steven Wilson has released his latest album with his jazz buds. The effort is called Hand Cannot Erase. The premise of the album is the story of a woman that died in an apartment but wasn't noticed for three years. The tale notes that while she died alone, she was a child, she was a mother, an aunt, she had a life. She wasn't always forgotten. Steven Wilson has made a career with sad depressing lyrics. Sometimes he outdoes himself. The last album had The Raven That Refused to Sing, an old man who is near death, desperate to hear the singing voice of his long lost sister of whom he lost when they were still kids. This album gives us Happy Returns, which, while seemingly full of hyperbole, is more depressing than Stop Swimming, Octane Twisted, and the Raven That Refused to Sing combined. It is that powerful. Often, Wilson creates stories with his songs, but Hand Cannot Erase goes beyond a story. It is a reality that has occurred for some, a reality that may occur to you (the listener). I have always enjoyed his music, but this is his first album that makes you think about your own life. The steps within it, the steps to come. The steps of other lives. Where we put the value. I've always pondered the day in - day out routine of life, about how much of life is wasted waiting for later. And this is all before we talk about the actual music, which is finely crafted, played by grossly awesome musicians. The lyrics themselves are haunting, story telling, entrapping. The vocal harmonies are nothing less than what one comes to expect in a Steven Wilson album. Wilson engineered the album, so it sounds as perfect as it possibly can. This album will be the best album in 2015 not to make it above the radar, being pushed aside by shallow music critics that put forth less thought worthy material as the prized material.

history.title: Live in Colombia [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Pretty a must have for an APP fan
history.text: Short story first. The only disappointment is that the set list follows along almost exactly with Livespan, with the only significant difference being Silence and I. Otherwise, great! Long story. The Region 0 Blu-ray, as noted by everyone else is playable on US players, no issue at all. The video quality is very good, though zooms of Parsons seem a little grainy. The audio quality is great. I was expecting a larger presence of the orchestra to add onto songs, however, the orchestra is generally used in the original role as on the albums, so people expecting a larger presence will be a little disappointed. However, when kept in context that the orchestra sections in the songs are being played by a live orchestra, that is very cool! The set list, while repetitive from the last album, is great and covers the Alan Parsons Project very well. I wish they'd get some material from Try Anything Once (Jigue or Re-Jigue would have been perfect!) or On Air / Time Machine into these shows. Those albums have some great tracks. The vocal harmonies, as with Livespan are incredible. The musicians play the songs very well. The leading vocals are great, with Greene, Olloson, and Cooper each adding a different tone for the songs they sing. For the price, if you are a fan, getting this is a no brainer.

history.text: I highly recommend this film, however the buyer needs to be aware that it is in PAL format, and I had to spend more than the movie cost me to have it transferred into a viewable format. Was it worth it? Yes! It really was.

history.title: Looper
history.text: I would recommend this to anyone who likes action, without high sophistication. I was an unusual story and certainly not boring.

history.title: GPLUSPKS PT# 1048073 Earloop Mask Ultrasoft Pink 50/Bx Manufactured by Henry Schein
history.text: I like everything about this product. It is the BEST of many I have ordered. Fits my face well and is cooler, yet more substantial, than others I have tried. The shipping was a bit slow, but the quality of the masks is so good, I am giving five stars anyway.

history.title: How I Live Now
history.review_title: At best this can be said to be puerile
history.text: At best this can be said to be puerile. There is little more to be said. It was probably intended for a teenage audience. I wouldn't recommend this unless perhaps to teenagers living in a fantasy world. Weak story, poorly acted, unenjoyable.

history.title: Fifty Shades of Grey [Blu-ray]
history.text: This is one of the worst films I've ever seen. It is excruciatingly boring. I kept watching because I thought that somehow, some way or other, there must be a point, but there wasn't. I wouldn't recommend this film to anyone and certainly not to anyone over twenty. Recommendation: Don't waste your money or time on this poorly written film.

history.title: Sicario [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD]
history.text: This film was a terrible letdown. Incredibly boring. The story is dull and pointless. The female lead, Emily Blunt, is not an actress and ruined the film. I bought it because it had a reasonably high rating, people said it was great, however, it is not. Please save your money. I hope to never see another film with Emily Blunt.

history.title: Alfred Hitchcock: 4 Tales of the Macabre - Secret Agent / The Lady Vanishes / The Man Who Knew Too Much / Sabotage [DVD]

history.text: very boring. Doesn't even rate an upper case V. Poor quality. Save your money.

history.text: This is okay, but I believe it is intended for a young audience...like children. I'll stick with David Attenborough.

history.review_title: If you like lemurs and sifaka, this is for you. Excellent presentation.
history.text: Excellent DVD!

history.title: Planet of the Apes [Blu-ray]
history.text: Very poor acting! Very dull. I watched it hoping to get some background for Rise, Dawn and War, but it was so poorly done, and it wasn't worth a nickel. Start with the trilogy, forget the silly original, it isn't needed.

history.title: All That Heaven Allows (Blu-ray + DVD)
history.text: This review is for the Criterion Blu-ray. I'm so disappointed. After reading a "professional" review of the Blu-ray version on another website, I was excited. This is one of my favorite movies, and the reviewer spoke of the brilliant colors and how they pop. I already owned the Criterion DVD, and after reading the review of how much better the Blu-ray was, I couldn't wait to see it. But when I received it and watched it, I was so disappointed. I can't tell any difference from the DVD version. I was hoping that the very grainy picture would be clearer, but it is ever so grainy still. Ugh! The facial tones are yellowish, not any different from the DVD. Has anyone else compared the two versions? What do you think? I wish I had my money back. If you want to see a huge difference and wonderfully brilliant upgrade from the DVD to the Blu-ray version, watch and enjoy "How the West Was Won." Incredible and mesmerizing.

history.title: Remember the Day
history.text: The 20th Century Fox Cinema Archives has produced several wonderful films, otherwise unobtainable on home video. This is a great film, very nostalgic and sentimental, but a disappointing transfer from the folks at 20th Century. The picture is very dark, even in the outdoor daytime scenes, which look as though they were filmed as day-for-night. Many scratches and dust specks are visible, as well as a constant graininess. At the 5:34 mark, there is a skip in the film, obliterating the third line of "(Back Home Again in) Indiana." The movie is watchable, however, a cut above the many public domain films available on home video, and the audio is clear. Given the production company of this transfer, I had higher expectations; my low rating is for the transfer, not the film itself.

history.title: Home Before Dark [Remaster]
history.text: Warner Archives did a great transfer of this movie---not a restoration, but the audio and video are more than adequate to enjoy the movie. But personally, I didn't enjoy this movie as much as I thought I would. Given the premise of a mental patient returning home after a year in a hospital to the very situation that caused her breakdown, and having Jean Simmons as that patient (she's a terrific actress), and with a great supporting cast (including Rhonda Fleming and Efrem Zimbalist, Jr.), I was expecting much more. I love film noir, suspense and gothic tales, but this movie didn't register as great in any of those three sub-genres. The movie was flat and dull with a lot of talk ... until Charlotte's entrance at the Boston restaurant decked out as her step-sister. That was the scene that finally drew me into the movie ... an hour and 45 minutes into it! I'm surprised I stuck it out that long. This could have been a great movie, but maybe the director (Mervyn LeRoy) had other things on his mind. As I watched "Home Before Dark," I couldn't help but think about one of the greatest movies of all time, "Now, Voyager" as both leads are women named Charlotte who live in or near Boston and have been in psychiatric care. In fact, a trivia item on IMDB for this movie says that the soundtrack of Voyager was used for this movie. Maybe Warners was trying to rekindle the greatness of "Now Voyager." ... They didn't.

history.title: The Last Laugh
history.text: The restored German version of The Last Laugh by Kino is excellent. From the crystal clear raindrops near the first of the film to the end, this is one of the best restorations of a silent film I've ever seen. The score is exquisite, and, unique for a silent, there are no title cards to read. Speakers of any language can easily follow the simple story of an aging bellhop who is demoted to washroom attendant when the hotel employing him deems him too old for his job. The camera angles and viewpoints---especially a moving shot from a glass elevator---are ahead of their time and make this story very entertaining. The movie also includes great special effects for the 1920s----or any decade.

history.title: Knock on Wood
history.text: I have several DVDs manufactured by Olive Films, and most of the transfers are excellent. However, Knock on Wood is not a great transfer. The best way to describe the picture is that it looks like a movie that was filmed in 3D. It looks like two pictures that are not aligned, slightly off so that it looks blurred, definitely far from a sharp image. The audio is great, and the story is as enjoyable as any other Danny Kaye film.

history.title: The Lady With a Lamp
history.review_title: Wonderful Transfer of a Wonderful Film
history.text: Nostalgia Family has given us another excellent transfer of a wonderful classic film. The video and audio are in great shape! The movie itself is recommended for those who love the classic biopics.

history.title: The Thirteenth Guest aka Lady Beware
history.review_title: Comparison of Alpha and Nostalgia Family
history.text: I have seen both the Alpha Video transfer and the Nostalgia Family transfer. The Alpha Video version was blurry, washed out and barely watchable; the Nostalgia Family, even though not restored, is a much better version in both audio and video quality

history.title: UPA: The Jolly Frolics Collection
history.text: The technical quality of the UPA Jolly Frolics Collection of cartoons is great, although I don't see the vibrant colors of the Disney or Looney Tunes of the period. This is mostly due to a different style of animation, probably, but these don't seem to be fully restored. A few scenes here and there within the cartoons are blurred---very few, though. And despite the buildup of these UPA cartoons and their animators in the introduction by Leonard Maltin, the plotlines and characters are just ho-hum for the most part. The artwork is interesting simply because it is different from the major studios' artwork at the time, and I can certainly see the influence this style had on Jay Ward and the later Rocky & Bullwinkle animators. Only two of these cartoons really stood out to me, The Tell-Tale Heart (which is now on the National Film Registry) and Madeline, which is based on the classic children's book. I love classic short cartoons, but was overall disappointed with these from UPA.

history.title: Smith!
history.text: I ordered this Disney DVD to complete my Disney collection through the 60s. The movie itself is lackluster, poorly acted, overlong and downright boring, even though it includes a murder trial. The only enjoyment I had was in listening to the young actor Christopher Shea's voice. He was the original voice of Linus in the Peanuts TV specials, and if I closed my eyes, I could imagine Linus saying those lines.

history.title: Snows of Kilimanjaro, The
history.text: Be sure to get the 20th Century Fox version, and not some third generation reprint (this film has fallen into the public domain). When you see the Technicolor cinematography, you'll be glad you spent a little more for some of the most beautiful colors to grace the silver screen. You can easily see why it was nominated for Best Color Cinematography. The story itself sways greatly from the Hemingway short story (a lot more story had to be fabricated to reach the length of a feature film) and for a movie set in Africa and Spain, with scenes of safaris, bullfights and civil war, it suffocates in too much talk too much of the time.

targets.title: Vivien Leigh Hollywood Classics (Dark Journey / Fire Over England / Sidewalks of London / Storm in a Teacup) [DVD]
Life With Father - William Powell, Irene Dunne - 1947

history.title: The Age Of Adaline [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD]
history.review_title: A beautiful, memorable, and enjoyable movie!
history.text: A beautiful story-line and visuals. This is a wonderfully made movie that kept my attention the entire time, I loved Blake Lively in this role. She was the epitome of grace and elegance. It is something that many would deem a gift, to never age, to never grow old in looks or body, but through amazing story telling, Adaline shows us that this "gift" is really a curse. I won't spoil the ending, but I absolutely loved it! There were parts in the movie that literally brought me to tears, or I was able to feel Adaline's joy or sorrow. This is an amazing movie, and will definitely remain a favorite!

history.title: The Jungle Book
history.review_title: Visually beautiful, but not much else...
history.text: Visually it is a beautiful movie. The CGI and graphics are very well done, but I did not enjoy the movie. I was surprised at the level of violence that the child faced, and some of the violent interactions between the animals, it seemed a little extreme for a PG movie. Obviously there is no comparison to the Disney animated version, the characters are similar, and they even tried to push in some of that old Disney music from the original movie, but the charm and enthusiasm were missing. The only part of the movie that I found interesting involved Scarlet Johansson's voice-over as the snake, whatever they did to modify her voice was amazing! Listening to her voice was hypnotizing! Overall, I thought this movie was a little too violent at times, annoying in others, and boring for the remainder. Sadly not a movie I have any interest in seeing again.

history.title: Masterpiece: Poldark
history.text: Beautifully made, well acted, and addictive to watch. I never read the books, so I knew nothing about the Poldark drama beyond what was written on the back of the DVD box. I was hooked the first episode! The scenery locations are stunning, as are the costumes and the buildings used. The acting is amazing, and the character of Poldark just draws you in. You come to truly care for him, his loved ones, and those less fortunate he tries to help and care for. You come to see that he is truly a good man, with a beautiful heart. I loved watching Demelza transformation from a "kitchen wench" to a strong beautiful lady. Ross and Demelza are so wondefully matched. I eagerly look forward to Season 2.

history.title: Pride + Prejudice + Zombies [Blu-ray]
history.text: I wasn't sure I would like this movie, but I decided to give it a try. I love Pride and Prejudice, I enjoy watching zombies (thanks to The Walking Dead) so I figured, why not watch something that combines the two. I was pleasantly surprised to find that after 30 or so minutes into the movie I was actually looking forward to seeing how this would all end. I have to say I LOVED the scene where Darcy proposes to Elizabeth, that was absolutely hilarious...I rewound that scene a few times. While I was originally skeptical of what I thought would be a cheesy horror, tongue in cheek movie, was really very entertaining! I did not care for the little clip after the credits, I thought that was unnecessary, I like my movies all tidily wrapped up, but overall I actually have the desire to watch this crazy movie again!

history.title: Legend of the Seeker: Season 2
history.text: One of the best TV shows I have seen in years. I have missed it for a long time since it was taken off the air. I still hope that someday they decide to make a movie, but won't hold my breath. The scenery and costumes are gorgeous, and the actors/actress are well casted into their roles. The story line is excellent, and well-acted. I watch it and re-watch it a couple of times a year, and it never gets old. I actually find or catch things that I may have missed prior, little nuances or quips that were over looked. People get all bent out of the shape that it doesn’t follow the books, I can care less about that because I only read the first book, and didn’t enjoy it. The TV show clearly says “based on”, nowhere does it say “an actual representation of the books.” So people can get off their pedestals and enjoy the show for what it is, and not what they want it to be. Overall, I love the TV show, and can’t recommend it enough.

I saw the movie on 4/21 for a school field trip. I really enjoyed the movie until the last 10 or so minutes of it. Prior to that everything was beautifully filmed and tastefully shot. For almost the entire movie the "predator/prey" sections were shown in such a way that the children were not exposed to any dramatic death scenes or graphic scenes of animals trying to kill and eat other animals. Even the hawk trying to catch the baby monkeys, and subsequently catching one of them only showed a one second clip of a faraway hawk with a monkey in its claws. All of this began to change when the Snow Leopard scenes began to progress. Prior to this any "predator/prey" scenes were only a second or two, and shot in such a way that we never saw the actual kill, just the limp prey’s body after the fact. Spoilers.... First we see the mother Snow Leopard injuring her paw on sharp rocks beneath the snow, there is some blood on the snow. Things become more dire as time progresses and she is unable to catch any prey to feed her 2 babies. The last 10 minutes of the film show the mother Snow Leopard desperate to catch anything as she and her babies are starving. She decides to attack a baby yak and the movie shows her clinging to the baby’s neck trying to drag/kill it. The mother yak shows up and begins to head-butt, stomp on, and gore the Leopard with her horns. This dragged out "predator/prey" scene is in my opinion unnecessary, and way too graphic. Whereas the prior scenes were only a second or two, this one went on for at least a minute, minute and a half. Why should any child have to see a Leopard trying to tear the throat out of a baby yak, or see that same Leopard brutalized by a yak. You can hear the sounds of the mother yak stomping on, head-butting, and goring the Leopard. The Leopard eventually releases the baby, and then we are left with the mother yak comforting her baby, and a mother Leopard that will suffer and die from her injuries. I know this is what happens in nature, however it’s not something that should have been shown in such a dragged out way. The mother Leopard is clearly going to die from her injuries, and her babies left without a provider or protector. This whole tragic ending just ruined the film. Disney of course tries to make light of it by talking about the circle of life, and showing birds jumping up and down in sun, and revealing a brand new baby panda, but the whole thing is ruined by seeing this mother’s death. According to the producer the 2 Leopard babies are "safe" but I am sure if they said anything otherwise the film would have been boycotted. I would never recommend this movie, nor ever consider watching it again.

history.title: Beauty And The Beast
history.text: I was really looking forward to this movie. Beauty and the Beast was one of my favorite Disney movies growing up, so I was excited to see the update! Unfortunately, I was deeply disappointed. The actors were lackluster, and the music/songs were not as good as the original. The "beast" was not very beastly nor convincing. Belle was boring, and just lacking charm. The CGI was alright, I didn't appreciate nor care for the added songs, it just seemed like they had to add something to make the movie longer. The back story of Belle's mother, and the Beast's "horrible" childhood were unnecessary and just seemed goofy. There was no point to either one of them, and it felt like another attempt to extend and further drag out the movie. There were a few scenes that I thought were lovely, but not enough to ever make me want to see this movie again. A very boring, and disappointing remake!

history.title: Passengers [Blu-ray]
history.text: I did not like the movie when I first saw it, but after watching it, it stuck with me. I have watched it a few times since, and really enjoy it! The graphics are amazing, and the actors are really good! The only thing that bugs me is the ending. I would have liked to have seen something that shows their life together, the years they had together. Maybe a few clips showing the progression of time...did they have kids? How did they die? How long did they live? What did they do together? It just seems to end abruptly, and we are left hanging with questions about their future.

Saw it at the show 12/21, and I absolutely loved it. I am eagerly looking forward to seeing it again, and will definitely purchase it when it comes out. I loved what they have done with the characters thus far, I felt like everything was handled appropriately regarding Luke's character, and Leia's. Kylo Ren and Rey had an amazing story line, and I am eagerly looking forward to the 9th episode. Compared to George Lucas, these new directors and story writers far exceed all expectations.

history.title: Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit (Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD)
history.review_title: Full of cliches, wooden acting, bad script
history.text: An embarrassment with the world's most vapid villain ever. Chris Pine saves this movie from being the total embarrassment it is. It's as if the Hollywood fools talked among themselves and said "we need a good fight scene here" - hey, don't tell me about what makes sense! I don't care that a few hours later you'll hear that the entire scene was completely unnecessary, begging the question why you'd go through with the charade if that's the case. Movie needs tension here so give it to me!" You'll know it when you see it and shake your head. Knightly is abysmally frigid as the girlfriend and there is ZERO chemistry. Jack Ryan PhD. is so dumb, as written, that he doesn't know how to dispense of a movie ticket properly (such as once he's already in the theatre). Cosner is not convincing as the veteran agent. And his character is so poorly written that he doesn't bother explaining how his crack team could have whiffed detecting the issue Jack Ryan has upon his arrival in Russia to start the main area in the film. And poor Kenneth Branagh. So brilliant that he falls for the most obvious and glaring lame gags that have been in movies for decades. HIs character in summation "scowl, look angry, say something menacing." And the pitiful plot. Suddenly the bait shows up. It's an insult how it happens. Nothing in the dialogue suggests it and how it's known to everyone but our protagonist is mind numbing. Again, the Hollywood geniuses said "fit plot mechanism in here to drive the movie in this direction which you've all seen before." The truth is this movie might be deserving of one star because of the dialogue but at least Pine makes it semi-watchable, which it is until the middle. I wasn't expecting this bad. But it's bad.

history.review_title: Good style but with B-movie editing, script and gaping plot holes
history.text: Good style over substance that devolves into shlock. It starts off promising and the two lead actors are excellent and make this film watchable, even during it's cringeworthy moments. Any comparison to Bladerunner is purely superficial with the 80s type soundtrack and dark, bleak visuals. While the movie begins with some promise about an experiment gone wrong, it's apparent rather early that the story is told in disjointed fashion and the science quickly devolves into total shlock scifi cliche. There is a connection between the doctor's sick daughter and his new assistant but the connection is not made clear, neither scientifically nor emotionally. "Cool concepts" are introduced that make you think that there is more going on, which there is, including the presence of your typical cardboard villain. There are many gaping plot holes and things that make you go "huh?" (such as why greater care wouldn't have been taken with machines... which is answered by the fact that the plot couldn't have moved in the direction it did if the script made too much sense.) Unfortunately the middle and ending are predictable and rather silly. Caity Lotz does a phenomenal job to pull off a believable android and Toby Stephens does a great job as the lead actor. But the script makes him a 2 dimensional character and all of the characters in this film are pure cardboard. There is no reason to care about them. What made Bladerunner such a great film is where this one fails by a very large margin. Someone could have helped with the choppy editing and a second and third pair of eyes to create a more plausible script with a meaningful message rather than what we've all seen before numerous times just done with a little more visual style. Watchable but if you're expecting Bladerunner or even decent scifi, you'll probably be disappointed.

history.title: The Island
history.review_title: Typical Michael Bay, sucks the intelligence out, explosions in
history.text: Michael Bay has a talent for producing lots of explosions and stripping films of intelligence, realism and emotion - ruining a good tale with terrible dialogue. It's watchable but there are so many awkward moments that the film just becomes a tiresome bore and exercise in frustration to watch. Do not believe the ratings. They grossly overestimate the intelligence of this film. McGregor lives in a facility along with all the others who are told that there is contamination above and that eventually they are being trained to go to "The Island" to enjoy life on the outside. Eventually he and others become a little curious why obvious questions aren't answered - and so will you as a viewer, finding the entire artificial existence implausible and unfortunately not so well thought through. Security is remarkably lax for such an important facility. While there he meets Johansson, another member of the white clad population. Eventually a situation arises and things change. Bean is excellent in his role as the doctor, a seasoned actor. Hounsou is wasted and sounds like he's reading his lines off a prompter. Embarrassing. I won't say his role because it will ruin the film. Buscemi is an out of place supervisor whose role is to help fuel the curiosity of McGregor even though his entire existence and what he has to arouse curiosity is so bizarrely out of place and is illogical. Throughout the movie you'll be groaning at being engrossed to then hearing some really dumb or awkward words come out of a character's mouth, including conspicuous product placement. Hello Heineken (among others.) I'd give this film a 2.5 solely for the visuals and having an incredible but wasted cast of actors who are the only reason this drivel is even watchable. Disappointing because in the hands of the right director, this would have been an intelligent film. Instead it's a very long chase with a bunch of explosions, car chases, etc. and is completely forgettable. High production value, very low scale of intellect. Any comparisons to Bladerunner, Dark City, Gattaca or even the Matrix (with it's ridiculous illogical ending about "guns") is absurd. This is a watchable, cable rerun on a lazy Saturday afternoon too keep yourself momentarily entertained.

history.title: Non-Stop
history.text: This is an amazing film - a script that continues to get more laughable, less intelligent and more implausible as it plods along. The only thing more amazing is how many people rated this film 4 stars. If you've been in an airport and on a flight before, it's even more insulting to the intelligence. Don't say you weren't warned. Liam Neeson plays the same role and character he starred in for the past 5 films. He's very good at that role but the script is horrendous. A situation arises on the plane and none of it is plausible. A who done it situation arises and the perp is so amazingly adept that stuff just happens as if it as magic. Every possible cliche imaginable is pulled out, every red herring and the ensuing conflict continues to get stupider and more farfetched as the situation arises. I've seen many bad movies but this one is as bad as represented. You'll probably stick with it because Neesom is a good actor and you'll probably want to just figure out who done it to end your curiosity. And when all plays itself out, you'll be rolling your eyes and laughing at the film. None of it adds up, only in a Hollywood boardroom. Don't say you weren't warned.

history.title: The Recruit
history.review_title: Terrible script ruins a great cast
history.text: Don't be fooled by the very high rating of this film. It's terrible. It starts out with a decent premise. Despite being awkwardly constructed and very difficult to believe, it's on the edge of suspension of belief. But soon after you're given the premise for the movie to kick into the next gear, the script shifts into serious B movie mode. Without giving away important parts of the movie, there is a scene where a character knows he's being followed. He could easily kill the follower. Oddly the character opts to just startle the follower and move on. The only explanation for this has to be that the move had to move in a certain direction. There are also such awkward moments to construct the plot moving forward that it's just laughable. Pacino does his usual superman cool performance, nothing special, as the star is Colin Ferrel. And while his acting is decent, he's really left with stilted moments because the script is so darn awkward. This is a B movie at best. Fine for a cable view on a lazy afternoon but don't expect anything near satisfaction based upon the star rating.

history.review_title: Frustrating example of Hong Kong Style and Form without any substance
history.text: This movie is frustrating. The look, feel and acting all have an attractive style. There is a chemistry between the protagonists. There is lots of mood, good sets. But everything else unfortunately reeks of amateurish B grade film making - at best. This movie is defined cliche, nothing you haven't seen before in poor, low budget, poorly written movies. My guess is that all the good reviews come from fans who don't care too much because they just like the style and "cool" the actors ooze, including when they walk into ridiculous odds and come out victorious or knowing that certain death probably awaits them. It's sad that this film delves into looking and feeling silly. Everything in this film is about "honor" yet none of it makes sense. Nobody is honorable but there is some type of contradictory code between hit men that we are supposed to admire. And they aren't really bad guys, just ordinary folks like you and me. Instead of making pizza or delivering mail, they kill people. Can't fault them for that, right? It's just a job. For all the "crack" shooting you see done by people who can't miss, it's amazing how often they do. I'm not sure if it's intentional but it's almost laughable how actors get shot, get hurt, pick themselves up off the pavement and carry on with their mission because this is what must happen in the movie. A man can't see faces clearly but he sure can shoot the lights out of a moving bicycle at 50 yards away. The longer the movie rolls, the more it looks like a set on a stage. If you watch this movie to the end, all I can say is that "if the jacket fit you can't acquit." Unless you're a fan, this is just a lot of flash with a predictable plot that has no real purpose other than move the film to different sets for lots of gunplay. Waste of an opportunity.

history.title: Cold Eyes (2013) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Another good, well acted, Korean crime drama
history.text: Like all Korean movies, the acting is very good and the dialogue is important to the film. While the film was predictable (for me) and lacks back story or details of the intricate plot you'd expect, it's still an entertaining watch. I wouldn't rank it near truly great films like the Vengeance trilogy. This is more like a good slightly bubble gum crime film. I think that the beginning is fun and part of what keeps you in the film. The premise is a young rookie police investigator with fantastic ability to recall people, places and things she observes on the job becomes acclimated with the difficulties on the job. Her first mission is to help the team stop a crime group that has already pulled off one extremely well planned heist.

history.title: CHOSEN - SEASON 01
history.review_title: Has early promise but becomes pointless and repetitive quickly
history.text: On the bright side - the lead does the best he can with the script. I'll give him that. On the dark side - what on earth is this? Basically it sucks you in with the "who is behind the crazy turn of events and why are they doing this?" After the first 2-3 20 minute episodes you begin to stop caring because the script becomes ridiculous and feels like an attempt to prolong the show and that most won't care about sloppy writing, cardboard cliches and artificial dialogue that only makes sense to move a plot along. You're best off just finding a spoiler to find out the why and getting over watching this silliness to the end. In short, Milo finds a box with a gun and a photo at his door. Through a strange turn of events, he discovers that he's supposed to kill this man he's never met and doesn't know. Over the course of time you realize there are others in this "game." A morality play is introduced and doesn't make much sense and it's like Saw all over again. Put people in a terrible situation and chances are most will do whatever it takes to survive. Got it. Seen it before. And every situation the characters say the same thing - same lines, different victim. And in each situation these idiots never learn from their previous experiences. So.... why bother with any of this? Saw didn't really make much sense either except become an exercise in torture porn, which much of this series seems to be. It's unfortunate because this series seems like it could have been something more than just "hey, this is a cool idea we've seen before so let's just roll with it and kind of connect the episodes." The actors around Ventimiglia vary from OK to pretty weak and it's probably because the script just doesn't allow for anything remotely realistic. It also requires you to buy into the premise that somehow these characters live in a vacuum and the rest of the world just allows it to go on.

history.review_title: Rehashed, poorly cast, cash in on Bourne's name for one last score
history.text: Greengrass called Damon and asked him if he'd like to score one last huge paycheck. Since Renner wasn't successful in the attempt to continue milking this franchise and the success of the first three films with "The Bourne Legacy", something had to be done to milk it just one, last time. Let's get in some big names to replace the usuals like Tommy Lee Jones and hot name newcomer, Alicia Vikander. Script, writing - doesn't matter. Just do something that relates to Snowden since all the kids love that kind of anti-establishment, government is bad and invading our privacy stuff. This film is a confirmation that the Bourne series is dead. Lazy writing, casting, research, acting and a gratuitous amount of shaky cam - it's all here. Story. You've seen it before. But we thought that Bourne had regained his memory. OK, he's still struggling with that one. And the man with his special set of skills can only resort to being paid menial amounts of money in bare knuckles boxing, living like a vagrant.At the same time Nicky Parsons is working on something we can't really decipher which involves her walking into some unidentified place, hacking into top security that no one else could prior access (because this film needs a McGuffin to chase) and the government is able to somehow plant a super virus onto her USB drive which she store files which would dictate the location of the drive the next time a computer tries to access it... even if it is in Iceland, unconnected to the Internet (I didn't see a connection) and opened by someone who is supposed to be a computer genius. This type of lazy, confusing story is evident everywhere. Bourne used to have to act smart and "doesn't do random", is carefully planned and doesn't make mistakes. Yet here he not only does random but he walks right into a US customs area to waltz into the country. We're worried about some Snowdenesque plot and todays computers can't even perform a simple facial recognition test? And America's most wanted isn't even up on border security? Unfortunately the laziness is abound everywhere and things just work because, well... they have to in order to move the plot forward. These inconsistencies with Bourne notwithstanding (still searching for the past, milk it, milk it...), the casting was terrible. Alicia Vikander is a capable actress but couldn't be more miscast. Perhaps it's also the directing. She has an absolutely invisible, tepid presence. Not for a minute does she convince anyone that she has any true skills other than touch typing commands into a computer that would embarrass anyone who works in IT. And her struggle to maintain something resembling an American accent is painful. Tommy Lee Jones looks like he's about 3 decades past retirement and the camera pans in and does close ups just to make 100% sure you didn't miss how ancient he looks and how miscast he is for the part. Was told "just do Tommy Lee, big dog, bark out orders and then lament that you knew Bourne was coming for you all along." VIncent Cassel - another great actor - is totally wasted. He's relegated to angry hit man who is part of the film's action time which goes on far too long for its running and enough to bore you silly. He does very little in this film other than play 'the asset" which is code for "agent to take out Bourne but will fail in some spectacular way." Add in copious doses of "shaky cam in dark" and you'll get motion sickness along with an inability to digest what it is you think you just saw. Which leaves us with our main character. Like Craig in Spectre, Damon looks terribly bored in this role. He's lifeless, humorless and driven by something we don't really know. Oh yes, there is a minor plot twist that might explain his motivation but it doesn't do so convincingly and in terribly confusing fashion. Same thing you've seen before (must... remember.... flash...) yet out of place considering how far Bourne had progressed in the last film. While I have seen worse, this is a total retread, same story, bored characters, grim and totally humorless dialogue, unbelievable characters, mail it in for the money script and performances. I doubt anyone wanted to do the film but it was easy money and guaranteed profit for just on more time at the box office. Watchable but not enjoyable at all.

history.title: Moss Two-Disc Special Edition (or Iggi)
history.review_title: Chilling, suspenseful and difficult to turn away for the entire duration. Great film.
history.text: Another unique, fantastic Korean thriller. This is a very long, creepy and sinister film - about 2 and a half hours. But it is never boring. And it is worth the payoff. The plot - a strange man who has repented from his sins seems to attract the village locals who fund him for his teachings. A police officer is influenced by a local priest who is jealous that all his donations are going to this strange man. But after a strange twist, the police officer is convinced that the strange man is the genuine article he seems to be. But after the man passes away under mysterious circumstances, his loser son is notified about the man's death. And while attending to his father's affairs, he can't help but notice that the village elders can't wait to try to push him out and back to the city as quickly as possible. But the son decides to stay on and continues to discover the strange workings of the town and his father's past... Riveting. Great acting. Very tense. Not a horror film but certainly chilling in every way, including the human interest side. They don't make them like this in Hollywood.

history.title: El Muerto (The Dead One)
history.text: El Muerto (The Mexican Crow) is based on the comic about a guy named Eric who gets killed, paints his face up and goes after bad people... oops wrong film, that was The Crow. Please let me start over. El Muerto (The Mexican Crow) is based on the comic about the foreign guy from That 70's Show who gets killed, paints his face up and goes after bad guys. Keep in mind that these two films (and I assume comics) are completely different from each other, after all The Crow was shot by bad guys before he gets his revenge and The Mexican Crow drives into a tree while concentrating on some mariachi radio station. To be perfectly honest I was impressed with this film, although it is a complete rip off from J. O'Barr. It was definitely smarter than the last 2 Crow movies and I hate to admit that Fez is adorable even without the accent. Check it out, you might surprise yourself.

history.title: The Final Patient
history.text: This film was alright for an indie flick; tolerable acting and a decent story... well for about 3/4 of it, that's when the concerns arise: The 400lb sheriff gets upset when the boys visit the doctor even though no crime was committed. Some crazy butterscotch lady either sleeps, hollers, or lays on the floor with her head in a duct throughout the whole movie. An exotic Buddhist elixir that dumbs itself down to common US rattlesnakes and my personal favorite, "Hey doc, you're bleeding real bad from your nose and mouth... are you OK?'. Overall I liked it, I think they should have left out Aunt Jemima and the snakes and maybe added a Twilight Zone type ending (old man finds elixir for amazing feats). It's still good though, I did not release my bowels once in shame during this film so it is worth a rental.

history.title: Salvage
history.text: This film is like having diarrhea. You sit there for 90 minutes doing your thing until you come to the realization your arse is numb and it's time to wipe, flush and go on with life. Nope, no sir, didn't like it.

history.title: Meat Market [DVD]
history.text: After watching this film I needed to clear my head by hitting it against a wall a few times. Although I have seen many bad movies in my day and many more worse than this film I still shudder to think how I sat through this movie without attempting to take my life. The Good 1. Lesbian Vampire Chicks 2. El Diablo - The Mexican Wrestler 3. Lesbian Vampire Chicks The Bad 1. Poor Writing 2. Really Poor Writing 3. Super 8 Filmed Antics The Ugly (Spoilers) 1. The fat chick running from the zombies would have never made it to safety. She would have either had to stop at a hot dog stand for a bite to eat, hence being attacked by zombies, OR she would have collapsed from exhaustion due her giganticism. 2. Dry humping in a dirty tirlet while zombies parade around your apartment building. I believe it is a zombie rule that if you are teamed with someone of the opposite sex and there are zombies around, you do not dry hump in a dirty tirlet. 3. I have eaten the flesh of many animals in my time from beef to chicken to snake to babies and not once did the first bite echo a disheartening crunch. The zombies in this film weren't eating flesh, they were eating celery and that's all you hear throughout the whole film... the crunching of celery. Had the lesbian vampire chicks and El Diablo been added earlier in the film I may have enjoyed it more. Unfortunately, they come in later in the film and by that time the voice in my head was telling me creative ways to take my life. I have yet to see the sequel and I prefer not to. It is a good attempt at film making but it's sad when grub worms are used for maggots, grandpas 1973 Super 8 handy cam is used and all the zombies are vegetarians.

history.review_title: The whole thing is so obviously stupid.
history.text: Don't be fooled by the reviews. This had promise, but was so poorly done. Did they not pay attention to their own script? Beautiful wilderness with beautiful running creek, yet they have no water. Then why the sink and faucet and dish rack? Even dish soap on the sink. The girl is dark skinned with brown eyes, but the mother and father are light skinned with blue eyes. The old man chops wood for their heat yet a barrel outside continues to burn. What??? The whole thing is so obviously stupid.
Really quite awful. Acting and effects awful. Not scary and really no plot. Only got thru half and couldn't stand it anymore. One star for a beautiful home and lighthouse.

Saw this on the big screen. Although very colorful with pretty scenery the movie itself is a disaster, really terrible. Decided to see this because I had a few hours before my dentist appointment. The dentist appointment was less painful. Yes, it is that bad.

history.title: The Cosmonaut
history.review_title: Could have been a great movie, but it wasn't.
history.text: OK? Can someone please tell me what that was? This movie had great potential. Space, romance, fairly good acting, great scenery and effects. So what the h happened. Too many confusing flashbacks in what order? Here is the movie in a nutshell; love triangle, one goes off to space, he comes back, it appears to earth in a different time zone or dimension, she can hear some of his transmissions. In the end it appears the other male entity of the triangle has had enough or maybe they both have. End of story. Like I said, this storyline could have been great. It wasn't.

I like it that the protagonist wasn't corrupt. Even at the very end, in Thornton's scene with William Hurt, the writer didn't succumb to sentimentality over character and the law. If you have a character who believes in law, he isn't going to break the law at the end for some sentimental reason. I felt all the twists and turns were interesting, and really surprising sometimes. It's seldom that a television show plot twist takes me by surprise, so it was great. Actors were all good, and convincing. Characters well-developed.

Man, this is bloody, graphic, dreadful. What was I thinking? Oh, I guess I was thinking, "Legolas, Boromir, Brad Pitt, Peter O'Toole . . ." Handsome men, but too violent. And the dialogue is awful, too. Creative writing 101, unedited. Anachronistic boats, weapons too, I understand (because I looked it up in Wikipedia, eh.) Boromir, though . . . and a young, smooth-cheeked Legolas. At least they don't kill off Sean Bean in this. Oops, was that a spoiler? His name's Odysseus, though. How could it be a spoiler? Odysseus goes off on a long adventure after the Trojan War.

Creepy and disorganized, yeah. Plot twists for the sake of plot twists. It's easy to figure out, though, rather early in the show and then it's just a long slow zombie-fest and gore galore to the end. I liked some of the actors, though, and the location is interesting. Could have been better. I got through the first nine episodes and then couldn't take it any more. So I watched the last episode just to see how it comes out. Started season two but it's a bore. Boring gore.

history.text: Could have been better, especially if they condensed it by one or two episodes. It got a bit dull toward the end. Otherwise, pretty good. Good scenery, good actors. Lots of surprising little plot twists, red herrings.

history.review_title: Arrest the writers! Life imprisonment for twaddle.
history.text: The first few seasons were good, light, charming, beautiful scenery. The plots weren't completely ridiculous. But season six! I just watched season six, episode 3. My gosh, the most awful embarrassing twaddle. No wonder the lead actor wanted to quit. The writers were phoning it in and ought to be drummed out of the writer's corps. So, I guess I won't be watching any more. Too bad Kris Marshall isn't the new Dr. Who. He would have been good in that role.

history.title: Thor
history.text: Pleasant film, lots of action and excitement. Tom Hiddleston is very good. I would like to have given it 3.5 stars, somewhere between "it's okay" and "I like it." Absolutely no depth at all. Motivation hinted at, not really developed. At least no gratuitous sex scenes and Natalie Portman remains completely clothed throughout the movie! I couldn't tell if it was meant to be funny, or thrilling. I think Thor's resemblance to Jack Black caused that confusion. Lots of color. Clearly there is carry-over to other movies. For instance, S.H.I.E.L.D. isn't explained. I guess the folks who read the comic books know more about it. Anyway, entertaining, pleasant, not a total waste of money.

history.title: Chronicles of the Ghostly Tribe
history.text: This is definitely worth watching. It has a story with huge plot holes, but who cares. A bit Indiana Jones thriller, a bit of magic, a bit of science fiction, plus monsters. Good actors, good monsters, lots of twists, some very funny comic actors and romance. Also, if you pay attention you get some idea of the Red Guard, just hints.Also some amazing photography and scenery. The ending is romantically tragic, but that's OK too.

history.text: Edge of the seat action all the way! I had to stop watching a couple of times because it all got so tense. Dwayne Johnson and the other actors did a good job. Visuals are great, too. Earthquakes, explosions, tsunami, lordy it was a lot.

Thank god and greyhound he's gone! Moffat that is, Steven Moffat. Awful writing which is a pity because Peter Capaldi and Pearl Mackie are excellent actors. It could have been an awesome series. As it was, this last episode was decidedly schmaltzy, cheesy, drowning in treacle. How can I put it? So mushy and sentimental, no real plot, just rehashing stuff. And now Peter Capaldi and Pearl Mackie are gone, and we don't know what a wonderful series it could have been if someone else had been doing the writing.

Kind of predictable, but funny in spots. I like Dwayne Johnson, and he had some funny bits. Every now and then Steve Carell would sound like the original Maxwell Smart, but mostly he played the role his way and that was OK.

history.title: FAQS
history.text: FAQs may not be entirely realistic, but that's not its point. It is a beautiful, well-crafted, touchingly acted, inventively directed independent film about disenfranchised, abused young gay people who protect and care for each other after being victimized by violent familial and societal fallout from our current (7/2006) government-endorsed homophobic culture. It is warm, loving, moving, angry, sexy, politically accurate, honest, triumphant. Straight people may not get its message nor be able to process its images--as with most of Everett Lewis' films, so they may want to buy something more accessible like "Latter Days" or "Brokeback Mountain" (both wonderful films, but more mainstream).

history.title: Rhinoceros
history.text: One would think that the combination of Eugene Ionesco, Zero Mostel, and Gene Wilder would be a guaranteed success. Sadly, such is not the case with the American Film Theatre production of "Rhinoceros" as committed to film in 1974. While the theme of maintaining one's identity as everyone else goes along with the herd (originally a metaphor for Nazism, McCarthyism, etc.) is intact, Ionesco's text has been so altered that is is destroyed. Here it becomes subject to slapstick, poor unfunny added situations, exaggerated performances, and clumsy direction. The film has been criticized for "staginess," but that is not the real problem. It makes use of camera movement, external sets, etc.; it just has no rhythm. It is a trial to get through it--certainly not the case with Ionesco's original, either on stage or as read to one's self. Gene Wilder is always diverting but the character he portrays has been so tampered with that it's just unpleasant and tedious. Karen Black's character is an embarrassment as are all the other minor characters. The only bright spot in this mess is Zero Mostel, whose fifteen minutes on screen are amazing, his transformation from a dandified fussbudget into a destructive rhinoceros an acting tour-de-force; done without makeup, it encapsulates the essence of the piece. But that's it: the other ninety minutes are dreary and awful. The DVD is very well transferred, but the extras are disappointing: e.g., an "interview" with Zero Mostel is simply text to be read frame by frame, and an article about Ionesco and the play is simply an on-screen text repetition of the liner notes. There is a very long interview with the director, in murky sound; after seeing his incompetence demonstrated in this film, no one will have any desire to see him drone on about it.

history.title: Breaking The Cycle [DVD]
history.text: "Breaking the Cycle," is poor, simulated, soft-core gay male erotica shot on video (not film). It attempts to be a romantic comedy with the "message" that surfing the internet for casual sex is no way to find a long-term relationship, hardly an earth-shattering piece of information. The guys are pleasant-looking but the acting is laughable. 10% Productions uses straight actors playing gay; nothing unusual there, but interviews with two of them reveal that they were very uncomfortable doing so. It is obvious that no one received much coaching because the simulated erotic scenes are clumsy and the guys are apparently nervous even about being seen kissing; as a result, they look like they have never kissed anyone, male or female. Everything about their participation is a real turn-off. Irresponsibly, nowhere is there a hint of safe-sex practices. The two principals are supposed to be roommates who are actors having trouble finding work. That premise is the only candid aspect of this mess: who would hire such talentless hacks? This item is a complete failure, falling flatter than a pancake either as comedy or erotica.

history.title: Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (Limited Edition)
history.text: I can see how some people would be disappointed that the superior original versions of the Star Wars Trilogy are relegated to "bonus discs" in these new 2-disc sets, that they are presented in simple 2.35:1 letterboxed widescreen rather than anamorphically enhanced for widescreen TVs, and that the prints have a certain amount of speckling and jitter. Nevertheless, the original theatrical versions, as presented, look quite respectable on normal, good-quality (if not HD) 4:3 TVs or monitors; they are basically crisp and correctly colored, better than any VHS, LD, or unauthorized, private DVD-R made from the LDs that I have seen. The 2.0 sound is accurately chosen; the original closing credits simply say "Dolby Noise Reduction": Dolby Digital 5.1, like any digital format, was certainly unknown in 1977. To those who have said that these are merely copies of the 1993 laser discs, I would point out that STAR WARS has the original title crawl, without the later-added "Episode IV: A New Hope": absolutely the first time we see it in any home video form, including the laser discs. On the other hand, some cleaning up of video speckling and anamorphic enhancement for 16x9 TVs would not have been difficult or costly these days; and the omission of special features present on the extra disc of the 2004 4-DVD set, like the "Empire of Dreams" documentary or any trailers, is disappointing. The original versions are packaged with Lucas' later revisions/remasterings ("Special Editions") which few people need (and many don't want) but the combination does provide an immediate way to compare and contrast. If the raw form in which the original films are offered was Lucas' way of trying to bias people toward the more opulent, restored 2004 revisions, he has erred again and accomplished exactly the opposite: the theatrical versions win, hands down, even in a less sophisticated presentation. If, as Lucas says, the original elements are in too poor condition to fully restore the old versions and these are the best he is willing or able to give us, I am not too disappointed: indeed, were he to find good elements and restore them, doubtless he would start tampering all over again. At least these imperfect prints show no marks of intrusion. Moreover, the color timing for the 2004 revisions was dramatically altered and, because film fades with age, any changes made to the content of the extant old prints or negatives would be guesswork. I suspect that the theatrical versions in these sets are as accurate as they can be. As I said, some print damage might have been corrected and anamorphic enhancement could have been added (even some private from-LD versions have it), but these are small matters in the overall scheme of things.

history.title: Star Wars V: The Empire Strikes Back (Limited Edition) [DVD]
history.text: I can see how some people would be disappointed that the superior original versions of the Star Wars Trilogy are relegated to "bonus discs" in these new 2-disc sets, that they are presented in simple 2.35:1 letterboxed widescreen rather than anamorphically enhanced for widescreen TVs, and that the prints have a certain amount of speckling and jitter. Nevertheless, the original theatrical versions, as presented, look quite respectable on normal, good-quality (if not HD) 4:3 TVs or monitors; they are basically crisp and correctly colored, better than any VHS, LD, or unauthorized, private DVD-R made from the LDs that I have seen. The 2.0 sound is accurately chosen; the original closing credits simply say "Dolby Noise Reduction": Dolby Digital 5.1, like any digital format, was certainly unknown in 1977. To those who have said that these are merely copies of the 1993 laser discs, I would point out that STAR WARS has the original title crawl, without the later-added "Episode IV: A New Hope": absolutely the first time we see it in any home video form, including the laser discs. On the other hand, some cleaning up of video speckling and anamorphic enhancement for 16x9 TVs would not have been difficult or costly these days; and the omission of special features present on the extra disc of the 2004 4-DVD set, like the "Empire of Dreams" documentary or any trailers, is disappointing. The original versions are packaged with Lucas' later revisions/remasterings ("Special Editions") which few people need (and many don't want) but the combination does provide an immediate way to compare and contrast. If the raw form in which the original films are offered was Lucas' way of trying to bias people toward the more opulent, restored 2004 revisions, he has erred again and accomplished exactly the opposite: the theatrical versions win, hands down, even in a less sophisticated presentation. If, as Lucas says, the original elements are in too poor condition to fully restore the old versions and these are the best he is willing or able to give us, I am not too disappointed: indeed, were he to find good elements and restore them, doubtless he would start tampering all over again. At least these imperfect prints show no marks of intrusion. Moreover, the color timing for the 2004 revisions was dramatically altered and, because film fades with age, any changes made to the content of the extant old prints or negatives would be guesswork. I suspect that the theatrical versions in these sets are as accurate as they can be. As I said, some print damage might have been corrected and anamorphic enhancement could have been added (even some private from-LD versions have it), but these are small matters in the overall scheme of things.
