Ida's aunt, a brave but self-destructing judge in communist Poland played by Agata Kulezsa, is the only bright spot in this film with her fine acting.

history.title: Panfilov's Twenty-Eight WORLD WAR II MOVIE DVD NTSC PANFILOV'S 28. LANGUAGE:RUSSIAN . SUBTITLES:ENGLISH
history.review_title: A missed chance by the Russian cinematography...
history.text: The film uses authentic weapons, tanks and other war material but it's weak on human expressions. Even though the actors wear authenitc uniforms and they act well, their well fed and clean faces, and most importantly, theis stares are not at all convincing. They are simply not the faces or the stares of weary war veterans who have suffered terribly in a winter of hard war against a powerful and seemingly unstoppable enemy as was the Wehrmacht in November 1941. The Germans are also portrayed as faceless zombies, novices, stupid and without initiative. A mediocre film which despite its excellent scenery can't put the viewer really into the battle and into the era.

history.title: Sands of Iwo Jima
history.review_title: John Wayne fighting as a tough Marine sergeant at Tarawa and Iwo Jima...
history.text: With the possible exception of Terence Malick's superb "The Thin Red Line", "Sands of Iwo Jima" is the best and most entertaining movie covering the Pacific theatre of the Second World War, and particularly the landings at Tarawa and Iwo Jima. As one song pointed out, John Wayne did not fight on Iwo Jima, but watching his performance today you feel that perhaps he could have done. He was deservedly Oscar nominated for his portrayal of tough Marine Sergeant John M Stryker, but eventually lost out to Broderick Crawford. Tough sergeant John Strycker leads a troublesome group of new recruits into battle. John Wayne plays his usual stereotype tough guy but does what he does very well and like his men you do find yourself warming up to Strycker. Based on a true story, the infamous battle of Iwo Jima this has very good performances from the whole cast and good battle scenes but although they are often interwoven with actual newsreel footage I could easily discern every time the real scenes from the fictional ones, hence it loses one star. Perhaps it's the way actual Marines moved on the battlefield, or the load they carried, or how they took cover than no actor, however well taught, could imitate. But a film made so closely to the actual era is surely unbeatable in terms of authenticity regarding the faces, the attitudes, the material, the scenery and the language. Unforgettable film!

history.title: Fast Runner Atanarjuat
history.review_title: "Apocalypto" transfered in the Arctic, with a family feud as its central theme instead of the ritualistic sacrifices...
history.text: An extraordinary film - written, produced and acted by Inuit people - and it transports the watcher to a world completely different than ours. The exact era that the story is taking place is very difficult to establish, because the Inuit do not use much metallic items or new technologies. It seems that every tool, clothes or transport means they use are hand made by them. It was a bit of a struggle to get into the film at the beginning and I found myself wondering just who was doing what to whom. It moves at a snail's pace (but that's part of its charm) and it goes on for nearly three hours but none of that time is wasted. It provides a stunning observation of Inuit culture and tradition, especially on how they deal with disputes and legal issues, with the core issue being that of the polygamy custom which is actually a matter of survival as women are provided only by their menfolk. The film only really takes off when the two sons of one of the families that has been cursed grow up. The film doesn't need any special effects because the Arctic backdrop provides them, and the spare and empty landscape gives this drama a mythic feel. It is worth hanging in there as it will captivate you soon enough. The film is VERY realistic and there are clear displays of cruelty towards animals, because beating dogs is obviously a part of everyday life in the Arctic and the director didn't want to hide it. A great film, unlike anything you've seen so far!

history.title: Red Tails
history.review_title: Great dogfight scenes but otherwise a missed opportunity...
history.text: “Red tails” is a movie that is inspired by a true story: the first unit in the US Air Force (the so called "Tuskegee pilots" after the small town in Alabama where their training started in 1943) in which all pilots as well as the ground crew were African-Americans. For a film that celebrates and commemorates the trail-blazing heroism of the first American black pilots against Nazism abroad and White Supremacy at home, is the grotesque racial stereotyping of the characters, who mostly appeared to be in the 'Amos and Andy', gumbo and watermelon, 'Chicken George' mould. These intelligent young guys were trained pilots at the serious business of powered flight and war and I somehow doubt they were constantly wisecracking and playing Blues guitar or ranting about 'Black Jesus' as if they had just stepped off the plantation. Also, I don't consider realistic that a black American would flirt in 1943-44 an Italian girl without a second thought, that she would accept a black foreigner as boyfriend or husband! It's completely out of the spirit of the epoch and not believable a all. The German enemy were similarly cartoonish and equally offensively stereotyped. Whenever a US pilot shoots down a German plane, he shouts in jubilation: “Yeah! I got him!” The pilots act like kids who are playing a video game. But this is not a game. It is a real battle about life and death.That said, the film features some very good special air to air effects, but not overdone and there are some decent flight and dogfight scenes in it. I tried to like this movie, but it did not work. There are too many flaws, which I cannot ignore. “Red Tails” cannot get more than three stars.

history.title: Dunkirk (DVD)
history.review_title: A very good BBC documentary about Dunkirk, not to be mistaken for latest Nolan’s film…
history.text: Although many people mistake this documentary drama in three parts for Christopher Nolan’s latest film (it is NOT), this is one of the best things the BBC has ever done, a brilliant testimony to a fantastic feat of determination. It gets the sense of urgency and desperation that Dunkirk was, across nicely without getting bogged down with too much detail. The time is equally shared between the Royal Navy and the British Army but unfortunately the RAF is totally missing from the story, hence it loses one star. It’s filmed in the same shakey camera way as “Saving Private Ryan” and feels gritty. I enjoyed the fact you see the decisions being made back in England and the views of the troops in France. Look out for Benedict Cumberbatch playing a British officer of the rearguard before he became the international star he is today. The German troops (mostly Waffen SS) are well depicted, as are some atrocities that took place those days of May 1940. All characters presented in the documentary are real people, and there is a small caption about their fate in the end of the film.

history.title: True Grit (1969)
history.review_title: An exceptional Western for which John Wayne rightly won his first and only Academy Award…
history.text: This is a GREAT classic of westerns and a GREAT classic of world cinema. When her father is murdered by one of his employees who also fled with the family savings, headstrong young girl Mattie Ross (Kim Darby) is determined to see justice done. It seems the justice system isn't up to the job so she has to hire a man with "true grit" to track the murderer down. She hires a drunken, cantankerous, one-eyed known as Deputy Marshal Rooster Cogburn (John Wayne), to find the man and see him punished. The Deputy Marshal is a tough, cynical, even cruel guy, with a foul tongue, bad manners, short temper and a great liking of whiskey and violence. When Cogburn's employer insists on accompanying the old gunfighter, sparks fly. And the situation goes from troubled to disastrous when the inexperienced but enthusiastic Texas Ranger Le Boeuf joins the party because he is also after the same man for the killing of a Waco senator and his bird-dog. All three set off for the Indian Territory after the murderer., and the interaction between the three main players is superb. Although there is a new version of the film with Jeff Daniels and Mat Damon, this one has an edge having the legend that is John Wayne and what makes this version so much better than the remake is it can be serious and light. The script is well written and funny and the acting is inspired. Dialogs (unusually articulate for a Western) and human relations rather than action are the greatest treasure in this film. The "true grit" turns out to be equally distributed between Mattie, Rooster and Le Boeuf. During the course of the mission, the three come to respect each other and Rooster and Mattie develop something close to a father/daughter relationship (he usually calls her “baby sister”). It's an excellent film with wonderful characters and classic scenes (Wayne says to a dying cowboy: "Your friend's done killed you, and I've done for him", to which the reply comes haltingly "He never done me wrong 'til he killed me"). Robert Duvall steals every scene he is in. John Wayne is a hoot and quite rightly he earned an Academy Award for his role in the film. Kim Darby, Strother Martin and Glenn Campbell are also okay. Well don't just take my word that this is the best “cowboy” movie ever - be swayed by the panel who gave John Wayne his one and only Oscar for “True Grit” - truly his very best. Many other supposedly classic westerns although they have good bits, overall have now lost much of the magic they once seemed to have. “True Grit” has not.

history.title: Look Who's Back ( Er ist wieder da ) ( Look Who is Back ) [ NON-USA FORMAT, PAL, Reg.2 Import - Germany ]
history.review_title: Adolf Hitler comes back to life in 2014 and what follows is funny but also truly terrifying…
history.text: “Er ist wieder da” is the original title of this absolute gem of a film from Germany and it is a comedy – of sorts. It uses the book’s basic premise and the characters from it, but does change the storyline and ending quite considerably. The plot is that Adolf materialises in 2014 straight from 1945 and is totally befuddled as to what has happened to the rubble, the enemy aircraft and why the youth don’t seem to recognise him or even worse they don’t know how to do the Nazi salute. There is also the parallel story of Fabian Sawatzki who is a freelance film maker in need of a break and he sees ‘Der Fuhrer’ as a handy meal ticket back into TV. The film has genuinely funny moments, but the underlying theme is dark. Hitler is not portrayed as a sympathetic character but the film captures, just like the original story, the ease with which he puts forwards his political views and gets them listened to in modern society. The actor playing Adolf Hitler is Oliver Masucci and he is an absolute show stealer. Apart from some minor mistakes (Hitler was not fond of touching other people or being touched) he plays his part nearly perfectly. Some of this has been adlibbed on actual German streets and other situations and some of the reactions of the public are remarkable for all the right and wrong reasons. The film is in German, which is only right (it would have seemed very strange to have the actors speaking in English, even worse if they used pretend German accents like in old war films). Therefore it is subtitled in English - so you need to give it your full attention. This is a fantastic film. It starts as a comedy -that's the way with far right politics, it's all fun and games until people start dying- but in the end it isn't funny at all, but truly terrifying.

history.title: Manchester By The Sea
history.review_title: A film that makes you think of life’s strange turns. Be prepared for a rollercoaster of emotion…
history.text: Brilliantly acted drama, great story, great acting, locations and music, and characters that build up throughout the movie. It’s really a work of art, very well observed and realistic. The whole thing was very human and believable. I like the way the plot (a little obscured in the first half) wove together. Initially you have the sense that it’s very slow moving and depressing but you can’t really get away from it. This movie had my full attention and Casey Afleck is great in this. This movie is heartbreaking and I spent days after watching it thinking about it. I enjoyed this slice of what could be a reality with struggles held bare. Human beings can withstand a lot but sometimes there are limits in the misery and bad luck we can manage. Absolutely brilliant, beautiful film which should have won the Oscar for Best Picture. A must-see!

history.title: Good Bye, Lenin! (Special Edition)
history.text: This is a delightful, charming film with English subtitles and Daniel Brühl as the main character (he played later the highly decorated German soldier in Tarantino’s “Inglourious Basterds” who had an astonishing shoot out with his loved one near the finale). Watch “Good-bye Lenin” if you want to get a true feeling for what it was really like in the old East Germany. The film swings always in perfect balance between tragedy and comedy. It gives a sideways look at Berlin and some of its characteristics and the irony cuts both ways – we really don’t know whether to cheer or mourn the coming down of the Wall. It is a wonderful blend of gentle humour and tugging on the heart strings as Alex (Daniel Brühl) attempts to protect his mother's fragile life by trying to convince her that her beloved DDR is still in existence despite its fall during her time in a coma. It is a great history lesson documented on a very personal level, a story about a family in crisis and about the things we will do for the people we love, regardless of the political situation we happen to be in. Whilst the film is humorous it is also quite sad and reflective. It shows that not everything changed for the best and all things western had their personal and societal costs. All in all a fantastic film where a beautiful blend of superb cinematography. Top-quality acting and an excellent sound track make it a film that you can see again and again and enjoy it everytime. Don't miss it!

Even though you expect the worst, it does not turn into a horror movie of exploitation, but rather introduces you into this world where one wealthy society exploits another. Moves slowly, but really just the pace of real life.

Interesting little film. Deals with questions of class, privilege, worker allegiance, and family loyalty and love, and how all of these elements might mix. The arrival of the daughter serves as the catalyst to bring all these reactants together and bring them to a boil. You can almost feel yourself right there, trying to navigate this difficult course between all of the characters. The acting is right on by all, and the directing sets a slow and steady pace.

history.review_title: Disappointing Video of Botanical Garden in Hawaii
history.text: Whether you will like this video or not will depend upon what you are looking for. Are you looking for a very tranquil video of flower pictures? Something to soothe the nerves?? Then this may be for you. If you are looking for something informative, this is not for you. The opening to this video was somewhat reminiscent of the PBS series: "Secret Gardens of the World," a very delightful series! This video is nothing like that! There is absolutely NO narration. I could have taken a video camera and came up with the same thing. In my opinion, that is what this video looked like. The music was very soothing and did sound somewhat tropical but I wanted something that sounded Hawaiian. I was greatly disappointed! Apparently, these videos were used by a travel type agency. This video does show the title of the Hawaiian Tropical Botanical Garden as they enter the garden. Other than that, there is no explanation or description of anything. The plants are not labeled. Having over 30 years of gardening in a sub-tropical climate, I was able to identify many of the plants. If not for that, I would not have known which plants were which. These were not specimen plants, either (of course), which made some of the plants more difficult to identify. Labels or an actual human voice identifying what was being seen would have made this a more enjoyable film. I wonder how many, over the years, who have watched this made the decision to include the Botanical Garden in their tour of Hawaii. As I have stated, the music was somewhat tropical. Since this was supposed to be a very tranquil presentation, I can understand the almost monotone music selection. However, a livelier, more Hawaiian sounding selection would have done wonders for this work. Sounds of birds would have helped this very uninspiring picture.

history.review_title: Well Done Gardening Video for the Beginner on Up
history.text: First, I liked this very informative video but only gave it 4 stars as much has changed since this was made in 1996. However, this is an interesting outdoor classroom for beginning gardeners. I, also, believe that more advanced gardeners may enjoy this. I love the step by step procedures that they give for planting perennials as well as propagating them. I like their clear explanations of things like the names of plants. I especially like that they inserted the names of the perennials as they showed them. Good photography. They clarified the need for the gardener to know their particular climate/zone, soil and light. They do their growing in the pacific northwest (Northwestern California). Therefore, some of the plants they worked with will not necessarily grow in a more desert climate (without making serious modifications), They did recommend that the gardener, who is new to growing in his area, go to the local nursery to get information on plants to grow in their area. It is usually best to check with more than one such nursery as some nursery personnel don't actually garden. Overall, a very enjoyable and informative gardening video regarding perennials.

history.review_title: Charming Story of 12 Christmas Trees & A Library & Love in Bloom
history.text: Twelve Trees of Christmas - 12/18/2014 At Christmas time, I am always searching for videos with a Christmas message. Sadly, they are so few and far between. This video is, yes, another "romance at Christmas time" video. But, there is another message about what?? Helping others! (Sadly, nothing about Christ, as has become the norm). It is about rescuing a Library that is being condemned and the benefits it provides to the community it serves. Love the 12 Christmas trees! And, oh no! It does have a few traditional Christmas songs scattered through it (appropriately) -- which I also listen for in today's imitation Christmas videos. The Christmas music is about the birth of Christ, which is most important to me! As a child, long before today's technologies (which I do embrace and enjoy), the local Library was a major source of learning and entertainment for me. As a seven year old, I walked across town (well over a mile) to the library, to check out books, such as Peter Pan, Jack in the Beanstalk & so many other children's stories. So, this video did revive many pleasant memories. This movie was entertaining and enjoyable. Whether you are Christian or not, I think you might enjoy this movie. If you hate things pertaining to Christmas, skip it. If you are looking for soft porn, skip it. It is a movie that all ages might enjoy (no embarrassing groping, no slurping kisses going down to the toenails, inside - no half naked bodies -- none of that stuff that removes the imagination & romance). It allows your imagination to continue this story. I do recommend this movie.

history.review_title: Doesn't do justice to the novel
history.text: First, the print from which the VHS version of this film was made is in TERRIBLE condition--lots of scratches and blotches, with a soundtrack of poor quality. As for the content, the technique of telling the story as a series of flashbacks was disappointing. A straight narrative approach would have 1) been easier to follow and 2) made better use of the terrific cast. Too much screen time is devoted to shots of the protagonist walking disconsolately along the beach as he experienced his many flashbacks.

history.title: A Tale of Two Cities
history.text: This 1980 film adaptation of Dickens' novel is superior in costume, set design, and cinematography to the 1935 version starring Ronald Colman as Sydney Carton but sadly, it is inferior dramatically. The acting of the main characters in this version is comparatively wooden (lacking in expressiveness). In particular, the portrayal of Lucie Manette by Alice Krige is a pale shadow of Elizabeth Allan's fine performance in the 1935 version. Nor does Sydney Carton's anguished worship of an idealized "spiritual" Lucie quite come off in this 1980 version. However, David Suchet gives a very convincing performance as the French spy, John Barsad. In general, the supporting cast in this production is stronger than the actors cast in the lead roles.

history.title: From the Terrace
history.text: Joanne Woodward is to be applauded for her skillful portrayal of Paul Newman's self-centered larger-than-life trophy wife in this story of a quest for happiness. The film is worth watching just to see Woodward in this uncharacteristic role. Paul Newman is less convincing as a WWII veteran (navy pilot) caught between his desire to outperform his cold father in the business arena and his desire for the love that he never received from his harsh father and alcoholic mother--only from the household servants while he was a boy. Myrna Loy's outstanding performance as Newman's mother, sunk deep in alcoholism, is particularly touching. The film has a curious static quality, possibly because of its pacing. Most of the shots are very carefully conceived to convey the underlying message of personal destiny. In the end, one cannot avoid comparing the fate of Newman's neglected mother with the prospects for his abandoned wife. Will Mary St. John have enough "guts" to resurrect herself from the wreckage of her marriage, or will her ungovernable temper be her downfall?

history.title: Journey to the Center of the Earth

history.title: Sleeping Beauty: A Gothic Romance
history.text: This version of "Sleeping Beauty" bears little relation to the classic version, other than Tchaikovsky's music. The Princess is deliberately portrayed as an adolescent klutz and the prince as a foolish adolescent tool of dark forces, personified by the Lilac "Fairy" danced by a male in pseudo-Gothic costume. If you like bare male torsos (one of Matthew Bourne's specialties) and females who are choreographed to dance like men, this is the ballet for you. Lovers of inventive, creative, graceful choroeography can skip this one as Mr. Bourne seems to have a very limited bag of tricks.

history.title: Doc Martin Bundle Package
history.review_title: This is a terrific series. Martin Clunes is brilliant as the curmudgeonly ...
history.text: This is a terrific series. Martin Clunes is brilliant as the curmudgeonly Dr. Ellingham, displaced by late-onset blood phobia from his career as a London surgeon to general practice in a small seaside village in Cornwall. Many if the medical situations (over-medication, diabetes, environmental toxins, inappropriate use of prescription drugs, etc.) encountered by the doctor will resonate with contemporary medical problems experienced by viewers. Likewise, some of the classroom situations encountered by Doc Martin's "friend" Louisa Glasson, head-teacher at the local elementary school will be familiar to educators. Underlying the entire series is the overwhelming contradiction between the social expectations one normally entertains of a doctor and the utter inability of Dr. Ellingham to "deliver" the requisite bedside manner. Is he autistic or just stubbornly individualistic?

history.review_title: largely due to James Fox's excellent interpretation.
history.text: This adaptation of Arthur Conan Doyle's story is definitely tainted by the all-pervasive values of Hollywood--a "romantic interest" has been added to the story by including a nubile young woman and her ineffectual guardian in the all-male cast of characters. Viewers please note that in the novel, the character Lord John Phillip Roxton is an experienced big-game hunter and NOT a womanizer. Also disappointing is the degree to which the crusty character of Professor Challenger is watered down. Indeed, the only character really true to the original story is Professor Summerlee, largely due to James Fox's excellent interpretation.

history.title: Maigret - Set 1
history.review_title: has the advantage of better casting and greater attention to the psychological dimension of ...
history.text: These adaptations of Simenon's detective fiction, 54 in all, made for French television, vary considerably in quality and in fidelity to the original text of the stories. Some of the episodes were shot in outdoor locations and other episodes are studio productions. On the whole, the studio productions are much more stylized and theatrical in interpretation, perhaps consciously so? In some of the episodes (for example: "Maigret Sets a Trap"), the casting leaves much to be desired, which weakens the psychological power of Maigret's solutions. Also, in the later episodes, there is a bizarre change in the way Maigret treats his subordinates at Judicial Police headquarters--he becomes much more peremptory, even nasty, which is contrary to the underlying warmth and respect for comrades exhibited by Maigret in the stories. Unfortunately, Madame Maigret is reduced to an unheard voice on the other end of the telephone in most of these adaptations. On the whole, the British series, starring Michael Gambon, has the advantage of better casting and greater attentiveness to the psychological dimension of the stories, but in some episodes the limitation imposed by their 60-minute format necessitated considerable paring down of the plot and action. Gambon's portrayal of Maigret captures the detective's stolid, brooding, impenetrable aspect more accurately than Cremer's somewhat light-hearted but fatalistic approach to the character. The British series also includes Madame Maigret in more episodes (portrayed by two different actresses), but her style of dress is more chic than Simenon intended. There will never be a perfect on-screen interpretation of Maigret because he is UNIQUE. We will get only an approximation of his indelible character.

history.title: And Then There Were None
history.review_title: but I was very disappointed and a bit bored by the obviousness of this ...
history.text: If you are a purist and prefer film adaptations to stick to the original text, this is NOT the version for you. In the book, Anthony Marston is not a drug user and there is no homophobic murder by William Blore, no late-night drunken orgy, and no sex between Philip Lombard and Vera Claythorne. Also, in the book, Vera hangs herself alone in her room and there is no final encounter between herself and Justice Wargrave--the method of his diabolical scheme is revealed in a postscript written by Wargrave himself. Also, the heavy brooding music and dark tone that dominates the film from beginning to end is contrary to the steady but incremental erosion of "normalcy" and it undercuts the element of surprise that makes Agatha Christie's original story so captivating. This version has been "modernized" for viewers who MUST have their hefty dose of sex and grisly violence (chalk one up to Hollywood!). I was hoping to find a version that preserved the subtleties of Christie's plot and characterization, but I was very disappointed and a bit bored by the obviousness of this heavy-handed interpretation.

history.title: Rock Dog
history.review_title: Someone seen Kung Fu Panda, Zootopia and Sing and decided to try to make a movie...
history.text: Rock Dog is the story of Bodi, a young dog from a small village, who finds he'd rather be a rock star than a guard dog. He travels to the city to pursue his dreams but finds it may be a little harder than he thought. This movie is kind of a mess. The first part of the movie focuses on Bodi's Village, a generic minion-like sheep village with a generic "I dont approve of your choices" father. Bodi, his father and the sheep really have no characters outside of "main character", "disapproving father" and "dumb villagers". There's also this odd "the wolves are coming to destroy the village" that seems like they ripped it straight from Kung Fu Panda 3, only they forgot to add a reasoning or any lore as to why the Mastiff family can do this 'magical attack' or why the wolves want to attack the village. This is probably the most boring part of the movie as Bodi just kind of meanders around for awhile until something happens to make him want to leave. The second part focuses on Bodi's adventures in the city, meeting the "rock god" Angus and meeting his future band in a world that seems like Bodi is awkwardly traveling through time to get to. Again, the characters here have no character, instead just saying lines and being as generic as possible. They are more tolerable than the sheep villagers, though. The best character by far, and the one that steals the entire movie, is Angus Scattergood. Dont get me wrong, he's not given much of a character. But his interactions with Bodi are at least amusing and Eddie Izzard's performance saves what would otherwise be a really generic "diva" character. And by the end of the movie, you're left questioning why anything even happened. Nothing is resolved, nothing is explained. Bodi plays a concert and that's it. Any semblance of any plotlines are just brushed under the rug. The animation on this isn't great but it's not bad either. It's colorful and it's got some nice music. Plus, there's nothing offensive or really objectionable. Younger kids might be amused by the second half of this movie (and bored by the first). However, for any older kids or adults, you're not going to find anything worth your time here. Definitely skip it. There's a lot better animated films out there.

history.title: Sing
history.text: Sing is cute, colorful, has snippets of great songs in it and the basis for great characters. There's nothing overtly objectionable in the movie that I could find and it's not offensive or mean spirited. The plot is pretty obvious from the get-go but it doesn't take away from the movie in general. It's a fun movie to pop in and watch while you're doing other things. It's a great movie to keep kids entertained. However, this movie has one big flaw and that's the characters. The characters are barely there. That is, they give them enough time to explain what their basic characteristic is (This one has dad issues, this one is a mom, this one is an angsty teenager, this one has stage fright, etc) and then just throw them together. Which is sad because I would have loved to see more of these characters and their backstories. Except Mike. Mike is a deplorable, wholly unlikable character that does nothing but be the catalyst for every bad thing that happens in this movie. They could have easily removed him and left time for the other character to at least develop a relationship with each other. As it is, there is kind of a lack of emotional impact when anything happens to these characters, either good or bad. And it's confusing why they seem to have this great team relationship halfway through the movie, despite barely or not even talking to each other at all. Had this movie put more work into actually developing these characters, this movie would be extremely fun to watch. But, as it is, it's just... not bad. Not great. But not bad. And while you'll probably have fun watching it the first time around, I can't image really finding any new enjoyment the second time around. Rent it once and enjoy it for it's cute, harmless fun.

history.title: Lego Batman Movie, The (Blu-ray) (BD)
history.text: The Lego Batman Movie is Cute. There's really no other way to describe it. It's got the same humor and fast-paced dialogue as The Lego Movie, so if you weren't a fan of that, you probably won't be a fan of this one. This movie did give me a few giggles at the old batman reference and a few jokes. It has a good moral and a predictable but nice plot. I wasn't a big fan of the whole Joker-Relationship gag as it felt a bit too close to what someone would write in their BatmanxJoker fanfiction (to be fair, I think that was the joke, but I found it more cringe than funny). There were quite a few jokes that did fall flat but the fact the movie was so quickly paced, you didn't have time to think about them. The animation, of course, is gorgeous and unique. And this movie decided to drop the whole live-action bit that the Lego Movie had, which I think is a major plus. Overall, I think this movie is great for everyone to watch at least once. It's definitely one of those movies that will make you feel happy watching it.

history.title: DISNEY DESCENDANTS 2
history.review_title: Wasted Potential in a Made-For-TV Format
history.text: Descendants 2 can only be described as a movie with a lot of really great ideas that never really go anywhere. The Made-For-TV length really hampers this movie as plotlines are introduced and then as quickly are pushed aside with no resolution. The characters, even after two movies, are still not really given time to shine, grow or evolve. And the new characters, that being Uma, Harry, Gil, Lonnie and Dizzy, are barely there. So much so that, if they simply replaced them with characters from the previous movie, there would have been absolutely no difference. All the characters could have been interesting by themselves, if given any sort of chance to do anything other than say "I'm the Son/Daughter of [insert character here]". They set them all up and give them little tidbits of possible foreshadowing and then, nothing. The idea of children of Fairytale characters has been done to death and while this franchise has some good ideas, it doesn't bother to expand on them, making this rendition of the old tale bland and unoriginal. There are some improvements from the last movie, though. By far the biggest is the music. They've, for the most part, dropped the bubblegum children's cartoon pop and awkward techno dubstep in favor of a more current music theme. The two standouts, for me, the Rap Battle-eque "It's Goin' Down" and the "Chillin' Like a Villain" song which sounds like it was inspired by Bruno Mars. They've also made the storyline and world bigger and set up future ideas down the road. However, this is all pointless as the runtime of the movie gives barely any time to do anything with it. The most insulting of all is that this movie is written and acted (for the most part) as if selling it to 8 year olds. Considering the source materials they're pulling from and the obvious success of projects like this in the past (see Once Upon a Time), having a little more time and effort put into the movie to appeal to all audiences would have not only been appreciated but would have helped propel their franchise in the long run. I could forgive the cheap sets but when the dialogue breaks your suspension of disbelief, it's hard to enjoy it at all. Children might enjoy this movie. It's full of catchy tunes and fun action scenes. However, for everyone else, it's a pass. Bad dialogue, poor acting, sterotypical plotlines, no character development, no actual conclusions and no real heart. It's a shame to see so much wasted potential.

history.title: Fantastic Beasts And Where To Find Them (2016)
history.review_title: Amazing Characters and Beasts, Terrible Plotline
history.text: Fantastic Beasts has great characters. Honestly, some of the most genuine and likeable characters i've seen in awhile. I wanted to root for these characters. I wanted to see these characters grow and evolve. I wanted to learn more about the creatures and why Newt has become so attached to protecting and learning about them. So, I was pretty disappointed to see where the film went and how it ultimately ended. The plot is just too heavy and gives no room for character development. The movie seems so focused on building the world and the American Magical Police/Government system that it barely takes time to explain anything it brings up. The beasts (you know, the creatures the movie is named after) are rarely shown or really spoken about and serve only as a MacGuffin and eventually a Deus ex Machina for the plot. And the plot itself is all over the place. Bouncing between plotlines I really could care less about and special effect extravaganzas that leave no lasting impact on the story. I was honestly bored through most of the film. I wanted a story about the characters and instead I got a bland story about the corruption of the American magical society and some evil guy who really had no reason being there. Which is extremely disappointing considering what they had to work with. I've heard of people absolutely loving this film. And, i'm really glad to hear it. Because I want this franchise to continue, if only for them to actually focus on the characters and drop the pointless side plots. I was never a fan of Harry Potter, so I dont know how well fans of that franchise will react to this movie. It's definitely not Harry Potter. However, i'd recommend people watch it if only for the characters. I do look forward to the next film, I just hope it'll fix the problems of this one.

history.title: Saban's Power Rangers [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital]
history.text: Yes, it's predictable and a bit corny but it's just a ton of fun the whole way through. The characters are interesting and likeable and the plot is fast paced and highly enjoyable. Fans of the old original series will get a bit more enjoyment out of the story as there are references and easter eggs galore (including a great cameo at the very end) but it's not required to enjoy the movie. If you're looking for something a bit more thought provoking, you'd be better off looking elsewhere. But, if you looking for a quick, fun movie with lots of great special effects and action, this one might be for you. (Just note that the first scene of the movie is not a reflection of the rest of it. Honestly, that scene should have been left on the cutting room floor.)

history.title: Once Upon a Time: Season 1
history.text: After casually watching Once Upon a Time's later seasons, I was ready to grab some popcorn and laugh at, what I assumed the train wreck of a first season would be. Surprisingly, I found myself not only enjoying it but thoroughly engaged in the character's stories and wanting to know what will happen next. The mix of "real world" character drama and fairytale stories was just fun to watch, even if the fairytales were more of an original story rather than a retelling of their book or movie counterpart. The story, for the most part, was obviously thought out in it's entirety (with the exception of the last few episodes but i'll get to that) as the episodes fit together seamlessly. So much so, that, if you were to cut it down a little, it would feel like a really long movie rather than a television show. However, despite all the good, this season has many, MANY flaws. First of all, the introduction and then immediate dismissal of characters. Maleficent was a blink and you'll miss it addition which only served to be the "big showdown" moment for Emma. Honestly, that wasn't the big showdown we all wanted. And Maleficent plays such a small role and defeated so easily, she could have been replaced with anyone and it wouldn't have mattered. Cinderella got her own episode but then was never spoken of again, making me wonder why she was needed in the first place as they could have used that time to expand on the world or characters. Hansel and Gretel, of whom was just a plot device to fuel Emma's character development and then promptly disappeared. And Finally, the Mad Hatter/Jefferson. Who played more of a role than the others previously mentioned but also got very little time to actually do anything other than be a catalyst for the plot to move along. I'm sure there were other characters, but they are treated so insignificantly that I dont even remember them or feel it's pointless to bring them up. Second of all, the reason for the "curse". The whole reason for the show to exist. Evil Queen/Regina's hate for Snow White. The writers attempted, in her backstory, to make her a sympathetic character. But then it fails when we are shown the actual reason why she has become the person she became. It makes no sense. It's such an out of nowhere moment, contradicting what they were trying to establish in the previous scenes, that is makes my scratch my head in confusion. Had there maybe been some time devoted to her backstory before, where we could have maybe seen some kind of evil tendencies, it would have been understandable. But, as it is, it made no sense for a plot point that big. And finally, the last few episodes. While I mentioned before the show being one big cohesive narrative that runs more like a movie, the last couple episodes are the exception. Emma doesn't believe, the plot forces her to suddenly have flashbacks to events weren't even hers followed by a bunch of fanfiction-esque events that aren't connected at all. And then there's a lack of magic but a magical beast in the basement that she has to go fight? But then Jefferson suddenly knows something he shouldn't? And then oops there's magic because of a potion made of true love? And why wasn't this used previously? And if there's no magic why did the "magic well" have magic? And even if so, how does a true love potion bring back magic? What is going on and why? Honestly, the last couple episodes are so rushed, so nonsensical that it's like the show has made it almost to the finish line only to trip at the last second. None of it made sense. It was a mess. That being said, however, the ending is at least one that wraps up the story nicely as well as sets up (albeit rather poorly) the next season. Overall, i'd recommend fans of dramatic character-driven stories with a fantasy twist give this a go. Almost everything about this season is great. If you can get past the rather iffy ending episodes, i'd give it a shot. Now, i'm off to season 2. We'll see where we go from here.

history.title: Wind River [Blu-ray]
history.text: This movie is depressing. Given the subject matter, that being the sexual assault and disappearance of Native American women on Reservations, it's not very surprising that this movie would be extremely bleak the entire way through. Don't let the box art or description fool you, this isn't a crime thriller or action movie. This is drama with very violent and graphic scenes. Jeremy Renner and Elizabeth Olsen are awesome as the main characters, Cory and Jane. However, they really dont get much interaction outside of what the plot needs to dump some exposition. In fact, i'm not sure what the point of the character of Jane was. I was expecting some big reveal that she had some past connection to the case but no, she just really wants to help, regardless of the fact that she shouldn't really be there (something the movie establishes only a few scenes after she appears). Cory's past with his daughter is never really explained either. Something happens, he doesn't know what, we never find out. It's these loose plot threads that kind of make the movie feel incomplete and give this odd sense of disconnect as if we're watching an episode of a TV show or the first movie in a series, rather than a standalone movie. The only part I really enjoyed with them together was at the end, where Cory and Jane get a small quiet moment where they just talk before it transitions back to the reservation. Had this been any other movie, they would have at least been given time to develop. The movie seems to hint this connection but i'm not fully convinced by the end. The movie's overall plot is very point-to-point. We never really get a sense of a mystery or overall character development, the plot just goes along and we find out things when the characters find out things/say it, never before. There's no plot twists, there's no suspense. The story just happens. While this isn't a bad way of telling a story, this does give the movie more of a bleak tone overall. There is no 'fun' to be had in this movie. There's no edge of your seat moments. And the side characters are nothing more than people who stand around and spout exposition or are simply there to move the plot forward. I didn't care what happened to them by the end. While I can't say I regret watching this movie, I definitely wouldn't watch it again. It's a good movie for what it's about. But it's extremely violent and graphic, on top of being overall bleak, so I wouldn't really recommend the movie either as I feel a lot of people wouldn't be willing to watch a movie containing some of the things this movie contains. However, if you're looking for a darker movie, can handle some of the extreme scenes in this movie and it sounds interesting, i'd say give it a go.

history.title: The Little Prince
history.review_title: A whimsical tale of loss and growing up
history.text: The Little Prince is a fairytale for adults. Despite it's kid-like design, the move isn't flashy or fast paced enough to keep most children's attention. However, it's themes (those of death/loss, growing up, regret, losing oneself and moving on from relationships) are very much things that adults can relate to. And it doesn't help that the movie's animation is absolutely gorgeous and pulls you right into the story. I have never read the actual book the story-within-a-story is based on. I have no idea about it's accuracy. But I do know it's inclusion, a mixture of unique animation and whimsical child-like logic, only added onto the amazing story and themes of this movie. I dont know how much a child would like it, but I would suggest a watch to any adult who has no problems watching an animated movie about an old man reading a story to a child. You might find the story is a lot more relatable than you think.

history.title: Leap
history.text: Leap is the story of Felicie, a orphaned girl who dreams of being a dancer. When she and her best friend Victor run away from their orphanage, she finds herself with the opportunity to join the Paris Ballet. However, her lack of experience might get her kicked out before she can even begin. Leap is a mixed bag. On one side, it's one of those underdog stories with the same storybeats as you'd expect but otherwise a nice, almost harmless upbeat story. It has very pretty visuals, smooth animation (specifically when it comes to the dance scenes) and a really nice setting. And on the other hand, the English dubbing is absolutely horrid. It has completely out of place references, forcing dialogue in where no one is actually speaking, non-stop talking for the first 10 minutes of the movie (even during scenes where it's clear there was no talking), adding in explanations/exposition when none are necessary as well as very out of place stock pop music which sticks out like a sore thumb. I did want to switch to the original french to see the difference but to my surprise, the movie didn't bother to come with a french track or any other language for that matter. There are some questionable messages in the film as well. By far the worst is the main lead outright stealing an invitation from another person so she can get into the Ballet and then tries to justify it to the woman whose job she put in risk by saying she "doesn't understand". There are no real consequences from this. Other than maybe the bad guy of the film doing bad things. Other than that, however, the film is otherwise harmless and sticks to the same story beats you expect these kind of stories to go through. Kids will probably enjoy this and some older viewers might slightly enjoy this if they can get past the terrible dubbing. But, I wouldn't really recommend it.

history.title: The Grey
history.review_title: FINALLY!! A film that has some really NEAT plot twists!!
history.text: ....I just finished watching this on TV. Liked it so much that I turned right around and bought the DVD! I've waited for YEARS to find a movie that was written by someone CREATIVE enough to NOT bring in the cavalry to make rescues at the last moment! LOVE it!! That said, though --- and this isn't a spoiler because it didn't happen in this movie --- I'm STILL waiting to see that which I MOST want to see i8n a movie. That being a situation where the day can be saved only by a last-minute save... and THEN the disaster happens irreversibly just BEFORE the rescuer arrives! There must be some INANE rule, written or unwritten, that writers and directors invariably follow, which calls for NEVER allowing that to happen! And... has anyone EVER yet seen a movie in which a toddler is playing out in a dusty street in a Western... and DOES get run over by a stagecoach and finished off just seconds before the would-be rescuer could reach him to scoop him up out of harm's way? (How I WISH I could write a screenplay with such stunning and unheard-of twists, and see it come to the big screen!!)

history.title: Amerika (TV miniseries)
history.text: My rating of this is based solely upon what my friends thought of it, and reported back to me, after i returned home from a trip I was on when it aired. I knew before I left that it would be on, and I remember being surprised at all the criticisms that were being leveled at it ahead of time. Many people seemed to think that it was to be over-critical of the USSR, and I was concerned that the network that aired it would KOWTOW to the whiney malcontents and tone it down/water it down/soft-pedal it. To date, I don't know it this mini-series suffered that fate, or instead survived intact and aired as originally filmed. I hope the latter! And I also hope to FINALLY get to see and own the DVDs of it someday. Because as I write this, it is only BARELY available, and GROSSLY over-priced!! Go figure that!! Ironically, I was in MOSCOW when it aired! The Russians get to see a LOT more of OUR TV than we see of theirs. (How I WISH we could receive ALL of Europe''s networks and TV shows over here in the USA... and that it would be free of any censorship. I should be lucky enough to LIVE that long! Considering the fact that the technology that would make that both possible and EASY to do has been around for several decades, it's AMAZING that it hasn't happened yet!) (Oh well --- we haven'r even been back to the MOON in the last 45 years, so such foot-dragging on America's part is par for the course, unfortunately.) When I was in Moscow, "Amerika" didn't air there in real time, so I don't know it the Russians have ever yet seen it, or if so, what they thought of it.

history.text: One of the worst films I have ever suffered through. The actors are great at their jobs, but without some sense of realism we lose touch with them. I could not believe in the chemistry between the two main characters other than to believe they had a strong sexual connection. We are meant to think, however, that they have a real marriage. I found it impossible to relate to that idea, not because they were so at odds with each other -- as that often happens in marriages. But that there was nothing to make me believe in them as human beings. Both are enormously selfish people, difficult to like as individuals, and grating as a pair. The policewoman, and the twin sister, were the only characters in the movie who seemed motivated by recognizable impulses. There is a lot of gratuitous sex and violence on top of the main flaw that prevents any sort of empathy toward the central characters. Finally, it is way too long. I couldn't wait for it to be over.

history.title: Charles & Camilla - Whatever Love Means
history.text: A sad effort. Lawrence Fox is excellent as Charles. The problem is, Charles is something of a stick: hates his father but is a total wimp in his presence; is socially inept despite years of training; and feels sorry for himself. With so little to recommend him personally, the efforts to pair him off with a suitable mate feel like an uphill battle. Camilla's affection seem to be stoked mostly by the rejection of her own husband. There is little in their relationship to arouse our admiration or concern: two rich snobs who believe they have every right to cheat those who trust them. But the main problem is that when the central character in a movie is dull as dishwater it is impossible to get interested in what happens to them.

A strange movie dominated by an apartment. The place in which most of the movie takes place is like another character -- the central motif and motivation of all the action that takes place within it and because of it. The acting is excellent but the story itself lacks verisimilitude. We are asked to believe that a 57 year old man, seemingly normal though not especially happy with his life and circumstances, will become unglued when he learns his Dad had an affair. His reaction, even when it appears he also lost his mother decades earlier because of the infidelity, feels extreme. Meanwhile, as the result of a casual comment, the Kristin Scott Thomas character ends an affair she has been having with a married man. This decision also seems unrealistic and arbitrary. Finally, two relative strangers become romantically involved way too quickly, given the back story and the repressed and furtive natures they express. Given the excellence of the production and the quality of the acting it would not be possible to dislike the overall experience. But the ability to believe in the characters and the changes that take place in their relationships seems forced upon them rather than an unfoldment to which the viewer can comfortably relate.

A bit slow going at first, with tension between a mother and son, the mother oddly jealous for his interest in the old man, and between the mother and Holmes over who is running the household. There is a focus on an old case, complicated by the failing memory of Holmes. But the real story is in the relationships of the three people in the house and how Holmes, after a life marked by a strict hold on his emotions and adherence to fact over fiction, finds some use in the latter and the value of allowing compassion to rule the day. A touching, heartfelt, and quietly satisfying picture.

history.title: The Age of Adaline [DVD]
history.text: First half of movie is slow going; hard to relate much to Adaline other than her scenes with her dog. But need to hang in as the entrance of a persistent and engaging man seems to wake her up. Also, movie gets another jolt [there are several others from genuine electrical sources] when Harrison Ford enters the situation. I have rarely enjoyed this actor as much as I did in this movie. Instead of coasting on his stardom and familiar moves and phrasing, he finds a center of the character he is playing and injects emotional sense into a bizarre and barely believable plotline. Ford adds gravitas to the situation. Romantically, the movie works because despite an absurd premise, the emotional interactions are quietly developed and gradually resonate with reality as we know it. Again, the earlier scenes have a distancing 'Ground Hog Day' quality that requires some patience. But the end result is affecting and worth the journey.

history.title: A Place to Call Home
history.text: Totally engrossing drama with two brilliantly played and written staring roles for women. There is balance between the negative energy of the matriarch, Elizabeth and the invading alien Sarah, and the positive relationship unfolding between George, Elizabeth's son, and Sarah. Because of her power-playing MO, Elizabeth recognizes her match in Sara -- instinctively at first -- and takes an instant dislike to her. That said, there are a few less compelling relationships -- Anna and her Italian lover, for example. The idea that a carefully bred beauty of her class and time would be reading 'Lady Chatterley.." and that her catholic-bred farm boy beau would, after reading a few pages of same, dismiss years of catholic indoctrination, feels contrived. The chemistry between the two is enough without this motivating prop. Other oddities that struck an off note: Sara's physical domination of a the local bully felt off. Women can be successful fighting off men, in certain circumstances. But what works dramatically fails to resonate humanly. No matter how violent their backstory, women don't borrow trouble by taking on men in open combat [unless armed], to the extent of pursuing them into their man-caves to humiliate them further. Doesn't scan. Yet, on the whole, this story, playing out in a grand family homestead set in magnificent Australian countryside, is a visual and emotional treat. The main characters are well written, believable, complex, and nicely played. It makes for great adult entertainment, assuming one has the hours to spend watching it.

This series thrives on the believability of its main character, Sidney Chambers. In the beginning I found him a bit much -- too handsome, too nice, too charming by half. But the writing is great and what brings us close to him is his relationship to two other main characters: the spoilt and difficult Amanda, who makes us understand -- by breaking his heart -- that his affections are not as superficial as we might imagine. The other is Georgie, a more edgy personality t, who challenges the young vicar with his good humored cynicism. There are many mysteries to solve in the series, but they seem more about bringing out moral and ethical choices than about solving crimes. Not having read the book I cannot say how well the filming of it reflects its ideas, but this series stands on its own as a worthwhile study of fully realized and dimensional people, working through relationships with each other. Absorbing and satisfying in myriad ways. Highly recommended.

history.review_title: ... the antics and improprieties of Sylvia [Rebecca Hall in fine form], that our sympathies lie with her long-suffering ...
history.text: The script telegraphs that we are supposed to be so offended by the antics and improprieties of Sylvia [Rebecca Hall in fine form], that our sympathies lie with her long-suffering husband Christopher Teigiens [Cumberbatch] and his suffragette sweetie [Clemens]. The problem with this is that in their few bedroom scenes together the chemistry between Tiegiens and Hall feels more real than what takes place between him and Clemens. The extra-marital romance simply fails to convince. Clemens character is so pure in her love for Christopher that it feels airbrushed, more articulated than felt. And his love for her seems feckless, though we are supposed to think it is his high-mindedness that keeps him from acting on it. To his credit, Cumberbatch lends substance to a character that might seem absurdly academic and repressed, and we grow to like him. But it is Hall who walks off with the movie. She displays more sensuality in a single turn of her head than her young rival can convey naked in bed with Silvia's husband. Bottom line: if you don't buy the affair, the series is without much to offer aside from the blood bath in the trenches and some great period piece costumes.

history.review_title: McAdams does a superb job of making it possible to believe she could go either way with a choice between a baffling husband or o
history.text: A disarming and surprising film. All characters thoughtfully cast. McAdams does a superb job of making it possible to believe she could go either way with a choice between a baffling husband or old love. Her children are drawn with more care than kids usually are, and we find ourselves paying more attention to what they are thinking. The privatized space aspect of the drama is sketchy, but believable enough. What makes it all work, however, is the artfully directed communications between the characters. The flirtation between Cooper and Stone is offbeat, quirky, sometimes hard to follow, and ultimately convincing. More than usual is asked of the audience to figure out what these two protagonists are thinking and saying. Communications between people are not scripted in the usual way. There is much conveyed with tone and body language. Much of this resonates with the backstory of the Hawaiian culture and its haunting music and story-telling dance movements. The silent husband has an eloquence of his own. But the scene in which the daughter discovers the truth about her real father is the most effective and demonstrates how much can be conveyed to another without words. This is not a movie for those who want the obvious. It forces the viewer to partake of a more subtle, more compassionate, version of human life and love.

Lovely acting but script doesn't quite scan. The idea that a paralyzed man would want to go to the wedding of his ex to best friend doesn't fit emotionally. This choice does, however, foreshadow his final solution to his problem. What William cares about most is his right to choose his destiny and, in his case, to martyr himself. Much of his reasoning is capsulated in a scene in which he reveals how much he loved his former life. This life, seen in bits of flashback, consisted largely of high risk sports activity and daring-do, at which he excelled when not busy with his career, not to mention a cushy role as son and heir of a castle owning dripping with money doting family. That such a lifestyle might make a man feel life in a wheelchair didn't quite 'cut it' is not surprising, nor an attitude confusing high achievement with self-knowledge. Despite being given every advantage money can offer in trying circumstances, not to mention the devotion of a bouncy Pollyanna from the other side of the tracks, he chooses to end his existence. One get the sense that he believes he has a right to make this decision the way he has a right to stay in five star hotels and select the best wine for dinner. For all his attractions -- and he is an attractive character despite his condition -- he fails to see that life is not something to toss aside, simply because there are others involved. What makes the film moving -- ironically -- is not the fate of the invalid but the deep love his parents have for him and the wonderful performance of the young woman who falls in love with him. The emotional struggles of these three characters ring true and clear, and restore a bit of the faith that the central character seems so unable to muster. What the film lacks is a moral message that is, in any way, inspired [though clearly the writer assumed we would respond differently]. William's gift to Ms. Clark -- in the form of some sort of trust fund -- falls terribly short of what she gives to him.

history.title: Jfk The Final Hours
history.review_title: A Mandatory Purchase For History Buffs
history.text: I don't currently own this but have seen it five times on TV. Each time is as good as the first time not bored with it in the least bit. It shows JFK in his whirlwind trip to Texas the last three days of his life. As for me I was 7 years old and saw JFK in San Antonio at his appearance at Brooks AFB. My Dad was stationed as a Drill Instructor at Lackland Air Force Base on the other side of San Antonio. My Dad told me not to go to school we were "going on a special trip and see someone special". Little did I know it was JFK. It was around 2:30 in the afternoon JFK gave a short speech we were standing out in this field about 100 yards away is my best guess. This special shows that appearance and the rest of his trip ending in Dallas. A lot of appearances by people who saw him on that trip 50 years ago including kids that were in elementary school up to his Secret Service Agents. To me the most amazing thing about this special is that each location is shown as it is nowadays and then is superimposed by how it was 50 years ago ! A must see for anyone who knows about JFK and his impact on America !!!! P.S. this will be my next purchase from Amazon !!!

I knew then I had to buy this. There are 26 episodes on 6 DVD's around 20 minutes each. I kind of thought they were longer. It follows General Dwight D. Eisenhower's book of the same name as he talks about World War 2. The narrator is Westbrook Van Vorhuis and someone who does the actual quotes from the book speaking as General Eisenhower I believe it is Maurice Joyce (it even sounds like him). There is footage I have never seen before in 90% of the set and I love history so if you like history and seeing new stuff this is something you should buy.

history.title: Superman The Movie: Extended Cut & Special Edition 2-Film Collection [Blu-ray]
history.text: It's too good to be true! Super rare TV cut here. For those wondering and as the story goes the Salkind producers put together a lengthier version for TV back in the 80's to pad time and get more money from the network. Don't confuse this with most versions that were aired on TV as this cut contained extra scenes and extensions, I think everything the producers could find really having seen a blurry cut of it myself. It only aired a few times to my knowledge and those scenes have never been restored or released officially in any format. So there was a TV cut which was always shown and this one that is the holy grail. Not saying it contains tons of scenes with Superman but true fans should have fun picking out the little moments added into the Bluray. A real gem we're getting here.

It moves fast which I like but some areas should've been longer/fleshed out. Much of the movie was assembling the team. Superman entered way too late for me, there was no black suit scenes which we were teased about either which would've put a nice layer of depth to the movie. Maybe if we get an extended version it will be more of a meaningful movie. The villain was okay, I found him kind of creepy. I may be just slightly bored with superhero movies so it was just average in my opinion. This is what can happen when things are reshot, recut, re-directed, overblown, overpriced, underwritten, etc. The movie suffers. WB was hyping this 3 years ago and it turned into a big mess going forward. It's time they look elsewhere for directors other than Weadon and Snyder.

The comedy saved it for me, it had some cool villains and action moments but again, these movies are way too long and get bogged down with laser beam FX and flashy CGI. The first half of the movie could've been trimmed for pacing cause once the ending battle was foreshadowed we were already a long 2hrs in. My brain starts to get clogged at this point. There's enough in here though to recommend I just wish they'd not shoot so much stuff that isn't needed story wise.

If only they would have hit the eject button on my DVD player.

history.title: Jeepers Creepers
history.text: I agree with a previous reviewer. This movie started out great but just fizzled in the end. Actually, it ran out of gas about the same time that Darry and Trish's car ran out of gas less than halfway through he film. That is where we get the diner scene that is a ripoff of Duel, and the introduction of the psychic character who dragged the story down. Shortly thereafter we get a glimpse of the sci fi (not horror) looking beast and we're ready for the credits to roll to save us from wasting any more time.

history.title: Phone [DVD]
history.text: Although I agree that this movie won't exactly scare you away from using your cell phone the way that Psycho scared you away from taking a shower, it's still an above average movie that is well worth viewing. Fans of Ha Ji-won, who plays the intrepid and persistent reporter, won't be disappointed to see that she has grown up from the teenage comedies she is better known for. The girl who plays Young-Ju does a convincing job of making you think she is possessed, which is all the more eerie for me since she resembles my Korean niece of about the same age. I don't buy many DVDs, but this one is in my collection because the story is good, the directing is slick, the actors are talented (and the females good looking, which doesn't hurt), and it's just overall a solid film.

history.title: Dead End
history.review_title: Dead End is no dead end.
history.text: I really enjoyed this flick. It very deftly combined comedy with horror, which is no easy task. I was totally caught off guard by the humor. Most horror movies either have no humor, or the humor is poorly executed. I expected the same here, until I found myself busting out laughing at several scenes. The "do you have to suck on the bottle like that?" line starting things rolling and there were several others that elicited more than just a chuckle. But a horror movie's main task is to frighten and scare you. This does that as well. Driving down a deserted road late at night makes for a nice setting. And as the events start happening to this family you can't help but feel their despair. Another thing I like is how they slowly start breaking down psychologically and turn on each other (some of the funniest lines come out here). And then you get the ending, which didn't turn me off like it did so many others. Overall an enjoyable ride that I'd gladly take again and again.

history.title: Train To Busan
history.review_title: Thrilling Ride from Seoul (almost) to Busan!
history.text: This is not your typical zombie smashup film. Fans of the genre wanting to see head bashing slaughter will be disappointed. There is plenty of edge of your seat action, just not gore or over the top killing. One scene is particularly memorable involving a chain of zombies clinging to a train caboose! This film is primarily about humans, the choices and sacrifices we make and how those choices (hopefully) affect the self-reflection of ourselves and how we are seen by others. The director very skillfully has our main protaganist go from a villian you are rooting against in the beginning to a person you hope survives from about the halfway point of the film. There is one character that's a bit over the top as far as his self-absorption, and some of the actions of characters involved are a bit unbelievable. However, on the whole a well presented and thrilling ride from Seoul (almost) to Busan.
